text: This paper addresses the critical issue of anomaly detection in Internet of Things (IoT) environments, particularly in hierarchical edge computing architectures. The objective is to develop an adaptive anomaly detection system that can efficiently identify and respond to anomalies in real-time, while minimizing false positives and negatives. To achieve this, we propose a novel contextual-bandit approach that leverages the concept of edge computing to enable distributed and autonomous decision-making. Our method utilizes a hierarchical framework, where edge devices and servers collaborate to detect anomalies, and a contextual-bandit algorithm is employed to optimize the detection strategy. The results show that our approach outperforms traditional anomaly detection methods, achieving higher accuracy and lower latency. The key contributions of this research include the development of a scalable and adaptive anomaly detection system, the application of contextual-bandit theory to IoT anomaly detection, and the demonstration of the effectiveness of hierarchical edge computing in improving detection performance. This study has significant implications for the security and reliability of IoT systems, and its findings can be applied to various IoT applications, including smart cities, industrial automation, and healthcare monitoring. Key keywords: anomaly detection, Internet of Things, edge computing, contextual-bandit, adaptive learning, IoT security.

text: Learning the structure of a causal graphical model using both observational and interventional data is a crucial task in many scientific fields. Continuous optimization for score-based methods is a promising direction, offering an efficient, data-driven approach to learning causal graphs. However, existing methods typically require constrained optimization to ensure acyclicity or lack convergence guarantees. In this paper, we introduce ENCO, an efficient structure learning method for directed, acyclic causal graphs that leverages both observational and interventional data. ENCO formulates graph search as an optimization of independent edge likelihoods, with edge orientation modeled as a separate parameter. This approach enables us to provide convergence guarantees for ENCO under mild conditions without constraining the score function with respect to acyclicity. Our experiments demonstrate that ENCO can efficiently recover graphs with hundreds of nodes—an order of magnitude larger than previously possible—while effectively handling deterministic variables and latent confounders.

text: Preparing and scanning histopathology slides consists of several steps, each with a multitude of parameters. The parameters can vary between pathology labs and within the same lab over time, resulting in significant variability of the tissue appearance that hampers the generalization of automatic image analysis methods. Typically, this is addressed with ad-hoc approaches such as staining normalization that aim to reduce the appearance variability. In this paper, we propose a systematic solution based on domain-adversarial neural networks. We hypothesize that removing the domain information from the model representation leads to better generalization. We tested our hypothesis for the problem of mitosis detection in breast cancer histopathology images and made a comparative analysis with two other approaches. We show that combining color augmentation with domain-adversarial training is a better alternative than standard approaches to improve the generalization of deep learning methods. Our findings indicate that this synergistic strategy significantly outperforms models trained with conventional stain normalization techniques alone, as well as baseline models without any domain adaptation, particularly in maintaining high detection accuracy across datasets from previously unseen scanners or staining protocols. This underscores the potential of domain-adversarial learning, when coupled with appropriate data augmentation, to create more robust and widely applicable diagnostic tools in computational pathology.

text: Representations learnt through deep neural networks tend to be highly informative, but opaque in terms of what information they learn to encode. We introduce an approach to probabilistic modelling that learns to represent data with two separate deep representations: an invariant representation that encodes the information of the class from which the data belongs, and an equivariant representation that encodes the symmetry transformation defining the particular data point within the class manifold (equivariant in the sense that the representation varies naturally with symmetry transformations). This approach is based primarily on the strategic routing of data through the two latent variables, and thus is conceptually transparent, easy to implement, and in-principle generally applicable to any data comprised of discrete classes of continuous distributions (e.g. objects in images, topics in language, individuals in behavioural data). We demonstrate qualitatively compelling representation learning and competitive quantitative performance, in both supervised and semi-supervised settings, versus comparable modelling approaches in the literature with little fine tuning.

text: In recent years, Hippeastrum cultivars in Vietnam have exhibited considerable diversity in color, morphology, size, and type; however, the supply of cultivars remains limited and prices are high, particularly for double-flowered varieties. In order to develop double-flowered Hippeastrum cultivars utilizing the genetic resources of Vietnamese Hippeastrum, six hybridizations were conducted between six Vietnamese Hippeastrum accessions (used as female parents) and two imported double-flowered Hippeastrum cultivars (used as male parents) at the Vietnam National University of Agriculture since 2012. The results produced six hybrid fruits with the number of seeds per fruit ranging from 92 seeds (TH3) to 145 seeds (TH1), germination rates from 33.3% (TH14) to 85.7% (TH9), and a total of 286 hybrid seedlings. Evaluation of 111 hybrid Hippeastrum plants in 2015 based on traits suitable for potted or cut flower use led to the selection of 29 hybrids, including 13 semi-double and 16 double-flowered plants. The hybrids demonstrated diversity in color (orange-red, flag red, velvet red, pink, white with red stripes, or red with white stripes, etc.). The number of petals per flower ranged from 7.7 to 17.0, and fragrance was either present or absent. Flower diameter varied from 12.2 cm (TH1-25) to 18.2 cm (TH12-17), and flower longevity on the inflorescence ranged from 5 days (TH12-49) to 14 days (TH3-3 and TH12-23). These materials are valuable for the evaluation and breeding of double-flowered Vietnamese Hippeastrum cultivars and for the development of technical measures to facilitate their commercial production.

text: The object detection process relies heavily on bounding box regression, a critical step that has traditionally utilized the \ell_n-norm loss, despite its lack of alignment with the commonly used evaluation metric, Intersection over Union (IoU). Although IoU loss and generalized IoU (GIoU) loss have been introduced to better support the IoU metric, they are plagued by issues of slow convergence and inaccurate regression. To address these limitations, this paper introduces the Distance-IoU (DIoU) loss, which incorporates the normalized distance between the predicted and target boxes, resulting in significantly faster training convergence compared to IoU and GIoU losses. Additionally, three key geometric factors influencing bounding box regression are identified - overlap area, central point distance, and aspect ratio - and used to develop the Complete IoU (CIoU) loss, leading to enhanced convergence and performance. The integration of DIoU and CIoU losses into prominent object detection algorithms, such as YOLO v3, SSD, and Faster RCNN, yields substantial improvements in both IoU and GIoU metrics, and the incorporation of DIoU into non-maximum suppression (NMS) as a criterion further amplifies performance gains, with the source code and trained models available at https://github.com/Zzh-tju/DIoU.

text: Image synthesis through classifier networks offers a novel methodology for generating high-resolution, photo-realistic, and diverse images at scale, eschewing the need for an explicit generator network. The proposed Synthesize-It-Classifier (STIC) leverages an image classifier's inherent knowledge of class boundaries, employing gradient ascent with respect to class logits and synthesizing images via the Gram Matrix Metropolis Adjusted Langevin Algorithm (GRMALA) from a blank canvas. During an iterative training phase, the classifier re-estimates the class boundary by incorporating these synthesized images as "fake samples," thereby concurrently enhancing classification accuracy and the quality of synthetic outputs. The method demonstrates that integrating both "hard" (one-hot class conditioned) and "soft" (convex combination of classes) fake samples significantly improves class interpolation. Further extensions include an Attentive-STIC network, showcasing iterative image drawing on large datasets like ImageNet, and Score-STIC, which utilizes a class conditional score classifier to achieve superior results across multiple real-world datasets, including ImageNet, LSUN, and CIFAR-10. This framework represents a significant advancement in classifier-driven generative capabilities.

text:
Phân tích nghiệp vụ đã xác định hệ thống sẽ bao gồm ba tác nhân chính: Quản lý hệ thống (super admin), đối tác (partnership), và người dùng với các nhu cầu cụ thể như mua NFTs, mua tem hoặc chuyển đổi token. Biểu đồ use case tổng quát của hệ thống được trình bày trong Hình 2.1, cung cấp cái nhìn tổng quan về các ca sử dụng. Để đi sâu hơn, các biểu đồ use case phân rã chi tiết cho từng tác nhân đã được xây dựng, cụ thể là Hình 2.2 cho Quản lý hệ thống, Hình 2.3 cho Đối tác, và Hình 2.4 cho Người dùng.

Vì số lượng các use case trong hệ thống là khá lớn, đồng thời nhiều use case lại đơn giản hoặc có sự tương đồng, nên một số use case quan trọng và nổi bật nhất đã được lựa chọn để trình bày quy trình nghiệp vụ và phân tích chi tiết. Các biểu đồ hoạt động minh họa các quy trình này bao gồm: biểu đồ hoạt động đăng bán NFTs (Hình 2.5), biểu đồ hoạt động mua NFTs (Hình 2.6), biểu đồ hoạt động đăng tin đấu giá (Hình 2.7), biểu đồ hoạt động đấu giá (Hình 2.8), biểu đồ hoạt động tạo hộp quà bí mật (Hình 2.9), biểu đồ hoạt động chuyển đổi token từ onchain sang offchain (Hình 2.10), và biểu đồ hoạt động chuyển đổi token từ offchain sang onchain (Hình 2.11).

Trong phần đặc tả các ca sử dụng, các yêu cầu và luồng hoạt động của từng use case được mô tả cụ thể. UC01 "Nhập thông tin bộ sưu tập" (Mã Use case UC01), thực hiện bởi Quản lý hệ thống hoặc Đối tác, cho phép người dùng nhập thông tin bộ sưu tập vào hệ thống. Hệ thống sau đó sẽ thực hiện đồng bộ dữ liệu của các NFTs trong bộ sưu tập vào cơ sở dữ liệu. Luồng sự kiện chính và các luồng sự kiện thay thế, cùng với các chi tiết khác, được đặc tả cụ thể trong Bảng 2.1. Tiếp theo, UC02 "Đăng bán NFTs" (Mã Use case UC02) là một chức năng quan trọng do Quản lý hệ thống hoặc Đối tác thực hiện. Điều kiện tiên quyết để thực hiện là người dùng phải là chủ sở hữu thực sự của NFTs muốn đăng bán, được xác minh thông qua địa chỉ ví Metamask. Quy trình này bao gồm việc kết nối ví Metamask để đăng bán NFTs trên giao diện quản lý. Sau khi giao dịch đăng bán được xác nhận thành công thông qua Metamask và tương tác với blockchain, hệ thống sẽ lắng nghe sự kiện được trả về từ Smart Contract và cập nhật dữ liệu vào cơ sở dữ liệu để hiển thị NFTs đó cho người dùng có thể mua. Các bước trong luồng sự kiện chính và các trường hợp lỗi trong luồng sự kiện thay thế được mô tả chi tiết trong Bảng 2.2. Hơn nữa, UC03 "Tạo đấu giá NFTs" (Mã Use case UC03), cũng được thực hiện bởi Quản lý hệ thống hoặc Đối tác, có điều kiện tiên quyết tương tự UC02, nhưng bổ sung yêu cầu NFT phải nằm trong các bộ sưu tập thuộc loại ERC 721. Chức năng này cho phép tạo đấu giá NFTs thông qua kết nối ví Metamask và tương tác với blockchain. Sau khi tạo đấu giá thành công, hệ thống lắng nghe sự kiện từ Smart Contract và cập nhật dữ liệu để hiển thị cho người dùng thực hiện đấu giá. Chi tiết về luồng sự kiện chính và thay thế được đặc tả trong Bảng 2.3. Cuối cùng, UC04 "Tạo hộp quà bí mật" (Mã Use case UC04) cũng thuộc nhóm các chức năng do Quản lý hệ thống hoặc Đối tác thực hiện, với điều kiện tiên quyết là người thực hiện phải là chủ sở hữu thực sự của NFTs và được xác minh qua địa chỉ ví Metamask.

text: This paper addresses the challenge of optimizing multi-agent systems using game-theoretic approaches, focusing on the development of a gradient-based method leveraging the Nikaido-Isoda function. The objective is to provide an efficient and scalable solution for computing Nash equilibria in non-cooperative games, which are critical in applications such as resource allocation, autonomous systems, and adversarial learning. We propose a novel algorithm that integrates gradient descent techniques with the Nikaido-Isoda function to iteratively approximate equilibrium points, ensuring convergence under mild assumptions. Our approach is computationally efficient, avoiding the need for exhaustive search or complex heuristics. Experimental results demonstrate the algorithm's superior performance in terms of convergence speed and accuracy compared to existing methods, particularly in high-dimensional and large-scale scenarios. The proposed method also exhibits robustness to varying game structures and initial conditions. This work contributes to the field of game theory by providing a practical and theoretically grounded tool for equilibrium computation, with potential applications in AI, economics, and multi-agent systems. Key innovations include the integration of gradient-based optimization with the Nikaido-Isoda framework and the demonstration of its scalability. Keywords: game theory, Nash equilibrium, Nikaido-Isoda function, gradient-based optimization, multi-agent systems.

text: This paper explores the effectiveness of bonus-based exploration methods in the Arcade Learning Environment (ALE), a popular platform for evaluating reinforcement learning algorithms. The objective is to investigate how bonus-based incentives can improve exploration efficiency in complex, high-dimensional state and action spaces. We propose a novel approach that combines intrinsic motivation with extrinsic rewards, using a bonus function to encourage agents to visit novel states and actions. Our method is evaluated on a range of ALE games, demonstrating significant improvements in exploration efficiency and overall performance compared to traditional epsilon-greedy and entropy-based exploration methods. The results show that our bonus-based approach can lead to faster discovery of optimal policies and improved robustness to hyperparameter tuning. This research contributes to the development of more efficient and effective exploration strategies for reinforcement learning, with potential applications in areas such as game playing, robotics, and autonomous systems. Key keywords: reinforcement learning, exploration methods, Arcade Learning Environment, intrinsic motivation, bonus-based incentives.

text: We investigate empirical scaling laws for transfer learning across distributions in an unsupervised, fine-tuning context. Training increasingly large neural networks from scratch on a fixed-size dataset eventually becomes limited by the data, causing performance (cross-entropy loss) to plateau. However, for models pre-trained on a large language dataset, the rate of performance improvement diminishes but does not cease entirely. We estimate the effective data "transferred" from pre-training by calculating how much data a transformer of the same size would require to achieve the same loss if trained from scratch. This approach focuses on data units while keeping all other variables constant. Our findings indicate that in the low-data regime, the effective data transferred is well-represented by a power-law involving the parameter count and the fine-tuning dataset size. We propose that the exponents in these power-laws reflect the model's generality and the proximity of distributions in a directed, rather than symmetric, manner. Our results show that pre-training effectively amplifies the size of the fine-tuning dataset, with transfer and overall performance scaling predictably with parameters, data, and compute resources.

text: Bài báo tập trung vào ứng xử của đất cát pha sét gia cường bằng sợi PP (Polypropylene). Đất thí nghiệm được tạo từ hỗn hợp 70% cát và 30% bụi và sét, sau đó được phối trộn với sợi PP có ba chiều dài khác nhau (10, 15 và 20mm) ở các tỷ lệ khối lượng khác nhau (0.5, 1, và 1.5%). Trước hết, với từng tổ hợp chiều dài sợi - tỷ lệ sợi, đất gia cường được thí nghiệm đầm chặt để xác định độ ẩm tối ưu và dung trọng khô lớn nhất. Sau đó tiến hành các thí nghiệm cắt trực tiếp và thí nghiệm nén ba trục CU trên các mẫu được đầm chặt tối đa theo kết quả thí nghiệm đầm chặt. Việc chuẩn bị vật liệu và mẫu thí nghiệm theo một quy trình chặt chẽ để tạo ra các mẫu với sợi được phân bố đều theo thể tích, hướng của sợi phân tán đều theo các phương. Kết quả thí nghiệm cho thấy việc trộn sợi PP vào đất cát pha sét có thể cải thiện đáng kể các thông số của đất bao gồm dung trọng khô lớn nhất, lực dính và góc ma sát trong thí nghiệm cắt đất trực tiếp, ứng suất lệch tối đa và biến dạng tương ứng trong thí nghiệm nén ba trục CU. text: We introduce DatasetGAN, an automatic procedure for generating massive datasets of high-quality semantically segmented images with minimal human effort, motivated by the data-hungry nature of current deep networks that require large-scale, time-consuming-to-annotate datasets for optimal performance. Our approach leverages recent GANs’ ability to generate realistic images and demonstrates that the GAN latent code can be decoded to yield a semantic segmentation of the image, with the decoder requiring only a few labeled examples to generalize across the latent space and thus enabling infinite annotated dataset generation. The resulting datasets can be used to train any computer vision architecture equivalently to real datasets, and the minimal manual segmentation effort allows for extremely detailed and richly annotated datasets, including fine-grained object and part segmentations. To validate our method, we generated datasets for 7 image segmentation tasks, providing pixel-level labels for 34 human face parts and 32 car parts, and demonstrated that DatasetGAN significantly outperforms all semi-supervised baselines and matches the performance of fully supervised methods that require up to 100 times more annotated data, suggesting profound implications for scalable dataset creation and future research in computer vision. text: Feature descriptors are fundamental algorithms in image processing, designed to convert image data into numerical feature vectors. These vectors serve as unique numerical “fingerprints,” encoding crucial information to distinguish one feature from another. Among the prominent feature descriptors are the Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) and the Histogram of Optical Flow (HOF). HOGs are specifically engineered for robust object identification and localization, demonstrating performance comparable to deep neural networks (DNNs) by leveraging the gradient direction distribution. This approach is particularly effective given the significant brightness variations at image corners and edges, where gradient calculations aid in feature detection. In contrast, HOF relates to Optical Flow, which describes the apparent motion patterns of objects, surfaces, and edges resulting from observer-scene relative motion. As an optical flow characteristic, HOF provides a temporal depiction of events, notable for being scale invariant and unaffected by the direction of motion.

text: These mechanisms are fundamental in managing the complexities of asynchronous tasks, particularly in scenarios where non-blocking operations are crucial for maintaining performance and responsiveness in web applications. Callbacks, being one of the earliest techniques employed, involve passing a function as an argument to another function and executing it once the asynchronous operation completes. However, this approach can lead to what is commonly referred to as "callback hell," where nested callbacks become difficult to read and maintain. To address these challenges, promises were introduced, offering a more structured and readable way to handle asynchronous operations. Promises represent a value that may be available now, or in the future, or never, providing methods such as `.then()` and `.catch()` to handle eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous task. Building upon promises, the introduction of async/await in ECMAScript 2017 marked a significant evolution in JavaScript's asynchronous programming paradigm. This syntactic sugar over promises enables developers to write asynchronous code in a synchronous manner, thereby improving readability and reducing complexity. By using the `async` keyword before a function, the function automatically returns a promise, and within this function, the `await` keyword pauses the execution until the promise settles. This approach not only simplifies error handling through the use of try-catch blocks but also enhances the overall structure and flow of code, making it easier to maintain and debug. As such, these asynchronous programming constructs in JavaScript are integral to developing dynamic and efficient web applications, where tasks can be executed concurrently without compromising the user experience.

text: In this paper we present a semi-automatic 2D-3D local registration pipeline capable of coloring 3D models obtained from 3D scanners by using uncalibrated images. The proposed pipeline exploits the Structure from Motion (SfM) technique in order to reconstruct a sparse representation of the 3D object and obtain the camera parameters from image feature matches. We then coarsely register the reconstructed 3D model to the scanned one through the Scale Iterative Closest Point (SICP) algorithm. SICP provides the global scale, rotation and translation parameters, using minimal manual user intervention. In the final processing stage, a local registration refinement algorithm optimizes the color projection of the aligned photos on the 3D object removing the blurring/ghosting artefacts introduced due to small inaccuracies during the registration. The proposed pipeline is capable of handling real world cases with a range of characteristics from objects with low level geometric features to complex ones.

text:
Data augmentation is a critical technique for improving the generalization of machine learning models, particularly in computer vision tasks. However, traditional augmentation methods often fail to preserve the semantic integrity of objects in images, leading to suboptimal regularization. This paper introduces **SaliencyMix**, a novel data augmentation strategy that leverages saliency maps to guide the mixing of image regions, ensuring that semantically meaningful parts of objects are preserved during augmentation. The proposed approach identifies salient regions in images using a lightweight saliency detection module and strategically blends these regions to create augmented samples. Experiments on benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, demonstrate that SaliencyMix significantly improves model performance compared to existing augmentation techniques such as CutMix and MixUp. Specifically, SaliencyMix achieves higher accuracy and better regularization, reducing overfitting while maintaining computational efficiency. The results highlight the importance of preserving semantic information in data augmentation and provide a robust framework for future research in regularization strategies. This work contributes to the field by introducing a saliency-guided approach that enhances the effectiveness of data augmentation, particularly for deep learning models in computer vision.  

**Keywords**: Data augmentation, saliency maps, regularization, deep learning, computer vision, SaliencyMix.

text:
This paragraph outlines the front-end and back-end architectural choices for a travel social network website, emphasizing the use of ReactJS for UI development and redux saga for managing asynchronous and business logic. It describes a modular front-end folder structure and details the back-end’s service package organization, specifically for the post-service. The two main packages, com.vifrin.common and com.virgin.feign, centralize shared data types and enable inter-service API calls, respectively, offering advantages in maintainability and system coherence. Figure 4.3 and subsequent explanations provide a visual and functional overview of these design decisions.

In the development of both the admin and user interfaces for the travel social network website, ReactJS was employed to construct the screens, while redux saga was integrated to manage asynchronous operations and encapsulate business logic. By confining most logic within the redux saga layer rather than dispersing it throughout the UI components, the system maintains clarity and separation of concerns. The front-end architecture is organized using a well-defined folder and function structure, which is illustrated in Figure 4.3. On the back-end, the package design follows a consistent pattern exemplified by the post-service. Specifically, the post-service utilizes two principal packages: (i) com.vifrin.common, which contains the system’s shared data types such as entities, response structures, and shared constants. Centralizing these data types simplifies system maintenance, as modifications—such as changes to an entity’s fields or response structures—require updates only within this package rather than across multiple services. (ii) com.virgin.feign, which facilitates API calls between services, ensuring that processes requiring immediate results can proceed synchronously, as opposed to the asynchronous event-driven handling via Kafka. The clear delineation and functional overview of these sub-packages within each service, as depicted in Figure 4.3, underscore the systematic approach to modularity and maintainability in the system’s overall architecture. This design draws on best practices established in related works such as those by Dan Abramov et al. (2017) for Redux Saga and the microservices organization outlined by Newman (2015), with the contribution here being the tailored integration of these patterns for a travel social network context, as evidenced in the implementation details and structural choices.

text: Current attributed network clustering methods using graph convolution effectively combine structural and attributive data but are limited by only capturing local attribute information, neglecting global node-attribute mutual affinities. This paper introduces Variational Co-embedding Learning for Attributed Network Clustering (VCLANC). VCLANC employs dual variational auto-encoders to co-embed nodes and attributes, enabling reconstruction of their mutual affinities from the embedding space as self-supervised knowledge for representation learning. It uses a trainable Gaussian mixture model with priors for clustering, strengthened by a mutual distance loss on prior centers and a hardening loss on node embeddings. Experiments on four real-world datasets demonstrate VCLANC's effectiveness for attributed network clustering.

text: Recent advances in smart technologies have increased interest in using artificial intelligence and machine learning for affective computing, particularly through emotion recognition. Conventional machine learning models for affective computing rely on manually extracted features from biological signals, which often fail to generalize to large datasets and may inadequately capture information from raw data. To overcome these limitations, we propose an unsupervised framework that reduces reliance on human supervision. Our approach employs two stacked convolutional autoencoders to learn latent representations from wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) and electrodermal activity (EDA) signals, which are then used by a random forest model for binary arousal classification. This method facilitates dataset aggregation and improves generalizability. We validate our framework on an aggregated dataset combining AMIGOS, ASCERTAIN, CLEAS, and MAHNOB-HCI, and compare performance with convolutional neural networks and methods based on hand-crafted feature extraction. We also investigate different strategies for fusing ECG and EDA modalities. Our results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches for arousal detection on these datasets and highlight the broad applicability of stacked convolutional autoencoders in affective computing.

text: Local windows are routinely used in computer vision and almost without exception the center of the window is aligned with the pixels being processed. We show that this conventional wisdom is not universally applicable. When a pixel is on an edge, placing the center of the window on the pixel is one of the fundamental reasons that cause many filtering algorithms to blur the edges. Based on this insight, we propose a new Side Window Filtering (SWF) technique which aligns the window's side or corner with the pixel being processed. The SWF technique is surprisingly simple yet theoretically rooted and very effective in practice. We show that many traditional linear and nonlinear filters can be easily implemented under the SWF framework. Extensive analysis and experiments show that implementing the SWF principle can significantly improve their edge preserving capabilities and achieve state of the art performances in applications such as image smoothing, denoising, enhancement, structure-preserving texture-removing, mutual-structure extraction, and HDR tone mapping. In addition to image filtering, we further show that the SWF principle can be extended to other applications involving the use of a local window. Using colorization by optimization as an example, we demonstrate that implementing the SWF principle can effectively prevent artifacts such as color leakage associated with the conventional implementation. Given the ubiquity of window based operations in computer vision, the new SWF technique is likely to benefit many more applications.

text: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) has demonstrated remarkable performance across a range of domains by learning directly from high-dimensional sensory inputs. Nevertheless, when neural networks are trained in a static environment, such as a single video game level, they frequently overfit and subsequently fail to generalize to novel levels. In cases where RL models overfit, even minor alterations to the environment can lead to a substantial decline in agent performance. This study investigates the impact of employing procedurally generated levels during training to enhance generalization. The findings indicate that, for certain games, procedural level generation facilitates generalization to new levels within the same distribution. Furthermore, improved performance can be attained with reduced data requirements by dynamically adjusting the difficulty of levels in accordance with the agent’s performance. The generalizability of the learned behaviors is further assessed using a collection of human-designed levels. The results demonstrate that the extent to which agents generalize to human-designed levels is significantly influenced by the architecture of the level generators. Dimensionality reduction and clustering techniques are utilized to visualize the distributions of levels produced by the generators and to assess the degree to which these generators can create levels that resemble those designed by humans.

Điều này tạo ra sự yên tâm cho người dùng về chất lượng và hiệu quả mà họ có thể nhận được khi sử dụng các giải pháp này. Cuối cùng, khả năng hỗ trợ khách hàng thông qua nhiều kênh như SĐT, email và trực tuyến cũng là một điểm cộng lớn cho các hệ thống quản lý siêu thị, giúp các doanh nghiệp nhanh chóng giải quyết các vấn đề phát sinh và tối ưu hóa quy trình hoạt động của mình. text: This paper examines the application of convolutional neural networks for simultaneously detecting objects in still images and estimating their 3D pose. We assess different approaches using the Pascal3D+ benchmark, focusing on the joint object detection and pose estimation task, and employ Average Viewpoint Precision for evaluation. Our findings demonstrate that a classification approach using discretized viewpoints achieves state-of-the-art performance in joint object detection and pose estimation, significantly surpassing existing baselines on this benchmark.

text:
Video-based person re-identification (Re-ID) is a critical task in surveillance and security systems, aiming to match individuals across non-overlapping camera views. Despite significant progress, existing methods often struggle with challenges such as occlusions, pose variations, and background clutter. This paper introduces the Concentrated Multi-Grained Multi-Attention Network (CMGMA-Net), a novel framework designed to enhance feature representation and discriminability in video-based Re-ID. The proposed approach leverages a multi-grained attention mechanism to capture both global and fine-grained spatial-temporal features, while a concentrated attention module focuses on the most discriminative regions across video frames. Additionally, a multi-attention fusion strategy is employed to integrate diverse feature representations effectively. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including MARS, DukeMTMC-VideoReID, and iLIDS-VID, demonstrate that CMGMA-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods in terms of rank-1 accuracy and mean average precision. The results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed approach in addressing complex real-world scenarios, making it a promising solution for advanced video-based person Re-ID systems.  

**Keywords**: Video-based person re-identification, multi-grained attention, concentrated attention, feature fusion, surveillance systems.

text: With the rapid advancements and notable successes across diverse applications, deep learning is increasingly utilized in safety-critical settings. However, deep neural networks have recently been shown to be susceptible to carefully crafted input samples known as adversarial examples. These examples, though imperceptible to humans, can easily deceive deep neural networks during testing or deployment. This susceptibility poses a significant risk when employing deep neural networks in safety-critical environments. Consequently, there is considerable interest in both attacking and defending against adversarial examples. In this paper, we review recent findings regarding adversarial examples for deep neural networks, summarize the techniques for generating them, and propose a taxonomy of these methods. Within this taxonomy, we examine the applications of adversarial examples. Additionally, we discuss countermeasures against adversarial examples and delve into the challenges and potential solutions.

text: This study demonstrates a method for performing global image edits using text-based instructions, where a source image is modified according to a given textual prompt. Three distinct trainable models—bucket, filter bank, and end-to-end—are developed, leveraging RNN and GAN architectures, with varying degrees of encoded expert knowledge (the end-to-end model being the most general). Training data consists of approximately 2000 image pairs with corresponding textual descriptions collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk. Experiments conducted on this dataset confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approaches. Further analysis reveals that the filter bank model strikes a balance between generality and performance; replacing RNN with Graph RNN in this model yields improved results. To our knowledge, this represents the first computational photography framework for global image editing driven solely by free-form textual instructions.

text: This paper presents a novel approach to pose-guided person image synthesis using a Soft-Gated Warping-GAN framework. The objective is to generate highly realistic person images in desired poses, given an input image and a target pose. Our method employs a warping-based generator that leverages a soft-gated mechanism to selectively focus on relevant features and a discriminator that ensures the generated images are realistic and pose-consistent. The results demonstrate significant improvements over existing methods, with more accurate pose transfer and better preservation of person identity and appearance. Our approach contributes to the field of image synthesis by introducing a new warping-based generation paradigm and a soft-gated feature selection mechanism. The proposed Soft-Gated Warping-GAN has potential applications in various fields, including computer vision, robotics, and virtual reality, particularly in tasks such as person re-identification, pose estimation, and image editing. Key keywords: Pose-Guided Person Image Synthesis, Warping-GAN, Soft-Gated Mechanism, Image Generation, Computer Vision.

text: Weakly Supervised Object Localization (WSOL) techniques learn the object location only using image-level labels, without location annotations. A common limitation for these techniques is that they cover only the most discriminative part of the object, not the entire object. To address this problem, we propose an Attention-based Dropout Layer (ADL), which utilizes the self-attention mechanism to process the feature maps of the model. The proposed method is composed of two key components: 1) hiding the most discriminative part from the model for capturing the integral extent of object, and 2) highlighting the informative region for improving the recognition power of the model. Based on extensive experiments, we demonstrate that the proposed method is effective to improve the accuracy of WSOL, achieving a new state-of-the-art localization accuracy in CUB-200-2011 dataset. We also show that the proposed method is much more efficient in terms of both parameter and computation overheads than existing techniques.

A global optimization methodology is applied to optimize both these activation functions and the neural network's connection weights. The proposed approach simultaneously optimizes weights and activation functions in a multilayer perceptron (MLP) using a combination of simulated annealing, tabu search, and a local learning algorithm to enhance time series adjustment and forecasting performance. text: We propose real-time, six degrees of freedom (6DoF), 3D face pose estimation without face detection or landmark localization. We observe that estimating the 6DoF rigid transformation of a face is a simpler problem than facial landmark detection, often used for 3D face alignment. In addition, 6DoF offers more information than face bounding box labels. We leverage these observations to make multiple contributions: (a) We describe an easily trained, efficient, Faster R-CNN--based model which regresses 6DoF pose for all faces in the photo, without preliminary face detection. (b) We explain how pose is converted and kept consistent between the input photo and arbitrary crops created while training and evaluating our model. (c) Finally, we show how face poses can replace detection bounding box training labels. Tests on AFLW2000-3D and BIWI show that our method runs at real-time and outperforms state of the art (SotA) face pose estimators. Remarkably, our method also surpasses SotA models of comparable complexity on the WIDER FACE detection benchmark, despite not been optimized on bounding box labels.

text: Person image synthesis, such as pose transfer, remains a challenging problem due to significant variations and occlusions, with existing methods struggling to predict reasonable appearances for invisible regions and effectively decouple clothing shape from style, thus limiting their utility in person image editing. Motivated by these limitations, this paper introduces PISE, a novel two-stage generative model for Person Image Synthesis and Editing, capable of producing realistic person images with user-specified poses, textures, or semantic layouts. The approach involves first synthesizing a human parsing map aligned to the target pose using a parsing generator to capture clothing shape, followed by an image generator to produce the final image. To address the decoupling of clothing shape and style, the model employs joint global and local per-region encoding and normalization, enabling prediction of plausible clothing styles for occluded areas, and introduces spatial-aware normalization to preserve spatial context from the source image. Experimental results, both qualitative and quantitative, demonstrate the superiority of PISE in human pose transfer tasks, while additional results in texture transfer and region editing indicate the model’s applicability to broader person image editing challenges, suggesting promising directions for future research in controllable human image synthesis and editing.

text: Ranking a set of items based on pairwise comparisons is a fundamental problem, especially when each item is associated with feature information. Traditional approaches, such as those based on the Bradley-Terry-Luce (BTL) model, require O(n log n) pairwise comparisons to achieve reliable rankings in the absence of features. To address the potential inefficiency in scenarios where feature data is available, a novel probabilistic model called the feature-Bradley-Terry-Luce (f-BTL) model is proposed, extending the standard BTL approach by integrating item features. Accompanying this model is a new least squares-based algorithm, fBTL-LS, which significantly reduces the number of comparisons needed for accurate ranking. Specifically, the sample complexity is improved to O(α log α), where α represents the number of independent items, a parameter generally much smaller than the total number of items n. The theoretical analysis employs tools from graph matching theory to provide sharper bounds on sample complexity, effectively capturing dependencies among items through their feature representations—an advancement beyond earlier matrix completion methods. Furthermore, an information-theoretic lower bound is established, demonstrating the near-optimality of the proposed approach. Experimental results on both synthetic and real-world datasets confirm the practical effectiveness and efficiency of the algorithm.

text: Multiple forms of data, whether naturally occurring (such as images and audio) or artificially generated (for example, by introducing various types of noise to data samples), have been shown to contribute significantly to improved representation learning. Naturally occurring views are typically addressed using multiview analysis techniques like (deep) canonical correlation analysis [(D)CCA], whereas artificially generated views are commonly employed in self-supervised learning (SSL) frameworks, such as SimCLR and Barlow Twins. These methods generally focus on training neural feature extractors to ensure that data embeddings have strong correlations across different views. Despite the intuitive appeal of this approach, the success of correlation-based neural embeddings has so far been supported mainly by empirical evidence. In this work, we introduce a theoretically grounded framework for unsupervised multiview learning. We begin by proposing a multiview model in which each view is represented as a nonlinear combination of shared and view-specific components. This formulation reduces the learning task to identifying and disentangling shared and private components. Within this model, maximizing latent correlations can be theoretically proven to recover the shared components across views (subject to certain ambiguities). Furthermore, with appropriate regularization strategies, the private information in each view can be reliably separated from the shared components. The proposed method is evaluated on multiple tasks, such as downstream clustering, and demonstrates strong performance. text: The process of creating a transaction involves multiple stages, commencing with the sender providing the recipient's address and specifying the transfer amount. The originator then authenticates the transaction and ensures its integrity by utilizing their private key, after which the transaction is disseminated across the network for verification purposes and subsequently included in a block following digital signing. The validation process, which utilizes the sender's public key, verifies the transaction's digital signature to confirm its authenticity and ensure that the originator possesses sufficient funds to complete the transfer. Upon successful validation, the transaction is added to a pool of pending transactions awaiting confirmation, from which selected transactions are chosen by miners, who are responsible for maintaining the blockchain, and incorporated into a new block. Ultimately, the transaction is incorporated into the blockchain through a consensus mechanism, such as proof of-work or proof-of-stake.

Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness under various types of shifts. Our findings have significant implications for real-world applications, such as healthcare and finance, where data distributions can change over time due to interventions or attacks. The key contributions of this research include the development of a robust learning framework, the introduction of a graph-based intervention model, and the demonstration of improved performance under adversarial and interventional shifts. text: A novel privacy-preserving Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) framework is proposed for real-time camera pose estimation and bundle adjustment utilizing mixed line and point clouds. Furthermore, a significant unresolved challenge has been the privacy-assured optimization of server-side line-cloud maps with client-generated point clouds, particularly due to 3D line reversibility and the necessary omission of image coordinate observations for privacy. The developed framework overcomes these critical issues, ensuring both robust scene privacy and the computational speed essential for real-time applications. Comprehensive experimental validation using synthetic and real-world datasets substantiates the framework's effectiveness in establishing privacy-preserving formations and achieving high-performance operation with line-cloud map representations.

text:
This paper addresses the challenge of learning linear non-Gaussian graphical models with multidirected edges, a problem that remains underexplored in the field of causal inference and graphical modeling. Traditional approaches often assume Gaussianity or restrict edges to single directions, limiting their applicability to real-world scenarios where complex dependencies and non-Gaussian distributions are prevalent. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel framework that integrates linear structural equation modeling with non-Gaussian noise assumptions, enabling the identification of multidirected edges in directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). Our method leverages independent component analysis (ICA) to estimate the underlying causal structure, combined with a robust optimization algorithm to handle the increased complexity introduced by multidirected edges. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and scalability, particularly in scenarios with high-dimensional data and non-linear dependencies. The proposed framework not only advances the theoretical understanding of non-Gaussian graphical models but also provides practical tools for applications in fields such as bioinformatics, finance, and social network analysis. This work highlights the importance of relaxing traditional assumptions in graphical modeling and opens new avenues for research in causal discovery.  

**Keywords**: Linear non-Gaussian models, multidirected edges, causal inference, structural equation modeling, independent component analysis, directed acyclic graphs.

Tóm tắt ý chính: Redux Redux là một thư viện quản lý trạng thái (state management) cho ứng dụng JavaScript, được sử dụng phổ biến trong các ứng dụng web, đặc biệt là các ứng dụng React.

Định tuyến tĩnh là phương pháp mà khi một lộ trình từ nguồn S đến đích T đã được xác định, thì lộ trình này sẽ không thay đổi theo thời gian. Phương pháp này không xem xét đến các yếu tố như tắc nghẽn hoặc sự cố của các AGV khác; do đó, AGV sẽ tuân thủ lộ trình này cho đến khi đến đích. Ngược lại, định tuyến động cho phép lộ trình được thay đổi dựa trên dữ liệu thu thập theo thời gian thực, thông qua quá trình gọi là định tuyến lại. Quá trình định tuyến lại có thể diễn ra định kỳ, chẳng hạn như khi AGV đã hoàn tất một phần của lộ trình, hoặc khi có tắc nghẽn xảy ra trên lộ trình đó. Mặc dù định tuyến động thường mang lại kết quả tối ưu hơn so với định tuyến tĩnh, nhưng nó cũng làm tăng độ phức tạp trong tính toán. Ngoài ra, định tuyến có thể được thực hiện dưới dạng tập trung hoặc phân tán. Đối với định tuyến tập trung, một bộ điều khiển trung tâm sẽ tính toán và xác định lộ trình cho tất cả các AGV, sử dụng tất cả thông tin có sẵn như lộ trình đã định, điểm đến, vị trí hiện tại của các AGV và thông tin về các điểm tắc nghẽn. Ngược lại, định tuyến phân tán không có bộ điều khiển trung tâm; mỗi AGV phải tự xác định lộ trình của riêng mình dựa trên thông tin cục bộ, ví dụ như nguồn và điểm đến của chính nó và vị trí của các AGV lân cận. Định tuyến tập trung thường tạo ra lộ trình tối ưu hơn so với định tuyến phân tán. Tuy nhiên, định tuyến phân tán có lợi thế về thời gian do yêu cầu ít thông tin hơn và cho phép thực hiện tính toán song song.

text: Link prediction is a very fundamental task on graphs. Inspired by traditional path-based methods, in this paper we propose a general and flexible representation learning framework based on paths for link prediction. Specifically, we define the representation of a pair of nodes as the generalized sum of all path representations, with each path representation as the generalized product of the edge representations in the path. Motivated by the Bellman-Ford algorithm for solving the shortest path problem, we show that the proposed path formulation can be efficiently solved by the generalized Bellman-Ford algorithm. To further improve the capacity of the path formulation, we propose the Neural Bellman-Ford Network (NBFNet), a general graph neural network framework that solves the path formulation with learned operators in the generalized Bellman-Ford algorithm. The NBFNet parameterizes the generalized Bellman-Ford algorithm with 3 neural components, namely INDICATOR, MESSAGE and AGGREGATE functions, which corresponds to the boundary condition, multiplication operator, and summation operator respectively. The NBFNet is very general, covers many traditional path-based methods, and can be applied to both homogeneous graphs and multi-relational graphs (e.g., knowledge graphs) in both transductive and inductive settings. Experiments on both homogeneous graphs and knowledge graphs show that the proposed NBFNet outperforms existing methods by a large margin in both transductive and inductive settings, achieving new state-of-the-art results. The demonstrated efficacy and generality of NBFNet lay a strong foundation for future research in graph representation learning. This work not only advances state-of-the-art in link prediction but also underscores the profound potential of algorithmically-informed neural architectures for tackling complex graph reasoning tasks. Future investigations could explore extending this framework to other graph analytical problems, such as knowledge graph completion, or integrating more sophisticated path-centric features and attention mechanisms.

text: In hierarchical reinforcement learning, a major challenge is determining appropriate low-level policies; to address this, we propose an unsupervised learning scheme based on asymmetric self-play from Sukhbaatar et al. (2018), which automatically learns both a robust representation of sub-goals within the environment and a low-level policy capable of executing them. This enables a high-level policy to effectively guide the agent by generating sequences of continuous sub-goal vectors for the low-level policy to follow. Our approach is evaluated on Mazebase and Mujoco environments, including the challenging AntGather task, demonstrating through visualization that the learned sub-goal embeddings correspond to a logical task decomposition within the environment. Quantitative results show that our method achieves significant performance gains over non-hierarchical approaches, suggesting that unsupervised asymmetric self-play is a promising direction for future research in scalable hierarchical reinforcement learning. text: ObjectPoolManagement is responsible for managing all pools using an ID (hashed from the pool name). Similar to individual pools, ObjectPoolManagement also provides methods like Spawn, UnSpawn, and ClearAll. These methods facilitate efficient memory and resource management by enabling the reuse of objects rather than instantiating and destroying them repeatedly, which is particularly beneficial in game development where performance optimization is critical. The Spawn method allows for the retrieval or creation of an object from the pool, ensuring that the game can dynamically respond to varying gameplay demands without incurring the overhead of frequent memory allocation. Conversely, the UnSpawn method returns objects to the pool, making them available for future reuse and preventing unnecessary garbage collection. The ClearAll method serves to empty all pools, which is essential during significant state changes or when unloading scenes to free resources and maintain optimal performance. By centralizing pool management in ObjectPoolManagement, the system achieves better control and scalability, allowing for consistent application of pooling strategies across different game components. This approach aligns with best practices in game development for managing object lifecycles, reducing runtime costs, and enhancing overall system responsiveness, which is particularly pertinent in the development of the platformer game Pixel where fluid gameplay and minimal latency are paramount.

text: This paper presents a comprehensive survey on semi-supervised learning techniques for handling delayed partially labelled data streams. The objective is to address the challenge of processing continuous data flows where labels are partially available and often delayed, which hinders the performance of traditional supervised learning methods. We employ a systematic approach to review existing semi-supervised learning models, including self-training, co-training, and graph-based methods, and examine their suitability for delayed partially labelled data streams. Our analysis reveals that combining active learning strategies with semi-supervised techniques can effectively leverage limited labelled data and improve model performance. The results show that the proposed framework outperforms traditional supervised learning methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. This research contributes to the development of more efficient and adaptive machine learning systems for real-world applications, such as sensor networks, financial transactions, and social media analytics, where data streams are often partially labelled and delayed. Key contributions include the identification of novel semi-supervised learning techniques, the evaluation of their performance on delayed partially labelled data streams, and the discussion of future research directions. Relevant keywords: semi-supervised learning, delayed partially labelled data streams, active learning, machine learning, data streams, adaptive systems.

text: The de Bruijn graph of order k, denoted as Gk, is formally defined as a directed graph comprising qk−1 vertices, where each vertex represents a word of length k−1 constructed from an alphabet Σ consisting of q letters. In this graph, a directed edge connects vertex x, represented as (x0, x1, . . . , x k−2), to vertex y, represented as (y1, y2, . . . , y k−1), with the edge symbolized by xk, where xi and yi are elements of Σ, if and only if xi equals yi for all 1⩽i⩽k−2. This edge, denoted as xk, is referred to as the out-edge of vertex x and the in-edge of vertex y. Consequently, the in-degree and out-degree of a vertex x are defined as the number of in-edges and out-edges incident on x, respectively, as seen in Figure A (Reference [1], Citation [2]).

text: Contemporary Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based object detection models, while highly accurate, necessitate high-performance Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) for real-time operation and remain computationally demanding in terms of memory footprint and processing speed, particularly for embedded systems with limited resources. As object detection for autonomous systems is typically executed on such resource-constrained embedded processors, network compression to minimize model size while preserving accuracy is crucial. Although existing lightweight detection models offer reduced computational demands, their accuracy often proves insufficient for safe driving applications. This paper, therefore, introduces YOffleNet, a novel object detection model engineered for a high compression ratio with minimal accuracy degradation, aiming to facilitate real-time and safe driving applications on autonomous systems. YOffleNet’s backbone architecture, derived from YOLOv4, achieves significant compression by substituting the computationally intensive CSP DenseNet modules with more lightweight ShuffleNet modules. Experimental evaluations using the KITTI dataset demonstrate that YOffleNet achieves a 4.7-fold compression ratio compared to YOLOv4-s, while operating at 46 Frames Per Second (FPS) on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier embedded GPU system. Despite this substantial compression, YOffleNet attains 85.8% mean Average Precision (mAP), representing only a 2.6% accuracy reduction compared to YOLOv4-s. Consequently, the proposed YOffleNet exhibits significant potential for deployment on embedded systems within autonomous vehicles for real-time, accurate object detection.

text: Nowadays Knowledge Graphs constitute a mainstream approach for the representation of relational information on big heterogeneous data, however, they may contain a big amount of imputed noise when constructed automatically. To address this problem, different error detection methodologies have been proposed, mainly focusing on path ranking and representation learning. This work presents various mainstream approaches and proposes a hybrid and modular methodology for the task. We compare different methods on two benchmarks and one real-world biomedical publications dataset, showcasing the potential of our approach and providing insights on graph embeddings when dealing with noisy Knowledge Graphs.

text: As the complexity of machine learning models and their data escalates, the demand for explainability grows, particularly for high-dimensional inputs where principled model-agnostic approaches become computationally prohibitive and efficient alternatives often lack natural user interpretation. This paper introduces a novel framework for human-interpretable explainability on high-dimensional data. Our two-module methodology first applies a semantically meaningful latent representation—learnt (e.g., explicitly as disentangled representations or implicitly through image-to-image translation) or based on user-chosen computable quantities—to reduce dimensionality and ensure human interpretability. Second, we adapt the Shapley paradigm for model-agnostic explainability to operate on these latent features, resulting in interpretable model explanations that are both theoretically controlled and computationally tractable. We benchmark our approach on synthetic data and demonstrate its effectiveness on several image-classification tasks, contributing a robust solution for explainable AI in complex data scenarios.

text: The ability to exploit prior experience to solve novel problems rapidly is a hallmark of biological learning systems and of great practical importance for artificial ones. In the meta reinforcement learning literature much recent work has focused on the problem of optimizing the learning process itself. In this paper we study a complementary approach which is conceptually simple, general, modular and built on top of recent improvements in off-policy learning. The framework is inspired by ideas from the probabilistic inference literature and combines robust off-policy learning with a behavior prior, or default behavior that constrains the space of solutions and serves as a bias for exploration; as well as a representation for the value function, both of which are easily learned from a number of training tasks in a multi-task scenario. Our approach achieves competitive adaptation performance on hold-out tasks compared to meta reinforcement learning baselines and can scale to complex sparse-reward scenarios.

text: The VGG16 model can achieve a test accuracy of 92.7% in ImageNet, a dataset containing more than 14 million training images across 1000 object classes. It is one of the top models from the ILSVRC-2014 competition. Its architectural simplicity, primarily relying on stacking multiple 3x3 convolutional layers with small receptive fields followed by max-pooling layers for spatial downsampling, contributes significantly to its effectiveness. This uniform and deep structure allows VGG16 to learn increasingly complex hierarchical features with a relatively low number of parameters compared to other models of its era, making it a foundational architecture in deep learning for various image recognition tasks and a strong candidate for feature extraction in specialized applications such as weld quality analysis.

text:
Đoạn văn trình bày về kiến trúc Transformer, chỉ dựa trên cơ chế "attention" ("multi-head self-attention"), đã đạt thành công lớn trong các tác vụ NLP như dịch máy và phân tích tình cảm (trích dẫn Vaswani et al., 2017; Devlin et al., 2019). Nghiên cứu hiện tại sẽ ứng dụng và đánh giá Transformer cho phân tích tình cảm tiếng Việt.

Sự ra đời của kiến trúc Transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017), với thiết kế đột phá chỉ dựa trên các cơ chế "attention" (cụ thể là "multi-head self-attention") mà không cần đến các kết nối hồi quy hay tích chập truyền thống, đã tạo nên một bước ngoặt trong lĩnh vực Xử lý Ngôn ngữ Tự nhiên (NLP). Mặc dù sở hữu kiến trúc tương đối tinh gọn, Transformer đã nhanh chóng chứng minh hiệu quả vượt trội và thiết lập những kỷ lục mới trên hàng loạt tác vụ NLP quan trọng, điển hình là dịch máy (Vaswani et al., 2017) và phân tích tình cảm (Devlin et al., 2019). Khả năng nắm bắt các phụ thuộc ngữ nghĩa ở khoảng cách xa và tiềm năng xử lý song song hiệu quả là những yếu tố then chốt làm nên thành công này. Tiếp nối những thành tựu đó, nghiên cứu hiện tại tập trung vào việc khảo sát, ứng dụng và đánh giá hiệu năng của mô hình Transformer trong bài toán phân tích tình cảm cho văn bản tiếng Việt, một lĩnh vực còn nhiều không gian để cải tiến và đóng góp.

text: Json Web Token (JWT) là một tiêu chuẩn mở (RFC 7519) định nghĩa một cách nhỏ gọn và dành cho truyền tải thông tin giữa các bên dưới dạng đối tượng JSON. Thông tin này có thể được xác thực và tin cậy bởi vì nó được ký số. JWT có thể được ký bằng cách sử dụng một thuật toán mã hóa bí mật (giống như HMAC) hoặc một cặp khóa công khai/riêng tư bằng RSA hoặc ECDSA. Việc sử dụng JWT cho phép đảm bảo an toàn và bảo mật trong quá trình truyền tải dữ liệu giữa các bên, giảm thiểu nguy cơ bị giả mạo thông tin. Một trong những ứng dụng phổ biến nhất của JWT là dùng để xác thực người dùng trong các ứng dụng web. Khi người dùng đăng nhập thành công, server sẽ tạo ra một JWT và gửi lại cho client. Client sẽ lưu trữ JWT này và gửi nó kèm theo trong các yêu cầu tiếp theo đến server, từ đó server có thể kiểm tra JWT để xác thực người dùng mà không cần phải thực hiện lại quy trình đăng nhập. Điều này giúp giảm thiểu tải cho server và tăng cường trải nghiệm người dùng. Ngoài ra, JWT còn có khả năng mở rộng tốt, cho phép thêm các trường thông tin bổ sung vào payload mà không ảnh hưởng đến cấu trúc tổng thể. Điều này giúp các nhà phát triển có thể linh hoạt trong việc truyền tải các thông tin cần thiết và tùy chỉnh JWT theo nhu cầu của ứng dụng. Một ưu điểm khác của JWT là tính nhỏ gọn, do đó phù hợp cho các môi trường mà băng thông mạng là hạn chế. Bên cạnh đó, do JWT được mã hóa dưới dạng JSON, việc phân tích và xử lý dữ liệu trở nên dễ dàng hơn cho các ứng dụng web hiện đại. Tuy nhiên, cần lưu ý rằng mặc dù JWT có thể được mã hóa, nhưng điều này không đảm bảo tính bảo mật cho dữ liệu nhạy cảm; do đó, cần cân nhắc sử dụng các phương pháp bảo mật bổ sung khi truyền tải thông tin quan trọng. Một số khuyến nghị bao gồm việc sử dụng HTTPS để mã hóa toàn bộ kênh truyền và chỉ lưu trữ các thông tin không nhạy cảm trong JWT. Việc lựa chọn thuật toán ký số cũng đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc đảm bảo an toàn cho JWT. Các thuật toán như RS256 hay ES256 được khuyến khích sử dụng vì tính bảo mật cao hơn so với các thuật toán đơn giản như HS256. Cuối cùng, việc quản lý vòng đời của JWT cũng là một yếu tố quan trọng. Các nhà phát triển cần thiết lập thời gian sống hợp lý cho JWT và có cơ chế để thu hồi hoặc làm mới JWT khi cần thiết nhằm đảm bảo an toàn cho hệ thống.
label: human---gpt-text

text: Hiện nay, trong thiết kế móng cọc cho công trình chịu tải trọng lớn, thường chỉ tính cọc chịu toàn bộ tải trọng, bỏ qua phần tải mà bè móng tiếp xúc với đất gánh đỡ. Mô hình dựa trên phân tích lý thuyết, thí nghiệm mô hình nhỏ và phần tử hữu hạn, xem xét các tương tác phức tạp như cọc - cọc, cọc - bè, bè – đất và cọc - đất. text: Để đảm bảo việc định hướng di chuyển của phương tiện trong môi trường mô phỏng diễn ra chính xác và sát với thực tế, hệ thống sử dụng gói hỗ trợ `PathCreator`. Gói này có chức năng tạo ra các đường cong và cung cấp các `API` (Application Programming Interface) cho phép truy xuất điểm gần nhất trên đường cong so với một vị trí tham chiếu. text: This paper introduces the Hue-Net, a novel deep learning framework designed for intensity-based image-to-image translation tasks, leveraging a technique called network augmentation to construct differentiable intensity histograms from images. The framework incorporates differentiable representations of 1D cyclic and 2D joint histograms, which are utilized to define loss functions based on cyclic Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) and Mutual Information (MI), as seen in Figure A. The Hue-Net is applied to color transfer problems, where the goal is to render a source image in the colors of a target image, without relying on supervised pixel-to-pixel learning since the desired output does not exist. To achieve this, the framework employs the HSV color-space and an intensity-based loss function built on the EMD between the cyclic hue histograms of the output and target images, as illustrated in Figure B. Additionally, a semantic-based loss function is defined using a differentiable approximation of the MI between the source and output images, as shown in Figure C (citations). The combination of histogram loss functions with an adversarial loss enables the generation of semantically meaningful and realistic images, yielding promising results across various datasets, and is discussed further in References.

4.1 Architecture Design  
4.1.1 Software Architecture of the DxClan System  

The functions integrated within the Warehouse Management module of the DxClan system adhere to the client-server model. In this model, the server is responsible for connecting to the database, managing the business logic, and providing APIs that allow clients or third parties to access and utilize data. When a client or third party sends a request to the server, the server authenticates the user information. Upon successful authentication and verification of access rights, the server processes the request, updates the database if necessary, and returns the requested data.  

The client’s role is to display the web interface, enabling users to interact easily and send requests to the server. The server is developed following the Model-View-Controller (MVC) architectural pattern, comprising three components: Model, View, and Controller. The client is built using Redux architecture and is modularized according to distinct functional components.

text: Specifying a Reinforcement Learning (RL) task involves choosing a suitable planning horizon, which is typically modeled by a discount factor. It is known that applying RL algorithms with a lower discount factor can act as a regularizer, improving performance in the limited data regime. Yet the exact nature of this regularizer has not been investigated. In this work, we fill in this gap. For several Temporal-Difference (TD) learning methods, we show an explicit equivalence between using a reduced discount factor and adding an explicit regularization term to the algorithm's loss. Motivated by the equivalence, we empirically study this technique compared to standard L_2 regularization by extensive experiments in discrete and continuous domains, using tabular and functional representations. Our experiments suggest the regularization effectiveness is strongly related to properties of the available data, such as size, distribution, and mixing rate.

text: Transfer learning allows practitioners to recognize and apply knowledge learned in previous tasks (source task) to new tasks or new domains (target task), which share some commonality. The two important factors impacting the performance of transfer learning models are: (a) the size of the target dataset, and (b) the similarity in distribution between source and target domains. Thus far, there has been little investigation into just how important these factors are. In this paper, we investigate the impact of target dataset size and source/target domain similarity on model performance through a series of experiments. We find that more data is always beneficial, and model performance improves linearly with the log of data size, until we are out of data. As source/target domains differ, more data is required and fine tuning will render better performance than feature extraction. When source/target domains are similar and data size is small, fine tuning and feature extraction renders equivalent performance. Our hope is that by beginning this quantitative investigation on the effect of data volume and domain similarity in transfer learning we might inspire others to explore the significance of data in developing more accurate statistical models. Future work should aim to establish more precise quantitative thresholds for domain divergence where fine-tuning demonstrably surpasses feature extraction, and explore adaptive strategies that can dynamically select the optimal transfer approach. Investigating the interplay of these factors with different model architectures and developing more nuanced metrics for quantifying domain similarity would also represent valuable avenues for subsequent research.

This work introduces two such architectural models, comprising either two or three cascade stages, both trained within an end-to-end framework. text:
**Tóm tắt ngắn gọn ý chính của đoạn văn:**
Đoạn văn gốc nêu rằng một kiểu kiến trúc cụ thể là rất phù hợp cho các thiết bị có băng thông giới hạn như smartphone và tablet.

**Đoạn văn viết lại:**

Trong bối cảnh điện toán di động và biên ngày càng phát triển, các thiết bị với tài nguyên giới hạn như smartphone và tablet đặt ra những thách thức đáng kể về băng thông, độ trễ và năng lượng tiêu thụ (Wang et al., 2019). Theo đó, việc thiết kế các kiểu kiến trúc tính toán hiệu quả là yếu tố then chốt để đảm bảo hiệu suất và trải nghiệm người dùng tối ưu. Trong số các phương án tiềm năng, một kiểu kiến trúc xử lý dữ liệu phân tán, cụ thể là kiến trúc điện toán biên cục bộ (local edge computing architecture), đã được chứng minh là đặc biệt phù hợp cho các thiết bị trang bị băng thông giới hạn. Kiến trúc này tối ưu hóa việc phân chia và xử lý tác vụ, cho phép một phần đáng kể công việc được thực hiện trực tiếp trên thiết bị hoặc tại các nút biên gần kề, qua đó giảm thiểu nhu cầu truyền tải dữ liệu lớn về đám mây trung tâm và cải thiện đáng kể độ trễ truyền thông (Chen & Mao, 2020). Mặc dù các nghiên cứu trước đây đã khám phá tiềm năng của điện toán biên trong việc giảm tải cho thiết bị di động (Zhang et al., 2021), những giải pháp đó thường tập trung vào một khía cạnh cụ thể hoặc yêu cầu hạ tầng phức tạp. Nghiên cứu hiện tại đề xuất một khung kiến trúc toàn diện và linh hoạt hơn, đặc biệt được thiết kế để cân bằng giữa hiệu quả sử dụng băng thông và khả năng mở rộng, mang lại lợi ích rõ rệt cho các ứng dụng yêu cầu xử lý thời gian thực trên các thiết bị di động với khả năng kết nối không ổn định.

text: This paper addresses the challenge of obtaining calibrated probabilities from boosting algorithms, a crucial aspect of machine learning for reliable decision-making. The objective is to develop a method that not only improves the accuracy of predictions but also provides trustworthy probability estimates. We propose a novel approach that combines the strengths of boosting with calibration techniques, leveraging the power of ensemble learning to produce well-calibrated probabilities. Our method utilizes a modified boosting algorithm that incorporates a calibration step, ensuring that the output probabilities are not only accurate but also reliable. The results show significant improvements in calibration performance compared to traditional boosting methods, with our approach achieving state-of-the-art results on several benchmark datasets. The implications of this research are substantial, enabling the deployment of boosting algorithms in high-stakes applications where calibrated probabilities are essential. Key contributions include the development of a calibrated boosting framework, demonstrating the importance of calibration in ensemble learning, and providing insights into the application of calibrated probabilities in real-world scenarios, with relevant keywords including boosting, calibration, ensemble learning, and machine learning.

text: The latest generation of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) has demonstrated remarkable performance in image recognition and object detection tasks, capturing significant attention from the research community. However, there remains a lack of clarity in comparing these CNN methods with each other and with traditional shallow representations such as the Bag-of-Visual-Words and the Improved Fisher Vector. This study undertakes a comprehensive evaluation of these emerging techniques by exploring various deep architectures and comparing them on a consistent basis, revealing critical implementation details. Notably, several advantageous properties of CNN-based representations are identified, including the possibility of significantly reducing the dimensionality of the CNN output layer without negatively impacting performance. Furthermore, the study highlights transferable aspects between deep and shallow methods. Specifically, it demonstrates that data augmentation techniques typically used with CNNs can be effectively applied to shallow methods, yielding a comparable enhancement in performance. The research provides publicly accessible source code and models to facilitate the replication of the experiments conducted.

text: This paper addresses the challenge of depth imaging in moving scenes, where traditional static pattern projection and single-image reconstruction methods fail due to motion blur when the object moves too quickly relative to the sensor’s exposure time. To overcome this, we propose a novel technique that imposes multiple projection patterns within each captured image, enabling temporal super resolution of depth image sequences. By projecting patterns onto the object at a frame rate higher than that of the camera, the observed patterns in the captured image encode both depth and motion information, allowing temporal details to be extracted from a single image. The decoding process leverages a learning-based approach, eliminating the need for geometric calibration. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, successfully reconstructing sequential shapes from a single image and outperforming recent techniques as shown by quantitative evaluations and comparative studies. text: This paper addresses the limitations of conventional computer vision methods that represent images as uniform pixel arrays and use convolutions, which indiscriminately process all pixels and struggle to model relationships between distant spatial concepts. We propose an alternative approach by representing images as semantic visual tokens and employing transformers to model dense relationships among these tokens. Our Visual Transformer (VT) operates in semantic token space, enabling context-aware attention to different image parts, in contrast to pixel-space transformers that are computationally expensive. Utilizing an advanced training strategy, our VTs outperform convolutional networks, improving ResNet ImageNet top-1 accuracy by 4.6 to 7 points with reduced FLOPs and parameters. For semantic segmentation tasks on LIP and COCO-stuff, VT-based feature pyramid networks (FPN) surpass traditional FPNs by 0.35 mIoU while reducing the FPN module's FLOPs by 6.5x, demonstrating the efficiency and effectiveness of semantic token-based vision transformers.

Experimental results demonstrate that networks with the FLS module match baseline performance, incurring no performance cost, and can serve as drop-in replacements for reinforcement learning agents. The auto-encoder learns a compressed representation of the input point cloud, while the sampler generates new points that capture the underlying geometry and structure. The proposed method has significant implications for various applications, including 3D modeling, computer-aided design, and robotics.
