text: Multi-source transfer learning has been proven effective when within-target labeled data is scarce. Previous work focuses primarily on exploiting domain similarities and assumes that source domains are richly or at least comparably labeled. While this strong assumption is never true in practice, this paper relaxes it and addresses challenges related to sources with diverse labeling volume and diverse reliability. The first challenge is combining domain similarity and source reliability by proposing a new transfer learning method that utilizes both source-target similarities and inter-source relationships. The second challenge involves pool-based active learning where the oracle is only available in source domains, resulting in an integrated active transfer learning framework that incorporates distribution matching and uncertainty sampling. Extensive experiments on synthetic and two real-world datasets clearly demonstrate the superiority of our proposed methods over several baselines including state-of-the-art transfer learning methods.

text: This paper proposes GasHis-Transformer, a novel multi-scale visual transformer approach designed for gastric histopathology image classification. The objective is to accurately classify gastric histopathology images into different categories, such as normal, inflammation, and cancer, which is crucial for diagnosis and treatment. Our approach utilizes a transformer-based architecture that incorporates multi-scale features to capture both local and global patterns in histopathology images. The GasHis-Transformer model is trained on a large dataset of gastric histopathology images and achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming traditional convolutional neural network (CNN) based methods. Our results show that the proposed approach can effectively classify gastric histopathology images with high accuracy, demonstrating its potential for clinical applications. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of a multi-scale visual transformer approach for histopathology image classification and the achievement of superior performance compared to existing methods. This study highlights the effectiveness of transformer-based architectures in medical image analysis, particularly in the context of gastric histopathology image classification, and has important implications for the development of AI-powered diagnostic tools. Key keywords: gastric histopathology, image classification, visual transformer, multi-scale features, medical image analysis, AI-powered diagnostics.

text:
3D Morphable Model (3DMM) hoạt động dựa trên nguyên tắc kết hợp các yếu tố hình học và kết cấu của khuôn mặt thông qua việc sử dụng các mô hình thống kê. Điều này cho phép mô phỏng và tái tạo các đặc điểm khuôn mặt một cách chân thực và chi tiết. Các điểm dữ liệu 3D từ hình ảnh khuôn mặt được thu thập và xử lý để xây dựng một không gian hình dạng và kết cấu. Mỗi khuôn mặt riêng biệt có thể được biểu diễn dưới dạng một vector trong không gian này, cho phép thực hiện các thao tác như biến đổi hình dạng, tạo ra các khuôn mặt mới từ các mẫu đã có hoặc thay đổi biểu cảm trên khuôn mặt. 

3DMM được xây dựng dựa trên một cơ sở dữ liệu lớn các mẫu khuôn mặt 3D đã được thu thập trước đó. Các dữ liệu này thường được thu thập thông qua các kỹ thuật quét 3D hoặc tái tạo từ các hình ảnh 2D. Sau khi thu thập dữ liệu, các phương pháp phân tích thống kê như Phân tích thành phần chính (PCA) được áp dụng để giảm chiều dữ liệu và tìm ra các thành phần chính đại diện cho sự thay đổi trong hình dạng và kết cấu khuôn mặt. Quá trình này cho phép mô hình hóa các biến thể của khuôn mặt trong một không gian có kích thước thấp hơn, giúp dễ dàng hơn trong việc xử lý và tổng hợp dữ liệu.

Việc sử dụng 3DMM không chỉ giới hạn ở việc phân tích và nhận dạng khuôn mặt. Nó còn được áp dụng rộng rãi trong các lĩnh vực khác như thực tế ảo, hoạt hình, và đặc biệt là trong các hệ thống giao tiếp giữa người và máy tính. Các đặc điểm khuôn mặt được mô phỏng có thể được tích hợp vào các nhân vật ảo, tạo ra những trải nghiệm tương tác phong phú và sống động hơn. Bên cạnh đó, 3DMM còn hỗ trợ trong việc cải thiện độ chính xác của các hệ thống nhận diện khuôn mặt bằng cách cung cấp thông tin chi tiết về cấu trúc khuôn mặt, giúp phân biệt rõ ràng hơn giữa các cá nhân.

Một trong những thách thức lớn đối với việc sử dụng 3D Morphable Model là sự phức tạp trong việc thu thập và xử lý dữ liệu 3D. Việc đảm bảo độ chính xác cao đòi hỏi cần có các công cụ và công nghệ tiên tiến, cũng như một lượng lớn dữ liệu chất lượng cao. Tuy nhiên, với sự phát triển của các công nghệ quét 3D và máy học, khả năng thu thập và xử lý dữ liệu đã được cải thiện đáng kể. Các phương pháp học sâu, đặc biệt là mạng nơ-ron tích chập (CNN), đã được ứng dụng để tự động hóa quá trình xử lý và cải thiện độ chính xác của các kết quả đầu ra. CNN có khả năng học các đặc trưng phức tạp từ dữ liệu lớn, giúp tối ưu hóa việc tái tạo và phân tích khuôn mặt 3D.

Tóm lại, 3D Morphable Model là một công cụ mạnh mẽ trong lĩnh vực thị giác máy tính, cho phép tái tạo và phân tích khuôn mặt 3D với độ chính xác cao. Sự kết hợp giữa 3DMM và các công nghệ học sâu hiện đại như CNN đã mở ra nhiều cơ hội mới trong việc phát triển các ứng dụng liên quan đến nhận diện và tổng hợp khuôn mặt, đồng thời cải thiện chất lượng và độ tin cậy của các hệ thống ứng dụng trong thực tế.

text: In agriculture, actinomycetes represent a superior biological control agent in inhibiting the growth of pathogenic microorganisms. Based on the actinomycete classification manual of the International Streptomyces Project (ISP) and the 16S-rRNA gene sequence, the actinomycete strain BT02 was identified as Streptomyces rochei BT02. This strain harbors two polyketide synthase genes, type I (pks-I) and type II (pks-II), associated with antibiotic biosynthesis. Experimental results indicate that S. rochei BT02 grows optimally at 31°C, 1% salt concentration, and pH 7.0, and is capable of assimilating various carbon and nitrogen sources. S. rochei BT02 exhibits antibacterial activity against three tested Ralstonia solanacearum strains, with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 15 mg/ml. Under net house conditions, this strain reduced the bacterial wilt index by 43.5%. These findings demonstrate that S. rochei BT02 may serve as a promising resource for the development of biological products.

text: This study introduces an approach for visual text recognition that does not rely on paired supervisory data. The text recognition problem is reframed as aligning the conditional distribution of strings predicted from input text images with lexically valid strings drawn from target corpora. This approach allows for fully automated and unsupervised learning using only line-level text images and unpaired text-string samples, eliminating the necessity for extensive aligned datasets. We provide a comprehensive analysis of several aspects of our method, including: (1) the effect of training sequence length on convergence, (2) the relationship between character frequencies and the sequence in which they are learned, (3) the generalization capacity of our recognition network to handle inputs of varying lengths, and (4) the influence of altering the text corpus on recognition accuracy. Ultimately, our method achieves high text recognition accuracy on both synthetically produced text images and scanned images of actual printed books, all without the use of labeled training examples.

Correspondingly, a JSON-RPC response includes `jsonrpc` (string, "2.0") and, crucially, a `result` string. The `result` is required upon successful method completion but must be omitted in case of error, with its value method-determined. text: Contrastive learning (CL) significantly benefits graph-based semi-supervised learning (SSL) by effectively supplementing the scarce task information derived from annotated nodes. Nevertheless, current graph CL (GCL) approaches do not account for the non-uniform distribution of task information across the graph, a consequence of its topology and the specific choice of annotated nodes. These methods apply CL uniformly to the entire graph, creating a suboptimal synergy between CL and graph learning. To rectify this, we introduce an adaptive application of CL within graph learning, considering the task information each node receives. We first employ Group PageRank to assess node information gain, revealing that CL is most effective for nodes topologically distant from the labeled ones. Subsequently, we present our Distance-wise Graph Contrastive Learning (DwGCL) method, which operates from two perspectives: (1) from a global viewpoint of task information distribution, it bolsters the CL effect on nodes topologically distant from labeled nodes; and (2) from a node-specific viewpoint of received information, it measures inter-node relative distances to adapt the GCL sampling strategy accordingly. Comprehensive experiments on five benchmark graph datasets demonstrate that DwGCL achieves significant improvements over prior GCL methods. Further analysis using eight graph neural networks of varied architectures and three distinct annotation settings substantiates the broad generalizability of DwGCL.

text: Binary grid mask representations are widely employed within the domain of instance segmentation, with Mask R-CNN being a notable example that generates masks on a 28x28 binary grid. However, low-resolution grids typically lack the granularity to capture intricate details, whereas high-resolution grids significantly escalate computational complexity during training. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel mask representation method that leverages the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) to efficiently encode high-resolution binary grid masks into a compact vector format. Our proposed method, designated as DCT-Mask, is readily integrable into the majority of existing pixel-based instance segmentation frameworks. Without requiring additional complexities or enhancements, DCT-Mask consistently demonstrates substantial performance improvements across various frameworks, backbone architectures, datasets, and training schedules. Furthermore, it obviates the need for pre-processing or pre-training steps and imposes minimal impact on inference speed. The method exhibits particular efficacy when applied to datasets with higher-quality annotations and when integrated with more complex backbone networks. We also conduct an analysis of the method's performance, focusing on the quality of its mask representation, concluding that DCT-Mask's superior performance is primarily attributable to its capacity to achieve high-quality mask representations with low computational complexity. The implementation code is publicly accessible at https://github.com/aliyun/DCT-Mask.git.
label: human---gemini-text

text: **Byte-level tokenization** is employed to segment the byte-level representation of textual data. This approach is rationalized by its inherent capability to process character-rich languages, such as Japanese and Chinese, effectively. However, a notable drawback is that the byte-level representation of a sentence is typically considerably longer than its character-level equivalent, which subsequently escalates the computational cost for the Neural Machine Translation (NMT) model. To mitigate the extended input sequence length, byte-level tokenization applies BPE tokenization directly to sequences of bytes. In practice, this method has demonstrated comparable performance of byte-level BPE-based NMT when contrasted with BPE based NMT. Further to this, **Subword tokenization** is a technique focused on identifying an optimal segmentation of words, thereby enabling a restricted set of word-pieces to effectively cover an extensive vocabulary. The rationale underpinning subword tokenization is that words are frequently composed of multiple morphemes; for instance, a plural countable noun comprises its root and the affix "s." By segmenting the root from the affix, the necessity of including both the singular and plural forms of a noun within the vocabulary is obviated, leading to a reduction in its overall size. In practical applications, subword tokenization significantly enhances vocabulary coverage and efficiently handles unseen words. The vocabulary for this method can be constructed either by applying the morphological rules intrinsic to the language or by learning through heuristic algorithms, such as Byte pair encoding (BPE ). The two most prominent subword tokenizations are **BPE tokenization** and **Sentence-piece tokenization**, which are founded on distinct approaches: frequency-based and sampling-based, respectively. These tokenization strategies collectively contribute significantly to addressing key challenges in NMT, including managing diverse linguistic structures, optimizing input sequence lengths, and improving vocabulary efficiency and robustness against unseen words.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have emerged as a powerful tool for learning representations of graph-structured data, with applications ranging from social networks to molecular modeling. However, a critical challenge lies in effectively propagating information across nodes, especially in heterogeneous graphs where nodes and edges exhibit diverse characteristics. This paper addresses this limitation by proposing a novel approach that enhances information propagation in GNNs through heterogeneous aggregations. Our method introduces a multi-level aggregation framework that dynamically adapts to the varying properties of nodes and edges, enabling more nuanced and context-aware feature learning. We evaluate the proposed model on benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in node classification and link prediction tasks compared to state-of-the-art GNN architectures. The results highlight the model's ability to capture complex dependencies and improve generalization in heterogeneous settings. This research contributes to advancing GNNs by providing a scalable and efficient solution for handling diverse graph structures, with potential applications in recommendation systems, knowledge graphs, and bioinformatics.  

**Keywords**: Graph Neural Networks, Heterogeneous Aggregation, Information Propagation, Node Classification, Link Prediction, Graph Representation Learning.

text: The position we advocate in this paper is that relational algebra can provide a unified language for both representing and computing with statistical-relational objects, much as linear algebra does for traditional single-table machine learning. To support our position, we have developed the FACTORBASE system, which uses SQL as a high-level scripting language for statistical-relational learning of a graphical model structure. The design philosophy of FACTORBASE is to manage statistical models as first-class citizens inside a database. Our implementation shows how our SQL constructs in FACTORBASE facilitate fast, modular, and reliable program development. Empirical evidence from six benchmark databases indicates that leveraging database system capabilities achieves scalable model structure learning.

Additionally, the model's performance is evaluated through a series of experiments that compare the summarization outputs against human-generated summaries using metrics such as ROUGE and BLEU, which are standard in evaluating the quality of text summarization. To further enhance the model's capability, the study incorporates a novel attention mechanism that accounts for the tonal and morphological characteristics inherent in Vietnamese, thus improving the coherence and fluency of the generated summaries. Moreover, the thesis also explores the integration of domain-specific knowledge by incorporating relevant ontologies and knowledge graphs, aiming to enrich the contextual understanding of the model. The results indicate that the proposed Vietnamese task-specific language model significantly outperforms existing baseline models in terms of both accuracy and readability of the summaries, demonstrating its potential applicability in real-world scenarios such as news aggregation and report generation. text: Deep reinforcement learning methods traditionally struggle with tasks where environment rewards are particularly sparse. While imitation learning successfully guides exploration in these sparse reward domains, it conventionally relies on artificial conditions, requiring access to the agent's exact environment setup and the demonstrator's action and reward trajectories. We propose a two-stage method that overcomes these limitations by leveraging noisy, unaligned footage without requiring such conventional data. First, we map unaligned videos from multiple sources to a common representation using self-supervised objectives across time and modalities (vision and sound). Second, we embed a single YouTube video in this representation to construct a reward function that encourages human gameplay imitation. This one-shot imitation method enables our agent to convincingly exceed human-level performance on the notoriously difficult exploration games Montezuma's Revenge, Pitfall!, and Private Eye for the first time, even without any environment rewards.

Bài báo này trình bày quá trình phát triển một bộ công cụ thực hành cho xác định và điều khiển tư thế, tên gọi ADCS kít, tại Trung tâm Vũ trụ Việt Nam dựa trên cơ sở kết quả nghiên cứu chuyên sâu về phân hệ này. Việc sử dụng công cụ chuyên dụng trong quá trình đào tạo và thực hành về xác định và điều khiển tư thế rất cần thiết với đặc thù hoạt động của vệ tinh trong môi trường không trọng lượng, không ma sát. text: Vanilla models for object detection and instance segmentation suffer from the heavy bias toward detecting frequent objects in the long-tailed setting. Existing methods address this issue mostly during training, e.g., by re-sampling or re-weighting. In this paper, we investigate a largely overlooked approach -- post-processing calibration of confidence scores. We propose NorCal, Normalized Calibration for long-tailed object detection and instance segmentation, a simple and straightforward recipe that reweighs the predicted scores of each class by its training sample size. We show that separately handling the background class and normalizing the scores over classes for each proposal are keys to achieving superior performance. On the LVIS dataset, NorCal can effectively improve nearly all the baseline models not only on rare classes but also on common and frequent classes. Finally, we conduct extensive analysis and ablation studies to offer insights into various modeling choices and mechanisms of our approach.

text: Learning embeddings from large-scale networks is an open challenge. Despite the overwhelming number of existing methods, is is unclear how to exploit network structure in a way that generalizes easily to unseen nodes, edges or graphs. In this work, we look at the problem of finding inductive network embeddings in large networks without domain-dependent node/edge attributes. We propose to use a set of basic predefined local encodings as the basis of a learning algorithm. In particular, we consider the degree frequencies at different distances from a node, which can be computed efficiently for relatively short distances and a large number of nodes. Interestingly, the resulting embeddings generalize well across unseen or distant regions in the network, both in unsupervised settings, when combined with language model learning, as well as in supervised tasks, when used as additional features in a neural network. Despite its simplicity, this method achieves state-of-the-art performance in tasks such as role detection, link prediction and node classification, and represents an inductive network embedding method directly applicable to large unattributed networks.

text:
This paper introduces MHER (Model-based Hindsight Experience Replay), a novel reinforcement learning framework designed to enhance sample efficiency and performance in sparse-reward environments. Traditional Hindsight Experience Replay (HER) methods rely on goal relabeling to improve learning in such settings but often suffer from inefficiencies due to limited exploration. To address this, MHER integrates a learned dynamics model with HER, enabling the agent to simulate and learn from synthetic trajectories. The proposed approach combines model-based planning with hindsight relabeling, allowing the agent to generate additional training data and refine its policy more effectively. Experiments conducted on benchmark robotic manipulation tasks demonstrate that MHER significantly outperforms standard HER and other baseline methods in terms of success rates and sample efficiency. The results highlight the framework's ability to leverage both real and simulated experiences to accelerate learning. MHER's contributions include a scalable and generalizable solution for sparse-reward problems, with potential applications in robotics, autonomous systems, and other domains requiring efficient reinforcement learning. Key innovations include the integration of model-based planning with hindsight relabeling and the generation of synthetic trajectories to augment training data.  

**Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Hindsight Experience Replay, Model-based Learning, Sparse Rewards, Robotics, Sample Efficiency.

text: Conventional neural networks are designed to process vector inputs, organizing neurons in sequential layers. This architecture necessitates transforming non-vector data like matrices into vectors, which introduces challenges. First, vectorization may eliminate spatial relationships within the data. Second, the expanded solution space increases computational demands and requires specialized parameter handling. To overcome these limitations, we introduce matrix neural networks (MatNet), which directly process matrix inputs. Each neuron aggregates information via bilinear mappings from preceding layers, similar to traditional feedforward networks. This structure enables efficient parameter optimization through backpropagation and gradient descent. Additionally, MatNet can be easily adapted for multimodal inputs. Evaluations on MNIST digit classification and image super-resolution demonstrate its effectiveness, achieving performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods with significantly lower complexity and minimal tuning.

text: Many real-world scenarios, such as human activity recognition (HAR) in IoT, can be formalized as a multi-task multi-view learning problem. Each specific task consists of multiple shared feature views collected from multiple sources, either homogeneous or heterogeneous. Common among recent approaches is to employ a typical hard/soft sharing strategy at the initial phase separately for each view across tasks to uncover common knowledge, underlying the assumption that all views are conditionally independent. On the one hand, multiple views across tasks possibly relate to each other under practical situations. On the other hand, supervised methods might be insufficient when labeled data is scarce. To tackle these challenges, we introduce a novel framework ASM2TV for semi-supervised multi-task multi-view learning. We present a new perspective named gating control policy, a learnable task-view-interacted sharing policy that adaptively selects the most desirable candidate shared block for any view across any task, which uncovers more fine-grained task-view-interacted relatedness and improves inference efficiency. Significantly, our proposed gathering consistency adaption procedure takes full advantage of large amounts of unlabeled fragmented time-series, making it a general framework that accommodates a wide range of applications. Experiments on two diverse real-world HAR benchmark datasets collected from various subjects and sources demonstrate our framework's superiority over other state-of-the-arts.

Nó được phát triển cho các tình huống giao thông mà tỷ lệ AGV vào hệ thống tại nguồn S và muốn đi đến điểm đến T được biết trước, cho tất cả các tổ hợp có thể của S và T trên môi trường. AGV vào hệ thống từ cùng một nguồn đến cùng một điểm đến có thể được phân bổ giữa nhiều con đường khác nhau. Cách tiếp cận này bao gồm hai mô hình quy hoạch tuyến tính phân cấp: mô hình ùn tắc và mô hình bất tiện. Đầu tiên, mô hình ùn tắc được giải quyết để giảm thiểu mức độ ùn tắc cao nhất trong hệ thống. Sau đó, mô hình bất tiện được giải quyết để giảm thiểu trọng số trung bình của sự bất tiện khi di chuyển, trong khi giữ cho hệ thống không bị ùn tắc hoặc dưới mức giới hạn trên về mức độ ùn tắc. Trước khi sử dụng các mô hình này, thuật toán sinh đường dẫn heuristic được sử dụng để sinh ra một tập con đường nhỏ hơn chứa phần lớn các con đường được sử dụng trong giải pháp tối ưu của mô hình bất tiện. Điều này được thực hiện bằng cách lặp lại việc tìm kiếm và chọn lựa các con đường tuân thủ với sự bất tiện trong ngưỡng tối đa cho phép và có thể đảm bảo giảm mức độ ùn tắc hiện tại của mạng lưới. Tại đây, cạnh ùn tắc nặng nhất được xóa tạm thời để tìm một con đường mới. Sau đó, việc gán heuristic cho các con đường được thực hiện bằng cách giải quyết mô hình bất tiện sử dụng tập con đường đã sinh ra. Độ phức tạp tính toán của cách tiếp cận này được xác định bởi số lượng con đường, trong trường hợp xấu nhất, có thể tăng theo cấp số nhân với số lượng vị trí và giao lộ trong mạng lưới.

text: The empirical results reveal that the global discriminative constraint significantly enhances the model's ability to distinguish between images by ensuring that the generated captions contain unique and identifying features, thus reducing the tendency to rely on generic descriptors. This capability is particularly evident in complex scenarios where multiple images share similar contexts or objects, as illustrated in Figure 2. Additionally, the local discriminative constraint effectively directs the model's focus towards underrepresented yet salient aspects of images, which are often overlooked by conventional models. This shift in focus not only enriches the descriptive quality of the captions but also aligns with human-like perceptual understanding, where nuanced details contribute to a holistic interpretation. The integration of these global and local constraints leads to a more balanced word usage, mitigating the effects of skewed word frequency that typically hampers the variability and specificity of automatically generated descriptions. Furthermore, the enhanced descriptive power of the captions is corroborated by improved performance metrics such as BLEU, METEOR, and CIDEr, which quantitatively confirm the superiority of our approach. In self-retrieval experiments, the ability of the captions to act as reliable identifiers is demonstrated by their success in accurately retrieving the corresponding images from a large pool, thereby validating the discriminability aspect of the proposed method. This advancement opens up new avenues for further exploration in enhanced image captioning models and suggests potential applications in fields such as automated content generation, digital asset management, and assistive technologies. Future work will aim to explore the integration of this framework with real-time image processing applications, potentially extending its utility across diverse domains.

Here is a 116-word abstract for the paper {file_name}:

Learning a distribution over complex, realistic indoor scenes remains a significant challenge, as existing generative radiance field models are specialized for single objects and lack the representational capacity for large, complex environments. To address this, we introduce Generative Scene Networks (GSN), which learns to decompose scenes into a collection of many local radiance fields renderable from a free moving camera. Our decomposition scheme scales effectively to larger and more complex scenes, preserving details and diversity. The learned prior enables high-quality rendering from viewpoints significantly different from observations and can be used to generate new scenes or complete scenes from sparse 2D observations. GSN quantitatively produces higher-quality scene renderings across several different scene datasets compared to existing models.

text: Field Type Required Description rows Vec<Binary> yes The shares given to each participant in the DKG protocol in order to construct their final share for encKey. These `rows`, typically derived from a master secret via Shamir’s Secret Sharing (SSS), represent individual portions of a cryptographic key, where a predefined threshold `t` out of `n` shares is required to reconstruct the original secret or generate a new one collaboratively, thereby enhancing security by eliminating single points of failure. In the context of a social login solution for Web3, each participant, which could include the user's social identity provider (e.g., Google, Facebook) and a set of independent recovery nodes or services, receives a unique `Binary` share, ensuring a decentralized and robust key management system. During the Distributed Key Generation (DKG) protocol, these participants engage in a secure, multi-party computation to combine their individual `rows` and collaboratively generate a new, jointly controlled key (`encKey`) without ever revealing their individual shares to one another, thus preserving the confidentiality of the underlying secret. Although an increasing volume of connectomic research highlights the potential of incorporating brain graphs in the diagnosis of neurological disorders, a dedicated geometric deep learning approach for predicting multiple target brain graphs from a single source brain graph has been absent. Notwithstanding the significant advancements in the domain of graph generation over the past two years, current methodologies exhibit two principal limitations. Primarily, the majority of these approaches endeavor to train a distinct model for each target domain to be generated from a source domain, which consequently constrains their capacity for the simultaneous prediction of multiple target domains. To address these challenges, the MultiGraphGAN architecture is introduced, designed not only to predict multiple brain graphs from a single source brain graph but also to preserve the topological structure of each predicted target graph. The principal contributions of this architecture encompass: (i) the development of a graph adversarial auto-encoder for the concurrent prediction of multiple brain graphs from a singular source graph; (ii) mitigation of the GAN mode collapse problem through the clustering of encoded source graphs and the introduction of a cluster-specific decoder; and (iii) the incorporation of a topological loss function to ensure the reconstruction of topologically accurate target brain graphs. The proposed MultiGraphGAN demonstrated superior performance compared to its variants, thereby indicating its substantial potential for multi-view brain graph generation from a single graph.

text: Transformers have been successful for many natural language processing tasks. However, applying transformers to the video domain for tasks such as long-term video generation and scene understanding has remained elusive due to the high computational complexity and the lack of natural tokenization. In this paper, we propose the Object-Centric Video Transformer (OCVT) which utilizes an object-centric approach for decomposing scenes into tokens suitable for use in a generative video transformer. By factoring the video into objects, our fully unsupervised model is able to learn complex spatio-temporal dynamics of multiple interacting objects in a scene and generate future frames of the video. Our model is also significantly more memory-efficient than pixel-based models and thus able to train on videos of length up to 70 frames with a single 48GB GPU. We compare our model with previous RNN-based approaches as well as other possible video transformer baselines. We demonstrate OCVT performs well when compared to baselines in generating future frames. OCVT also develops useful representations for video reasoning, achieving start-of-the-art performance on the CATER task. These promising results pave the way for future research into scaling OCVT for more complex scenarios and significantly longer video sequences. Further investigations could explore its utility in controllable video generation and adapt its learned object-centric representations for a wider array of video understanding applications beyond generation and reasoning.

text: This study identified optimal culture media for the in vitro rapid propagation and flowering of *Rosa sericea Lindl* accessions collected from Phu Tho, Vietnam. A high percentage (99.78%) of *Rosa sericea* stem explants exhibited shoot proliferation when cultured on Murashige and Skoog (MS) medium augmented with 2.0 mg/l BA and 0.05 mg/l α-NAA. The most effective medium for shoot multiplication was determined to be MS medium supplemented with 1.5 mg/l BA. Rooting of in vitro *Rosa sericea* shoots was achieved with 100% success on quarter-strength MS (¼ MS) medium. The incorporation of AgNO3 and CoCl2 into the culture medium positively influenced the in vitro flowering of *Rosa sericea*. Specifically, media fortified with 30 µM AgNO3 or 30 µM CoCl2 resulted in flowering rates of 50% and 20%, respectively. Furthermore, flowers cultured on medium containing 30 µM AgNO3 exhibited a post-bloom longevity of 14 days, whereas those on medium with 30 µM CoCl2 remained viable for only 7-8 days after anthesis.

text:
Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for addressing complex decision-making problems in environments where multiple autonomous agents interact. This paper provides a selective overview of the foundational theories and algorithms that underpin MARL, focusing on their applicability and scalability in real-world scenarios. We begin by outlining the key challenges in MARL, such as non-stationarity, partial observability, and the curse of dimensionality, which arise due to the dynamic interactions among agents. To address these challenges, we review state-of-the-art algorithms, including value-based, policy-based, and hybrid approaches, and discuss their theoretical guarantees and practical limitations. Furthermore, we explore recent advancements in cooperative, competitive, and mixed-motive settings, highlighting the role of communication, coordination, and learning equilibria in multi-agent systems. Our analysis reveals that while significant progress has been made, scalability and generalization remain critical open problems. The paper concludes by identifying promising research directions, such as the integration of MARL with deep learning and transfer learning, to enhance the adaptability and efficiency of multi-agent systems. This work aims to serve as a comprehensive resource for researchers and practitioners seeking to leverage MARL for solving complex, real-world problems.  

**Keywords**: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning, MARL, cooperative learning, competitive learning, equilibria, scalability, deep reinforcement learning.

text: The presence of channel redundancy within the feature maps of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) significantly contributes to the intensive consumption of memory and computational resources. This study introduces a novel Slim Convolution (SlimConv) module, specifically engineered to enhance the performance of CNNs through the reduction of channel redundancies. The proposed SlimConv module comprises three principal stages—Reconstruct, Transform, and Fuse—which facilitate the decomposition and subsequent efficient reorganization of features, thereby enabling effective compression of learned weights. Notably, a central component of this model is a weight flipping operation, which significantly enhances feature diversity and is critical for overall performance improvement. SlimConv functions as a versatile, plug-and-play architectural unit, allowing for direct substitution of conventional convolutional layers within CNN architectures. The efficacy of SlimConv was rigorously validated through comprehensive experimentation conducted across multiple benchmark datasets, including ImageNet, MS COCO2014, Pascal VOC2012 segmentation, and Pascal VOC2007 detection. Experimental results consistently demonstrate that models incorporating SlimConv exhibit superior performance and reduced consumption of both memory and computational resources compared to their unequipped counterparts. For instance, a ResNet-101 architecture augmented with SlimConv attained a 77.84% top-1 classification accuracy on ImageNet, utilizing 4.87 GFLOPs and 27.96 million parameters, representing an approximate 0.5% improvement in performance coupled with a reduction of approximately 3 GFLOPs and 38% in parameters.

text:
Graph embedding techniques have become essential for analyzing and processing complex relational data in various domains, such as social networks, bioinformatics, and recommendation systems. This paper introduces a novel approach for inductive graph embeddings that leverages locality encodings to capture structural and relational patterns within graphs. Unlike traditional methods that rely on transductive learning, our approach generalizes to unseen nodes and graphs, making it highly scalable and applicable to dynamic environments. We propose a framework that combines locality-sensitive hashing with graph neural networks to encode local neighborhood information efficiently. The model is trained to preserve both local and global graph properties, ensuring robust representations for downstream tasks such as node classification, link prediction, and graph clustering. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed technique also exhibits strong generalization capabilities, particularly in scenarios with limited labeled data. This work contributes to advancing inductive graph representation learning by providing a scalable and effective solution for real-world applications.  

**Keywords**: Graph embeddings, inductive learning, locality encodings, graph neural networks, node classification, link prediction.

text:
This paper explores the application of regularized tensor factorizations and higher-order principal components analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction and feature extraction in multi-dimensional datasets. Traditional PCA methods are limited to two-dimensional data, whereas real-world applications often involve higher-order structures, such as time-series, spatial, or multi-modal data. To address this, we propose a novel framework that integrates regularization techniques into tensor factorization models, enabling robust decomposition and improved interpretability of high-dimensional data. Our approach leverages sparsity-inducing norms and smoothness constraints to enhance the stability and accuracy of the factorization process. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms conventional tensor factorization and higher-order PCA techniques in terms of reconstruction error, computational efficiency, and feature interpretability. The framework is particularly effective in applications such as image processing, recommendation systems, and network analysis. This research contributes to the advancement of tensor-based data analysis by providing a scalable and adaptable solution for extracting meaningful patterns from complex, high-dimensional datasets.  

**Keywords**: Tensor factorization, higher-order PCA, regularization, dimensionality reduction, multi-dimensional data, sparsity, interpretability.

text: The incorporation of Non-Local (NL) blocks in mobile neural networks has been largely unexplored, primarily due to two significant challenges: the high computational cost associated with NL blocks, which poses difficulties in resource-constrained applications, and the lack of an optimal configuration for integrating NL blocks into mobile neural networks. To address these challenges, we introduce AutoNL, a novel approach that firstly proposes a Lightweight Non-Local (LightNL) block, which reduces computational costs by 400 times compared to conventional NL blocks without compromising performance, achieved through the optimization of transformation operations and the utilization of compact features. Secondly, by rendering the LightNL block's structure differentiable during training, we develop an efficient neural architecture search algorithm that enables the end-to-end learning of an optimal LightNL block configuration. Notably, our AutoNL model, which was searched using only 32 GPU hours, achieves a top-1 accuracy of 77.7% on ImageNet under typical mobile settings (350M FLOPs), substantially outperforming existing mobile models, including MobileNetV2 (+5.7%), FBNet (+2.8%), and MnasNet (+2.1%), with code and models available at https://github.com/LiYingwei/AutoNL.

text: Mục tiêu của nghiên cứu này là đánh giá vai trò của cộng hưởng từ khuếch tán (DWI) trong việc phân biệt u mô mềm lành tính và ác tính vùng cơ xương khớp, bao gồm các khối u có nguồn gốc từ mô sợi, mô thần kinh và mô cơ. Nghiên cứu cắt ngang này được thực hiện trên 67 bệnh nhân có u mô mềm, được xác nhận bằng giải phẫu bệnh và chụp cộng hưởng từ tại Bệnh viện Ung Bướu TP.HCM từ tháng 01/2022 đến 06/2024. Các giá trị hệ số khuếch tán biểu kiến (ADC) của thành phần đặc trong tổn thương được đo bằng hình DWI/ADC sử dụng giá trị b = 0 và b = 1000. Tổng cộng có 67 bệnh nhân (33 nam, 34 nữ) tham gia nghiên cứu, trong đó có 34 tổn thương lành tính và 33 tổn thương ác tính. Giá trị ADC trung bình của thành phần đặc trong các tổn thương ác tính thấp hơn đáng kể so với các tổn thương lành tính (p < 0,0001). Phân tích đường cong ROC và chỉ số Youden lớn nhất cho thấy ngưỡng cắt tối ưu để chẩn đoán u ác tính là 1,112 x 10-3mm2/s. Với giá trị ADC nhỏ hơn ngưỡng này, độ nhạy đạt 85,29%, độ đặc hiệu 90,91%, giá trị tiên đoán dương 83,33%, giá trị tiên đoán âm 93,55% và độ chính xác 88,06%. Nghiên cứu kết luận rằng cộng hưởng từ khuếch tán (DWI), đặc biệt là giá trị ADC trung bình của thành phần đặc trong tổn thương, có vai trò đáng kể trong chẩn đoán phân biệt u mô mềm lành tính và ác tính.

This work first proves that no method can guarantee OOD detection performance beyond random chance without assumptions on relevant out-distributions. We then interrogate the typical set hypothesis, highlighting consequences of assuming support overlap between in- and out-distributions and the arbitrariness of the typical set for OOD detection. Our results suggest estimation error, rather than a fundamental misalignment between likelihood-based OOD detection and out-distributions of interest, is the more plausible explanation for these failures. We illustrate how even minimal estimation error can cause OOD detection failures, yielding implications for future work in DGMs and OOD detection.

text: Goal-oriented dialogue has garnered significant attention within the field of artificial intelligence owing to its diverse applications. Such tasks involve interactions where a questioner poses an action-oriented query, and an answerer responds with the objective of guiding the questioner towards a correct action. Deep learning and reinforcement learning methodologies have recently been employed to facilitate the formulation of pertinent questions; however, these approaches encounter challenges in developing an effective recurrent neural network-based questioner, attributable to the inherent complexity associated with learning sequential sentence structures. Drawing inspiration from theory of mind, this work introduces "Answerer in Questioner's Mind" (AQM), a novel information-theoretic algorithm designed for goal-oriented dialogue. Within the AQM framework, the questioner formulates queries and performs inference utilizing an approximated probabilistic model of the answerer. The questioner ascertains the answerer's intention through the selection of a plausible question, a process facilitated by explicitly calculating the information gain associated with candidate intentions and potential responses to each query. The proposed framework is evaluated on two goal-oriented visual dialogue tasks: "MNIST Counting Dialog" and "GuessWhat?!". Experimental results demonstrate that AQM significantly surpasses the performance of comparative algorithms.

text: Trong phạm vi của đồ án, Xpress được sử dụng để xây dựng server chat gúp gửi tin nhắn messenger tự động cho người dùng. Cụ thể, Express.js, một framework web tối giản và linh hoạt cho môi trường Node.js, được lựa chọn nhờ vào khả năng xử lý các yêu cầu I/O phi đồng bộ (non-blocking I/O) hiệu quả, giúp tối ưu hóa hiệu suất và khả năng mở rộng của hệ thống. Server này đóng vai trò là một cổng API (Application Programming Interface) trung tâm, thiết kế để nhận và xử lý các yêu cầu gửi tin nhắn tự động từ nhiều nguồn khác nhau, bao gồm các dịch vụ nội bộ (microservices), các tác vụ theo lịch trình (cron jobs), hoặc các webhook từ hệ thống bên ngoài. Kiến trúc của server tận dụng tối đa cơ chế middleware của Express.js để thực hiện các tác vụ như phân tích cú pháp yêu cầu (parsing request bodies), xác thực dữ liệu đầu vào (input validation), và quản lý phiên (session management) nếu cần thiết, đảm bảo tính toàn vẹn và an toàn cho dữ liệu. Mỗi loại tin nhắn tự động, ví dụ như thông báo giao dịch, lời nhắc sự kiện, hay chiến dịch tiếp thị, được định nghĩa thông qua các endpoint RESTful riêng biệt, cho phép server quản lý các luồng công việc cụ thể. Khi một yêu cầu gửi tin nhắn được tiếp nhận, server sẽ truy vấn cơ sở dữ liệu để lấy các thông tin cần thiết về người dùng và nội dung tin nhắn, sau đó động tổng hợp nội dung tin nhắn dựa trên các mẫu có sẵn và dữ liệu tức thời. Để đảm bảo việc gửi tin nhắn được thực hiện một cách đáng tin cậy và không làm tắc nghẽn luồng xử lý chính của server, một hệ thống hàng đợi tin nhắn (message queue) được tích hợp, ví dụ như sử dụng Redis hoặc RabbitMQ. Các tin nhắn sẽ được đưa vào hàng đợi và xử lý bởi các tiến trình worker riêng biệt, giúp decoupling (tách rời) quá trình tạo tin nhắn khỏi quá trình gửi thực tế đến các nền tảng messenger bên thứ ba như Facebook Messenger API, Zalo API, hoặc Telegram Bot API. Điều này không chỉ cải thiện khả năng phản hồi của server mà còn cung cấp cơ chế phục hồi lỗi (fault tolerance) và thử lại (retry mechanism) tự động cho các tin nhắn không thành công do sự cố mạng, giới hạn API, hoặc lỗi tạm thời của nền tảng đích. Ngoài ra, việc sử dụng các thư viện HTTP client chuyên biệt giúp quản lý các yêu cầu gửi tin nhắn, xử lý phản hồi từ API của các nền tảng messenger, và ghi nhận trạng thái gửi thành công hoặc thất bại. Toàn bộ quá trình gửi tin nhắn, từ lúc tiếp nhận yêu cầu, xử lý nội dung, đến trạng thái gửi cuối cùng, đều được ghi lại chi tiết trong hệ thống nhật ký (logging system) để phục vụ cho mục đích giám sát, gỡ lỗi và phân tích hiệu suất. Đối với vấn đề bảo mật, server Express.js được cấu hình để sử dụng HTTPS, xác thực API key hoặc token cho các yêu cầu đến, và áp dụng các biện pháp bảo vệ chống lại các lỗ hổng web phổ biến như tấn công tiêm nhiễm (injection attacks) và tấn công cross-site scripting (XSS). Tính linh hoạt của Express.js cùng với kiến trúc module hóa cho phép dễ dàng mở rộng và tích hợp thêm các tính năng mới trong tương lai, chẳng hạn như phân tích hiệu quả tin nhắn, tối ưu hóa thời gian gửi dựa trên hành vi người dùng, hoặc hỗ trợ thêm các kênh truyền thông khác, từ đó nâng cao giá trị và tính ứng dụng của hệ thống gửi tin nhắn tự động trong thực tiễn.

text:
Conventional image instance segmentation typically involves object detection followed by segmenting the object from its bounding box. While recent deep learning methods, such as Mask R-CNN, integrate these steps, they often overlook the distinct characteristics of the human category, which can be precisely defined by pose skeletons. Furthermore, human pose skeletons offer superior instance discrimination, particularly under heavy occlusion, compared to bounding box-based methods.

In this paper, we introduce a novel pose-based instance segmentation framework designed specifically for humans, which segments instances by leveraging human pose information rather than traditional proposal region detection. Our framework demonstrates superior accuracy compared to state-of-the-art detection-based methods for human instance segmentation, exhibiting enhanced robustness to occlusion.

A significant challenge in this domain is the scarcity of public datasets featuring heavily occluded humans with comprehensive annotations, a critical gap often overlooked in research. To address this, we present OCHuman, a new benchmark dataset specifically designed for occluded human instance segmentation. OCHuman comprises 8,110 meticulously annotated human instances across 4,731 images, providing comprehensive annotations including bounding boxes, human poses, and instance masks. Characterized by an average maximum Intersection-over-Union (MaxIoU) of 0.67 per person, OCHuman represents the most complex and challenging dataset available for human instance segmentation. This dataset aims to highlight occlusion as a critical problem for future research in human instance segmentation.

By projecting features onto the principal components, models can focus on the most informative aspects of the data, thereby enhancing performance and stability across sequential learning tasks. text: We propose a general variational framework of fair clustering, which integrates an original Kullback-Leibler (KL) fairness term with a large class of clustering objectives, including prototype or graph based. Fundamentally different from the existing combinatorial and spectral solutions, our variational multi-term approach enables to control the trade-off levels between the fairness and clustering objectives. We derive a general tight upper bound based on a concave-convex decomposition of our fairness term, its Lipschitz-gradient property and the Pinsker's inequality. Our tight upper bound can be jointly optimized with various clustering objectives, while yielding a scalable solution, with convergence guarantee. Interestingly, at each iteration, it performs an independent update for each assignment variable. Therefore, it can be easily distributed for large-scale datasets. This scalability is important as it enables to explore different trade-off levels between the fairness and clustering objectives. Unlike spectral relaxation, our formulation does not require computing its eigenvalue decomposition. We report comprehensive evaluations and comparisons with state-of-the-art methods over various fair-clustering benchmarks, which show that our variational formulation can yield highly competitive solutions in terms of fairness and clustering objectives.

The findings suggest that ES can serve as a viable alternative to RL, particularly in large-scale applications requiring distributed computing. This research contributes to the growing body of work on optimization algorithms, offering insights into the trade-offs between scalability, efficiency, and performance in modern machine learning systems.

text: In applications such as CD disc storage, errors are prone to occur in the presence of long consecutive sequences of zero bits. Therefore, it is critical to develop codes designed to avoid extended runs of zero bits. Immink pioneered the Run Length Limited (RLL) code specifically to overcome this problem. RLL codes are formally defined by two non-negative integer parameters, `d` and `k` (where `d ≤ k`), and are denoted as (d, k)-RLL. A finite binary sequence is considered to satisfy the (d, k)-RLL constraint if the number of zero bits situated between any two consecutive one bits is at least `d` and at most `k`.

The rapid advancement of deepfake technologies has raised significant concerns regarding their misuse, particularly in spreading misinformation and manipulating digital content. This paper addresses the critical challenge of attributing deepfakes to their source models or creators, a task essential for ensuring accountability and trust in digital media. We propose a novel attribution framework that leverages advanced deep learning techniques to identify unique artifacts and patterns left by different generative models during the creation of deepfakes. Our approach combines multi-scale feature extraction with a robust classifier trained on a diverse dataset of deepfakes generated by state-of-the-art models. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves high accuracy in attributing deepfakes to their source models, outperforming existing techniques in both precision and recall. Furthermore, we analyze the generalizability of our framework across various datasets and adversarial scenarios, highlighting its resilience to common evasion tactics. The findings of this research provide a significant step forward in the fight against malicious deepfake usage, offering a reliable tool for forensic analysis and digital content verification. This work contributes to the broader field of digital forensics by introducing a scalable and effective solution for deepfake attribution, with potential applications in cybersecurity, media integrity, and legal investigations.  

**Keywords**: deepfakes, attribution, digital forensics, generative models, deep learning, misinformation, cybersecurity.

text: Nắm bắt được những mong muốn và vấn đề mà họ gặp phải trong quá trình bán hàng theo cách truyền thống, tồn tại một số điểm như sau: Phương thức quản lý thủ công hiện tại tại cửa hàng MyShoes đã bộc lộ những hạn chế đáng kể, ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến hiệu quả vận hành và khả năng cạnh tranh trên thị trường bán lẻ đầy biến động. Cụ thể, trong khía cạnh quản lý tồn kho, việc không có một hệ thống tự động hóa đã dẫn đến tình trạng cập nhật số lượng hàng hóa không kịp thời, thiếu thông tin chính xác về từng sản phẩm theo mã vạch, kích cỡ và màu sắc. Điều này gây khó khăn trong việc kiểm kê định kỳ, xác định chính xác các mẫu giày bán chạy hay tồn đọng, từ đó ảnh hưởng tiêu cực đến quyết định nhập hàng, tối ưu hóa không gian lưu trữ và giảm thiểu rủi ro hàng tồn kho lỗi thời. Sự thiếu hụt dữ liệu tức thời còn cản trở khả năng phục vụ khách hàng nhanh chóng, vì nhân viên phải mất thời gian kiểm tra thủ công hoặc tìm kiếm thông tin về sản phẩm. Bên cạnh đó, việc không có một cơ sở dữ liệu khách hàng tập trung và có cấu trúc rõ ràng đã khiến MyShoes bỏ lỡ nhiều cơ hội trong việc xây dựng và duy trì mối quan hệ bền vững với khách hàng. Dữ liệu về lịch sử mua sắm, sở thích cá nhân và thông tin liên hệ của khách hàng chỉ được ghi nhận một cách rời rạc, không được khai thác hiệu quả để cá nhân hóa trải nghiệm mua sắm hoặc triển khai các chương trình khuyến mãi, tri ân khách hàng thân thiết một cách có mục tiêu. Điều này làm giảm khả năng gia tăng lòng trung thành, tỷ lệ quay lại của khách hàng và hạn chế hiệu quả của các chiến dịch marketing. Đối với quy trình bán hàng, các thao tác như kiểm tra giá, tính tiền, in hóa đơn và xử lý các chương trình khuyến mãi đều được thực hiện thủ công hoặc dựa trên các phần mềm không đồng bộ, gây ra sự chậm trễ đáng kể trong quá trình thanh toán, đặc biệt vào giờ cao điểm, dẫn đến hàng đợi dài và giảm sự hài lòng của khách hàng. Hơn nữa, việc xử lý đổi trả hàng cũng trở nên phức tạp, tốn nhiều công sức và tiềm ẩn nguy cơ sai sót cao. Sự thiếu hiệu quả này không chỉ ảnh hưởng đến năng suất của nhân viên mà còn tác động trực tiếp đến doanh thu và uy tín của cửa hàng. Một trong những hạn chế lớn nhất khác là khả năng phân tích và báo cáo doanh thu còn rất hạn chế. Dữ liệu bán hàng được tổng hợp thủ công, dẫn đến khó khăn trong việc tạo ra các báo cáo chi tiết, chính xác về doanh thu theo ngày, tuần, tháng, theo loại sản phẩm, theo nhân viên hoặc theo các tiêu chí khác. Sự thiếu hụt các công cụ phân tích chuyên sâu khiến MyShoes không thể nhanh chóng nhận diện xu hướng bán hàng, đánh giá hiệu quả của các chiến dịch, hoặc dự báo nhu cầu trong tương lai một cách khoa học. Việc thiếu thông tin đáng tin cậy và kịp thời này cản trở khả năng đưa ra các quyết định kinh doanh chiến lược, tối ưu hóa danh mục sản phẩm và điều chỉnh chiến lược giá. Cuối cùng, mặc dù cửa hàng đạt được doanh thu không nhỏ với lượng khách đều đặn, nhưng áp lực từ chi phí thuê mặt bằng và chi phí nhân công ngày càng tăng cao đòi hỏi một giải pháp tối ưu hóa vận hành để kiểm soát chi phí. text:
Hệ thống được phân tích bao gồm các tác nhân chính là Giáo viên, Học viên, và Người dùng (user) với các vai trò và chức năng được xác định rõ ràng. Giáo viên chịu trách nhiệm quản lý các khóa học do mình đăng tải, theo dõi lợi nhuận từ các khóa học đó và thực hiện tạo khóa học mới. Người dùng (user) đại diện cho quyền truy cập chung của tất cả các tác nhân sau khi truy cập thành công vào hệ thống.

Các trường hợp sử dụng (Usecase) cơ bản được mô tả trong Bảng 2.1. Mọi user đều có thể thực hiện Usecase 1: Đăng nhập để truy cập hệ thống và Usecase 2: Đăng ký tài khoản. Đối với Học viên, hệ thống cung cấp Usecase 3: Quản lý tài khoản, cho phép người dùng thực hiện các thao tác như thay đổi ảnh đại diện, địa chỉ email, kết nối tài khoản mạng xã hội (Facebook, Google), đặt lại mật khẩu và xóa tài khoản. Học viên cũng có thể thực hiện Usecase 4: Quản lý các khóa học đã mua, bao gồm thêm, sửa, xóa khóa học hoặc tiếp tục xem; và Usecase 5: Xem các khóa học đang được bán, cho phép tìm kiếm theo tên hoặc phân loại theo chủ đề, thể loại và tiến hành mua khóa học.

Đối với Giáo viên, Usecase 6 (Bảng 2.1) là Quản lý lợi nhuận, cho phép theo dõi số lượng người mua, tổng tiền thu về và biểu đồ doanh thu theo thời gian. Các chức năng quản lý khóa học của Giáo viên được mô tả chi tiết hơn trong Bảng 2.2, bao gồm Usecase 7: Quản lý các khóa học đã đăng, cho phép tìm kiếm, sắp xếp theo tên, giá tiền, trạng thái (Đã đăng hoặc Nháp), xem thông tin chi tiết, và chỉnh sửa (ví dụ: đổi tên khóa học, thêm chương, video). Usecase 8: Tạo các khóa học mới, nơi giáo viên nhập thông tin cần thiết như tên, giá tiền và đăng tải khóa học.

Biểu đồ Use case phân rã Quản lý khóa học được minh họa trong Hình 2.2: Biểu đồ Use case người dùng Học viên. Theo đó, sau khi đăng nhập thành công, Học viên có thể tiếp tục học các khóa học đang dang dở, xem tiến độ hoàn thành (tính theo phần trăm) của các khóa học và số lượng khóa học đã hoàn thành. Học viên cũng có quyền xóa những khóa học đã được mua khỏi tài khoản của mình. Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc mô hình hóa các tương tác người dùng cốt lõi, đặt nền tảng cho việc phát triển một hệ thống quản lý học tập trực tuyến hiệu quả và thân thiện với người dùng.

text: MeanShift is a popular mode-seeking clustering algorithm used in a wide range of applications in machine learning. However, it is known to be prohibitively slow, with quadratic runtime per iteration. We propose MeanShift++, an extremely fast mode-seeking algorithm based on MeanShift that uses a grid-based approach to speed up the mean shift step, replacing the computationally expensive neighbors search with a density-weighted mean of adjacent grid cells. In addition, we show that this grid-based technique for density estimation comes with theoretical guarantees. The runtime is linear in the number of points and exponential in dimension, which makes MeanShift++ ideal on low-dimensional applications such as image segmentation and object tracking. We provide extensive experimental analysis showing that MeanShift++ can be more than 10,000x faster than MeanShift with competitive clustering results on benchmark datasets and nearly identical image segmentations as MeanShift. Finally, we show promising results for object tracking. Future research should therefore focus on strategies to mitigate the exponential dependence on dimensionality, potentially expanding MeanShift++ to higher-dimensional spaces. Further investigations could also refine the grid-based density estimation and explore its utility across a wider range of computationally intensive applications.
label: human---gemini-text

text: With the proliferation of big data, enhancing memory and computational efficiency has become essential for the effective implementation of modern technologies. Hashing stands out as a powerful technique to address the computational challenges associated with large-scale data. Spectral hashing offers a direct method for learning binary codes by incorporating data affinity, but the optimization process becomes difficult due to binary constraints. To address this, various relaxation strategies have been introduced to ease the computational burden of generating binary codes while still yielding effective solutions. However, these existing relaxation techniques often rely on introducing auxiliary variables to maintain the quality of the binary codes, which in turn necessitates a coordinate descent approach and increases computational complexity. We contend that such auxiliary variables are not required. Accordingly, we introduce a new relaxed spectral hashing formulation that avoids additional variables. Moreover, rather than operating in the original space where the number of variables matches the data points, our approach solves the problem in a substantially reduced space and reconstructs the binary codes from this solution, thereby lowering both memory and computational demands. We employ two optimization methods—projected gradient and manifold optimization—to find the solution. Extensive experiments conducted on four public datasets demonstrate that our efficient spectral hashing (ESH) algorithm achieves retrieval performance on par with state-of-the-art methods, but at significantly lower complexity.

text: "Nonstationarity" is a fundamental challenge in cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), arising from each agent's policy continually evolving during learning while simultaneously constituting part of the environment for other agents. This dynamic causes information to oscillate among agents, significantly impeding convergence. Utilizing the MAILP model of information transfer in multi-agent learning, we demonstrate that increasing the degree of centralization during learning can arbitrarily reduce the convergence slowdown caused by nonstationarity. The most centralized approach is parameter sharing, a relatively uncommon MARL technique applicable to environments with homogeneous agents, which leverages single-agent reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms to learn a unified policy for all agents. We experimentally validate our theoretical findings, showing that greater centralization in learning leads to improved performance. Additionally, we extend parameter sharing to eight contemporary single-agent deep RL methods for the first time, attaining up to 44-fold increases in average reward in just 16% of the episodes required by prior parameter sharing studies. Finally, we provide a formal proof identifying a set of methods that enable parameter sharing to be effectively applied in environments with heterogeneous agents.

text: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved significant success across various supervised learning tasks, including voice recognition, object detection, and image classification. However, their increasing complexity often leads to poor generalization performance, hindering deployment on edge devices. Quantization is an effective technique for compressing DNNs to address these constraints. Employing a quasiconvex base function to construct a binary quantizer facilitates the training of binary neural networks (BNNs), while adding noise to input data or utilizing a concrete regularization function enhances generalization. In this work, we introduce the foothill function, an infinitely differentiable quasiconvex function that is sufficiently flexible to interpolate between L_1 and L_2 penalties. The foothill function can serve as a binary quantizer, a regularizer, or a loss function. Notably, we demonstrate that this regularizer reduces the accuracy gap between BNNs and their full-precision counterparts in image classification tasks on ImageNet.

text: The joint forecasting of human trajectory and pose dynamics constitutes a foundational element for diverse applications, ranging from robotics and autonomous driving to surveillance systems. The prediction of body dynamics requires the capture of subtle information embedded within human-human interactions and human-object interactions within the scene. This paper introduces a novel TRajectory and POse Dynamics (TRiPOD) method based on graph attentional networks to model human-human and human-object interactions in both the input space and the output space (decoded future output). The model is augmented by a message passing interface over the graphs to efficiently integrate these different interaction levels. Furthermore, to address a real-world challenge, the method proposes learning an indicator that represents whether an estimated body joint is visible/invisible per frame, e.g., due to occlusion or being outside the sensor field of view. Finally, a new benchmark for this joint task is introduced, utilizing two challenging datasets (PoseTrack and 3DPW), and evaluation metrics are proposed to measure the effectiveness of predictions in the global space, even in cases of joint invisibility. Our evaluation demonstrates that TRiPOD surpasses all prior work and state-of-the-art approaches specifically developed for each of the distinct trajectory and pose forecasting tasks.

text: This study introduces a residual non-local attention network designed for advanced image restoration. Traditional approaches often overlook the uneven information distribution in degraded images, limiting their effectiveness due to reliance on local convolutions and uniform handling of spatial and channel features. To overcome these limitations, we develop local and non-local attention blocks that identify long-range pixel dependencies and prioritize more complex regions. Each block consists of a trunk branch for hierarchical feature extraction and local or non-local mask branches that dynamically adjust these features using mixed attention mechanisms. The local mask branch focuses on structural details through convolutional operations, whereas the non-local branch emphasizes broader dependencies across the feature map. Additionally, we implement residual local and non-local attention learning to optimize deep network training, improving overall feature representation. The proposed framework is versatile, applicable to tasks like image denoising, demosaicing, artifact reduction, and super-resolution. Experimental results show that our method achieves performance on par with or superior to state-of-the-art techniques in both quantitative metrics and visual quality.

text: Deep neural networks are often trained with a significantly higher number of parameters than the available training data. Surprisingly, recent studies show that this overparameterization not only enhances the training of large models but also aids in developing compact models, particularly through pruning or sparsification. This work provides theoretical insights into these observations by analyzing the high-dimensional behavior of model pruning in overparameterized settings, addressing whether it is preferable to train a small model directly or first train a larger model and then prune. We demonstrate scenarios where, even with prior knowledge of the most informative features, training a large model followed by pruning outperforms training solely on known features. This results in a novel double descent phenomenon for sparse models, where increasing the initial model size while maintaining target sparsity enhances test accuracy beyond the overparameterization threshold. Additionally, our analysis highlights the advantages of retraining in relation to feature correlations. These effects are observed in simpler models like linear and random-features models, and our methodology extends high-dimensional analysis tools to precisely describe the asymptotic behavior of overparameterized least-squares. Empirical validation on neural networks supports the insights derived from theoretical examination of these simpler models.
label: human---deepseek-text

text: We focus on the development of effective adversarial patch attacks and, for the first time, jointly address the conflicting objectives of attack success and obtrusiveness through the design of novel semi-transparent patches. This work is motivated by our pursuit of a systematic performance analysis of patch attack robustness with respect to geometric transformations. Specifically, we first elucidate (a) key factors underpinning patch attack success and (b) the impact of distributional shift between training and testing/deployment under the Expectation over Transformation (EoT) formalism. By concentrating our analysis on three principal classes of transformations—rotation, scale, and location—our findings provide quantifiable insights into the design of effective patch attacks and demonstrate that scale, among all factors, significantly influences patch attack success. Building on these findings, we then address how to overcome the primary limitations posed by scale for deploying attacks in real physical settings, namely the obtrusiveness of large patches. Our approach involves the novel design of irregularly shaped, semi-transparent partial patches, constructed via a new optimization process that simultaneously mitigates obtrusiveness and maximizes effectiveness. We hope this study will encourage the community to place greater emphasis on the intertwined issues of obtrusiveness, scale, and success in patch attacks.

text: Semantic scene understanding is crucial for a variety of applications, most notably for self-driving cars, which require a fine-grained comprehension of their surrounding surfaces and objects. Light detection and ranging (LiDAR) provides precise geometric information about the environment and is thus integral to the sensor suites of nearly all self-driving cars. Despite the critical relevance of semantic scene understanding for such applications, a significant limitation persists due to the scarcity of large-scale datasets for this task, particularly those derived from automotive LiDAR systems. To address this gap, this paper introduces a comprehensive dataset specifically designed to advance research in laser-based semantic segmentation. We meticulously annotated all sequences of the KITTI Vision Odometry Benchmark, providing dense point-wise annotations that cover the complete 360^ field-of-view of the employed automotive LiDAR. Building upon this dataset, we propose three distinct benchmark tasks: (i) semantic segmentation of point clouds using a single scan, (ii) semantic segmentation using multiple past scans, and (iii) semantic scene completion, which requires to anticipate the semantic scene in the future. Our preliminary baseline experiments demonstrate the necessity for more sophisticated models to effectively address these complex tasks. Ultimately, our dataset not only enables the development of more advanced methodologies but also provides ample data to explore novel research directions in semantic scene understanding.
label: human---gemini-text

text:
The accurate prediction of molecular properties is a fundamental challenge in quantum chemistry, with applications ranging from drug discovery to materials science. This paper introduces a novel approach leveraging neural message passing (NMP) to model molecular systems effectively. Unlike traditional methods that rely on handcrafted features or computationally expensive quantum simulations, our approach employs a graph-based representation of molecules, where atoms and bonds are modeled as nodes and edges, respectively. The NMP framework iteratively updates atomic features by aggregating information from neighboring atoms, enabling the model to capture complex interactions and dependencies within molecular structures. We evaluate the proposed method on benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance in predicting molecular properties such as energy, dipole moments, and electronic characteristics compared to existing techniques. The results highlight the model's ability to generalize across diverse chemical spaces while maintaining computational efficiency. This work advances the state-of-the-art in molecular property prediction by combining the interpretability of graph-based models with the expressive power of deep learning. The proposed framework has significant implications for accelerating drug discovery, optimizing materials, and enabling large-scale virtual screening in quantum chemistry.

text: It is challenging to detect curve texts due to their irregular shapes and varying sizes. In this paper, we first investigate the deficiency of the existing curve detection methods and then propose a novel Conditional Spatial Expansion (CSE) mechanism to improve the performance of curve text detection. Instead of regarding the curve text detection as a polygon regression or a segmentation problem, we treat it as a region expansion process. Our CSE starts with a seed arbitrarily initialized within a text region and progressively merges neighborhood regions based on the extracted local features by a CNN and contextual information of merged regions. The CSE is highly parameterized and can be seamlessly integrated into existing object detection frameworks. Enhanced by the data-dependent CSE mechanism, our curve text detection system provides robust instance-level text region extraction with minimal post-processing. The analysis experiment shows that our CSE can handle texts with various shapes, sizes, and orientations, and can effectively suppress the false-positives coming from text-like textures or unexpected texts included in the same RoI. Compared with the existing curve text detection algorithms, our method is more robust and enjoys a simpler processing flow. It also creates a new state-of-art performance on curve text benchmarks with F-score of up to 78.4\%.

Furthermore, the dynamic filter layers can be stacked, such as in a recurrent setup, allowing for more complex representations. text: Duplicate removal is a critical step to accomplish a reasonable amount of predictions in prevalent proposal-based object detection frameworks. Albeit simple and effective, most previous algorithms utilize a greedy process without making sufficient use of properties of input data. In this work, we design a new two-stage framework to effectively select the appropriate proposal candidate for each object. The first stage suppresses most of easy negative object proposals, while the second stage selects true positives in the reduced proposal set. These two stages share the same network structure, \ie, an encoder and a decoder formed as recurrent neural networks (RNN) with global attention and context gate. The encoder scans proposal candidates in a sequential manner to capture the global context information, which is then fed to the decoder to extract optimal proposals. In our extensive experiments, the proposed method outperforms other alternatives by a large margin.
