text: This paper introduces DeeSIL, a novel Deep-Shallow Incremental Learning approach designed to efficiently adapt deep neural networks to evolving data streams. The objective is to address the challenge of catastrophic forgetting in incremental learning scenarios, where models must learn from a stream of data without forgetting previously acquired knowledge. DeeSIL achieves this by combining the strengths of deep and shallow learning techniques, leveraging the representational power of deep networks while incorporating the flexibility of shallow models to adapt to new data. Our approach utilizes a hybrid architecture that incrementally updates the model as new data arrives, ensuring a balance between knowledge retention and new information acquisition. Experimental results demonstrate that DeeSIL outperforms state-of-the-art incremental learning methods, exhibiting improved accuracy and reduced forgetting on several benchmark datasets. The proposed method has significant implications for real-world applications, such as continuous learning in autonomous systems, incremental data processing, and edge AI. Key contributions include the development of a novel deep-shallow incremental learning framework, improved performance on incremental learning tasks, and enhanced adaptability to changing data distributions. Relevant keywords: incremental learning, deep neural networks, shallow learning, catastrophic forgetting, edge AI, continuous learning.

text: Instance segmentation, a critical task within computer vision, focuses on identifying and segmenting individual object instances at a pixel-wise granularity within an image. While Mask R-CNN represents a seminal approach to instance segmentation, our observations indicate that its generated masks often exhibit imprecision and blurriness, particularly in proximity to object contours. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel loss function, termed contour loss, which is inspired by the principles of contour matching utilizing distance transformation images. This contour loss is specifically engineered to refine the contour regions of predicted masks, thereby facilitating more precise instance segmentation. To enable its joint optimization within contemporary neural network architectures, we developed a differentiable k-step distance transformation image calculation module, capable of approximately computing truncated distance transformation images for both predicted and ground-truth masks in an online manner. The versatility of the proposed contour loss is highlighted by its seamless integration into existing instance segmentation methodologies, such as Mask R-CNN, allowing combination with their inherent loss functions without necessitating alterations to inference network architectures. Empirical evaluations conducted on the COCO dataset demonstrate the efficacy of contour loss in significantly enhancing instance segmentation performance.

text: Blazor facilitates the creation of interactive web user interfaces (UIs) by leveraging C# instead of JavaScript. It is composed of reusable web UI components developed with C#, HTML, and CSS, enabling the sharing of code and libraries across both client and server sides as a feature of ASP.NET, a prominent web development framework extending the .NET platform. While numerous UI frameworks are available (e.g., reactjs, vuejs), Blazorise was chosen for this research due to its contemporary nature and inherent compatibility with C#, which is also utilized for backend development. Specifically, Blazor Web Assembly is employed, offering significant advantages for client-side web development, including enhanced ease of development and high performance attributed to its capacity to leverage current hardware capabilities. Furthermore, it provides superior client-side security compared to JavaScript by effectively functioning across both backend and frontend. This technology is currently supported by major browsers: Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge, and is anticipated to gain further prominence in client-side web development. Complementing this, the ABP Framework offers a structured, opinionated architecture for developing enterprise software solutions built upon the .NET and ASP.NET Core platforms, adhering to established best practices. It furnishes the foundational infrastructure, production-ready startup templates, modules, themes, tooling, guides, and comprehensive documentation to implement this architecture effectively and automate repetitive development tasks. The ABP Framework demonstrates versatility by integrating seamlessly with various UI frameworks, such as Angular, MVC page razor, and Blazor, and accommodating diverse database providers, including entity framework core, MongoDB, and dapper. The implementation in this research specifically adopts a domain-driven design architecture.

The methodology employs a deep reinforcement learning algorithm to learn an optimal policy, which is then refined by a model-based optimizer to ensure feasibility and optimality. Results show that the proposed approach outperforms traditional rule-based methods, achieving significant improvements in economic benefits and reducing energy losses. The conclusion highlights the potential of this innovative approach to transform the operation of battery energy storage systems, enabling greater grid resilience and renewable energy integration. Key contributions include the development of a novel reinforcement learning framework and the demonstration of its effectiveness in optimizing battery energy storage dispatch. text: The reliance on large amounts of annotated data in current deep learning paradigms highlights the variability in annotation quality among different labelers, particularly in critical applications such as medical image analysis. Multi-observer studies investigate these variances, but they impose additional burdens due to the need for professional expertise. Recently, automated annotation methods driven by natural language processing (NLP) algorithms have emerged as a promising alternative, leveraging existing diagnostic reports in clinical systems. While these algorithms produce noisier labels compared to human labelers, they can still be valuable. This study introduces an innovative approach to utilize noisy annotations from various algorithm-based labelers to enhance the learning of classification tasks. The attention-on-label concept is presented, which dynamically samples more effective label sets during training. A meta-training-based label-sampling module is designed to optimize label selection through additional back-propagation processes. The efficacy of the attention-on-label scheme is demonstrated with a synthetic noisy CIFAR-10 dataset and further validated with a significant improvement in classification performance on chest x-ray images from the MIMIC-CXR and OpenI datasets, achieving a 3-5% increase in disease classification AUCs compared to conventional training methods.

text: Outdoor vision robotic systems and autonomous cars suffer from many image-quality issues, particularly haze, defocus blur, and motion blur, which we will define generically as "blindness issues". These blindness issues may seriously affect the performance of robotic systems and could lead to unsafe decisions being made. However, existing solutions either focus on one type of blindness only or lack the ability to estimate the degree of blindness accurately. Besides, heavy computation is needed so that these solutions cannot run in real-time on practical systems. In this paper, we provide a method which could simultaneously detect the type of blindness and provide a blindness map indicating to what degree the vision is limited on a pixel-by-pixel basis. Both the blindness type and the estimate of per-pixel blindness are essential for tasks like deblur, dehaze, or the fail-safe functioning of robotic systems. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on the KITTI and CUHK datasets where experiments show that our method outperforms other state-of-the-art approaches, achieving speeds of about 130 frames per second (fps).

text: The effectiveness of single-agent reinforcement learning (RL) in Internet of Things (IoT) systems motivates the exploration of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), which, though more challenging, holds greater utility for large-scale IoT applications. This paper investigates a voting-based MARL problem where agents make collective decisions through voting, with the objective of maximizing globally averaged returns. To this end, the MARL problem is formulated based on the linear programming representation of the policy optimization problem, and a distributed primal-dual algorithm is proposed to derive the optimal solution. A novel voting mechanism is also introduced, enabling the distributed learning to achieve the same sublinear convergence rate as centralized learning, thereby demonstrating that distributed decision-making does not impede the process of reaching global consensus on optimality. The convergence of the proposed algorithm is validated through numerical simulations, and its application is further explored via case studies in practical multi-agent IoT systems.

text: Partial multi-label learning (PML), which tackles the problem of learning multi-label prediction models from instances with overcomplete noisy annotations, has recently started gaining attention from the research community. In this paper, we propose a novel adversarial learning model, PML-GAN, under a generalized encoder-decoder framework for partial multi-label learning. The PML-GAN model uses a disambiguation network to identify noisy labels and uses a multi-label prediction network to map the training instances to the disambiguated label vectors, while deploying a generative adversarial network as an inverse mapping from label vectors to data samples in the input feature space. The learning of the overall model corresponds to a minimax adversarial game, which enhances the correspondence of input features with the output labels in a bi-directional mapping. Extensive experiments are conducted on multiple datasets, while the proposed model demonstrates the state-of-the-art performance for partial multi-label learning.

text: Mô hình Client-Server là kiến trúc nền tảng cho hầu hết các hệ thống phân tán hiện đại, đặc biệt là ứng dụng web và di động. Mô hình này phân tách hệ thống thành hai thành phần chính: máy khách (client) chịu trách nhiệm giao diện người dùng và tương tác trực tiếp với người dùng, trong khi máy chủ (server) quản lý logic nghiệp vụ, lưu trữ và xử lý dữ liệu, cung cấp tài nguyên. Sự phân tách này mang lại ưu điểm vượt trội về khả năng mở rộng (scalability) do các thành phần có thể được mở rộng độc lập, dễ dàng bảo trì và cập nhật, cũng như tăng cường bảo mật thông tin do dữ liệu được tập trung và kiểm soát chặt chẽ tại máy chủ. Giao tiếp giữa máy khách và máy chủ được thực hiện qua các giao thức mạng chuẩn như HTTP/HTTPS. Để hiện thực hóa mô hình Client-Server hiệu quả, việc tận dụng các thư viện lập trình và framework là không thể thiếu. Ở phía máy khách, các thư viện và framework giao diện người dùng như React, Angular, hoặc Vue.js cung cấp công cụ mạnh mẽ để xây dựng ứng dụng đơn trang (Single Page Application - SPA) năng động, tối ưu hóa trải nghiệm người dùng thông qua quản lý trạng thái và cấu trúc thành phần tái sử dụng. Về phía máy chủ, các framework như Spring Boot (Java), Node.js Express (JavaScript), hoặc Django/Flask (Python) là xương sống, cung cấp cấu trúc sẵn có cho việc phát triển API RESTful, quản lý phiên, xác thực, ủy quyền, và tích hợp cơ sở dữ liệu thông qua các thư viện ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) hoặc ODM (Object-Document Mapping). Các thư viện bổ trợ khác cũng được sử dụng rộng rãi cho các tác vụ như xử lý dữ liệu, ghi log, kiểm thử, và quản lý các tác vụ bất đồng bộ, giúp tăng tốc độ phát triển và nâng cao chất lượng mã nguồn. Sau giai đoạn phát triển, việc triển khai hệ thống lên môi trường sản phẩm đòi hỏi sự hỗ trợ của các công cụ chuyên biệt nhằm đảm bảo tính ổn định và khả năng vận hành liên tục. Công nghệ container hóa, điển hình là Docker, cho phép đóng gói ứng dụng cùng toàn bộ phụ thuộc vào một môi trường biệt lập, đảm bảo tính nhất quán trên mọi môi trường. Để quản lý và điều phối các container ở quy mô lớn, các nền tảng điều phối (orchestration) như Kubernetes trở nên thiết yếu, tự động hóa việc triển khai, mở rộng, cân bằng tải và tự phục hồi cho ứng dụng. Quy trình Tích hợp Liên tục/Triển khai Liên tục (CI/CD) sử dụng các công cụ như GitLab CI/CD, Jenkins hoặc GitHub Actions giúp tự động hóa toàn bộ chu trình phát triển từ mã nguồn đến triển khai, đảm bảo các bản cập nhật được đưa ra nhanh chóng và ít lỗi. Việc lựa chọn các nền tảng đám mây công cộng như Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, hoặc Google Cloud Platform (GCP) cung cấp cơ sở hạ tầng linh hoạt và các dịch vụ quản lý giúp tối ưu hóa chi phí và hiệu suất vận hành. Cuối cùng, các công nghệ cụ thể được sử dụng để thiết kế và hiện thực hóa hệ thống được lựa chọn dựa trên yêu cầu về hiệu năng, khả năng mở rộng, bảo mật và khả năng bảo trì. Ngôn ngữ lập trình cho backend có thể bao gồm Java (với Spring Boot) hoặc Python (với Django/Flask) nhờ sự mạnh mẽ và cộng đồng hỗ trợ lớn; hoặc Node.js cho các ứng dụng yêu cầu xử lý I/O cao. Frontend sẽ sử dụng JavaScript kết hợp với các framework đã nêu. Hệ quản trị cơ sở dữ liệu sẽ bao gồm cả cơ sở dữ liệu quan hệ (ví dụ: PostgreSQL) cho dữ liệu có cấu trúc chặt chẽ và yêu cầu tính toàn vẹn cao, cùng với cơ sở dữ liệu NoSQL (ví dụ: MongoDB, Redis) cho các trường hợp cần linh hoạt về schema, khả năng mở rộng ngang hoặc caching. Giao tiếp giữa các thành phần sẽ chủ yếu dựa trên kiến trúc API RESTful qua giao thức HTTP/HTTPS để đảm bảo tính tương thích và bảo mật. Các nguyên tắc thiết kế như kiến trúc hướng dịch vụ (SOA) hoặc vi dịch vụ (Microservices), nếu phù hợp, cũng sẽ được cân nhắc để nâng cao khả năng quản lý và phát triển độc lập từng phần của hệ thống.
label: human---gemini-text

text: This study aimed to identify suitable environmental components (carbon source, carbon concentration, nitrogen source) and fermentation conditions (temperature, pH) to enhance the antagonistic activity of *Streptomyces* sp. VNUA116 (strain VNUA116) against *Fusarium oxysporum* f. sp. *cubense* Tropical Race 4 (Foc Tr4), the causal agent of Panama wilt in banana plants. Employing the agar diffusion method, strain VNUA116 was found to exhibit potent antagonism against Foc Tr4 under fermentation conditions consisting of YIM 301 mineral medium, carbon source CB1 (soluble starch 40 g/l, D-glucose 1 g/l), and nitrogen source N1 (beef extract 3 g/l, yeast extract 5 g/l, peptone 3 g/l). Furthermore, under optimal fermentation parameters of pH 7 and a temperature of 30°C, strain VNUA116 demonstrated maximal antifungal activity against Foc Tr4, achieving an inhibition zone diameter of 30.67±0.58 mm after 10 days of cultivation. This research determined that, under optimal fermentation conditions, strain VNUA116 exhibited up to 93.20% inhibition of Foc Tr4, a level comparable to that achieved by Ridomil gold 68WG at a concentration of 3 g/l *in vitro*. These findings underscore the significant potential of strain VNUA116 for development into a biological control agent for managing Panama disease in banana cultivation.

text:
This paper addresses the challenge of achieving high-quality image super-resolution (SR) with minimal computational overhead, a critical requirement for real-time applications on resource-constrained devices. We propose a novel Adaptive Weighted Learning Network (AWLN), a lightweight deep learning framework designed to enhance image resolution while maintaining efficiency. The AWLN leverages an adaptive weighting mechanism that dynamically adjusts the contribution of feature maps during the reconstruction process, enabling the model to focus on the most relevant details for SR. Unlike traditional SR methods, which often rely on computationally expensive architectures, our approach achieves a balance between performance and efficiency by optimizing network parameters and reducing redundancy. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that AWLN outperforms existing lightweight SR models in terms of both peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM), while significantly reducing inference time. The proposed method also exhibits robust generalization across diverse image domains, making it suitable for practical applications such as medical imaging, surveillance, and mobile photography. This work contributes to the field by introducing an innovative, resource-efficient solution for image SR, paving the way for deployment in real-world scenarios where computational resources are limited.  

**Keywords**: Image super-resolution, lightweight networks, adaptive weighting, deep learning, computational efficiency, real-time applications.

text:
This paper addresses the challenge of training neural networks effectively in scenarios where high-fidelity data is scarce or expensive to obtain, while low-fidelity data is abundant. We propose a novel approach that leverages \ell 1-regularization combined with bi-fidelity data to enhance model performance and generalization. The \ell 1-regularization technique is employed to promote sparsity in the network weights, reducing overfitting and improving interpretability. Simultaneously, the bi-fidelity framework integrates both low- and high-fidelity data to train the model, ensuring robust learning even with limited high-quality data. Our methodology involves a two-stage training process: first, the model is pre-trained on low-fidelity data to capture general patterns, followed by fine-tuning using high-fidelity data to refine accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms traditional methods in terms of prediction accuracy and computational efficiency, particularly in resource-constrained environments. The findings highlight the potential of combining regularization techniques with multi-fidelity data for training neural networks, offering a scalable solution for applications in scientific computing, engineering, and beyond. This work contributes to the growing body of research on efficient neural network training and provides a practical framework for leveraging heterogeneous data sources.  

**Keywords**: Neural networks, \ell 1-regularization, bi-fidelity data, sparsity, model training, machine learning.

text: Psychological violence, also referred to as emotional or mental abuse, constitutes the deliberate application of verbal and non-verbal communication aimed at inflicting psychological or emotional harm, or exerting control over an individual. The impact of such violence can be as significant as that of physical forms, often leading to severe psychological trauma, including anxiety, depression, or post-traumatic stress disorder. This thorough conceptualization highlights diverse manifestations, including expressive aggression (e.g., humiliating and degrading behaviours), coercive control (e.g., limiting access to resources or persons, and excessive monitoring of whereabouts or communications), threats of physical or sexual violence, control over reproductive or sexual health, and the exploitation of personal vulnerabilities (e.g., immigration status or disability). This detailed categorization contributes significantly to a clearer understanding of non-physical violence, essential for targeted intervention strategies.

text:
Visual Transformers (ViTs) have emerged as a powerful paradigm for image representation and processing in computer vision, leveraging the success of transformer architectures originally designed for natural language processing. This paper explores the application of token-based image representation, where images are divided into patches and treated as sequences of tokens, enabling transformers to capture global dependencies and spatial relationships effectively. We propose a novel framework that enhances the efficiency and scalability of ViTs by introducing adaptive tokenization strategies and lightweight attention mechanisms. Our approach addresses key challenges such as computational complexity and memory usage, making it suitable for real-time applications. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in image classification, object detection, and segmentation tasks, outperforming traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and existing transformer-based models. The findings highlight the potential of token-based image processing to revolutionize computer vision, offering improved accuracy and flexibility for diverse applications. This research contributes to advancing the understanding of transformer architectures in visual domains and provides a foundation for future innovations in scalable and efficient vision systems.  

**Keywords**: Visual Transformers, Token-based Representation, Computer Vision, Attention Mechanisms, Image Processing, Adaptive Tokenization.

text: Agent modelling is vital for understanding multi-agent interactions and effective decision-making. Existing methods commonly assume access to modelled agents' local observations and actions during execution, a restrictive assumption. To address this, we propose a novel approach that extracts robust representations of other agents solely from the controlled agent's local information using encoder-decoder architectures. These representations are learned during training by conditioning on other agents' observed data, then seamlessly integrated to augment the controlled agent's deep reinforcement learning policy. This crucial design enables the policy to operate effectively during execution without requiring any direct access to other agents' information. Comprehensive evaluations and ablation studies across cooperative, competitive, and mixed multi-agent environments demonstrate that our method achieves significantly higher returns compared to baseline approaches lacking these learned representations.

text:
Breast cancer remains one of the most prevalent and life-threatening diseases worldwide, necessitating accurate and early diagnosis. This paper introduces ICADx, an interpretable computer-aided diagnosis system designed to improve the detection and classification of breast masses using medical imaging data. The primary objective of ICADx is to provide clinicians with a reliable, transparent, and explainable tool that enhances diagnostic accuracy while maintaining interpretability. The proposed system leverages a hybrid approach combining deep learning techniques with explainable AI (XAI) methods, specifically integrating convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for feature extraction and gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) for visual interpretability. ICADx was trained and validated on a large dataset of mammograms and ultrasound images, achieving a classification accuracy of 94.7% and an AUC of 0.96, outperforming existing methods. Furthermore, the system provides detailed visual explanations of its predictions, enabling clinicians to understand the decision-making process and build trust in the AI-driven diagnosis. The results demonstrate that ICADx not only improves diagnostic performance but also bridges the gap between advanced AI technologies and clinical usability. This research contributes to the growing field of interpretable AI in healthcare, offering a practical solution for early and accurate breast cancer diagnosis with significant potential for real-world clinical applications.  

**Keywords**: Computer-aided diagnosis, breast cancer, interpretable AI, deep learning, explainable AI, medical imaging, Grad-CAM.

The foundational structure of JSON-RPC messages, essential for facilitating remote procedure calls, adheres to a well-defined set of fields for both requests and responses.

A standard JSON-RPC request mandates the inclusion of the following parameters:
*   **`jsonrpc`** (string, required): This field unequivocally specifies the version of the JSON-RPC protocol being utilized, a value that must consistently be "2.0".
*   **`method`** (string, required): This parameter designates the specific remote procedure intended for execution on the JSON-RPC server.
*   **`id`** (number, required): An identifier, established by the client, uniquely associated with the request. This numerical value is crucial for correlating the subsequent response with its originating request.
*   **`params`** (Object, required): A structured value comprising the parameters necessary for the successful invocation of the specified method.

Conversely, a JSON-RPC response, particularly one indicating successful execution, incorporates distinct fields to convey the outcome. While the `jsonrpc` field (string, required, "2.0") is also present for versioning consistency, the pivotal `result` field is structured as follows:
*   **`result`** (string, optional): This member is conditionally present within a response. It is **required** upon successful completion of the method invocation, indicating the data returned by the procedure. Conversely, it **must not** be included if an error occurred during the execution of the method. The ultimate value encapsulated within this member is dynamically determined by the output of the method invoked on the server.

text: Reinforcement learning offers a promising approach for optimizing cache manager decisions, which are critical to the overall performance and efficiency of computer systems. Cache managers are responsible for determining which objects to cache, the duration of caching, and eviction policies when the cache reaches capacity; these decisions directly influence the cache hit rate and the storage resources required. An optimal cache manager seeks to maximize cache hits, minimize unnecessary operations, and use storage efficiently to reduce reliance on slower backend systems. This research explores the application of reinforcement learning by developing three specialized agents, each responsible for a distinct cache manager task, and further examines advanced architectures such as a unified multi-task agent and a multi-agent system suitable for multi-decision environments. A novel framework is introduced to facilitate the abstraction of computer system modeling into reinforcement learning tasks, supporting delayed experiences and flexible scaling to multiple agents. Experimental simulations using a recognized database benchmark demonstrate that reinforcement learning agents not only surpass heuristic algorithms in cache hit rate and space efficiency but also exhibit the ability to adapt to dynamic workloads by adjusting their strategies in real-time. The proposed generic model extends applicability to various cache scenarios, including file system caches, and represents a novel contribution by framing cache management as a multi-task control challenge.

text: This paper introduces SCALoss, a novel loss function designed to improve the accuracy of bounding box regression in object detection tasks. The objective is to enhance the alignment of predicted boxes with ground truth boxes, particularly focusing on the often-ignored side and corner regions. To achieve this, SCALoss employs a unique approach that combines the alignment of sides and corners of bounding boxes, providing a more comprehensive regression loss. The method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in box regression accuracy and overall object detection performance. Key findings show that SCALoss outperforms state-of-the-art loss functions, such as Smooth L1 Loss and IoU Loss, in terms of precision and recall. The proposed loss function has important implications for applications requiring precise object localization, such as autonomous driving, surveillance, and robotics. By highlighting the importance of side and corner alignment, SCALoss contributes to the advancement of object detection research, offering a valuable tool for improving the accuracy of bounding box regression models. text: This paper addresses the challenge of determining stopping criteria in Contrastive Divergence (CD), a widely used algorithm for training Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs). The traditional approach relies on the reconstruction error, which can be misleading and lead to suboptimal model performance. We propose alternative stopping criteria that leverage the underlying principles of CD, including the contrastive divergence objective and the model's log-likelihood. Our approach employs a combination of metrics, such as the log-likelihood of the training data and the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the model's distribution and the empirical data distribution. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed criteria outperform the traditional reconstruction error-based approach, leading to improved model generalization and faster convergence. The contributions of this research include the development of novel stopping criteria for CD, which can be applied to various deep learning models and applications, such as dimensionality reduction, feature learning, and generative modeling. However, their effectiveness remains inferior to that of a transfer learning baseline, which serves as an alternative approach for learning from limited examples. Additionally, in the transfer learning context, although existing SSL methods yield some improvements, the presence of out-of-class data often has a negative impact. In this scenario, the combination of standard fine-tuning followed by distillation-based self-training emerges as the most reliable approach. text: Recent developments in the field of deep learning for 3D data have demonstrated promising potential for end-to-end learning directly from point clouds. In this paper we address this issue by employing a weighted augmentation to increase classes that contain fewer points. By mitigating the class im-balance present in the data we demonstrate that a standard PointNet++ deep neural network can achieve higher performance at inference on validation data. This was observed as an increase of F1 score of 19% and 25% on two test benchmark datasets; ScanNet and Semantic3D respectively where no class im-balance pre-processing had been performed. This paper addresses the challenge of learning graphical models, a fundamental problem in machine learning and probabilistic inference, with a focus on improving efficiency and scalability. We propose a novel approach based on the multiplicative weights update (MWU) method, a widely used optimization technique in theoretical computer science and game theory. Our method leverages MWU to iteratively refine the parameters of graphical models, such as Bayesian networks and Markov random fields, by efficiently balancing exploration and exploitation in the parameter space. The proposed algorithm is designed to handle high-dimensional data and complex dependencies, offering a robust alternative to traditional gradient-based methods. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive performance in terms of accuracy and convergence speed, particularly in scenarios with sparse or noisy data. Furthermore, the method exhibits strong theoretical guarantees, including convergence under mild assumptions. The implications of this work extend to applications in probabilistic reasoning, anomaly detection, and structured prediction, where scalable and accurate graphical models are critical. This research contributes a new perspective on leveraging multiplicative weights for graphical model learning, highlighting its potential as a versatile and efficient tool in modern machine learning pipelines.  

**Keywords**: graphical models, multiplicative weights update, Bayesian networks, Markov random fields, probabilistic inference, machine learning.

text: Short-term traffic forecasting based on deep learning methods, especially long short-term memory (LSTM) neural networks, has received much attention in recent years. However, the potential of deep learning methods in traffic forecasting has not yet fully been exploited in terms of the depth of the model architecture, the spatial scale of the prediction area, and the predictive power of spatial-temporal data. In this paper, a deep stacked bidirectional and unidirectional LSTM (SBU- LSTM) neural network architecture is proposed, which considers both forward and backward dependencies in time series data, to predict network-wide traffic speed. A bidirectional LSTM (BDLSM) layer is exploited to capture spatial features and bidirectional temporal dependencies from historical data. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time that BDLSTMs have been applied as building blocks for a deep architecture model to measure the backward dependency of traffic data for prediction. The proposed model can handle missing values in input data by using a masking mechanism. Further, this scalable model can predict traffic speed for both freeway and complex urban traffic networks. Comparisons with other classical and state-of-the-art models indicate that the proposed SBU-LSTM neural network achieves superior prediction performance for the whole traffic network in both accuracy and robustness.

text: Accurate sales forecasting is essential for E-commerce businesses, but current techniques often rely on univariate methods that only consider historical sales data for a single product. However, when numerous related time series are available, leveraging the past behavior of similar time series can enhance forecast accuracy. The product hierarchy in E-commerce platforms comprises numerous related products with correlated sales demand patterns, prompting our approach to integrate cross-series information into a unified model. To achieve this, we train a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network globally to capture non-linear demand relationships within the product assortment hierarchy. Additionally, we propose a pre-processing framework to address E-commerce challenges and introduce product grouping strategies to support LSTM learning in cases where sales patterns vary across products. Our forecasting framework is empirically evaluated using a real-world dataset from Walmart.com, yielding competitive results at the category and super-departmental levels that surpass state-of-the-art techniques.

text: This paper introduces Deep Distributed Random Samplings (DDRS), a novel approach to supervised learning that challenges the traditional dominance of Random Forests. The objective is to develop an alternative method that can efficiently handle complex datasets and improve predictive accuracy. Our approach employs a distributed framework, where multiple random samplings are performed in parallel, and the results are aggregated using a deep neural network. This methodology enables the capture of intricate relationships between features and targets, leading to enhanced model performance. Experimental results demonstrate that DDRS outperforms Random Forests on several benchmark datasets, achieving higher accuracy and reduced overfitting. The key findings suggest that DDRS can be a viable alternative to Random Forests, offering improved scalability and flexibility. This research contributes to the development of innovative machine learning techniques, with potential applications in areas such as data mining, image classification, and natural language processing. Key keywords: Deep Learning, Distributed Computing, Random Samplings, Supervised Learning, Alternative to Random Forests.

text:
Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) has shown promise in solving complex tasks by decomposing them into manageable subgoals. However, learning effective goal representations remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel approach to learning goal embeddings through self-play, enabling agents to autonomously discover and represent meaningful subgoals in hierarchical tasks. Our method leverages a two-phase training process: first, agents engage in self-play to explore the environment and generate diverse goal-directed behaviors; second, a goal embedding network is trained to encode these behaviors into a compact, actionable representation. We evaluate our approach on a suite of benchmark environments, demonstrating significant improvements in task completion rates and sample efficiency compared to existing HRL methods. The learned embeddings not only enhance the agent's ability to generalize across tasks but also provide interpretable representations of subgoals. Our results highlight the potential of self-play in advancing HRL, offering a scalable and adaptive framework for complex decision-making problems. Key contributions include a robust goal discovery mechanism, improved hierarchical policy learning, and a flexible architecture applicable to diverse domains.  

**Keywords**: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning, Goal Embeddings, Self-Play, Subgoal Discovery, Decision-Making, AI.

**Tóm tắt ngắn gọn:**
Đoạn văn mô tả "Xskt Learn" là một mở rộng tích hợp chặt chẽ với "Scikit Learn" nhằm tăng cường các thuật toán và công cụ học máy.

---

Thư viện Scikit-learn đóng vai trò nền tảng trong lĩnh vực học máy, cung cấp một bộ sưu tập phong phú các thuật toán và công cụ mạnh mẽ cho nhiều tác vụ phân tích dữ liệu (Pedregosa et al., 2011). Tuy nhiên, với sự phát triển liên tục của các phương pháp học máy và nhu cầu ngày càng cao về các giải pháp chuyên biệt, việc mở rộng khả năng của các thư viện hiện có là cần thiết. Nghiên cứu hiện tại giới thiệu **Xskt Learn**, một framework được thiết kế để tích hợp chặt chẽ với Scikit-learn, nhằm bổ sung và mở rộng các thuật toán cũng như công cụ học máy tiên tiến. Sự tích hợp này cho phép **Xskt Learn** tận dụng kiến trúc vững chắc của Scikit-learn, đồng thời cung cấp các chức năng bổ sung phục vụ cho các bài toán phức tạp hơn hoặc các lĩnh vực đặc thù mà Scikit-learn gốc chưa hỗ trợ đầy đủ (ví dụ, Smith et al., 2020). Điều này góp phần nâng cao hiệu quả và phạm vi ứng dụng của các giải pháp học máy.

text: In recent times, with convolutional neural networks achieving significant success across various challenging domains of machine learning, the limitations of manually designed neural networks have become evident due to the substantial cost involved in their creation. Consequently, the automatic generation of network architectures has garnered increasing interest and focus. Some studies on automatically generated networks have shown promising results; however, these primarily focus on selecting a sequence of individual layers, such as convolution or pooling layers, in isolation. Noteworthy and innovative designs exist within meticulously hand-crafted neural networks, including the Inception block in GoogLeNet, the residual block in the residual network, and the dense block in the dense convolutional network. Leveraging reinforcement learning and the strengths of these networks, we propose a novel automatic methodology for designing a multi-block neural network, wherein the architecture incorporates multiple aforementioned block types. This approach aims to facilitate structure learning in deep neural networks and investigate the feasibility of combining different blocks to construct an efficient neural network. The optimal network is developed by a Q-learning agent trained to sequentially select different block types. To validate the efficacy of our proposed method, we employ the auto-generated multi-block neural network for experiments on image benchmark datasets, specifically the MNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR-10 image classification tasks, under restricted computational resources. The experimental outcomes indicate that our method is highly effective, achieving performance that is comparable to, or surpasses, that of manually designed networks and advanced auto-generated neural networks.

Gym-ANM utilizes a model-free RL approach, integrating with popular RL libraries to enable the development and testing of customized RL algorithms. The software includes a range of features, including simulation environments, data analysis tools, and visualization interfaces. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of Gym-ANM in training RL agents to optimize power system performance, with significant improvements in stability and efficiency. The contributions of this research lie in the development of a flexible and accessible platform for power system management, enabling the exploration of innovative RL applications. text: The backpropagation algorithm is widely regarded as essential for training effective feature detectors in the early layers of artificial neural networks, thereby enabling their utility for tasks performed by higher layers of the network. However, the traditional form of backpropagation is biologically implausible. This paper introduces a novel learning rule, possessing a degree of biological plausibility, which is motivated by Hebb's principle of local synaptic plasticity—that is, the modification of synaptic strength based solely on the activities of pre- and post-synaptic neurons. The proposed algorithm utilizes global inhibition in the hidden layer and is capable of learning early-layer feature detectors in a fully unsupervised manner. These learned lower-layer feature detectors can then be used to train subsequent layer weights in a conventional supervised manner, yielding full network performance comparable to that of standard feedforward networks trained end-to-end with the backpropagation algorithm.

text: Multi-task learning, as it is understood nowadays, consists of using one single model to carry out several similar tasks. From classifying hand-written characters of different alphabets to figuring out how to play several Atari games using reinforcement learning, multi-task models have been able to widen their performance range across different tasks, although these tasks are usually of a similar nature. In this work, we attempt to widen this range even further, by including heterogeneous tasks in a single learning procedure. To do so, we firstly formally define a multi-network model, identifying the necessary components and characteristics to allow different adaptations of said model depending on the tasks it is required to fulfill. Secondly, employing the formal definition as a starting point, we develop an illustrative model example consisting of three different tasks (classification, regression and data sampling). The performance of this model implementation is then analyzed, showing its capabilities. Motivated by the results of the analysis, we enumerate a set of open challenges and future research lines over which the full potential of the proposed model definition can be exploited.

text: This paper presents a novel generative model to synthesize fluid simulations from a set of reduced parameters. A convolutional neural network is trained on a collection of discrete, parameterizable fluid simulation velocity fields. Due to the capability of deep learning architectures to learn representative features of the data, our generative model is able to accurately approximate the training data set, while providing plausible interpolated in-betweens. The proposed generative model is optimized for fluids by a novel loss function that guarantees divergence-free velocity fields at all times. In addition, we demonstrate that we can handle complex parameterizations in reduced spaces, and advance simulations in time by integrating in the latent space with a second network. Our method models a wide variety of fluid behaviors, thus enabling applications such as fast construction of simulations, interpolation of fluids with different parameters, time re-sampling, latent space simulations, and compression of fluid simulation data. Reconstructed velocity fields are generated up to 700x faster than re-simulating the data with the underlying CPU solver, while achieving compression rates of up to 1300x.

Chính sách an toàn vĩ mô và ổn định ngân hàng là một trong những vấn đề quan trọng được các quốc gia quan tâm, đặc biệt là Việt Nam. Trong những năm gần đây, Việt Nam đã thực hiện nhiều biện pháp để đảm bảo an toàn vĩ mô và ổn định ngân hàng.

Một trong những biện pháp quan trọng là việc xây dựng và thực hiện các chính sách an toàn vĩ mô. Chính phủ Việt Nam đã ban hành nhiều chính sách nhằm kiểm soát lạm phát, ổn định kinh tế vĩ mô và đảm bảo an toàn cho hệ thống ngân hàng.

Bên cạnh đó, Việt Nam cũng đã thực hiện nhiều biện pháp để tăng cường ổn định ngân hàng. Các ngân hàng thương mại đã được yêu cầu tăng cường quản lý rủi ro, cải thiện hệ thống quản lý và tăng cường giám sát.

Ngoài ra, Việt Nam cũng đã ký kết và thực hiện các thỏa thuận quốc tế nhằm đảm bảo an toàn vĩ mô và ổn định ngân hàng. Các thỏa thuận này đã giúp Việt Nam tăng cường hợp tác quốc tế và đảm bảo an toàn cho hệ thống ngân hàng.

Tổng kết lại, chính sách an toàn vĩ mô và ổn định ngân hàng tại Việt Nam đã được thực hiện một cách hiệu quả. Các biện pháp đã được thực hiện đã giúp đảm bảo an toàn vĩ mô và ổn định ngân hàng, góp phần thúc đẩy sự phát triển kinh tế của đất nước.

text:
This paper introduces Wasserstein Dictionary Learning (WDL), a novel unsupervised framework for non-linear dictionary learning that leverages optimal transport theory. Traditional dictionary learning methods often rely on linear approximations, which can limit their effectiveness in capturing complex data structures. To address this, we propose a non-linear approach that integrates the Wasserstein distance, enabling the model to learn dictionaries that better preserve the geometric and statistical properties of the data. Our method employs an optimal transport-based optimization framework to minimize the Wasserstein distance between the data distribution and the dictionary representation, ensuring robust and interpretable learning outcomes. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that WDL outperforms conventional linear dictionary learning techniques in terms of reconstruction accuracy and feature representation. Furthermore, the proposed framework exhibits superior performance in downstream tasks such as clustering and classification. The key contribution of this work lies in the integration of optimal transport with dictionary learning, offering a new perspective for unsupervised representation learning in high-dimensional and complex data spaces. This research has potential applications in areas such as image processing, natural language processing, and bioinformatics, where capturing non-linear relationships is critical.  

**Keywords**: Wasserstein distance, optimal transport, dictionary learning, unsupervised learning, non-linear representation, feature extraction.

text: This paper proposes a novel method for fuzzy time series forecasting, integrating interval index numbers and membership values with support vector machines (SVMs). The objective is to enhance the accuracy of forecasting by leveraging the strengths of both fuzzy logic and machine learning. The approach involves converting time series data into fuzzy sets, represented by interval index numbers and corresponding membership values, which are then used to train an SVM model. The results show significant improvements in forecasting accuracy compared to traditional methods, with the proposed model demonstrating robust performance across various datasets. The conclusion highlights the potential of this innovative method for applications in finance, economics, and other fields where time series forecasting is crucial. Key contributions include the introduction of a new fuzzy time series representation and the successful integration of SVMs with fuzzy logic, offering a promising direction for future research in forecasting and predictive analytics, with relevant keywords including fuzzy time series, support vector machine, interval index number, membership value, and forecasting accuracy.

text: Furthermore, implementing RFID technology within automated inventory systems in logistics warehouses necessitates the development of robust software solutions capable of efficiently managing large datasets, as each RFID tag is uniquely tied to specific product information stored in the database. This software must facilitate real-time synchronization between the physical presence of goods and their digital records, ensuring data consistency and accuracy for inventory rotation processes. Advanced query and filtering mechanisms should be integrated to enable warehouse personnel to rapidly locate, verify, and update goods’ status or location, thereby streamlining the entire inventory lifecycle. Additionally, the system must incorporate security protocols to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive product information stored both on RFID tags and in backend databases, addressing potential vulnerabilities inherent in wireless communication technologies. Continuous monitoring and logging of all RFID tag interactions are essential for auditability and traceability, allowing for swift identification and rectification of discrepancies, which is critical for maintaining operational efficiency and minimizing losses due to misplacement or theft. Lastly, the scalability of such systems should be considered to accommodate future expansion in warehouse operations, ensuring that inventory management remains responsive and adaptive to evolving logistical demands.

text: Recent advances in deep-learning-based denoisers have demonstrated superior performance over state-of-the-art conventional methods such as BM3D. These denoisers are typically trained to minimize the mean squared error (MSE) between the output of a deep neural network (DNN) and a noiseless ground truth image, necessitating access to high-quality ground truth data for optimal results. However, obtaining noiseless images is often challenging or infeasible in many practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a method for training DNN denoisers using only noisy images with Gaussian noise, leveraging Stein's unbiased risk estimator (SURE). Our SURE-based approach enables the training of DNN denoisers without ground truth data, achieving performance close to that of networks trained with noiseless ground truth for both grayscale and color images. Additionally, we introduce a SURE-based refinement method that utilizes a noisy test image to further enhance denoising performance. This rapid refinement technique consistently outperforms conventional BM3D, deep image prior, and, in many cases, networks trained with ground truth. We also explore the potential extension of our SURE-based methods to the Poisson noise model.
label: human---gpt-text

text: This paper presents a novel approach to object detection using transformer-based architectures. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets. Compared to traditional convolutional neural network-based methods, our transformer-based object detection system exhibits improved robustness to scale and orientation variations. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of a transformer-based architecture for object detection and the demonstration of its potential for real-world applications, such as autonomous driving and surveillance. text: The data layer acts as an intermediary between the application and the database, ensuring that data operations are executed in a consistent and efficient manner. It is responsible for maintaining data integrity through the implementation of constraints and validation rules, which prevent data anomalies and ensure that only valid data is stored. Furthermore, the data layer often incorporates transaction management features to ensure that database operations are atomic, consistent, isolated, and durable (ACID properties). These features facilitate error handling and recovery, thereby enhancing the robustness of the application. Additionally, the data layer may abstract the complexity of the database schema through the use of data access objects (DAOs) or repositories that provide a simplified interface for interacting with the underlying data store. This abstraction enables developers to perform data operations without needing to understand the intricacies of the database management system (DBMS) being used. Moreover, caching mechanisms can be integrated within the data layer to improve performance by reducing the frequency of direct database access, thus decreasing latency and enhancing the user experience. As a result, the data layer is a critical component in the architecture of modern applications, playing a pivotal role in managing how data is stored, accessed, and manipulated.

text: In Neural Machine Translation (NMT), the encoder transforms a source sequence of word embeddings into real-valued vectors (hidden states or contextualized embeddings) within a high-dimensional latent space. This process integrates each token's representation with its context—the surrounding words—enabling the NMT model to condition translations effectively on this context. Common encoder architectures, each with distinct advantages and disadvantages, include Recurrent encoders (e.g., Elman, 1990; Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997) that incorporate preceding tokens, Convolutional encoders (e.g., Kim, 2014) leveraging a local window, and Attention-based encoders (e.g., Vaswani et al., 2017) that weigh the entire input sequence. For instance, the Recurrent encoder preserves token order by processing tokens sequentially from left to right. However, a significant drawback of this approach is its inherent slowness in encoding the input sequence.

We describe how to apply the RL formulation to branch predictors, show that existing predictors can be succinctly expressed in this formulation, and study two RL-based variants of conventional BPs. The proposed RL framework not only offers a powerful and systematic lens for understanding and classifying existing branch predictors, but also unlocks a vast and previously underexplored design space for novel, high-performing architectures. Our preliminary studies on RL-based variants underscore the potential for this approach to enable dynamically adaptive predictors that can learn from program behavior, promising substantial gains in prediction accuracy and efficiency. This work lays the foundation for a new generation of self-optimizing branch predictors, poised to address persistent performance bottlenecks and enhance energy efficiency in future processor designs by minimizing costly misprediction penalties.

text: Graph-based multi-view clustering seeks to partition data across multiple views. While significant progress has been made, effectively fusing diverse view-specific characteristics into a unified representation for clustering remains a key challenge. We propose the Consistent Multiple Graph Embedding Clustering (CMGEC) framework. CMGEC employs a multiple graph auto-encoder (M-GAE) with a multi-graph attention fusion encoder to flexibly capture complementary information from multi-view data. A Multi-view Mutual Information Maximization (MMIM) module preserves intra-view neighborhood similarity within the common representation. Furthermore, a graph fusion network (GFN) explores inter-graph relationships, generating a consensus graph essential for the M-GAE. Jointly training these components yields a common latent representation that encodes richer complementary information and provides a more comprehensive data depiction. Experiments on three multi-view dataset types demonstrate CMGEC outperforms state-of-the-art clustering methods.

text: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have witnessed prevailing success in yielding outstanding images, however, they are burdensome to deploy on resource-constrained devices due to ponderous computational costs and hulking memory usage. Although recent efforts on compressing GANs have acquired remarkable results, they still exist potential model redundancies and can be further compressed. To solve this issue, we propose a novel online multi-granularity distillation (OMGD) scheme to obtain lightweight GANs, which contributes to generating high-fidelity images with low computational demands. We offer the first attempt to popularize single-stage online distillation for GAN-oriented compression, where the progressively promoted teacher generator helps to refine the discriminator-free based student generator. Complementary teacher generators and network layers provide comprehensive and multi-granularity concepts to enhance visual fidelity from diverse dimensions. Experimental results on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that OMGD successes to compress 40x MACs and 82.5X parameters on Pix2Pix and CycleGAN, without loss of image quality. It reveals that OMGD provides a feasible solution for the deployment of real-time image translation on resource-constrained devices. Our code and models are made public at: https://github.com/bytedance/OMGD.

text: Memory-based neural networks process temporal data by retaining information over extended durations. However, their capacity for intricate relational reasoning with stored information remains uncertain. We initially validate the hypothesis that conventional memory architectures may underperform in tasks requiring deep comprehension of entity relationships—specifically those involving relational reasoning. To address these limitations, we introduce a novel memory module—the Relational Memory Core (RMC)—that facilitates memory interactions through multi-head dot product attention. We evaluate the RMC on various tasks benefiting from enhanced relational reasoning in sequential data, demonstrating significant improvements in reinforcement learning (e.g., Mini PacMan), program evaluation, and language modeling. The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on the WikiText-103, Project Gutenberg, and GigaWord datasets.

text: Coordinate-based Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) networks, despite their capability to learn neural implicit representations, generally underperform in internal image synthesis applications; consequently, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are typically employed for a variety of internal generative tasks, albeit at the cost of larger model sizes. We propose Neural Knitwork, an architecture for learning neural implicit representations of natural images that achieves image synthesis by adversarially optimizing the distribution of image patches and enforcing consistency between the patch predictions. To our knowledge, Neural Knitwork is the first coordinate-based MLP implementation specifically tailored for synthesis tasks such as image inpainting, super-resolution, and denoising. We demonstrate the utility of this technique by training it on these three tasks, with results showing that modeling natural images using patches, rather than pixels, produces higher fidelity outcomes. Furthermore, the resulting Neural Knitwork model requires 80% fewer parameters than alternative CNN-based solutions while achieving comparable performance and training time.

text: Real-time segmentation of surgical instruments, essential for robot-assisted surgery, faces challenges from the high computational demands and slow inference of deep learning models. An attention-guided lightweight network (LWANet) addresses these limitations through an efficient encoder-decoder architecture. The encoder utilizes MobileNetV2, while the decoder incorporates depthwise separable convolutions to reduce model size and computational costs, an attention fusion block to capture global contexts and encode semantic dependencies between channels for emphasizing target regions, and transposed convolutions for refining segmentation edges. This design enables LWANet to achieve real-time segmentation with significantly reduced computational overhead, demonstrating an inference speed of 39 frames per second on 960x544 inputs with only 3.39 GFLOPs and a compact model size of 2.06 million parameters. Evaluation on two public datasets, Cata7 and EndoVis 2017, confirms its superior performance, achieving a state-of-the-art 94.10% mean Intersection over Union (IOU) on Cata7 and setting a new record on EndoVis 2017 with a 4.10% improvement in mean IOU.

text:
Title: Self-Consistent Gaussian Process Theory for Finite Deep Neural Networks and Feature Learning  
Abstract (139 words): Deep neural networks (DNNs) in the infinite width/channel limit have received much attention recently, as they provide a clear analytical window to deep learning via mappings to Gaussian Processes (GPs). Despite its theoretical appeal, this viewpoint lacks a crucial ingredient of deep learning in finite DNNs, laying at the heart of their success -- feature learning. Here we consider DNNs trained with noisy gradient descent on a large training set and derive a self consistent Gaussian Process theory accounting for strong finite-DNN and feature learning effects. Applying this to a toy model of a two-layer linear convolutional neural network (CNN) shows good agreement with experiments. We further identify, both analytical and numerically, a sharp transition between a feature learning regime and a lazy learning regime in this model. Strong finite-DNN effects are also derived for a non-linear two-layer fully connected network. Our self consistent theory provides a rich and versatile analytical framework for studying feature learning and other non-lazy effects in finite DNNs.

text: For unsupervised representation learning, supervised evaluation often guides training aspects like data augmentation, which is problematic for real-world unlabeled data. We demonstrate that evaluating learned representations via a self-supervised image rotation task strongly correlates (rank correlation > 0.94) with standard supervised evaluations across diverse settings. Based on this, we propose SelfAugment, an algorithm that automatically and efficiently selects augmentation policies without requiring supervised labels. Our key finding is that augmentation policies learned by SelfAugment achieve comparable performance to those determined through exhaustive supervised evaluations, despite operating entirely without labeled data. This work enables more practical application of unsupervised learning where labels are scarce.

text: Inspired by human vision, we propose a new periphery-fovea multi-resolution driving model that predicts vehicle speed from dash camera videos. The peripheral vision module of the model processes the full video frames in low resolution. Its foveal vision module selects sub-regions and uses high-resolution input from those regions to improve its driving performance. We train the fovea selection module with supervision from driver gaze. We show that adding high-resolution input from predicted human driver gaze locations significantly improves the driving accuracy of the model. Our periphery-fovea multi-resolution model outperforms a uni-resolution periphery-only model that has the same amount of floating-point operations. More importantly, we demonstrate that our driving model achieves a significantly higher performance gain in pedestrian-involved critical situations than in other non-critical situations. These results pave the way for future investigations into refining gaze-informed foveal selection algorithms and exploring the adaptability of such multi-resolution systems to more complex driving scenarios or other visuomotor tasks. Further research could also focus on leveraging this approach to enhance robustness and interpretability in safety-critical autonomous systems, particularly by examining how dynamically allocated high-resolution processing can improve response to unforeseen hazards.

text:
Time series data analysis is a critical component of numerous applications in finance, healthcare, and environmental monitoring. However, preprocessing such data to ensure robustness against noise, outliers, and missing values remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces *tsrobprep*, an R package designed to address these challenges by providing a comprehensive suite of robust preprocessing techniques for time series data. The package integrates advanced methods for outlier detection, imputation, and smoothing, leveraging statistical and machine learning approaches to enhance data quality. Key features include adaptive thresholding for outlier identification, iterative imputation algorithms for handling missing data, and customizable smoothing functions tailored to diverse time series characteristics. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that *tsrobprep* outperforms existing tools in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency, particularly in scenarios with high noise levels or irregular sampling intervals. The package is open-source, user-friendly, and extensible, making it a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners. By improving the reliability of time series preprocessing, *tsrobprep* contributes to more accurate downstream analyses and decision-making processes.  

**Keywords**: time series, robust preprocessing, outlier detection, imputation, smoothing, R package.

text: Authentication Through tx.origin :tx.origin is a Solidity global variable that stores the initial value of the first EOA to perform a transaction. This vulnerability occurs when a contract is used tx.origin to authorize, can lead to a phishing attack. This vulnerability can be fixed by using msg.sender to authenticate instead of tx.origin because msg.sender returns the value of the transaction requestor’s address. The critical distinction lies in their behavior when a transaction is mediated by another contract: while `tx.origin` will always point to the original Externally Owned Account (EOA) that initiated the entire call chain, `msg.sender` refers to the address of the immediately calling entity, which could be another contract. Consequently, an attacker can deploy a malicious contract that, when called by a legitimate user, subsequently calls a vulnerable target contract that relies on `tx.origin` for authorization. In such a scenario, the vulnerable contract's logic would incorrectly attribute the call to the legitimate user's EOA (via `tx.origin`), even though the malicious contract (as `msg.sender`) is the true initiator of the action on its behalf. This allows the attacker's contract to bypass access controls or execute privileged operations without the user's explicit consent for that specific action, illustrating a severe security flaw. Therefore, adhering to the principle of using `msg.sender` for all access control and authorization checks is a fundamental best practice in smart contract development to prevent such reentrancy and phishing-related exploits, as it accurately reflects the immediate caller and thus the true context of the transaction.

text: Triplet Loss là một phương pháp cải tiến so với các hàm mất mát truyền thống, trong đó giá trị đầu ra của mạng thường chỉ được so sánh với ground truth thực tế của dữ liệu. Triplet Loss giới thiệu một công thức mới sử dụng ba giá trị đầu vào: anchor xa, là ảnh đầu ra của mạng; positive xp, là ảnh của cùng một người với anchor; và negative xn, là ảnh của một người khác so với anchor. Trong kiến trúc FaceNet, được minh hoạ ở Hình 3.5, mô hình áp dụng phương pháp học từ đầu đến cuối, sử dụng ZDNet hoặc Inception Network làm nền tảng cơ bản. Để tối ưu hóa số lượng tham số, FaceNet tích hợp thêm các phép chập 1*1. Mô hình này tạo ra các vectơ nhúng hình ảnh f(x) và thực hiện chuẩn hóa L2 cho chúng. Các vectơ nhúng này sau đó được đưa vào hàm mất mát để tính toán tổn thất. Mục tiêu của hàm mất mát là giảm thiểu khoảng cách bình phương giữa các vectơ nhúng của cùng một danh tính (độ tương đồng), đồng thời tăng khoảng cách bình phương giữa các vectơ nhúng của các danh tính khác nhau (độ khác biệt). text: Encoded, or ciphered, manuscripts represent a unique class of historical documents characterized by their encrypted content. Automatically recognizing these documents is particularly challenging due to the variability of cipher alphabets across different manuscripts, the scarcity of annotated datasets for effective training, and the complexity introduced by overlapping symbols that complicate segmentation. To address these challenges, we introduce an innovative approach to handwritten cipher recognition utilizing few-shot object detection techniques. Our approach initially identifies all symbols from a specified alphabet within a line image, after which a decoding process translates symbol similarity scores into the final sequence of transcribed symbols. Through training on synthetically generated data, we demonstrate that our model can accurately recognize handwritten ciphers featuring previously unseen alphabets. Furthermore, when fine-tuned with a small number of labeled pages sharing the same alphabet, our approach outperforms current unsupervised and supervised handwriting text recognition (HTR) methods for ciphers.

text: Multivariate time-series modeling and forecasting is an important problem, but traditional VAR (vector auto-regressive) models and modern RNNs (recurrent neural networks) alone often struggle with combined linear and nonlinear dependencies, leading to poor predictive performance or complex models with large training times. In this work, we propose a hybrid model called R2N2 (Residual RNN), which first models the time series with a simple linear model (like VAR) and then models its residual errors using RNNs. R2N2s can be trained using existing algorithms for VARs and RNNs. Through an extensive empirical evaluation on two real world datasets (aviation and climate domains), we show that R2N2 is competitive, usually better than VAR or RNN, used alone. We also show that R2N2 is faster to train as compared to an RNN, while requiring less number of hidden units. These results imply R2N2's significant potential for efficiently addressing complex time-series problems exhibiting both linear and nonlinear components in future research.

text: A variant of the Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (CGAN) can be employed to train a deep neural network to emulate the outcomes of processing sequences. Prior research indicates that CGAN can enhance performance even for deterministic sequences, characterized by a singular output corresponding to a specific input processing. Counterintuitively, our empirical evaluations employing CGAN on deterministic geophysical processing sequences did not yield a substantive enhancement compared to the application of an L_p loss function; consequently, we herein present an initial theoretical rationale for this observation. Our analytical approach transitions from non-deterministic scenarios to their deterministic counterparts. This investigation culminated in the development of an adversarial methodology for training a content loss, which subsequently demonstrated superior performance on our dataset.

text:
This paper investigates the role of attention mechanisms in generating saliency maps for Atari game-playing agents, introducing a novel approach termed "Free-Lunch Saliency." The objective is to leverage inherent attention layers within deep reinforcement learning models to produce interpretable saliency maps without additional computational overhead. We propose a method that extracts attention weights from transformer-based architectures and visualizes them as saliency maps, providing insights into the decision-making process of the agent. Experiments are conducted on a suite of Atari games using state-of-the-art reinforcement learning frameworks. Results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves comparable or superior interpretability compared to traditional saliency techniques, while maintaining computational efficiency. The findings highlight the potential of attention-based saliency as a lightweight and effective tool for understanding agent behavior in complex environments. This work contributes to the growing field of explainable AI by offering a practical, resource-efficient solution for saliency generation in reinforcement learning systems.  

**Keywords**: Saliency maps, attention mechanisms, reinforcement learning, Atari games, explainable AI, transformer models.

State-of-the-art results on WIDER-Attribute and RAP databases demonstrate its effectiveness. This success suggests future research in robust HAR and refining attention mechanisms.

text: Loãng xương, gây ra các hệ quả gãy xương, là một bệnh chuyển hóa xương phổ biến. Nghiên cứu được thực hiện trên 100 phụ nữ trên 50 tuổi, bao gồm 50 người mắc loãng xương và 50 người không mắc bệnh. Phương pháp nghiên cứu là thiết kế bệnh chứng (Case-control study). Các chất chuyển hóa (metabolites) liên quan đến bệnh được xác định bằng phương pháp định danh không mục tiêu sử dụng hệ thống LC-MS/MS. Chẩn đoán loãng xương dựa trên việc đo MĐX tại hai vị trí: cổ xương đùi (FNBMD) và cột sống lưng (LSBMD), sử dụng kỹ thuật DXA với máy Hologic Horizone. Trong số 166 chất chuyển hóa được định danh, kết quả cho thấy 12 chất có sự khác biệt có ý nghĩa thống kê (p < 0,0001) giữa nhóm loãng xương và nhóm không loãng xương. Cụ thể, hai chất là L-Carnitine và Glycerophosphocholine có liên quan đến MĐX thấp (LSBMD), và một chất liên quan đến việc tăng MĐX (FNBMD); mối liên quan này vẫn duy trì ý nghĩa thống kê sau khi điều chỉnh cho các yếu tố như độ tuổi, BMI và hoạt động thể chất. Kết luận, nghiên cứu này đã bước đầu xác định được một số chỉ dấu chuyển hóa của MĐX, cho thấy tiềm năng hỗ trợ các chỉ số lâm sàng hiện tại trong việc phát hiện sớm và phòng ngừa loãng xương.

text: Moreover, by leveraging the octree structure, IMLSNets efficiently handle varying levels of detail, allowing for adaptive refinement in regions with complex geometry while maintaining coarser representations in simpler areas. This hierarchical approach not only reduces computational overhead but also improves the fidelity of the reconstructed surfaces. We further explore the integration of local priors into the implicit function, which enhances the network's ability to capture fine-grained surface details and preserve sharp features that are often lost in traditional point set representations. Additionally, the decoupling of implicit function evaluation from the neural network inference enables practical applications in real-time scenarios, such as interactive modeling and augmented reality, where rapid surface queries are essential. Future work may investigate extending this framework to handle dynamic scenes and incorporate temporal coherence, as well as to explore more sophisticated priors learned from diverse datasets to generalize across a broader range of shapes and categories. Overall, our approach represents a significant step towards bridging the gap between discrete point sets and continuous surface representations in deep learning, offering a promising direction for high-quality 3D shape generation and reconstruction.

text: Physical modeling method, represented by simulation and visualization of the principles in physics, is introduced in the shape extraction of the active contours. The objectives of adopting this concept are to address the several major difficulties in the application of Active Contours. Primarily, a technique is developed to realize the topological changes of Parametric Active Contours (Snakes). The key strategy is to imitate the process of a balloon expanding and filling in a closed space with several objects. After removing the touched balloon surfaces, the objects can be identified by surrounded remaining balloon surfaces. A burned region swept by Snakes is utilized to trace the contour and to give a criterion for stopping the movement of Snake curve. When the Snakes terminates evolution totally, through ignoring this criterion, it can form a connected area by evolving the Snakes again and continuing the region burning. The contours extracted from the boundaries of the burned area can represent the child snake of each object respectively. Secondly, a novel scheme is designed to solve the problems of leakage of the contour from the large gaps, and the segmentation error in Geometric Active Contours (GAC). It divides the segmentation procedure into two processing stages. By simulating the wave propagating in the isotropic substance at the final stage, it can significantly enhance the effect of image force in GAC based on Level Set and give the satisfied solutions to the two problems. Thirdly, to support the physical models for active contours above, we introduce a general image force field created on a template plane over the image plane. This force is more adaptable to noisy images with complicated geometric shapes.

text:
**Tóm tắt ý chính:**

**Đoạn văn viết lại:**
Phạm vi triển khai của nghiên cứu này được giới hạn trong nội bộ Chi bộ Đảng xã Ngọc Lũ, huyện Bình Lục, tỉnh Hà Nam, nhằm mục tiêu hỗ trợ thực hiện các nhiệm vụ quản lý thông tin đảng viên một cách dễ dàng và thuận lợi hơn. text: Đặt vấn đề: Bệnh hen phế quản (HPQ) ở trẻ nhỏ là một trong những bệnh mạn tính phổ biến, gây tăng gánh nặng cho hệ thống y tế, gia đình và xã hội. Tuy nhiên, hiệu quả của các chương trình tư vấn kiểm soát HPQ dành cho cha/mẹ của trẻ tại bệnh viện chưa được đánh giá toàn diện. Mục tiêu: So sánh sự thay đổi điểm số trung bình về kiến thức và thực hành (KT-TH) của cha/mẹ cùng mức độ kiểm soát HPQ của trẻ trước và sau 6 tháng tư vấn. Phương pháp: Nghiên cứu can thiệp không nhóm chứng được tiến hành trên 98 cha/mẹ của trẻ mắc HPQ, sử dụng bảng câu hỏi tự điền. Để so sánh điểm KT-TH trước và sau 6 tháng tư vấn giáo dục về HPQ, t-test hoặc Wilcoxon signed-rank test dạng bắt cặp được áp dụng. Mối liên quan giữa mức độ kiểm soát HPQ tốt và KT-TH HPQ tốt được ước lượng theo Prevalence Ratio với kiểm định chi-square. Kết quả: Điểm trung bình trong 3 nhóm kiến thức đều được cải thiện sau tư vấn (p<0,001). Tổng điểm kiến thức về bệnh HPQ trung bình trước tư vấn là 21,1 điểm, sau tư vấn tăng thêm 4,6 điểm (22%) (p<0,001). Điểm trung bình thực hành chăm sóc trẻ HPQ sau tư vấn tăng gấp 13 lần so với trước (p<0,001). Tỷ lệ trẻ HPQ được bác sĩ đánh giá kiểm soát bệnh tốt tăng từ 12% trước tư vấn lên 73% sau tư vấn (p<0,001). Có mối liên quan giữa KT-TH tốt và mức độ kiểm soát HPQ ở trẻ: mức độ kiểm soát HPQ tốt cao gấp 1,4 lần ở nhóm có kiến thức tốt và cao gấp 3,2 lần ở nhóm có thực hành tốt. Kết luận: Việc tư vấn - giáo dục sức khỏe hiệu quả trong việc nâng cao KT-TH của cha/mẹ có con bị HPQ, cũng như tăng tỷ lệ trẻ HPQ được kiểm soát tốt sau 6 tháng tư vấn.
