text: Visual explanation enables human to understand the decision making of Deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), but it is insufficient to contribute the performance improvement. In this paper, we focus on the attention map for visual explanation, which represents high response value as the important region in image recognition. This region significantly improves the performance of CNN by introducing an attention mechanism that focuses on a specific region in an image. In this work, we propose Attention Branch Network (ABN), which extends the top-down visual explanation model by introducing a branch structure with an attention mechanism. ABN can be applicable to several image recognition tasks by introducing a branch for attention mechanism and is trainable for the visual explanation and image recognition in end-to-end manner. We evaluate ABN on several image recognition tasks such as image classification, fine-grained recognition, and multiple facial attributes recognition. Experimental results show that ABN can outperform the accuracy of baseline models on these image recognition tasks while generating an attention map for visual explanation. Our code is available at https://github.com/machine-perception-robotics-group/attention_branch_network.

text:
Phồng rộp nền gạch lát sàn là hiện tượng phổ biến trong xây dựng, đặc biệt là ở các khu vực ẩm ướt như nhà tắm, nhà bếp. Hiện tượng này thường xuất hiện do sự kết hợp của các yếu tố như độ ẩm cao, sự chênh lệch nhiệt độ và áp suất không khí.

Nguyên nhân chính của hiện tượng phồng rộp nền gạch lát sàn bao gồm:

- Độ ẩm cao: Nước từ các nguồn như giếng nước, bể bơi, nhà tắm hoặc nhà bếp có thể thấm vào nền gạch, gây ra sự phồng rộp.

- Áp suất không khí: Sự thay đổi áp suất không khí cũng có thể gây ra sự phồng rộp nền gạch.

- Sử dụng vật liệu chịu nước: Sử dụng vật liệu chịu nước như gạch chịu nước hoặc vật liệu xây dựng chuyên dụng để xây dựng nền gạch.

text: Phương án giải quyết a, Xác thực JSON Web Token (JWT) là một chuẩn mở (RFC 7519) định nghĩa một cách nhỏ gọn và khép kín để truyền một cách an toàn thông tin giữa các bên dưới dạng đối tượng JSON. Thông tin này được xác minh và đáng tin cậy vì nó có chứa chữ ký số. Một JWT thường bao gồm ba phần được phân tách bằng dấu chấm: Header, Payload và Signature. Phần Header chứa metadata về token như loại token (JWT) và thuật toán mã hóa chữ ký (ví dụ: HS256, RS256). Phần Payload mang theo các "claims" (khẳng định) về người dùng và các thông tin liên quan khác, chẳng hạn như `iss` (issuer), `exp` (expiration time), `sub` (subject), `aud` (audience). Cuối cùng, phần Signature được tạo ra bằng cách ký lên Header đã mã hóa và Payload đã mã hóa bằng một khóa bí mật (hoặc khóa riêng tư) và thuật toán đã định nghĩa trong Header. Cơ chế này không chỉ đảm bảo tính toàn vẹn và xác thực của dữ liệu mà còn cho phép triển khai xác thực phi trạng thái (stateless authentication), giảm thiểu gánh nặng lưu trữ phiên trên máy chủ và nâng cao khả năng mở rộng của hệ thống.

text: To improve detector generalization in domain adaptive object detection (DAOD), this paper addresses the limitations of existing methods that primarily align feature-level distributions, often neglecting domain-specific information, by focusing on extracting domain-invariant object representations. Our approach introduces a novel disentangled method based on vector decomposition, where an extractor separates domain-invariant representations from the input for object proposal generation. Domain-specific representations are defined as the differences between the input and domain-invariant representations; this difference operation enlarges the gap between them, promoting domain-invariant representations to contain more domain-irrelevant information. Experiments demonstrate significant performance gains over baseline methods in four single-target domain-shift scenes, and for the compound-target case (i.e., the target is a compound of two different domains without domain labels), our method outperforms baselines by around 4%. text: Recent studies have utilized Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) to predict medical images from a single modality, such as generating FLAIR MRI from T1 MRI. Nevertheless, these frameworks are mainly tailored for image-based applications, which restricts their applicability to non-Euclidean data like brain graphs. Although connectomic research has highlighted the potential of incorporating brain graphs in diagnosing neurological disorders, existing geometric deep learning approaches have not been designed to predict multiple target brain graphs from a single source graph. The field of graph generation has gained significant traction in the past two years, but current methods have two major limitations: they typically require learning a separate model for each target domain, limiting their ability to jointly predict multiple domains, and they only consider the global graph structure while neglecting local topological features, such as node centrality. To address these challenges, we propose the MultiGraphGAN architecture, which can predict multiple brain graphs from a single graph while preserving their topological structure. The key contributions of our approach include: (i) developing a graph adversarial auto-encoder for joint prediction of brain graphs, (ii) mitigating the mode collapse issue in GAN by clustering encoded source graphs and using a cluster-specific decoder, and (iii) introducing a topological loss function to ensure the generation of topologically coherent target brain graphs, as shown in Figure A, B, C (References: [citation]). Our MultiGraphGAN demonstrates superior performance compared to its variants, showcasing its potential in generating multi-view brain graphs from a single graph.

This approach not only enhances the accuracy of machine translation systems in capturing subtle linguistic nuances and terminologies unique to particular domains, but also allows for faster inference and easier deployment in real-world applications, such as medical or legal document translation, where both precision and speed are crucial. Furthermore, knowledge distillation can be combined with domain adaptation techniques to further refine translation quality, ensuring that the student model inherits both general language understanding and specialized domain expertise, which is critical for the successful implementation of English-Vietnamese domain-oriented machine translation systems.

Expectation Propagation (EP) is a widely used approximate Bayesian inference method, but its convergence can be slow, limiting its applicability in large-scale or time-sensitive scenarios. This paper addresses the challenge of accelerating EP convergence while maintaining its accuracy and robustness. We propose a novel family of fast convergent algorithms that leverage adaptive step-size optimization and dynamic message scheduling to improve the efficiency of EP. Our approach integrates advanced optimization techniques with probabilistic inference, ensuring faster convergence without compromising the quality of the approximation. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed algorithms achieve up to 40% faster convergence compared to traditional EP methods, while maintaining comparable or superior accuracy. Furthermore, we provide theoretical insights into the conditions under which our algorithms guarantee convergence. The proposed methods are particularly beneficial for applications requiring real-time inference, such as online learning and large-scale Bayesian networks. This work contributes to the broader field of probabilistic machine learning by offering a scalable and efficient solution for approximate Bayesian inference, with potential applications in areas such as computer vision, natural language processing, and decision-making systems.  

**Keywords**: Expectation Propagation, Bayesian Inference, Fast Convergence, Adaptive Optimization, Probabilistic Machine Learning, Real-Time Inference.

text:
Mật mã bất đối xứng là một mô hình mật mã học nền tảng, trong đó mỗi người dùng được cấp một cặp khóa duy nhất bao gồm một khóa bí mật (secret key hay private key) và một khóa công khai (public key). Khóa bí mật được người dùng bảo mật tuyệt đối và chỉ mình họ nắm giữ, trong khi khóa công khai có thể được phổ biến tự do. Thông thường, khóa bí mật được liên kết với thuật toán giải mã và khóa công khai với thuật toán mã hóa, tuy nhiên, điều này không phải là một quy tắc bắt buộc. Trong nghiên cứu này, chúng ta ký hiệu khóa riêng là z và khóa công khai là Z.

Hoạt động cơ bản của hệ thống mật mã bất đối xứng được biểu diễn qua hai hệ thức chính:
1.  $X = D(z, E(Z, X))$ (1)
2.  $X = E(Z, D(z, X))$ (2)

Trong đó, hệ thức (1) minh họa cho bài toán truyền tin mật, một khía cạnh quan trọng của bảo mật thông tin. Bất kỳ người dùng nào khác như B, C, D,... muốn gửi thông tin X một cách bảo mật cho người dùng A, họ chỉ cần mã hóa thông tin đó bằng khóa công khai ($Z_A$) của A rồi gửi đi. Chỉ có người dùng A mới có khả năng sử dụng khóa riêng ($z_A$) của mình để giải mã và truy cập được nội dung thông tin gốc. Điều này đảm bảo rằng các bên không được ủy quyền, chẳng hạn như kẻ nghe trộm Eve, không thể giải mã và thu thập thông tin do không sở hữu khóa $z_A$. Sự phát triển của mật mã bất đối xứng, với những đóng góp tiên phong của Diffie và Hellman (1976) trong trao đổi khóa và Rivest, Shamir, và Adleman (1978) với thuật toán RSA, đã tạo nền tảng vững chắc cho các hệ thống bảo mật hiện đại. Nghiên cứu hiện tại tiếp tục khai thác và mở rộng ứng dụng của các nguyên lý mật mã bất đối xứng để giải quyết các thách thức bảo mật ngày càng phức tạp.

text:
Ranking structured objects, such as graphs, is a fundamental challenge in various domains, including social network analysis, recommendation systems, and bioinformatics. Traditional ranking methods often struggle to capture the complex relationships and dependencies inherent in graph-structured data. This paper introduces a novel approach leveraging Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to rank structured objects effectively. The proposed method employs a GNN-based architecture to learn node and graph-level representations, enabling the model to capture both local and global structural information. We evaluate the approach on multiple benchmark datasets, comparing its performance against state-of-the-art ranking algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate that the GNN-based model consistently outperforms existing methods in terms of ranking accuracy and scalability. The findings highlight the potential of GNNs in addressing ranking challenges for structured data, offering significant improvements in applications such as personalized recommendations and network analysis. This work contributes to advancing the understanding of graph-based ranking and provides a robust framework for future research in this domain.  

**Keywords**: Graph Neural Networks, structured data, ranking algorithms, graph representation learning, recommendation systems.

text:
This paper investigates the design and implementation of autonomous agents with distinct behavioral traits—prosocial and selfish—for contract negotiation scenarios using reinforcement learning (RL). The objective is to explore how varying agent behaviors influence negotiation outcomes, fairness, and efficiency in multi-agent systems. We propose a novel RL-based framework where agents are trained to exhibit either prosocial (cooperative) or selfish (competitive) tendencies, enabling them to adapt their strategies during negotiations. The approach leverages deep Q-learning with reward structures tailored to each behavior type, ensuring agents learn optimal policies aligned with their designated traits. Experimental results demonstrate that prosocial agents achieve higher overall system utility and fairness, while selfish agents maximize individual gains at the expense of collective outcomes. Comparisons with baseline negotiation strategies highlight the effectiveness of the proposed framework in modeling diverse agent behaviors. The findings provide valuable insights into the design of multi-agent systems for real-world applications, such as supply chain management and automated trading, where balancing individual and collective interests is critical. This research contributes to the growing field of AI-driven negotiation by introducing a behavior-aware RL approach that enhances adaptability and realism in agent interactions.  

**Keywords**: reinforcement learning, contract negotiation, prosocial behavior, selfish behavior, multi-agent systems, deep Q-learning, fairness, utility optimization.
label: deepseek-text

text: In any Multiclass Classification (MCC) setting, defined by a labeled point cloud dataset and its associated feature set, we extract stochastic partial orderings from all possible triplets of data points without explicitly measuring their pairwise distances. This collection of partial orderings efficiently constructs a label embedding tree geometry within the label space. This tree, in turn, yields a predictive graph—a network characterized by precisely weighted linkages. These two multiscale geometries collectively represent the coarse-scale information content of MCC. They jointly illuminate explainable insights into the genesis of labels and facilitate robust prediction, potentially supporting multiple candidate labels based on data. To reveal within-label heterogeneity, we further label naturally occurring clusters within each point cloud and similarly derive a complementary multiscale geometry representing its fine-scale information content. This fine-scale analysis demonstrates the scalability of our computational framework to MCC settings with large label spaces. Overall, the computed multiscale collection of data-driven patterns and insights provides a foundation for constructing explainable subject matter intelligence regarding the system of interest.

text: We propose a novel attention gate (AG) model for medical imaging that automatically learns to focus on target structures of varying shapes and sizes, addressing the challenge of highlighting salient features while suppressing irrelevant regions in input images without requiring explicit external tissue/organ localisation modules in cascaded convolutional neural networks (CNNs). AGs can be seamlessly integrated into standard CNN architectures such as U-Net with minimal computational overhead, leading to increased model sensitivity and prediction accuracy. We evaluate the proposed Attention U-Net architecture on two large CT abdominal datasets for multi-class image segmentation, where experimental results demonstrate that AGs consistently enhance the prediction performance of U-Net across different datasets and training sizes while maintaining computational efficiency. The code for the proposed architecture is publicly available. (Word count: 122)

text: This paper explores self-supervised learning of amodal 3D feature representations from RGB and RGB-D posed images and videos, agnostic to object and scene semantic content, and evaluates the resulting scene representations in the downstream tasks of visual correspondence, object tracking, and object detection. The model infers a latent3D representation of the scene in the form of 3D feature points, where each continuous world 3D point is mapped to its corresponding feature vector. The model is trained for contrastive view prediction by rendering 3D feature clouds in queried viewpoints and matching against the 3D feature point cloud predicted from the query view. Notably, the representation can be queried for any 3D location, even if it is not visible from the input view. Our model brings together three powerful ideas of recent exciting research work: 3D feature grids as a neural bottleneck for view prediction, implicit functions for handling resolution limitations of 3D grids, and contrastive learning for unsupervised training of feature representations. We show the resulting 3D visual feature representations effectively scale across objects and scenes, imagine information occluded or missing from the input viewpoints, track objects over time, align semantically related objects in 3D, and improve 3D object detection. We outperform many existing state-of-the-art methods for 3D feature learning and view prediction, which are either limited by 3D grid spatial resolution, do not attempt to build amodal 3D representations, or do not handle combinatorial scene variability due to their non-convolutional bottlenecks.

Thuật toán tối ưu đàn kiến (Ant Colony Algorithm - ACA) mô phỏng hành vi của kiến trong việc tìm đường giữa tổ và nguồn thức ăn. Ban đầu, kiến di chuyển ngẫu nhiên quanh tổ, để lại pheromone đặc trưng trên đường đi, và lượng pheromone này sẽ bay hơi theo thời gian. Các kiến khác cảm nhận pheromone do kiến trước để lại và chọn đi theo những đường có nhiều pheromone, đồng thời tiếp tục để lại pheromone trên đường đi đó. Qua thời gian, pheromone trên các đường ít đi lại sẽ giảm dần, trong khi đường nào được kiến đi nhiều lần (thường là đường ngắn hơn) sẽ có mật độ pheromone cao hơn. Khi đó, xác suất kiến chọn đường ngắn nhất tăng lên, dẫn đến tất cả kiến cuối cùng di chuyển trên đường ngắn nhất.

Thuật toán tối ưu đàn kiến (Ant Colony Algorithm - ACA) dựa trên hành vi tìm đường giữa tổ và nguồn thức ăn của kiến. Ban đầu, kiến di chuyển ngẫu nhiên quanh tổ và để lại pheromone trên đường đi, lượng pheromone này bay hơi theo thời gian. Các kiến tiếp theo sẽ cảm nhận pheromone và ưu tiên đi theo những đường có nhiều pheromone, đồng thời tiếp tục để lại pheromone trên đường di chuyển. Qua thời gian, pheromone trên các đường ít được chọn sẽ giảm, còn trên đường ngắn hơn, pheromone tích tụ nhiều hơn. Do đó, xác suất kiến chọn đường ngắn nhất tăng dần, cuối cùng tất cả kiến sẽ di chuyển trên đường ngắn nhất.

text: Khá nệm về State State trong ReactJS cho phép quản lý các giá trị thay đổi của component trong quá trình chạy. Một State là một đối tượng JavaScript chứa các giá trị mà component sử dụng để hiển thị dữ liệu hoặc cập nhật trạng thái của mình. Khác với props, state là giá trị có thể thay đổi. Khi một state được thay đổi, ReactJS sẽ tự động cập nhật lại giao diện hiển thị của component. State được tạo ra trong phương thức khởi tạo (constructor) của một component. State chỉ thay đổi được bở component chứa nó và không thể thay đổi bởi các component khác. Để thay đổi giá trị của state, developer sử dụng phương thức `this.setState()`. Phương thức này nhận vào một đối tượng chứa các thuộc tính state muốn cập nhật, hoặc một hàm (functional update) để tính toán state mới dựa trên state trước đó. Việc sử dụng `setState()` đảm bảo rằng React có thể tối ưu hóa quá trình cập nhật giao diện bằng cách gộp (batching) nhiều thay đổi state lại thành một lần render duy nhất. Điều quan trọng cần lưu ý là `setState()` là một thao tác bất đồng bộ, nghĩa là các thay đổi state không diễn ra ngay lập tức sau khi gọi hàm. Do đó, developer không nên dựa vào giá trị state ngay sau khi gọi `setState()` mà nên sử dụng hàm callback thứ hai của `setState()` hoặc lifecycle method `componentDidUpdate` nếu cần thực hiện hành động sau khi state được cập nhật hoàn tất. Ngoài ra, việc cập nhật state cần được thực hiện theo nguyên tắc bất biến (immutability), tức là không thay đổi trực tiếp đối tượng state hiện tại mà tạo ra một đối tượng state mới với các giá trị đã cập nhật. Với sự ra đời của React Hooks, cụ thể là `useState` Hook, việc quản lý state trong các functional component trở nên đơn giản và mạnh mẽ hơn, cung cấp một giải pháp thay thế hiệu quả cho `this.state` và `this.setState()` trong class component.

text: Delegate call Injection remains a critical security concern in the realm of smart contract development, particularly due to the inherent trust assumptions embedded in the delegatecall opcode. When a contract employs delegate calls without stringent validation mechanisms, it inadvertently exposes itself to exploitation whereby an adversary could inject malicious code or alter the contract's internal state, leading to severe consequences including financial losses and compromised system integrity. This vulnerability stems from the contract's failure to authenticate the target contract or sanitize the input parameters before delegating control, thereby enabling unintended logic execution within the context of the calling contract's storage. Addressing this issue requires a multifaceted approach: developers must rigorously audit the codebase to identify potential delegate call vectors, implement comprehensive input validation to ensure only trusted contracts are invoked, and enforce robust access controls that restrict delegate call permissions to authorized entities. Furthermore, employing defensive programming patterns, such as limiting the scope of delegate calls and incorporating fail-safe mechanisms, can enhance resilience against such attacks. The adoption of formal verification techniques and automated vulnerability detection tools can also aid in early identification and remediation of delegate call injection flaws. Collectively, these measures contribute to fortifying smart contracts against delegate call injection, thereby enhancing the overall security posture of decentralized applications and safeguarding stakeholders' assets.

text: Recent advancements have drawn greater attention to semi-supervised classification methods that incorporate graph-based information. Emerging learning models now fundamentally depend on classifying data following an initial graph convolution step. To evaluate this approach, we analyze the classification of Gaussian mixtures, where node attributes in a stochastic block model represent the data. Our findings demonstrate that graph convolution enhances linear separability by approximately a factor of 1/D, with D denoting the expected node degree, compared to using the mixture model data alone. Additionally, we observe that the linear classifier derived by minimizing cross-entropy loss post-convolution generalizes effectively to out-of-distribution data, even when the unseen data exhibits varying intra- and inter-class edge probabilities relative to the training set.

Đối với các môn lý luận chính trị ở trường đại học, việc đổi mới kiểm tra - đánh giá theo định hướng phát triển năng lực đã trở thành một yêu cầu cấp thiết.

Mục tiêu của việc đổi mới kiểm tra - đánh giá là giúp học sinh phát triển năng lực tư duy, phân tích, đánh giá và ứng dụng kiến thức vào thực tế. Thay vì chỉ tập trung vào việc nhớ và tái hiện kiến thức, học sinh sẽ được khuyến khích phát triển khả năng tự học, tự nghiên cứu và tự đánh giá.

Để đạt được mục tiêu này, các trường đại học cần thực hiện một số biện pháp đổi mới kiểm tra - đánh giá. Thứ ba, cần tăng cường sự tham gia của học sinh trong quá trình đánh giá, giúp họ trở thành chủ thể của quá trình học tập.

Bằng cách đổi mới kiểm tra - đánh giá theo định hướng phát triển năng lực, các trường đại học có thể giúp học sinh phát triển toàn diện, trở thành những người có khả năng tư duy, sáng tạo và ứng dụng kiến thức vào thực tế. text: Checksum, một phương pháp bảo mật phổ biến, đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc xác thực tính toàn vẹn của dữ liệu truyền tải giữa máy chủ và trình duyệt. Trong hệ thống Lewre, checksum không chỉ đơn thuần là một công cụ bảo vệ mà còn là một phần không thể thiếu của mỗi phản hồi và yêu cầu nhằm đảm bảo rằng dữ liệu không bị giả mạo trong quá trình truyền tải. Khi một yêu cầu hoặc phản hồi được gửi đi, thay vì truyền trực tiếp các giá trị của biến từ trình duyệt, hệ thống Lewre thực hiện một quy trình tạo mã băm từ những giá trị đó. Mã băm này, được tạo ra bằng cách áp dụng thuật toán checksum, sẽ được gửi kèm theo phản hồi đến máy chủ. Quy trình này giúp phát hiện bất kỳ sự can thiệp nào vào dữ liệu, bởi bất kỳ thay đổi nhỏ nào trong dữ liệu gốc đều dẫn đến một mã băm khác biệt hoàn toàn. Việc sử dụng checksum trong hệ thống Lewre không những tăng cường mức độ bảo mật mà còn nâng cao độ tin cậy của hệ thống, đảm bảo rằng dữ liệu nhận được là nguyên vẹn và chưa bị chỉnh sửa. Hơn nữa, việc áp dụng checksum còn giúp giảm nguy cơ tấn công từ các hacker, những người có thể lợi dụng lỗ hổng trong quá trình truyền tải dữ liệu để chèn mã độc hoặc thay đổi thông tin. Mã băm checksum cung cấp một lớp bảo vệ bổ sung, ngăn chặn các tấn công từ chối dịch vụ hoặc các hình thức tấn công mạng khác, bảo vệ không chỉ người dùng mà còn cả hệ thống thông tin của tổ chức. text: The subsequent chapters of this thesis are structured as follows. Chapter 4 investigates the intrinsic properties of the longest run length limited de Bruijn sequence, addressing fundamental inquiries regarding its length, rate, and maximal asymptotic rate. Furthermore, this chapter details methodologies for generating the longest run length limited de Bruijn sequence of order k and for precisely locating the position of each length k sub-string within such a sequence. Combinatorial objects, including binary complementary sequences, Hadamard matrices, and de Bruijn sequences, constitute a primary focus in coding theory. De Bruijn sequences, originally introduced in 1946, have been extensively studied and applied across diverse fields. The distinctive contribution of this thesis lies in its exploration of their novel application for synchronization in quantum communication.

text: In the context of analyzing and designing software to check weld quality using image processing technology and segmentation deep learning, the principle of separation of concerns, as implemented by the MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel) architectural pattern, becomes especially valuable. This modularity not only facilitates independent development and testing of core functionalities—such as preprocessing image data, applying segmentation models, and interpreting output for weld defect classification—but also simplifies future upgrades, such as retraining models on new datasets or enhancing the UI to support additional visualization tools for weld inspection results. Moreover, the clear separation enforced by MVVM allows for more robust unit testing of the data processing and inference logic, which is crucial in high-stakes applications like automated weld quality assurance where precision and reliability are paramount. By adhering to these principles, the software architecture not only supports current requirements but also scales with advances in deep learning techniques and evolving user needs, ensuring the system remains maintainable and adaptable over time.

text:
Video summarization aims to condense lengthy videos into concise, informative summaries, a task that remains challenging due to the complexity of capturing both temporal and semantic dependencies. This paper introduces *Query Twice: Dual Mixture Attention Meta Learning (QT-DMAML)*, a novel framework designed to enhance video summarization by leveraging dual attention mechanisms and meta-learning principles. The proposed approach employs a dual mixture attention module to simultaneously focus on local and global video features, enabling more comprehensive content understanding. Additionally, QT-DMAML integrates meta-learning to adaptively optimize summarization models across diverse video domains, addressing the limitations of traditional methods that struggle with generalization. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that QT-DMAML outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior performance in terms of summarization accuracy and efficiency. The framework’s ability to generalize across varying video types highlights its potential for real-world applications, such as video indexing, surveillance, and content recommendation. This research contributes a robust and adaptive solution to video summarization, paving the way for future advancements in multimedia analysis.  

**Keywords**: Video summarization, dual attention, meta-learning, adaptive optimization, multimedia analysis.

text: This paper re-examines NOTEARS for Bayesian network learning, addressing observed algorithmic behavior. Subsequently, we derive KKT conditions for an equivalent reformulation, proving their necessity and, for convex scores, sufficiency for local minimality. Informed by this, a local search post-processing algorithm is proposed. This algorithm substantially and universally improves all tested algorithms' structural Hamming distance, typically by a factor of 2 or more. Consequently, some combinations are both more accurate and efficient than original NOTEARS, significantly enhancing practical structural learning.

text: Neural architecture search (NAS) enables researchers to automatically explore broad design spaces in order to improve efficiency of neural networks. This efficiency is especially important in the case of on-device deployment, where improvements in accuracy should be balanced out with computational demands of a model. In practice, performance metrics of model are computationally expensive to obtain. Previous work uses a proxy (e.g., number of operations) or a layer-wise measurement of neural network layers to estimate end-to-end hardware performance but the imprecise prediction diminishes the quality of NAS. To address this problem, we propose BRP-NAS, an efficient hardware-aware NAS enabled by an accurate performance predictor-based on graph convolutional network (GCN). What is more, we investigate prediction quality on different metrics and show that sample efficiency of the predictor-based NAS can be improved by considering binary relations of models and an iterative data selection strategy. We show that our proposed method outperforms all prior methods on NAS-Bench-101 and NAS-Bench-201, and that our predictor can consistently learn to extract useful features from the DARTS search space, improving upon the second-order baseline. Finally, to raise awareness of the fact that accurate latency estimation is not a trivial task, we release LatBench -- a latency dataset of NAS-Bench-201 models running on a broad range of devices.

text: We address the problem of automatically learning the main steps to complete a certain task, such as changing a car tire, from a set of narrated instruction videos. The contributions of this paper are three-fold. First, we develop a new unsupervised learning approach that takes advantage of the complementary nature of the input video and the associated narration. The method solves two clustering problems, one in text and one in video, applied one after each other and linked by joint constraints to obtain a single coherent sequence of steps in both modalities. Second, we collect and annotate a new challenging dataset of real-world instruction videos from the Internet. The dataset contains about 800,000 frames for five different tasks that include complex interactions between people and objects, and are captured in a variety of indoor and outdoor settings. Third, we experimentally demonstrate that the proposed method can automatically discover, in an unsupervised manner, the main steps to achieve the task and locate the steps in the input videos.

Đầu tiên, hệ thống cần thiết kế một mô hình dữ liệu hợp lý để lưu trữ thông tin về người dùng, nhóm người dùng cùng các quyền hạn tương ứng. Thông thường, mô hình này bao gồm các bảng như Users, Groups, Roles, Permissions và các bảng liên kết nhằm đảm bảo tính linh hoạt trong việc gán quyền cho từng cá nhân hoặc nhóm. Song song đó, kiến trúc hệ thống phải hỗ trợ kiểm tra quyền truy cập ở cả tầng giao diện người dùng lẫn tầng xử lý nghiệp vụ, nhằm ngăn chặn các truy cập trái phép từ phía người dùng hoặc các tác nhân độc hại. Đối với các hệ thống quy mô lớn, việc xây dựng các chính sách kiểm soát truy cập dựa trên thuộc tính (Attribute-based Access Control - ABAC) hoặc vai trò (Role-based Access Control - RBAC) trở nên phổ biến, giúp đơn giản hóa quá trình quản lý quyền hạn khi số lượng người dùng và chức năng tăng lên nhanh chóng. Ngoài ra, việc tích hợp tính năng ghi nhận lịch sử thao tác (audit log) giúp giám sát và truy vết các hoạt động liên quan đến thay đổi quyền truy cập, từ đó nâng cao tính minh bạch và hỗ trợ quá trình kiểm tra, đánh giá bảo mật hệ thống. Trong bối cảnh các hệ thống phần mềm ngày càng mở rộng và liên kết với nhiều dịch vụ bên ngoài, việc hỗ trợ các tiêu chuẩn xác thực và phân quyền phổ biến như OAuth2, OpenID Connect hay LDAP cũng là một yêu cầu quan trọng, đảm bảo khả năng tương tác và đồng bộ thông tin người dùng giữa các hệ thống khác nhau. text: This paper presents PointNetLK, a novel approach to point cloud registration that leverages the strengths of deep learning and traditional registration methods. The objective is to develop a robust and efficient algorithm for aligning two point clouds, which is a fundamental task in various computer vision and robotics applications. Our approach utilizes the PointNet architecture to learn a compact and informative representation of the point clouds, and then employs the Lucas-Kanade algorithm to iteratively refine the registration. The results demonstrate that PointNetLK outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of registration accuracy and efficiency, especially in the presence of noise, outliers, and partial overlap. The key contributions of this work include the integration of PointNet with the Lucas-Kanade algorithm, and the development of a robust and efficient point cloud registration framework. This research has significant implications for various applications, including 3D reconstruction, object recognition, and robotic mapping. text: Motivated by the simplistic nature of image representations learned from class labels, this paper demonstrates learning transferable image representations without manual annotations by modeling human visual attention. Using a unique gaze tracking dataset of sonographers, a convolutional neural network (CNN) was trained to predict gaze on ultrasound video frames via visual saliency prediction or gaze-point regression. The learned representations were evaluated for transferability to ultrasound standard plane detection through fine-tuning the CNN with limited labeled images and by training a simple softmax regression on feature activations. Fine-tuning the saliency predictor resulted in superior performance over random initialization, with an average F1-score improvement of 9.6% overall and 15.3% for cardiac planes. Moreover, attention models derived strong representations, approaching the precision of a fully-supervised baseline model for all but the last layer. These findings highlight modeling human attention as a promising method for representation learning, suggesting future research should explore its broader applications and refinements, particularly in contexts with scarce labeled data.

text: This paper addresses the issue of limited sample availability in human parsing tasks by employing a self-learning approach, which involves generating pseudo-labels for unlabeled data to fine-tune the model. However, the use of noisy pseudo-labels can lead to error propagation, which is mitigated by proposing a trainable graph reasoning method that leverages the topological structure of the human body to correct two common errors in pseudo-labels: global structural errors and local consistency errors. To rectify global errors, a high-level graph model is constructed from category-wise features, which is then decoupled to reconstruct category features that better capture the human body's topology. Additionally, local errors are reduced by enlarging the receptive field of features, achieved by projecting feature pixels into a local graph model to capture pixel-wise relations, and then reversing the relation information back to the pixels. The integration of global structural and local consistency modules enables the generation of confident pseudo-labels for retraining, as evidenced by extensive experiments on the LIP and ATR datasets, which demonstrate the superiority of our approach over state-of-the-art methods in supervised human parsing tasks, as shown in Figure A, B, C (References: [citation]).

text: A multitude of compression schemes have been devised to address the issue of Deep Neural Networks' (DNNs) excessive size, including the teacher-student approach, which involves transferring knowledge from a complex teacher network to a simpler student network. This paper introduces a novel methodology, termed the teacher-class network, wherein a single teacher network conveys knowledge to multiple student networks, collectively referred to as a class of students. Unlike traditional methods, where knowledge is transferred to a single student for problem-specific logits, the proposed approach enables each student to learn a subset of the teacher's knowledge, represented as a dense representation, allowing the collective knowledge of the student class to be applied to various problems. The student networks are designed to operate within a specified budget, with their combined parameters comparable to, or fewer than, those of a single student in the conventional teacher-student framework, as demonstrated by maintaining the collective parameters of all students less than or equivalent to that of a single student in the teacher-student approach. Furthermore, these compact student networks can be trained independently, facilitating deployment on devices with limited memory and parallel processing systems, such as data centers. The efficacy of the proposed teacher-class architecture is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, including MNIST, FashionMNIST, IMDB Movie Reviews, and CAMVid, across multiple tasks, including classification, sentiment classification, and segmentation, with results indicating that the approach surpasses the state-of-the-art single student method in terms of accuracy and computational cost, often achieving accuracy comparable to the teacher network with 10-30 times fewer parameters.

text:
Sparse graphical models are widely used to represent complex dependencies in high-dimensional data, but their estimation from truncated samples remains a significant challenge. This paper addresses the problem of efficiently estimating sparse graphical models when data is subject to truncation, a common scenario in real-world applications such as sensor networks, genomics, and social network analysis. We propose a novel approach that combines penalized likelihood estimation with a tailored optimization framework to handle the constraints imposed by truncated samples. Our method leverages sparsity-inducing regularization to ensure scalability and robustness in high-dimensional settings. Through extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, we demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of estimation accuracy and computational efficiency. The results highlight the ability of our method to recover the underlying graph structure even under severe truncation, making it a practical tool for applications where data incompleteness is a critical issue. This work contributes to the field by providing a computationally efficient and statistically sound solution for sparse graphical model estimation from truncated samples, with potential applications in diverse domains such as anomaly detection, network inference, and causal discovery.  

**Keywords**: sparse graphical models, truncated data, penalized likelihood, high-dimensional statistics, optimization, network inference.
label: deepseek-text

(6.2) Hệ thống hiển thị giao diện thống kê với các biểu đồ và bảng dữ liệu tổng quan mặc định (ví dụ: thống kê doanh thu theo tháng gần nhất). (6.3) Quản Lý lựa chọn loại thống kê cần xem (ví dụ: thống kê người dùng mới, thống kê giao dịch thành công, thống kê sản phẩm bán chạy) và áp dụng các bộ lọc chi tiết như khoảng thời gian (theo ngày, tuần, tháng, quý, năm), trạng thái hoạt động hoặc các tiêu chí liên quan khác để thu hẹp phạm vi dữ liệu. text:
Image inpainting, the task of reconstructing missing or damaged regions in images, remains a challenging problem in computer vision. This paper introduces **CR-Fill**, a novel generative image inpainting framework that leverages **auxiliary contextual reconstruction** to enhance the quality and coherence of inpainted regions. Unlike traditional methods that rely solely on generative adversarial networks (GANs) or diffusion models, CR-Fill integrates a dual-path architecture that simultaneously predicts missing content and reconstructs the surrounding context. This approach ensures that inpainted regions are not only visually plausible but also semantically consistent with the overall image structure.  

The proposed method employs a **contextual reconstruction module** that extracts and refines high-level features from the input image, guiding the generative process to produce more accurate and realistic results. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including Places2 and CelebA, demonstrate that CR-Fill outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both qualitative and quantitative metrics, such as peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM).  

CR-Fill's key contribution lies in its ability to address common inpainting challenges, such as blurring and artifacts, by explicitly modeling contextual relationships. The framework's versatility makes it suitable for applications in photo editing, medical imaging, and autonomous systems. This work advances the field of image inpainting by introducing a robust and efficient solution that bridges the gap between generative and reconstruction-based approaches.  

**Keywords**: Image inpainting, generative models, contextual reconstruction, GANs, computer vision, deep learning.

The primary actor for this use case is the Customer, with the Application serving as the secondary actor facilitating the interaction. Preconditions for UC03 include the Customer being successfully logged into the system and having navigated to the details page of a desired service, which must have available booking slots. Upon successful completion of this use case, an appointment record (including service, provider, date, and time) is accurately created and stored within the system database, the Customer receives an immediate confirmation of their booking, and the respective Provider is automatically notified of the new appointment. The normal flow of events proceeds as follows: The Customer first selects a desired service from the available list and navigates to its dedicated booking interface. The application then presents a calendar displaying available dates and time slots for that service. The Customer chooses a preferred date and time slot from the presented options, reviews the booking summary to ensure accuracy, and subsequently confirms their selection. The system then performs a real-time validation check for the chosen slot's availability. Upon successful validation, the application securely processes and creates the appointment record, concurrently dispatching a confirmation message to the Customer and a notification to the Provider. Alternative Flow: If the chosen time slot becomes unavailable during the booking process due to simultaneous booking by another user, the application prompts the customer to select another available slot, displaying the updated availability. Exception Flow: In the event of a system error occurring during the critical appointment creation process (e.g., database connection failure), the application displays an appropriate error message to the user, advising them to retry the booking, and logs the incident internally for administrative review and debugging.

text: Similarly, machine learning clustering algorithms analyze the intrinsic properties of data points to identify underlying patterns and group similar instances together without prior knowledge of class labels. Data points that are closer together in this space are assumed to share similar characteristics and are therefore assigned to the same cluster. Common clustering techniques, including K-Means, hierarchical clustering, and DBSCAN, employ distinct methodologies to achieve this grouping, often aiming to maximize intra-cluster similarity while minimizing inter-cluster similarity. The effectiveness of a clustering algorithm is frequently evaluated by metrics that assess the compactness and separation of the resulting clusters, providing valuable insights into the inherent structure of the dataset for various applications, such as anomaly detection, market segmentation, and document analysis.

text: Contemporary contrastive representation learning techniques are fundamentally based on estimating the mutual information (MI) between various perspectives or "views" of an underlying context. For instance, different views of an image can be generated via data augmentation, or a sequence can be divided into views representing its past and future relative to a specific point. Although contrastive lower bounds for MI are straightforward to optimize, they suffer from a substantial underestimation bias when attempting to approximate large amounts of mutual information. To overcome this, we propose breaking down the entire MI estimation problem into a sum of smaller, more tractable estimation problems. This is achieved by partitioning one of the original views into progressively more detailed subviews and then applying the chain rule for mutual information across these decomposed views. The resulting expression is a sum of both unconditional and conditional MI terms, each quantifying only a modest segment of the total MI, which facilitates their approximation using contrastive bounds. To maximize this sum, we formulate an efficiently approximable contrastive lower bound specifically for the conditional MI terms. Our general approach is designated as Decomposed Estimation of Mutual Information (DEMI). We demonstrate that DEMI can capture a greater quantity of MI than standard non-decomposed contrastive bounds in a synthetic environment, and it leads to the learning of improved representations in the vision domain and for dialogue generation.

text: The advancement of socioeconomic conditions has led to an increasing demand for non-material well-being, encompassing aspects such as physical enhancement and healthcare. Consequently, a significant number of contracts pertaining to these domains have been concluded. Evidently, in the event of a contract breach, all parties involved naturally seek the protection of their rights and interests. Therefore, should a contract breach result in non-pecuniary damage (THVTT), liability for compensation for such THVTT is established pursuant to Điều 419 Bộ luật Dân sự (BLDS) năm 2015. However, Vietnamese contract law exhibits several inadequacies concerning liability for compensating THVTT arising from contract breaches, specifically regarding: i) the circumstances warranting such compensation; ii) the quantum of compensation; and iii) the modalities of compensation. Consequently, this article undertakes an analysis of international experiences pertaining to liability for compensating THVTT due to contract breaches, juxtaposing them with Vietnamese legal provisions and judicial precedents. This comparative approach aims to contribute to the refinement of relevant legislation and enhance the efficacy of its practical implementation within the country.

Tóm tắt ý chính:
Khi triển khai hệ thống thực tế, việc sử dụng giao thức HTTPS là bắt buộc để đảm bảo giao tiếp an toàn giữa server và client, cho phép trao đổi thông tin bảo mật trên Internet.

Đoạn văn viết lại:
Trong bối cảnh các ứng dụng web ngày càng phức tạp và xử lý lượng lớn dữ liệu nhạy cảm, việc đảm bảo an toàn thông tin trong quá trình truyền tải giữa máy chủ (server) và máy khách (client) trở thành một yêu cầu tiên quyết. Đối với các hệ thống triển khai trong môi trường thực tế, giao thức truyền tải siêu văn bản an toàn (HTTPS) đóng vai trò then chốt, thiết lập một kênh liên lạc mã hóa nhằm bảo vệ tính bí mật và toàn vẹn của dữ liệu trao đổi qua mạng Internet (Rescorla, 2001; Fielding et al., 1999). Việc áp dụng HTTPS không chỉ ngăn chặn hiệu quả các hình thức tấn công nghe lén (eavesdropping) hay tấn công xen giữa (man-in-the-middle) mà còn góp phần xây dựng niềm tin cho người dùng cuối. Nghiên cứu này, trong quá trình phát triển và triển khai hệ thống [Tên hệ thống/ứng dụng cụ thể của nghiên cứu], đã tuân thủ nghiêm ngặt việc sử dụng HTTPS, qua đó đóng góp vào việc xây dựng một giải pháp không chỉ đáp ứng yêu cầu chức năng mà còn đảm bảo các tiêu chuẩn an ninh mạng hiện hành, tạo tiền đề cho việc vận hành ổn định và bảo mật trong thực tiễn.

text: This paper proposes a novel approach to video summarization by transforming multi-concept attention into a concise and informative summary. The objective is to address the challenge of effectively capturing key concepts in videos and representing them in a condensed form. Our method employs a deep learning-based model that integrates multi-concept attention mechanisms to identify and weigh important frames in a video. The approach utilizes a transformer-based architecture to learn contextual relationships between frames and concepts, enabling the model to generate summaries that balance relevance and diversity. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming state-of-the-art video summarization methods in terms of summary quality and user engagement. The key contributions of this research include the introduction of a multi-concept attention framework for video summarization and the demonstration of its potential to improve summary accuracy and user experience. This work has significant implications for applications such as video analysis, content creation, and media consumption, and highlights the importance of attention mechanisms in video understanding. Key keywords: video summarization, multi-concept attention, transformer, deep learning, attention mechanisms.

text: Delay-based netcode constitutes an extension of the simpler, classic "Lockstep" synchronization model. Within the Lockstep paradigm, game progression is paused until all necessary inputs are collected from connected clients. This mechanism is frequently implemented in turn-based games, where the strategic nature of gameplay provides ample time for player deliberation, rendering a half-second delay largely unnoticeable. However, to successfully apply Lockstep netcode to real-time genres like fighting games, the incorporation of input latency is essential. Input latency purposefully introduces a delay between a player's inputs and their corresponding in-game actions, ensuring that both players have received the other's input prior to simulation advancement. The outcome of this approach is the consistent synchronization of all local game versions. The integration of the Lockstep model with input latency is broadly termed "Delay-Based Networking," a technique employed for decades in various video games, notably "Age of Empires." This approach is appealing due to its straightforward implementation, often requiring minimal alterations to the core game loop. Nevertheless, Delay-Based Networking inherently sacrifices responsiveness and flexibility. Significant spikes or variances in network latency, typically indicative of a poor connection, can cause the game to pause extensively as it awaits the complete reception of all inputs.
label: gemini-text

text: Building upon Nakamoto’s foundational work, the integration of smart contracts and decentralized applications has further expanded the potential of blockchain technology. Smart contracts, which are self-executing contracts with the terms directly written into code, enable automated, trustless transactions without intermediaries, thereby reducing costs and increasing efficiency. In the context of decentralized video sharing platforms, leveraging smart contracts facilitates transparent content distribution, fair compensation for creators, and enhanced user control over data privacy. By utilizing Eueno, a decentralized framework that supports peer-to-peer interactions and content sharing, the system can ensure that video content is distributed in a censorship-resistant manner, mitigating concerns related to centralized hosting vulnerabilities and content monopolization. Moreover, the immutability and transparency of blockchain ledgers help verify content authenticity and track usage metrics in real-time, fostering a more equitable ecosystem for both creators and consumers. This approach addresses critical challenges faced by traditional video sharing websites, such as data ownership, revenue distribution, and content moderation biases. Consequently, the fusion of distributed ledger technology with smart contracts and decentralized platforms paves the way for innovative, user-centric solutions that promote openness, security, and fairness across digital content sharing landscapes.

text: Furthermore, our method allows for enhanced interpretability of the learned latent spaces, as the separation between invariant and equivariant factors facilitates targeted manipulation and analysis of each component individually. By disentangling class-specific information from within-class variability, we enable downstream tasks such as data augmentation, class-conditional generation, and transfer learning to be performed with greater control and efficacy. Experimental results indicate that the invariant representations cluster distinctly according to class labels, while the equivariant representations systematically capture variations attributable to transformations within each class, as evidenced by visualizations provided in Figure A and Figure B. Additionally, ablation studies confirm the necessity of maintaining both latent pathways for optimal performance, with model variants lacking either component exhibiting reduced accuracy and less meaningful latent structure. These findings underscore the flexibility and robustness of our approach, suggesting its potential utility for a broad range of applications where interpretability and adaptability of learned representations are paramount.

text: This study aims to investigate the differences between Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Independent Component Analysis (ICA) from a data distribution perspective. PCA and ICA are widely used dimensionality reduction techniques in data analysis, but they have distinct approaches to extracting meaningful features. Our approach involves applying both PCA and ICA to various datasets and comparing the resulting component distributions. The results show that ICA is more effective in capturing non-Gaussian and independent components, whereas PCA is better suited for Gaussian data distributions. Our findings indicate that the choice of technique depends on the underlying data structure, and selecting the appropriate method can significantly impact the accuracy of subsequent analyses. This research contributes to the understanding of PCA and ICA by highlighting their strengths and limitations, providing valuable insights for data analysts and researchers. Key keywords: PCA, ICA, dimensionality reduction, data distribution, feature extraction, data analysis.

text: Progress in generative modelling, especially generative adversarial networks, have made it possible to efficiently synthesize and alter media at scale. Malicious individuals now rely on these machine-generated media, or deepfakes, to manipulate social discourse. In order to ensure media authenticity, existing research is focused on deepfake detection. Yet, the adversarial nature of frameworks used for generative modeling suggests that progress towards detecting deepfakes will enable more realistic deepfake generation. Therefore, it comes at no surprise that developers of generative models are under the scrutiny of stakeholders dealing with misinformation campaigns. At the same time, generative models have a lot of positive applications. As such, there is a clear need to develop tools that ensure the transparent use of generative modeling, while minimizing the harm caused by malicious applications.   Our technique optimizes over the source of entropy of each generative model to probabilistically attribute a deepfake to one of the models. We evaluate our method on the seminal example of face synthesis, demonstrating that our approach achieves 97.62% attribution accuracy, and is less sensitive to perturbations and adversarial examples. We discuss the ethical implications of our work, identify where our technique can be used, and highlight that a more meaningful legislative framework is required for a more transparent and ethical use of generative modeling. Finally, we argue that model developers should be capable of claiming plausible deniability and propose a second framework to do so -- this allows a model developer to produce evidence that they did not produce media that they are being accused of having produced.

text: Tình trạng xói lở bãi và sạt lở bờ biển đã và đang diễn ra khá phổ biến ở nhiều khu vực vùng ven biển các tỉnh đồng bằng sông Cửu Long (ĐBSCL), trong đó vùng ven biển thuộc bán đảo Cà Mau (BĐCM) là một trong những khu vực có tình trạng xói lở khá nghiêm trọng. text: User data confidentiality poses a significant challenge for conventional data-driven model compression, risking performance degradation without data. Current data-free image generation methods, relying on biased feature statistics and inexact low-to-high dimension inversion, suffer from poor generalizability and unsatisfactory performance. To address these limitations, we propose MixMix, based on two simple yet effective techniques: Feature Mixing, which constructs a universal feature space from various models for generalized inversion; and Data Mixing, which combines synthesized images and labels for exact label information. We theoretically and empirically prove MixMix's effectiveness. Extensive experiments show MixMix significantly outperforms existing data-free compression methods on mainstream tasks including quantization, knowledge distillation, and pruning, achieving up to 4% and 20% accuracy uplift on quantization and pruning, respectively. This work provides a robust solution for data-free model compression, enhancing both generalizability and accuracy.

text: The registration of 3D point clouds remains a formidable challenge, particularly when dealing with partial correspondences and the absence of initial estimation information, which complicates the determination of the rigid transformation between two point clouds. To address this issue, this paper proposes a comprehensive deep-learning-based approach for point cloud registration. The methodology involves the utilization of a revised LPD-Net for feature extraction and aggregation via a graph network, followed by the application of self-attention and cross-attention mechanisms to enhance structural and corresponding information between the two input point clouds. The approach then generates virtual corresponding points using a soft pointer-based method and ultimately resolves the registration problem through the implementation of the SVD method. The efficacy of the proposed approach is demonstrated through comparative results on the ModelNet40 dataset, which indicate state-of-the-art performance in point cloud registration tasks, and experimental results on the KITTI dataset, which validate its effectiveness in real-world applications, with the source code available at \url.

text: Deep person re-identification (re-ID) methods predominantly focus on CNN architectures, neglecting loss functions. Current verification and identification losses have limitations: verification loss suffers slow convergence and instability with large datasets, while identification loss overlooks explicit intra-class variance reduction. To address these issues, we propose the support neighbor (SN) loss, which utilizes positive and negative support neighbor sets for richer contextual information and stable performance. We formulate a softmax-like function for scalability and separability, and penalize the distance between the anchor's nearest positive and furthest positive samples to reduce intra-class variance. Integrated with Resnet50, SN loss achieves superior re-ID results compared to state-of-the-art methods on several datasets. This novel loss function offers a promising direction for future research in designing more robust and high-performing deep re-ID systems by focusing on neighborhood structure in loss design.

text:
Person re-identification (Re-ID) is a critical task in computer vision, aiming to match individuals across non-overlapping camera views. Despite significant progress, existing methods often struggle with intra-class variations and inter-class similarities, limiting their effectiveness. This paper introduces **Cluster Loss**, a novel loss function designed to enhance feature discrimination and clustering in person Re-ID. Unlike traditional triplet or contrastive losses, Cluster Loss leverages the inherent structure of feature clusters to optimize both intra-class compactness and inter-class separation. We propose a deep learning framework that integrates Cluster Loss with a convolutional neural network (CNN) backbone, enabling end-to-end training. Experiments on benchmark datasets, including Market-1501 and DukeMTMC-reID, demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods in terms of rank-1 accuracy and mean average precision (mAP). The results highlight the effectiveness of Cluster Loss in improving feature representation for person Re-ID. This work contributes a robust and scalable solution to the Re-ID problem, with potential applications in surveillance, security, and video analytics.  

**Keywords**: Person re-identification, Cluster Loss, feature discrimination, deep learning, computer vision, CNN.

text:
Reinforcement Learning (RL) has shown significant promise in solving complex decision-making tasks, yet challenges remain in scenarios where rewards are delayed, making it difficult to establish effective learning policies. This paper addresses the problem of off-policy reinforcement learning in environments with delayed rewards, aiming to improve the efficiency and stability of learning algorithms under such conditions. We propose a novel approach that integrates temporal difference learning with reward redistribution mechanisms to better align delayed rewards with the actions that caused them. Our method leverages a combination of experience replay and prioritized sampling to enhance the learning process, ensuring that critical experiences are revisited and learned from effectively. Experimental results on benchmark environments demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing off-policy RL methods in terms of convergence speed and final performance, particularly in tasks with sparse and delayed rewards. The proposed framework provides a robust solution for real-world applications where reward signals are inherently delayed, such as robotics, healthcare, and financial systems. This work contributes to advancing RL methodologies by addressing a critical limitation in reward handling, offering a scalable and efficient solution for delayed reward scenarios.  

**Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Off-Policy Learning, Delayed Rewards, Temporal Difference Learning, Reward Redistribution, Experience Replay.

The findings demonstrate that RETAIN surpasses the random forest and matches the LSTM network in both standard accuracy measures and clinical relevance metrics, establishing its validity for glucose prediction. Additionally, we introduce methods to leverage RETAIN's interpretability, which provides valuable insights for both patients and healthcare providers, facilitating better comprehension of model predictions and informing the development of future glucose forecasting systems.

text: In dynamic environments, agents possessing a restricted field of view or limited resources are unable to fully observe a scene prior to its analysis, making the deployment of conventional semantic segmentation architectures impractical. This paper presents a method for progressively segmenting a scene using a sequence of partial observations. The fundamental principle is to refine an agent's comprehension of its surroundings by concentrating on areas where its uncertainty is highest. Our approach incorporates a self-supervised attention mechanism and a specialized architecture designed to maintain and exploit spatial memory maps for inferring unseen areas within the environment. The agent can selectively attend to specific regions, utilizing cues from previously visited locations to reconstruct other parts. We achieved mean pixel-wise accuracies of 78.1%, 80.9%, and 76.5% on the CityScapes, CamVid, and Kitti datasets, respectively, by processing only 18% of the image pixels via 10 retina-like glimpses. An ablation study was conducted to investigate the influence of the number of glimpses, input image size, and the effectiveness of retina-like glimpses. Our method was compared against several baselines, demonstrating that optimal results are obtained when a very low-resolution view of the scene is available at the first timestep.

text: Bladder cancer (BC) is a prevalent malignant pathology within the genitourinary system. With continuous advancements in imaging diagnostics and functional exploration, bladder cancer is increasingly diagnosed early and accurately. This study aims to describe the imaging characteristics of bladder cancer on computed tomography (CT). Methodology: A retrospective study was conducted on 194 BC patients who underwent surgical treatment at Binh Dan Hospital from January 2020 to the end of June 2020. Pre-operative CT scans of 16 or 64 slices were performed. Results: BC frequently occurs on the lateral and posterior walls, typically manifesting as polypoid tumors with narrow pedicles in 84% of cases. The average tumor size was 30.7 ± 18.1 mm, with tumors measuring 11 - 50mm accounting for 71.7%. Bladder tumors are often detected during the arterial phase alone or in combination with the venous and excretory phases, characterized by strong enhancement (70%) and the formation of filling defects in the excretory phase.

text: Recent advances in self-supervised learning (SSL) have largely closed the gap with supervised ImageNet pretraining. Despite their success these methods have been primarily applied to unlabeled ImageNet images, and show marginal gains when trained on larger sets of uncurated images. We hypothesize that current SSL methods perform best on iconic images, and struggle on complex scene images with many objects. Analyzing contrastive SSL methods shows that they have poor visual grounding and receive poor supervisory signal when trained on scene images. We propose Contrastive Attention-Supervised Tuning(CAST) to overcome these limitations. CAST uses unsupervised saliency maps to intelligently sample crops, and to provide grounding supervision via a Grad-CAM attention loss. Experiments on COCO show that CAST significantly improves the features learned by SSL methods on scene images, and further experiments show that CAST-trained models are more robust to changes in backgrounds.

Video classification at scale remains a challenging task due to the complexity of processing large volumes of frame-level features while maintaining computational efficiency. This paper introduces **NeXtVLAD**, a novel neural network architecture designed to efficiently aggregate frame-level features for large-scale video classification. The proposed model addresses the limitations of traditional approaches by leveraging a lightweight yet powerful feature aggregation mechanism, which reduces computational overhead without compromising accuracy. NeXtVLAD employs a hierarchical structure to capture both local and global temporal dependencies, enabling robust representation learning across diverse video datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that NeXtVLAD achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets, outperforming existing methods in terms of both accuracy and inference speed. Furthermore, the model's scalability and efficiency make it suitable for real-world applications, such as video recommendation systems and content-based retrieval. This work contributes a significant advancement in video understanding by providing a computationally efficient solution for large-scale video classification tasks.  

**Keywords**: Video classification, feature aggregation, neural networks, large-scale datasets, computational efficiency, NeXtVLAD.

Additionally, MySQL’s native security features, though adequate for many applications, lack some of the advanced auditing and encryption capabilities necessary for highly sensitive data typical in large enterprises. This means that organizations with stringent compliance requirements might find MySQL insufficient without significant customization or supplementary tools. Additionally, users need to ensure that they have the appropriate resources and knowledge to use it effectively. Effective MySQL deployment requires skilled database administrators who can optimize query performance, manage backups, and configure replication or clustering setups to ensure high availability. Without proper expertise, the risk of suboptimal performance, data loss, or security breaches increases, which can be detrimental to the sales staff management system’s reliability and integrity. text:
Pose-guided person image synthesis is a challenging task in computer vision, aiming to generate realistic images of a person in a target pose while preserving their appearance. This paper introduces Soft-Gated Warping-GAN, a novel generative adversarial network (GAN) framework designed to address key limitations in existing methods. The proposed approach leverages a soft-gated warping mechanism to dynamically align source and target poses, ensuring high-fidelity image synthesis with minimal artifacts. The framework integrates a multi-scale discriminator to enhance texture details and spatial consistency, while a pose-aware feature extraction module captures fine-grained pose and appearance information. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that Soft-Gated Warping-GAN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of visual quality, structural accuracy, and pose alignment. The model achieves significant improvements in both quantitative metrics and qualitative evaluations, showcasing its ability to handle complex pose variations and occlusions. This work contributes to advancing pose-guided image synthesis, with potential applications in virtual try-on, animation, and augmented reality.  

**Keywords**: Pose-guided image synthesis, GAN, soft-gated warping, person image generation, computer vision, deep learning.

text:
Deep Metric Learning (DML) has emerged as a powerful approach for learning semantic similarity in high-dimensional data, particularly in applications such as image retrieval, clustering, and classification. However, the lack of interpretability in DML models poses a significant challenge, limiting their adoption in critical domains where transparency is essential. This paper addresses the problem of providing visual explanations for DML models to enhance their interpretability and trustworthiness. We propose a novel framework that integrates gradient-based visualization techniques with DML architectures to generate intuitive visual explanations of similarity metrics learned by the model. Our approach leverages class activation maps and feature attribution methods to highlight regions of input data that contribute most to the learned embeddings. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework not only maintains competitive performance in terms of retrieval accuracy but also provides meaningful insights into the decision-making process of DML models. The results show significant improvements in interpretability without compromising model efficiency. This work contributes to bridging the gap between model performance and explainability in DML, paving the way for its broader application in domains requiring both accuracy and transparency.  

**Keywords**: Deep Metric Learning, Visual Explanation, Interpretability, Feature Attribution, Image Retrieval, Explainable AI.

text: This paper presents a novel approach for vehicle trajectory prediction utilizing graphical representations. Vehicles are represented as Gaussian distributions within a Bird's-Eye View (BEV) perspective, and a U-Net architecture performs sequence-to-sequence prediction of future scene states. The task is formulated as image-to-image regression, wherein the network learns underlying spatiotemporal relationships among traffic participants. The approach thereby generates an estimation of future scene appearance, rather than explicit numerical trajectories. A dedicated post-processing step subsequently extracts vehicle positions from this predicted graphical representation at subpixel resolution. Evaluation of various network configurations demonstrates prediction errors, for horizons up to three seconds, on the order of the graphical representation's resolution. text: The benefits of using the natural gradient are well known in a wide range of optimization problems. However, for the training of common neural networks the resulting increase in computational complexity sets a limitation to its practical application. Helmholtz Machines are a particular type of generative model composed of two Sigmoid Belief Networks (SBNs), acting as an encoder and a decoder, commonly trained using the Wake-Sleep (WS) algorithm and its reweighted version RWS. For SBNs, it has been shown how the locality of the connections in the graphical structure induces sparsity in the Fisher information matrix. The resulting block diagonal structure can be efficiently exploited to reduce the computational complexity of the Fisher matrix inversion and thus compute the natural gradient exactly, without the need of approximations. We present a geometric adaptation of well-known methods from the literature, introducing the Natural Wake-Sleep (NWS) and the Natural Reweighted Wake-Sleep (NRWS) algorithms. text: For the deployment of deep learning models in production environments, it is imperative that the models exhibit both high accuracy and compactness to satisfy latency and memory constraints. This requirement typically leads to architectures that are deep to ensure performance while remaining thin to enhance computational efficiency. In this study, we introduce an efficient training methodology for deep thin networks, accompanied by a theoretical guarantee. Our approach is inspired by model compression techniques and involves three stages. Initially, we substantially widen the deep thin network and train it to convergence. Subsequently, the well-trained deep wide network is employed to warm up or initialize the original deep thin network through layerwise imitation, wherein the thin network is compelled to replicate the intermediate outputs of the wide network at each layer. Finally, the pre-initialized deep thin network undergoes further fine-tuning. The theoretical assurance is derived from neural mean field analysis, which substantiates the superiority of our layerwise imitation strategy compared to conventional backpropagation. Comprehensive large-scale empirical evaluations corroborate the efficacy of the proposed method, demonstrating that ResNet50 trained via our approach surpasses ResNet101, and BERT Base achieves performance comparable with BERT Large when the latter models are trained using standard procedures documented in the literature.

text: For safety-critical applications such as autonomous driving, CNNs have to be robust with respect to unavoidable image corruptions, such as image noise. While previous works addressed the task of robust prediction in the context of full-image classification, we consider it for dense semantic segmentation. We build upon an insight from image classification that output robustness can be improved by increasing the network-bias towards object shapes. We present a new training schema that increases this shape bias. Our basic idea is to alpha-blend a portion of the RGB training images with faked images, where each class-label is given a fixed, randomly chosen color that is not likely to appear in real imagery. This forces the network to rely more strongly on shape cues. We call this data augmentation technique ``Painting-by-Numbers''. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our training schema for DeepLabv3+ with various network backbones, MobileNet-V2, ResNets, and Xception, and evaluate it on the Cityscapes dataset. With respect to our 16 different types of image corruptions and 5 different network backbones, we are in 74% better than training with clean data. For cases where we are worse than a model trained without our training schema, it is mostly only marginally worse. However, for some image corruptions such as images with noise, we see a considerable performance gain of up to 25%.

text: Temporal super-resolution depth imaging for fast-moving scenes using coded patterns overcomes the challenge of acquiring accurate 3D information from rapidly moving objects, where conventional static pattern projection leads to motion blur and reconstruction failure. Each captured image thus subtly encodes temporal variations reflective of the object's depth and motion. A learning-based decoding framework then extracts this embedded temporal information, enabling the reconstruction of high-temporal-resolution depth sequences from a single image without requiring geometric calibration. Experimental validation confirms the method's effectiveness, successfully recovering sequential object shapes from individual exposures. text: Referring Expression Comprehension (REC) is an emerging research spot in computer vision, which refers to detecting the target region in an image given an text description. Most existing REC methods follow a multi-stage pipeline, which are computationally expensive and greatly limit the application of REC. In this paper, we propose a one-stage model towards real-time REC, termed Real-time Global Inference Network (RealGIN). RealGIN addresses the diversity and complexity issues in REC with two innovative designs: the Adaptive Feature Selection (AFS) and the Global Attentive ReAsoNing unit (GARAN). AFS adaptively fuses features at different semantic levels to handle the varying content of expressions. GARAN uses the textual feature as a pivot to collect expression-related visual information from all regions, and thenselectively diffuse such information back to all regions, which provides sufficient context for modeling the complex linguistic conditions in expressions. On five benchmark datasets, i.e., RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg, ReferIt and Flickr30k, the proposed RealGIN outperforms most prior works and achieves very competitive performances against the most advanced method, i.e., MAttNet. Most importantly, under the same hardware, RealGIN can boost the processing speed by about 10 times over the existing methods.
