text: Other UDA techniques focus on transferring the source domain's style to the target domain. These methods aim to reduce the domain gap between source and target domains by translating source images to mimic the style of the target domain. Yang and Soatto observed that the Fourier transform simplifies the retrieval of comparable information for domain adaptation. In their Fourier Domain Adaptation (FDA) method, frequency responses of both source and target images are first computed, and then the low frequencies from the source image are replaced with those from the target image. Subsequently, training is conducted using these stylised visuals. The FDA technique outperforms earlier style-based approaches, and its adaptation performance is further enhanced when combined with self-supervision. CyCADA was among the earliest methods to directly add style to images. This method combines style transfer with adversarial domain adaptation. The styling procedure utilizes the adversarial image translation model CycleGAN to facilitate bi-directional image translation between source and target domains. The models are trained using a combination of an adversarial loss (facilitated by a discriminator), a cycle consistency loss, and a semantic consistency loss. The discriminator aims to differentiate between real target images and source images translated to the target domain style.

text: Due to the vulnerability of deep neural networks to adversarial examples, numerous works on adversarial attacks and defenses have been burgeoning over the past several years. However, there seem to be some conventional views regarding adversarial attacks and object detection approaches that most researchers take for granted. In this work, we bring a fresh perspective on those procedures by evaluating the impact of universal perturbations on object detection at a class-level. We apply it to a carefully curated data set related to autonomous driving. We use Faster-RCNN object detector on images of five different categories: person, car, truck, stop sign and traffic light from the COCO data set, while carefully perturbing the images using Universal Dense Object Suppression algorithm. Our results indicate that person, car, traffic light, truck and stop sign are resilient in that order (most to least) to universal perturbations. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time such a ranking has been established which is significant for the security of the data sets pertaining to autonomous vehicles and object detection in general.

Hơn nữa, Eloquent ORM (Object-Relational Mapper) của Laravel đơn giản hóa tương tác với cơ sở dữ liệu bằng cách ánh xạ các bảng cơ sở dữ liệu thành các đối tượng PHP, cho phép các nhà phát triển làm việc với các bản ghi dữ liệu một cách trực quan. Hệ thống định tuyến (routing) mạnh mẽ của nó cho phép tạo ra các URL sạch và có ý nghĩa, cải thiện khả năng điều hướng và tối ưu hóa công cụ tìm kiếm. Ngoài ra, hệ sinh thái rộng lớn của Laravel, được hỗ trợ bởi một cộng đồng lớn và năng động, cung cấp nguồn tài nguyên dồi dào, các gói (packages) thông qua Composer và các bản cập nhật liên tục, đảm bảo rằng các ứng dụng được xây dựng bằng Laravel luôn hiện đại, bảo mật và hiệu quả. Mạng lưới hỗ trợ mạnh mẽ này tạo điều kiện thuận lợi đáng kể cho chu trình phát triển nhanh chóng và khả năng bảo trì lâu dài của các giải pháp web phức tạp. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in learning meaningful representations from instruction videos, outperforming existing unsupervised learning approaches. Our research contributes to the development of more intelligent and autonomous systems, with potential applications in human-robot interaction, education, and knowledge acquisition. text: Abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of nonconvex optimization in learning overcomplete representations, specifically in sparsely used overcomplete dictionaries and convolutional dictionaries, relevant to high-dimensional data analysis. Despite the empirical success of simple nonconvex algorithms, theoretical underpinning has been lacking. We formulate these learning problems as \(\ell^4\)-norm optimization problems with spherical constraints and explore their nonconvex optimization landscapes. Our findings reveal that these landscapes possess benign (global) geometric structures, where every local minimizer is proximate to a target solution and every saddle point displays negative curvature. This insight facilitates the design of globally guaranteed optimization methods with straightforward initializations. The benign geometric structures ensure that local search algorithms, such as Riemannian gradient descent, can effectively approximate target solutions. Numerical experiments corroborate our theoretical findings, establishing a robust framework for understanding nonconvex optimization in overcomplete representations.

Word2vec là một mô hình phổ biến và đơn giản dùng để tạo biểu diễn nhúng (embedding) cho từ trong không gian có số chiều thấp hơn nhiều lần so với số từ trong từ điển. Ý tưởng chính của Word2vec là các từ xuất hiện trong cùng ngữ cảnh (context word) thường mang ý nghĩa gần nhau, và mô hình này dựa vào đó để dự đoán một từ mục tiêu (target word) dựa trên các từ xung quanh trong câu. Ví dụ, trong câu “Chó là ... 4 chân”, có thể suy luận từ điền vào chỗ trống là “động vật”, và Word2vec sẽ học cách xác suất để từ “động vật” được điền vào vị trí này là cao nhất. Các từ xuất hiện gần từ mục tiêu trong phạm vi một nửa độ dài C (với C là số nguyên dương) được xác định là từ ngữ cảnh. text: This paper investigates the generalization error of generalized linear models (GLMs) in high-dimensional settings, where the number of features exceeds the sample size. Our objective is to understand how GLMs behave when the dimensionality of the data increases, and to develop a framework for predicting their performance. We employ a combination of theoretical analysis and numerical simulations to study the generalization error of GLMs, using tools from statistical learning theory and high-dimensional statistics. Our results show that the generalization error of GLMs can be bounded by a quantity that depends on the dimensionality of the data, the sample size, and the regularization parameter. We also demonstrate that our bounds are tight, in the sense that they cannot be improved upon by more than a constant factor. Our findings have important implications for the application of GLMs in high-dimensional settings, such as genomics, finance, and computer vision, where the number of features can be extremely large. Key contributions of this work include the development of a novel framework for analyzing the generalization error of GLMs, and the provision of new insights into the behavior of these models in high-dimensional settings. Relevant keywords: generalized linear models, high-dimensional statistics, generalization error, statistical learning theory, regularization techniques.

text: Automatic analysis of scanned historical documents encompasses a broad spectrum of image analysis tasks, which often pose significant challenges for machine learning algorithms due to the scarcity of human-annotated training samples. With the emergence of deep neural networks, a promising strategy to address this limitation is to pre-train models on images from alternative domains and subsequently fine-tune them on historical document datasets. In the present study, a representative instance of such cross-domain transfer learning involves employing neural networks pre-trained on the ImageNet database for object recognition. Whether this pre-training is beneficial for the analysis of historical documents—given their fundamentally different visual characteristics compared to ImageNet—remains largely unresolved. In this paper, we conduct a comprehensive empirical survey to assess the impact of ImageNet pre-training across a range of historical document analysis tasks, including character recognition, style classification, manuscript dating, semantic segmentation, and content-based retrieval. Although our findings for pixel-level semantic segmentation are mixed, we consistently observe that ImageNet pre-training yields positive effects on both classification and content-based retrieval tasks across various network architectures.

text: Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) are general unsupervised learning devices to ascertain generative models of data distributions. RBMs are often trained using the Contrastive Divergence learning algorithm (CD), an approximation to the gradient of the data log-likelihood. A simple reconstruction error is often used to decide whether the approximation provided by the CD algorithm is good enough, though several authors (Schulz et al., 2010; Fischer & Igel, 2010) have raised doubts concerning the feasibility of this procedure. However, not many alternatives to the reconstruction error have been used in the literature. In this manuscript we investigate simple alternatives to the reconstruction error in order to detect as soon as possible the decrease in the log-likelihood during learning.

text: Nhãn ( Dimocarpus longan) là một loại quả đặc sản rất được ưa chu ộng tại Việt Nam. Tuy nhiên, qu ả nhãn có thời hạn bảo quản rất ngắn, nguyên nhân ch ủ yếu là do v ỏ quả bị nâu hóa và qu ả bị thối hỏng do vi sinh v ật. Nghiên cứu này nh ằm kh ảo sát ảnh hư ởng của phương pháp x ử lý sau th u hoạch đến sự biến đổi chất lượng của nhãn ‘‘Hương Chi’’ trong quá trình b ảo quản lạnh. M ột số chỉ tiêu hóa h ọc, màu s ắc, hàm lư ợng polyphenol, ch ỉ số nâu hóa, hao h ụt khối lượng tự nhiên và ch ỉ số bệnh do vi sinh v ật được định kỳ phân tích t ại thời điểm thu ho ạch và sau 10, 20, 30 và 35 ngày b ảo quản. Kết quả cho th ấy quả sau khi đư ợc xử lý với dung d ịch carbendazim 0 ,1%, sau đó nhúng trong dung d ịch axit oxalic 4 mM, bao gói trong túi polypropylene có di ện tích đ ục lỗ tương đ ối 0,008% sau 35 ngày b ảo quản ở 4 ± 1oC, độ ẩm 95 % đã hạn chế được sự nâu hóa v ỏ quả, bệnh do vi sinh v ật và gi ảm thi ểu đáng kể tổn thất các ch ỉ tiêu ch ất lượng so v ới mẫu nhãn không qua x ử lý. Cụ thể, chỉ số nâu hóa của vỏ quả ở lô xử lý duy trì ở mức thấp (ví dụ, giá trị L* cao hơn và chỉ số browning index thấp hơn có ý nghĩa thống kê, P < 0,05) trong suốt 35 ngày, trong khi ở lô đối chứng, hiện tượng nâu hóa xuất hiện rõ rệt chỉ sau 10-20 ngày bảo quản. Tương tự, tỷ lệ quả bị bệnh và chỉ số bệnh do vi sinh vật ở lô xử lý thấp hơn đáng kể, với hầu hết các quả vẫn giữ được trạng thái tốt, trong khi lô đối chứng cho thấy sự phát triển mạnh mẽ của nấm mốc và tỷ lệ thối hỏng cao. Hàm lượng polyphenol tổng số trong vỏ quả, một chỉ tiêu quan trọng liên quan đến khả năng chống oxy hóa và màu sắc, ở lô xử lý được duy trì ở mức cao hơn so với lô đối chứng, cho thấy tác dụng bảo vệ của axit oxalic trong việc ức chế hoạt động của enzyme polyphenol oxidase (PPO). Hao hụt khối lượng tự nhiên của quả ở lô xử lý cũng thấp hơn, điều này có thể được giải thích do tác dụng của bao bì polypropylene giúp giảm sự mất nước. Các phân tích về hàm lượng chất rắn hòa tan tổng số (TSS), axit hữu cơ tổng số (TA) và vitamin C cũng cho thấy sự suy giảm chậm hơn ở lô xử lý, qua đó duy trì tốt hơn giá trị cảm quan và dinh dưỡng của quả nhãn "Hương Chi" trong điều kiện bảo quản lạnh kéo dài.

text:
Reinforcement Learning (RL) has shown significant promise in solving complex continuous control tasks. However, its performance often degrades under model misspecification, where the learned policy fails to generalize due to discrepancies between the training environment and real-world conditions. This paper addresses the challenge of robust RL in continuous control settings by proposing a novel framework that enhances policy robustness against model uncertainties. Our approach integrates a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) technique with deep RL algorithms, enabling the agent to learn policies that are resilient to environmental variations. We evaluate the proposed method on a suite of benchmark continuous control tasks, including robotic manipulation and autonomous navigation, under varying levels of model misspecification. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework outperforms existing RL methods in terms of stability, generalization, and task performance. The key contributions of this work include a theoretically grounded robust RL formulation and a practical algorithm that bridges the gap between simulation and real-world deployment. This research advances the state-of-the-art in robust RL and provides a foundation for deploying RL-based systems in safety-critical applications where model uncertainties are prevalent.  

**Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Continuous Control, Model Misspecification, Robust Optimization, Deep RL, Generalization.
label: deepseek-text

text: Local windows are a staple in computer vision, typically centered on the pixels being processed. However, this standard approach is not always the best. When a pixel is located on an edge, centering the window on the pixel often leads filtering algorithms to blur the edges. To address this, we introduce the Side Window Filtering (SWF) technique, which positions the window's side or corner with the pixel. The SWF technique is remarkably simple, theoretically sound, and highly effective in practice. We demonstrate that numerous traditional linear and nonlinear filters can be adapted to the SWF framework. Comprehensive analysis and experiments reveal that the SWF principle substantially enhances edge-preserving capabilities and achieves exemplary performance in applications such as image smoothing, denoising, enhancement, structure-preserving texture-removing, mutual-structure extraction, and HDR tone mapping. Beyond image filtering, we extend the SWF principle to other applications utilizing local windows. For instance, in colorization by optimization, the SWF principle effectively prevents artifacts like color leakage common with traditional methods. Given the widespread use of window-based operations in computer vision, the new SWF approach is poised to benefit numerous other applications.

text: Video-based person re-identification (Re-ID) aims at matching video sequences of pedestrians across non-overlapping cameras. It is a practical yet challenging task of how to embed spatial and temporal information of a video into its feature representation. While most existing methods learn the video characteristics by aggregating image-wise features and designing attention mechanisms in Neural Networks, they only explore the correlation between frames at high-level features. In this work, we target at refining the intermediate features as well as high-level features with non-local attention operations and make two contributions. (i) We propose a Non-local Video Attention Network (NVAN) to incorporate video characteristics into the representation at multiple feature levels. (ii) We further introduce a Spatially and Temporally Efficient Non-local Video Attention Network (STE-NVAN) to reduce the computation complexity by exploring spatial and temporal redundancy presented in pedestrian videos. Extensive experiments show that our NVAN outperforms state-of-the-arts by 3.8% in rank-1 accuracy on MARS dataset and confirms our STE-NVAN displays a much superior computation footprint compared to existing methods.

Inventory management constitutes a fundamental aspect of logistics warehouse operations, irrespective of the specific products handled by a company. While inventory procedures may differ across businesses, effective management extends beyond basic stockkeeping to involve comprehensive control over all inventory items. In practice, corporations frequently implement cycle counting strategies, whereby inventory is divided into smaller, more manageable batches that are counted periodically, instead of performing complete stocktaking at a single point in time. text: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) perform a specific type of multivariate extrapolation, producing outputs for any input pattern, even when such patterns were not encountered during training. These extrapolations should not always be considered reliable, especially for safety-critical applications, necessitating a means for these systems to indicate the level of uncertainty in their outputs relative to the training data. Although some may assume this issue is already addressed by fundamental pattern recognition principles, we clarify that this is not the case. The conventional approach, which involves the (Likelihood estimate of) conditional probability of classification, does not accurately measure this uncertainty. We discuss traditional interpretations of this issue and demonstrate how a quantitative solution, grounded in established methodologies, can be effectively implemented. These methods are exemplified in the context of the early diagnosis of dementing diseases through Magnetic Resonance Imaging.

text: This paper addresses the challenge of self-supervised scene flow estimation by introducing an adversarial metric learning approach. The objective is to improve the accuracy of scene flow estimation by learning to distinguish between trustworthy and untrustworthy neighboring pixels. Our method employs a novel adversarial framework that pits a scene flow estimator against a discriminator, which attempts to identify incorrect estimates. The estimator is trained to fool the discriminator, resulting in more robust and accurate scene flow predictions. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming state-of-the-art self-supervised methods by a significant margin. Our contributions include a new adversarial metric learning formulation and a robust scene flow estimation model that can handle complex and dynamic scenes. The proposed method has potential applications in autonomous driving, robotics, and computer vision, and highlights the importance of careful consideration of neighboring pixel relationships in scene flow estimation. Key keywords: self-supervised learning, scene flow estimation, adversarial metric learning, computer vision, robotics.

text: Despite the development of numerous methods to understand complex predictive models and the high expectations placed on post-hoc model explainability, such explanations often prove to be neither robust nor trustworthy and are susceptible to adversarial manipulation. This paper presents techniques for attacking Partial Dependence (plots, profiles, PDP)—one of the most popular methods for explaining predictive models trained on tabular data—and demonstrates that PD can be adversarially manipulated. This vulnerability is particularly alarming in financial or medical applications where auditability is a critical requirement for supporting black-box models. This adversarial manipulation is achieved by poisoning the training data to distort explanations—bending or shifting them in a desired direction—using genetic and gradient algorithms. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work performing attacks on variable dependence explanations. Furthermore, the novel application of a genetic algorithm for this purpose offers high transferability, as it generalizes in both a model-agnostic and an explanation-agnostic manner.

text: Multi-Task Learning (MTL) networks offer significant potential for knowledge transfer between diverse tasks but face obstacles like overfitting on limited-data tasks, catastrophic forgetting, and negative task interference. In Natural Language Processing (NLP), optimal performance typically requires dedicated models per task, yet conventional fine-tuning methods are parameter-inefficient—often necessitating new models for each task—and prone to losing pretrained knowledge. We introduce an innovative Transformer architecture featuring a conditional attention mechanism and task-specific modules that enhance weight sharing. This design improves parameter efficiency and reduces forgetting by freezing half of the pretrained model's weights. Additionally, we employ a novel multi-task data sampling technique to counteract data imbalance effects. Our approach outperforms single-task fine-tuning methods while maintaining parameter and data efficiency, requiring only about 66% of data for weight updates. On GLUE benchmarks, our 8-task model exceeds other Adapter methods by 2.8%, and our 24-task model surpasses MTL and single-task fine-tuning approaches by 0.7-1.0%. A scaled-up version of our unified multi-task model achieves competitive performance across 26 NLP tasks, setting new benchmarks on multiple test and development sets. Our code is accessible at https://github.com/CAMTL/CA-MTL.

text: Among 2D convolutional networks on point clouds, point-based approaches consume point clouds of fixed size directly. By analysis of PointNet, a pioneer in introducing deep learning into point sets, we reveal that current point-based methods are essentially spatial relationship processing networks. In this paper, we take a different approach. Our architecture, named PE-Net, learns the representation of point clouds in high-dimensional space, and encodes the unordered input points to feature vectors, which standard 2D CNNs can be applied to. The recommended network can adapt to changes in the number of input points which is the limit of current methods. Experiments show that in the tasks of classification and part segmentation, PE-Net achieves the state-of-the-art performance in multiple challenging datasets, such as ModelNet and ShapeNetPart.

Our approach utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, fine-tuned on a dataset of spectral CT images, to extract relevant features and improve classification performance. The results show a significant improvement in accuracy compared to traditional machine learning methods, with our model achieving a high degree of precision in distinguishing between primary and metastatic lung tumors. The proposed system has important implications for clinical practice, enabling more accurate diagnosis and treatment planning for patients with lung cancer. Key contributions of this research include the application of transfer learning to spectral CT images and the development of a robust classification framework for lung nodule analysis, with potential applications in computer-aided diagnosis and personalized medicine. text:
Bài toán tối ưu hóa ban đầu nhằm xây dựng mô hình với xác suất cao cho từ ngữ cảnh khi có từ mục tiêu, và thấp cho từ ngoài ngữ cảnh. Hàm `softmax` biểu diễn điều này, nhưng việc tính toán cho toàn bộ từ điển rất tốn kém. Vì vậy, phương pháp `negative sampling` đã được lựa chọn để giảm chi phí.

Trong mô hình `negative sampling`, chỉ một số ít từ "âm" (mạng nơron cần xuất ra 0) được chọn ngẫu nhiên để cập nhật trọng số. Thông thường, 520 từ cho bộ dữ liệu nhỏ và 25 từ cho các tập dữ liệu lớn là hiệu quả. Các "mẫu âm" này được lấy theo `phân phối ingram`, ưu tiên các từ xuất hiện thường xuyên.

Trong đoạn mã `C` và thuật toán, một `bảng ingram` cực lớn (hàng triệu phần tử) được sử dụng. `bảng ingram` này được điền chỉ mục từ vựng, với số lần xuất hiện của mỗi chỉ mục tỷ lệ thuận với tần suất từ và kích thước bảng. Để chọn mẫu âm, một số nguyên ngẫu nhiên được tạo ra trong khoảng từ 0 đến kích thước `bảng ingram`, và từ tại chỉ mục đó được lấy. Điều này đảm bảo các từ có xác suất cao hơn được chọn thường xuyên hơn.

Trong ngữ cảnh xử lý thông tin, việc đánh giá mức độ quan trọng của một thuật ngữ thường dựa trên hai tiêu chí chính: điểm phổ biến và điểm phân biệt.

**Điểm phổ biến** của một thuật ngữ (`t`) trong một tài liệu (`d`) được định nghĩa là tần suất xuất hiện của nó, ký hiệu là `tf(t, d)`. Đối với các tài liệu được gán trọng số (`wc,d`), tần suất của thuật ngữ này cũng được đánh trọng số tương ứng theo mức độ quan trọng của tài liệu. Cụ thể, giá trị điểm phổ biến của thuật ngữ tại một nút (`c`) được tính theo công thức sau: `pop(c, t) = Σ d∈D wc,d · tf(t, d) / PNETWORK d`. Công thức này thể hiện tần suất thuật ngữ có trọng số tương đối của thuật ngữ tạo nút `Taxonomy c`.

Mặt khác, **điểm phân biệt** của một thuật ngữ tại một nút `Taxonomy c` đòi hỏi tần suất thuật ngữ có trọng số tương đối của nó tại nút `c` phải lớn hơn đáng kể khi so sánh với các nút anh em của nó, bao gồm `c′ 1, c′ 2, ..., c′ m`. Để xác định tỷ lệ này, một thuật toán cụ thể đã được phát triển.

text:
Phổ vi khuẩn gây nhiễm trùng bàn chân đái tháo đường và tính đề kháng kháng sinh đang trở thành một vấn đề nghiêm trọng trên toàn thế giới. Nhiễm trùng bàn chân đái tháo đường (DFI) là một loại nhiễm trùng da phổ biến ở người mắc bệnh đái tháo đường, đặc biệt là ở chân.

Vi khuẩn là nguyên nhân chính gây DFI, và một số loại vi khuẩn phổ biến bao gồm Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa và Escherichia coli. Những vi khuẩn này có thể gây nhiễm trùng da và mô mềm, dẫn đến các triệu chứng như đỏ, sưng, đau và mùi hôi.

Tính đề kháng kháng sinh là một vấn đề nghiêm trọng trong việc điều trị DFI. Nhiều loại vi khuẩn gây DFI đã phát triển đề kháng kháng sinh, khiến việc điều trị trở nên khó khăn hơn. Điều này đòi hỏi các bác sĩ phải sử dụng các phương pháp điều trị khác nhau, bao gồm sử dụng kháng sinh mới, tăng cường vệ sinh và chăm sóc chân, và sử dụng các phương pháp điều trị không sử dụng kháng sinh.

Để ngăn chặn và điều trị DFI, người mắc bệnh đái tháo đường cần thực hiện các biện pháp phòng ngừa như giữ chân sạch sẽ, không tự chẩn đoán và điều trị, và đến gặp bác sĩ khi xuất hiện các triệu chứng. Bác sĩ cũng cần được trang bị kiến thức và kỹ năng để điều trị DFI một cách hiệu quả.

text: This work introduces Pix2Seq, a streamlined and broadly applicable framework for object detection. Diverging from prevalent methodologies that overtly incorporate prior knowledge specific to the task, this research conceptualizes object detection as a language modeling problem contingent upon observed pixel inputs. Object descriptions, encompassing elements such as bounding boxes and class labels, are formulated as sequences of discrete tokens; subsequently, a neural network is trained to perceive the input image and generate the corresponding target sequence. The proposed methodology is predicated principally on the premise that if a neural network possesses knowledge regarding the location and identity of objects, it merely requires instruction on how to articulate this information. Aside from the application of task-specific data augmentations, the presented approach incorporates minimal assumptions regarding the task, yet demonstrates competitive performance on the demanding COCO dataset when compared against highly specialized and extensively optimized detection algorithms.

text: Finding compact state embeddings from high-dimensional Markov state trajectories, particularly where the transition kernel exhibits a small intrinsic rank, presents a notable challenge. An efficient method, inspired by diffusion maps, is proposed for learning low-dimensional state embeddings that effectively capture the process's dynamics. This approach also introduces a kernel reshaping technique to enhance the accuracy of nonparametric estimation of the transition function. Such state embeddings facilitate the clustering of states into metastable sets, thereby identifying the slow dynamics inherent in the system. Theoretical analysis provides sharp statistical error bounds and misclassification rates for this methodology. Empirical validation through experiments on a simulated dynamical system demonstrates the method's capability to reveal metastable structures. Furthermore, application to time series generated by layers of a Deep-Q-Network playing an Atari game shows that the embedding method successfully identifies game states as similar if they share comparable future events, even when their raw data representations differ significantly.
label: gemini-text

In these scenarios, the application of machine learning techniques becomes essential, as they enable computers to learn from extensive historical observation data. By leveraging machine learning algorithms, computational models can identify complex patterns and correlations within the data, thereby significantly enhancing the accuracy and reliability of weather forecasts compared to traditional human-based predictions. text:
Tất cả các cạnh nối trong mạng. Dòng đầu tiên là số lượng nút có ở nodeinfo và số lượng cạnh có trong file. Định dạng các dòng tiếp theo là [nguồn] [đích] [trọng số]. Giá trị trọng số thể hiện mức độ liên kết của các nút. File `edges.txt` này đóng vai trò là một thành phần cốt lõi trong việc định nghĩa và mô tả cấu trúc quan hệ của một mạng lưới, nơi mà các kết nối giữa các thực thể (nút) được biểu diễn một cách tường minh. Dòng đầu tiên của file, với định dạng "số lượng nút" và "số lượng cạnh", không chỉ cung cấp thông tin tổng quan mà còn là dữ liệu thiết yếu cho các thuật toán xử lý đồ thị. Thông tin về số lượng nút tham chiếu đến dữ liệu trong `nodeinfo` giúp đảm bảo tính nhất quán và toàn vẹn của tập dữ liệu mạng, đồng thời cho phép các ứng dụng có thể cấp phát bộ nhớ một cách hiệu quả trước khi tải toàn bộ dữ liệu đồ thị. Ví dụ, việc biết trước số lượng nút cho phép khởi tạo ma trận kề hoặc danh sách kề với kích thước phù hợp, tối ưu hóa hiệu suất xử lý.

Các dòng tiếp theo, mỗi dòng mô tả một cạnh cụ thể, tuân thủ định dạng `[nguồn] [đích] [trọng số]`. `[nguồn]` và `[đích]` là các định danh số nguyên duy nhất cho các nút tham gia vào một kết nối. Các định danh này thường được gán một cách tuần tự (ví dụ, từ 0 đến N-1 hoặc 1 đến N, với N là tổng số nút), tạo điều kiện thuận lợi cho việc ánh xạ đến các chỉ mục trong cấu trúc dữ liệu lập trình. Sự phân biệt rõ ràng giữa nút nguồn và nút đích ngụ ý rằng các cạnh trong mạng là có hướng, nghĩa là một mối quan hệ hoặc luồng thông tin chỉ di chuyển từ nút nguồn đến nút đích. Điều này rất quan trọng trong các phân tích về luồng, phân cấp, hoặc đường đi có hướng trong mạng. Tuy nhiên, nếu mạng là vô hướng, mỗi cạnh giữa hai nút A và B thường được biểu diễn bằng hai dòng riêng biệt (A B W và B A W) hoặc phần mềm phân tích sẽ xử lý nội bộ để đảm bảo tính đối xứng của mối quan hệ. Việc sử dụng định danh số nguyên giúp giảm thiểu chi phí tính toán khi xử lý dữ liệu và truy xuất thông tin về các nút.

Giá trị `[trọng số]` là một tham số định lượng, thường là một số thực hoặc số nguyên dương, biểu thị "mức độ liên kết của các nút". Ý nghĩa cụ thể của trọng số phụ thuộc vào ngữ cảnh của mạng đang được mô hình hóa. Chẳng hạn, trong một mạng xã hội, trọng số có thể biểu thị tần suất tương tác, độ mạnh của mối quan hệ; trong mạng giao thông, nó có thể là khoảng cách vật lý, thời gian di chuyển, hoặc chi phí; trong mạng lưới truyền thông, trọng số có thể đại diện cho băng thông hoặc độ tin cậy của kết nối. Một giá trị trọng số lớn có thể biểu thị một mối liên kết mạnh mẽ, một khoảng cách ngắn, hoặc một chi phí thấp, tùy thuộc vào cách thức định nghĩa trọng số trong hệ thống. Sự hiện diện của trọng số biến đồ thị thành một đồ thị có trọng số, mở ra khả năng áp dụng các thuật toán phân tích phức tạp hơn như tìm đường đi ngắn nhất (ví dụ: thuật toán Dijkstra), tính toán luồng cực đại, hoặc phân tích ảnh hưởng của các cạnh trong cấu trúc tổng thể của mạng. Đối với các mạng không có trọng số, giá trị này thường được mặc định là 1, biểu thị một kết nối đơn thuần mà không có thuộc tính định lượng bổ sung. Tóm lại, `edges.txt` cung cấp một mô tả chi tiết, có cấu trúc về các mối quan hệ trong mạng, là dữ liệu đầu vào không thể thiếu cho mọi phân tích đồ thị sâu rộng, từ việc xác định các cụm (community detection), tính toán độ tập trung của nút (centrality measures), cho đến việc tìm kiếm các đường đi tối ưu trong mạng lưới.

text: {file_name}: The Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network architecture addresses the vanishing gradient problem that plagues traditional Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) by incorporating three specialized gates: the input gate, the output gate, and the forget gate. These gates are instrumental in regulating the flow of information within the network, allowing it to retain essential information over extended sequences and discard irrelevant data. The input gate determines the degree to which new information flows into the memory cell, while the forget gate decides what information is discarded from the cell state, thus enabling the model to prioritize relevant information over time. The output gate, on the other hand, controls the exposure of the internal memory state to the external environment, thereby influencing the subsequent hidden states. This gating mechanism is crucial for maintaining long-term dependencies, which are often necessary for tasks such as language modeling and time series prediction. Section 3.2 elaborates on the visualization of the LSTM network, providing insights into how these gates interact dynamically during the learning process. The visualization further elucidates the roles of these gates, highlighting their contributions to the model’s ability to handle complex sequence dependencies. The subsequent analysis in Section 3.3 delves into the performance metrics of LSTM networks, comparing their efficacy against standard RNNs. Through empirical evaluations, it is demonstrated that LSTM networks significantly outperform their predecessors in tasks requiring memory retention over long periods, thereby confirming their superiority in handling sequential data with long-range dependencies.

The key advantage of this modular strategy lies in its ability to introduce new representations to the network, rather than overwriting existing ones through fine-tuning. text: Humans perceive by concurrently fusing high-dimensional inputs from multiple modalities, yet machine perception models for tasks like video classification are typically modality-specific, predominantly relying on `late-fusion'. We introduce a novel transformer-based architecture that utilizes `fusion bottlenecks' for modality fusion at multiple layers. Unlike traditional pairwise self-attention, our model forces information between different modalities to pass through a small number of bottleneck latents. This mechanism compels the model to collate and condense the most relevant information in each modality, sharing only what is necessary. We demonstrate that this strategy significantly improves fusion performance while simultaneously reducing computational cost. Extensive ablation studies and state-of-the-art results on multiple audio-visual classification benchmarks, including Audioset, Epic-Kitchens, and VGGSound, validate our approach. All code and models will be released to facilitate future research and application.

text: Executing smart contracts on blockchain networks like Ethereum uses gas, a met ric for the computing effort necessary to complete a transaction. The cost of gas increases with query complexity and with the size of the data being requested. This can make it economically impossible to run complicated queries or query massive datasets. For a decentralized video sharing website, this presents a critical challenge, as operations such as storing video metadata (e.g., titles, descriptions, tags), managing user profiles, and indexing content links would incur prohibitive gas fees if performed entirely on-chain. Even retrieving simple data like a video's creator or its unique identifier could become costly if the underlying data structure is complex or frequently queried. Furthermore, storing the actual video content directly on a blockchain is largely impractical due to both the immense data size and the associated exorbitant gas costs, rendering such a system unsustainable for mass adoption. Consequently, this economic barrier necessitates the exploration of hybrid architectures that offload large data storage and complex computational tasks from the main blockchain, thereby ensuring scalability, reducing transaction fees for users, and making the decentralized video sharing platform economically viable.

text: We propose a reinforcement learning agent designed to solve hard exploration games by learning a range of directed exploratory policies. To train these policies, an episodic memory-based intrinsic reward is constructed using k-nearest neighbors over the agent's recent experience, thereby encouraging the agent to repeatedly revisit all states within its environment. A self-supervised inverse dynamics model trains the embeddings for this nearest-neighbor lookup, biasing the novelty signal towards aspects of the environment the agent can control. The Universal Value Function Approximators (UVFA) framework is employed to simultaneously learn numerous directed exploration policies within the same neural network, each characterized by different trade-offs between exploration and exploitation. This use of a single neural network for varying degrees of exploration and exploitation facilitates knowledge transfer from predominantly exploratory policies, thereby yielding more effective exploitative policies. The proposed method can be integrated with modern distributed RL agents that gather extensive experience from multiple actors operating in parallel on separate environment instances. Our approach doubles the base agent's performance in all hard-exploration games within the Atari-57 suite while maintaining very high scores across the remaining games, achieving a median human-normalised score of 1344.0%. Notably, this method is the first algorithm to achieve non-zero rewards (with a mean score of 8,400) in the game of Pitfall! without using demonstrations or hand-crafted features.

The objective is to develop a theoretical framework that enables TD-learning algorithms to efficiently track changes in the optimal policy. Our approach combines TD-learning with adiabatic techniques, allowing the algorithm to adapt to shifting policies while maintaining convergence guarantees. The results have significant implications for applications in dynamic environments, such as robotics and game playing, where policies may change over time. Our contributions include a new adiabatic theorem that provides a theoretical foundation for policy tracking with TD-learning, as well as empirical evaluations that highlight the effectiveness of our approach. text: Besides the graph-based approach, there are other well-known methods to construct such sequences, including LFSR, recursive methods, greedy methods, and concatenation approaches. Linear Feedback Shift Registers (LFSRs), for instance, are highly favored for their simplicity, hardware efficiency, and ability to generate maximal length sequences (m-sequences) that inherently possess de Bruijn properties for certain tap connections; these sequences exhibit excellent statistical properties crucial for robust synchronization and noise immunity in quantum communication channels, particularly beneficial in quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols by providing pseudo-randomness for basis choices or measurement randomization. Recursive methods build sequences from smaller, pre-existing components, systematically ensuring adherence to run-length constraints at each step of construction, which is vital for practical implementations to prevent baseline wander and maintain stable clock recovery in high-speed optical or quantum links where long strings of identical bits can cause signal degradation. Greedy algorithms offer a flexible approach, iteratively extending sequences by making locally optimal choices to satisfy both the de Bruijn property and specific run-length limits, proving adaptable for scenarios with complex or non-standard constraints on the allowed runs of identical symbols that might arise from physical limitations of quantum devices or encoding schemes. Furthermore, concatenation approaches, often employed within recursive frameworks, enable the modular construction of arbitrarily long run-length limited de Bruijn sequences by joining shorter segments, ensuring continuity of run-length rules across segment boundaries, thereby facilitating scalable design of secure and reliable quantum communication systems that require extensive sequence lengths for enhanced security or data throughput.

text: The paper investigates the potential of Decentralized Online Learning in networks, driven by the need for data providers to collaboratively solve online problems without sharing sensitive data. The study addresses the limitations of the existing best regret bound \Ocal}, which can be reached without network communication, prompting an exploration of when communication can effectively reduce regret. The research introduces a characterization of loss functions into adversarial and stochastic components. It demonstrates that the decentralized online gradient (DOG) algorithm can achieve a regret bound of \OcalG + \sigma}, where G reflects the adversarial component's magnitude and \sigma captures the data's stochastic nature. This finding indicates that randomness in private data offers advantages through information exchange. Additionally, the paper contributes by examining dynamic regret for tracking users' changing interests. Empirical evaluations support the theoretical analysis, suggesting promising directions for future research in optimizing decentralized online learning systems.

SPARQL đóng vai trò then chốt trong việc tương tác và khai thác dữ liệu được biểu diễn dưới dạng RDF, tương tự như cách SQL được sử dụng để truy vấn các cơ sở dữ liệu quan hệ nhưng với khả năng thích ứng cao hơn cho mô hình đồ thị của RDF. Ngôn ngữ này được thiết kế đặc biệt để xử lý các mối quan hệ phức tạp, dữ liệu không đồng nhất và dữ liệu phân tán trên Semantic Web, vượt trội so với các mô hình truy vấn truyền thống vốn tập trung vào cấu trúc bảng cứng nhắc. SPARQL cung cấp một cú pháp mạnh mẽ để định nghĩa các mẫu đồ thị (graph patterns), cho phép người dùng không chỉ trích xuất thông tin cụ thể mà còn có thể tạo ra các đồ thị RDF mới, kiểm tra sự tồn tại của các bộ ba (triples) hoặc mô tả chi tiết các tài nguyên. Cấu trúc cơ bản của một truy vấn SPARQL thường bao gồm mệnh đề `SELECT` để chỉ định các biến cần trả về, và mệnh đề `WHERE` chứa các mẫu đồ thị cần khớp. Ngoài ra, SPARQL hỗ trợ một tập hợp phong phú các toán tử và mệnh đề nâng cao như `FILTER` để áp dụng các ràng buộc điều kiện, `OPTIONAL` cho phép khớp các mẫu dữ liệu không bắt buộc mà không loại bỏ toàn bộ kết quả, `UNION` để kết hợp các tập kết quả từ các mẫu khác nhau, cũng như các mệnh đề sửa đổi kết quả như `ORDER BY`, `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, `LIMIT` và `OFFSET`. Những tính năng này giúp người dùng có thể thực hiện các truy vấn phức tạp, tổng hợp dữ liệu, và quản lý việc phân trang kết quả một cách linh hoạt và hiệu quả. Bên cạnh hình thức truy vấn `SELECT` phổ biến, SPARQL còn hỗ trợ các hình thức khác như `CONSTRUCT` để tạo ra một đồ thị RDF mới dựa trên kết quả truy vấn, `ASK` để kiểm tra sự tồn tại của một mẫu đồ thị và trả về giá trị boolean, và `DESCRIBE` để cung cấp thông tin mô tả ngữ cảnh về một tài nguyên cụ thể. Sự linh hoạt và khả năng biểu diễn phong phú của SPARQL làm cho nó trở thành công cụ không thể thiếu trong việc xây dựng các ứng dụng trên nền tảng dữ liệu liên kết (Linked Data) và Semantic Web, nơi tính mở và khả năng kết nối dữ liệu là ưu tiên hàng đầu. Cụ thể trong ngữ cảnh của luận văn này, việc sử dụng SPARQL sẽ đóng vai trò trung tâm trong việc truy vấn và khai thác hiệu quả các thông tin về địa giới hành chính đã được mô hình hóa bằng ontology. Chẳng hạn, một truy vấn SPARQL có thể dễ dàng lấy danh sách tất cả các quận/huyện thuộc một tỉnh/thành phố nhất định, tìm kiếm thông tin chi tiết của một đơn vị hành chính dựa trên tên duy nhất hoặc một phần tên, hoặc xác định các mối quan hệ phân cấp phức tạp giữa các đơn vị hành chính từ cấp quốc gia đến cấp xã/phường. Điều này đặc biệt hữu ích khi phát triển các hệ thống thông tin địa lý (GIS), các cổng dữ liệu mở cho chính phủ, hoặc các ứng dụng phân tích dữ liệu hành chính đòi hỏi khả năng truy xuất dữ liệu có ngữ cảnh và linh hoạt. Khả năng truy vấn liên kết dữ liệu từ nhiều nguồn khác nhau (federated queries) thông qua SPARQL Protocol cũng mở ra tiềm năng lớn trong việc tích hợp dữ liệu từ các ontology hoặc kho dữ liệu RDF phân tán khác, từ đó nâng cao đáng kể giá trị và tính ứng dụng của mô hình dữ liệu đã xây dựng. text: The `payload` defines the structure of data requests originating from the client-side, crucial for a travel social network where diverse user interactions occur, including JSON objects for creating a new travel post (e.g., `{'post_content': 'My adventure in Machu Picchu', 'location_tag': 'Machu Picchu', 'media_urls': ['url1', 'url2']}`), submitting comments, applying filters for travel searches, or updating user profiles with new travel interests. The `type` field categorizes common system operations, encompassing `action type` for distinct user interactions like `POST_CREATE`, `USER_FOLLOW`, or `TRIP_PLAN_SHARE`, and `notification type` to handle events such as `NEW_LIKE_ON_POST` or `FRIEND_CHECK_IN_NEARBY`, which are fundamental for routing requests to appropriate API endpoints and triggering specific backend processes or real-time updates. The `entity` definitions establish the foundational data model, detailing `field property` and `relationship between them` within the database; for a travel social network, key entities include `User` (with attributes like username, travel preferences), `Post` (containing content, location, and references to media), `Location` (for geotagging and exploration), and `Comment`, with explicit foreign key relationships (e.g., `Post.user_id` references `User.user_id`) ensuring data integrity and enabling complex queries to retrieve associated information, such as all posts by a specific user or comments on a particular travel destination. Specifically, the `com.vifrin.post:` module signifies the architectural component responsible for encapsulating all business logic and data access layers pertaining to user-generated travel posts, from their creation and storage to retrieval and interaction management within the `vifrin` system.

Nghiên cứu này nhằm xác định tỷ lệ sống còn 5 năm và các yếu tố tiên lượng liên quan ở bệnh nhân UTBMTBG. Thiết kế nghiên cứu là đoàn hệ hồi cứu với 239 bệnh nhân UTBMTBG đến khám và điều trị tại BV NDGĐ từ 01/01/2016 đến 31/12/2020, được theo dõi kết cục sống, tử vong hoặc mất dấu cho đến khi kết thúc nghiên cứu. Độ tuổi trung bình của bệnh nhân là 62,4 tuổi, tỷ lệ nam:nữ là 3,2:1; 31% không xơ gan, trong số còn lại: xơ gan Child A chiếm 55,2%, Child B 35,6% và Child C 9,2%. text: In this paper we consider the task of estimating the non-zero pattern of the sparse inverse covariance matrix of a zero-mean Gaussian random vector from a set of iid samples. Note that this is also equivalent to recovering the underlying graph structure of a sparse Gaussian Markov Random Field (GMRF). We present two novel greedy approaches to solving this problem. The first estimates the non-zero covariates of the overall inverse covariance matrix using a series of global forward and backward greedy steps. The second estimates the neighborhood of each node in the graph separately, again using greedy forward and backward steps, and combines the intermediate neighborhoods to form an overall estimate. The principal contribution of this paper is a rigorous analysis of the sparsistency, or consistency in recovering the sparsity pattern of the inverse covariance matrix. Surprisingly, we show that both the local and global greedy methods learn the full structure of the model with high probability given just O(d\log(p)) samples, which is a  improvement over state of the art \ell_1-regularized Gaussian MLE (Graphical Lasso) that requires O(d^2\log(p)) samples. Moreover, the restricted eigenvalue and smoothness conditions imposed by our greedy methods are much weaker than the strong irrepresentable conditions required by the \ell_1-regularization based methods. We corroborate our results with extensive simulations and examples, comparing our local and global greedy methods to the \ell_1-regularized Gaussian MLE as well as the Neighborhood Greedy method to that of nodewise \ell_1-regularized linear regression (Neighborhood Lasso).

text: The design of effective neural networks remains a critical and practical challenge in deep learning. Beyond architectural elements like depth, convolution type, normalization, and nonlinearities, topological connectivity also plays a crucial role. While previous rule-based modular design principles simplify architectural construction, they inherently constrain the exploration of diverse topological spaces. This paper proposes a novel approach to optimize the topological connectivity in neural networks. Specifically, we introduce a topological perspective that represents a neural network as a complete graph, where nodes denote feature aggregation and transformation operations, and edges delineate information flow. By assigning learnable parameters to these edges, quantifying connection strengths, we enable a differentiable learning process. Furthermore, an auxiliary sparsity constraint is incorporated into the distribution of edge parameters to encourage the learned topology to prioritize critical connections. This differentiable learning process is compatible with existing network architectures and demonstrates adaptability to larger search spaces and diverse tasks. Quantitative experimental results demonstrate that the learned connectivity patterns are superior to traditional rule-based designs, including random, residual, and complete topologies. Furthermore, our approach yields significant performance improvements in both image classification and object detection tasks without incurring substantial computational overhead.

text: Universal adversarial perturbations (UAPs), a.k.a. input-agnostic perturbations, has been proved to exist and be able to fool cutting-edge deep learning models on most of the data samples. Existing UAP methods mainly focus on attacking image classification models. Nevertheless, little attention has been paid to attacking image retrieval systems. In this paper, we make the first attempt in attacking image retrieval systems. Concretely, image retrieval attack is to make the retrieval system return irrelevant images to the query at the top ranking list. It plays an important role to corrupt the neighbourhood relationships among features in image retrieval attack. To this end, we propose a novel method to generate retrieval-against UAP to break the neighbourhood relationships of image features via degrading the corresponding ranking metric. To expand the attack method to scenarios with varying input sizes or untouchable network parameters, a multi-scale random resizing scheme and a ranking distillation strategy are proposed. We evaluate the proposed method on four widely-used image retrieval datasets, and report a significant performance drop in terms of different metrics, such as mAP and mP@10. Finally, we test our attack methods on the real-world visual search engine, i.e., Google Images, which demonstrates the practical potentials of our methods.

Example 4.1 (Lyndon words).
The word 00101 is a Lyndon word because it is lexicographically smaller than all of its cyclic rotations: 01010, 10100, 01001, 10010. Conversely, the word 01100 is not a Lyndon word, as one of its cyclic rotations, 00011, is lexicographically smaller than it. Similarly, the word 011011 is not a Lyndon word, since its cyclic rotation by 3 letters yields the identical word, thereby demonstrating its lack of primitivity.

text: The intricacies of sequence reconstruction, a challenge extensively explored in computational biology, particularly in DNA fragment assembly, offer a foundational analogue for the robust data structuring required in quantum communication. For example, the seminal work by P. A. Pevzner, H. Tang, and M. S. Waterman, “A new approach to fragment assembly in dna sequencing,” in Proceedings of the fifth annual international conference on Computational biology , 2001, pp. 256–267., introduced novel algorithmic strategies for overcoming the inherent complexities of reconstructing large genomes from fragmented reads. While the specific biological domain differs significantly, the underlying computational challenges of ensuring data integrity, managing overlaps, and facilitating efficient reconstruction resonate strongly with the demands of transmitting information through nascent quantum channels. Specifically, the development and application of run-length limited (RLL) de Bruijn sequences present a promising avenue for encoding quantum information. These sequences, characterized by strict constraints on the maximum number of consecutive identical symbols, are crucial in classical communication systems for mitigating inter-symbol interference and enhancing signal reliability. Applying this principle to quantum states, RLL de Bruijn sequences can theoretically improve the distinguishability of encoded quantum states, thereby reducing error rates in inherently noisy quantum environments. This robust encoding scheme, leveraging the combinatorial properties of de Bruijn graphs and the practical benefits of RLL constraints, aims to establish highly fault-tolerant communication protocols essential for the progression of quantum networks, directly addressing the vulnerabilities posed by decoherence and quantum noise through carefully structured information paradigms.

text: Transfer learning enables practitioners to leverage knowledge acquired from previous tasks (source tasks) to enhance performance on new tasks or domains (target tasks) that share underlying commonalities. Two key factors influencing the effectiveness of transfer learning models are (a) the size of the target dataset and (b) the degree of similarity between source and target domain distributions. However, the relative importance of these factors remains underexplored. In this paper, we systematically examine the effects of target dataset size and source–target domain similarity on model performance through a series of controlled experiments. Our results indicate that increasing data volume consistently benefits model performance, with improvements scaling linearly with the logarithm of data size until saturation. When source and target domains differ substantially, larger datasets are required, and fine-tuning yields superior performance compared to feature extraction. Conversely, when domains are similar and data is limited, fine-tuning and feature extraction perform equivalently. By initiating this quantitative analysis of data volume and domain similarity in transfer learning, we aim to encourage further research into the critical role of data in constructing accurate statistical models.

text: The efficacy of continual relation extraction models is critically dependent on the robustness and disentanglement of learned feature representations, particularly in mitigating the pervasive issue of catastrophic forgetting. In this context, strategies aimed at decorrelating features are paramount, as highly correlated features can lead to increased interference between learned tasks and hinder the model's ability to generalize to new relation types without compromising performance on previously acquired knowledge. Foundational work in learning robust feature spaces, such as that presented by R. Hadsell, S. Chopra andY. LeCun, “Dimensionality reduction by learning an invariant mapping,” in2006 IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR’06) volume 2, 2006, pages 1735–1742., highlights techniques for constructing invariant mappings that project data into lower-dimensional, more discriminative spaces. This principle of dimensionality reduction, when applied judiciously, can serve as a potent mechanism for achieving feature decorrelation by identifying and emphasizing independent components of information while suppressing redundant or highly correlated attributes. For continual relation extraction, adopting such invariant and decorrelated representations is essential to ensure that the model can incrementally learn new relation patterns without suffering from feature interference that degrades performance on previously mastered relations, thereby fostering more stable and efficient knowledge accretion within dynamic linguistic environments.

text: The embedding space, where semantically similar objects are clustered together and dissimilar ones are dispersed, is fundamental to various computer vision applications. However, conventional methods typically employ a single metric to represent all data points in this space, which can exhibit complex, non-uniform distributions with diverse notions of similarity, such as appearance, shape, color, or semantic meaning. These single-metric approaches often struggle to capture the multitude of relationships between objects and fail to generalize effectively. This paper presents a novel, straightforward divide-and-conquer approach to deep metric learning, which achieves significant improvements over the current state-of-the-art. By partitioning both the data and embedding space into K smaller sub-problems, our method learns K distinct distance metrics in non-overlapping subspaces defined by neural network embedding layer neuron groups. This approach enhances convergence speed and generalization by reducing the complexity of each sub-problem relative to the original one, as demonstrated by its substantial outperformance of state-of-the-art methods on CUB200-2011, CARS196, Stanford Online Products, In-shop Clothes, and PKU VehicleID datasets in retrieval, clustering, and re-identification tasks.

text: We present a new method for forecasting systems of multiple interrelated time series. The method learns the forecast models together with discovering leading indicators from within the system that serve as good predictors improving the forecast accuracy and a cluster structure of the predictive tasks around these. The method is based on the classical linear vector autoregressive model (VAR) and links the discovery of the leading indicators to inferring sparse graphs of Granger causality. We formulate a new constrained optimisation problem to promote the desired sparse structures across the models and the sharing of information amongst the learning tasks in a multi-task manner. We propose an algorithm for solving the problem and document on a battery of synthetic and real-data experiments the advantages of our new method over baseline VAR models as well as the state-of-the-art sparse VAR learning methods.

text: The research by Y. M. Chee, T. Etzion, H. M. Kiah, S. Marcovich, A. Vardy, E. Yaakobi, et al. , “Locally-constrained de bruijn codes: Properties, enumeration, code constructions, and applications,” IEEE Transactions on Information Theory , vol. 67, no. 12, pp. 7857–7875, 2021, provides a foundational understanding of codes that are inherently relevant to the construction and analysis of run length limited de Bruijn sequences, which are paramount in managing channel constraints and ensuring reliable data transmission, particularly in emerging fields like quantum communication. These locally-constrained de Bruijn codes, by definition, encompass sequences where specific patterns, such as consecutive identical symbols (runs), are bounded, making them a direct generalization of run length limited (RLL) sequences critical for avoiding detrimental effects like baseline wander and clock synchronization issues in classical systems, and equivalently, for mitigating state-dependent noise and decoherence in quantum channels. The exploration of their "Properties" provides insights into their combinatorial structure, essential for designing efficient encoding and decoding algorithms, while "enumeration" is crucial for determining the maximum achievable code rate and the diversity of sequences available for quantum state preparation or measurement schemes. Furthermore, the detailed "code constructions" offer practical methodologies for generating these sequences, which can be adapted for quantum channel coding to ensure robust transmission of quantum information by limiting long runs of specific quantum states that might be more prone to environmental interaction or errors, thereby enhancing the fidelity of quantum key distribution (QKD) or the efficiency of quantum error correction (QEC) protocols. Finally, the "applications" section, although initially classical, establishes a theoretical framework that can be extended to address the unique challenges of maintaining quantum coherence and minimizing errors over noisy quantum communication links by intelligently structuring the transmitted quantum states.

text: The rapid advancement of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) necessitates the move towards digitalization to enhance network efficiency. Digital Twin technology emerges as a key enabler in this transformation, enabling the creation of virtual replicas of physical objects. Despite its potential, achieving network efficiency in IIoT is challenging due to constraints such as limited device resources, unpredictable tasks, and resource heterogeneity. Efficient exploitation of distributed resources through computation offloading can mitigate energy consumption and improve data processing efficiency. The introduction of Digital Twin Networks (DTN) provides a novel framework for constructing network topology and modeling stochastic task arrivals in IIoT systems. This study addresses the stochastic computation offloading and resource allocation problem, aiming to minimize long-term energy consumption. By employing Lyapunov optimization, the stochastic problem is transformed into a deterministic per-time slot problem, facilitating solution derivation. The Asynchronous Actor-Critic (AAC) algorithm is then applied to determine the optimal computation offloading policy. Empirical results indicate that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms existing benchmarks, demonstrating its efficacy in enhancing network efficiency within IIoT environments.

text: Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization (WDRO) attempts to learn a model that minimizes the local worst-case risk in the vicinity of the empirical data distribution defined by Wasserstein ball. While WDRO has received attention as a promising tool for inference since its introduction, its theoretical understanding has not been fully matured. Gao et al. (2017) proposed a minimizer based on a tractable approximation of the local worst-case risk, but without showing risk consistency. In this paper, we propose a minimizer based on a novel approximation theorem and provide the corresponding risk consistency results. Furthermore, we develop WDRO inference for locally perturbed data that include the Mixup (Zhang et al., 2017) as a special case. We show that our approximation and risk consistency results naturally extend to the cases when data are locally perturbed. Numerical experiments demonstrate robustness of the proposed method using image classification datasets. Our results show that the proposed method achieves significantly higher accuracy than baseline models on noisy datasets.

text: We address the problem of finding influential training samples for a particular case of tree ensemble-based models, e.g., Random Forest (RF) or Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (GBDT). A natural way of formalizing this problem is studying how the model's predictions change upon leave-one-out retraining, leaving out each individual training sample. Recent work has shown that, for parametric models, this analysis can be conducted in a computationally efficient way. We propose several ways of extending this framework to non-parametric GBDT ensembles under the assumption that tree structures remain fixed. Furthermore, we introduce a general scheme of obtaining further approximations to our method that balance the trade-off between performance and computational complexity. We evaluate our approaches on various experimental setups and use-case scenarios and demonstrate both the quality of our approach to finding influential training samples in comparison to the baselines and its computational efficiency.

text: A key challenge in systems biology is developing statistical methods that automatically identify causal relationships in gene regulatory networks without prior knowledge of connectivity. While many methods target time series data, discovery from steady-state data is often necessary and preferable due to the high cost or infeasibility of time series collection in many biological systems. Conventional approaches rely on causal Bayesian networks, but their estimation is ill-posed, often yielding only a large class of indistinguishable equivalent networks rather than a unique causal structure. We propose a novel discovery algorithm that uniquely identifies the underlying causal gene network. To our knowledge, this is the first algorithm for learning gene networks based on the fully identifiable causal model LiNGAM. We compare our method to competing algorithms using artificially generated data, although validation with real microarray gene expression data remains preferable.

text: The application of mixup to enhance transfer learning with pre-trained models can be suboptimal, often leading to overfitting in high-capacity architectures. Self-Distilled Mixup for EffIcient Transfer LEarning (SMILE) proposes a refined regularization strategy to counteract this. SMILE uniquely compels convolutional neural network feature extractors to learn from mixed feature vectors of input samples—termed sample-to-feature mixup—in conjunction with traditional mixed labels. This is achieved through a self-distilling mechanism where a mean teacher, inherited from the pre-trained model, provides the original input feature vectors. These vectors are then mixed and guided by a novel triplet regularizer, which strategically balances the mixup influence in both feature and label spaces while also bounding inter-sample linearity relevant to pre-training tasks. Extensive comparative studies confirm that SMILE significantly outperforms standard fine-tuning and other advanced transfer learning techniques, even when they incorporate basic mixup, by substantially improving mixup efficacy and model generalization on both training and testing data.

text: Unlike conventional frame-based sensors, event-based visual sensors output information through spikes at a high temporal resolution. By only encoding changes in pixel intensity, they showcase a low-power consuming, low-latency approach to visual information sensing. To use this information for higher sensory tasks like object recognition and tracking, an essential simplification step is the extraction and learning of features. An ideal feature descriptor must be robust to changes involving (i) local transformations and (ii) re-appearances of a local event pattern. To that end, we propose a novel spatiotemporal feature representation learning algorithm based on slow feature analysis (SFA). Using SFA, smoothly changing linear projections are learnt which are robust to local visual transformations. In order to determine if the features can learn to be invariant to various visual transformations, feature point tracking tasks are used for evaluation. Extensive experiments across two datasets demonstrate the adaptability of the spatiotemporal feature learner to translation, scaling and rotational transformations of the feature points. More importantly, we find that the obtained feature representations are able to exploit the high temporal resolution of such event-based cameras in generating better feature tracks.

text:
Urban traffic data is often incomplete due to sensor malfunctions or sparse coverage, posing significant challenges for traffic management and prediction systems. This paper addresses the problem of spatiotemporal traffic data imputation by proposing a novel tensor completion framework. The objective is to accurately reconstruct missing traffic data across both spatial and temporal dimensions, enabling more reliable traffic analysis and decision-making. Our approach leverages a low-rank tensor decomposition model combined with spatiotemporal regularization to capture the inherent correlations and patterns in urban traffic networks. The proposed method is evaluated on real-world traffic datasets from multiple cities, demonstrating superior performance in imputation accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques. Experimental results show that our model achieves a 15% improvement in mean absolute error (MAE) and a 20% reduction in root mean squared error (RMSE) over baseline methods. The framework also exhibits robustness under varying levels of data sparsity, making it suitable for diverse urban environments. This research contributes to the field of intelligent transportation systems by providing a scalable and efficient solution for traffic data imputation, with potential applications in traffic forecasting, congestion management, and urban planning.  

**Keywords**: spatiotemporal data, tensor completion, traffic imputation, urban traffic analysis, low-rank decomposition, intelligent transportation systems.

text: A key challenge in location-based modeling and forecasting is determining appropriate spatial and temporal resolutions, with spatial partitioning significantly impacting forecasting performance. This paper investigates two common tessellation strategies—Geohash and Voronoi—for partitioning city space in the context of real-time taxi demand forecasting, utilizing two distinct taxi demand datasets across multiple time scales. Classical time-series methods are employed to model spatio-temporal demand, and it is found that the efficacy of each tessellation approach varies based on city geography, data distribution, and time of day, with no single strategy performing optimally across all scenarios. To address this, a hybrid tessellation algorithm is introduced, selecting the most effective strategy at each moment based on recent performance, modeled as a non-stationary variant of the HEDGE algorithm for expert advice selection. Experimental results demonstrate that the hybrid approach consistently outperforms either individual tessellation strategy across datasets, time scales, and evaluation metrics, achieving an average accuracy exceeding 80% per km^2 at 60-minute aggregation intervals. This paper introduces a novel logic-based approach to generatively defined discriminative modeling, addressing the challenge of integrating generative and discriminative paradigms in machine learning. The proposed method leverages formal logic frameworks to define generative models that inherently support discriminative tasks, enabling improved interpretability and performance. By combining probabilistic reasoning with logical constraints, the approach ensures robust feature representation and decision-making capabilities. The methodology is implemented using a hybrid architecture that integrates symbolic reasoning with neural networks, allowing for efficient training and inference. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in classification accuracy and model interpretability compared to traditional discriminative models. The findings highlight the potential of logic-based generative definitions to enhance discriminative modeling, offering a pathway for developing more transparent and effective machine learning systems. This research contributes to advancing the integration of symbolic and statistical AI, with applications in areas such as natural language processing, computer vision, and decision support systems.  

**Keywords**: generative modeling, discriminative modeling, logic-based AI, hybrid architectures, interpretability, machine learning.

text: The characterisation of the brain as a functional network in which the connections between brain regions are represented by correlation values across time series has been very popular in the last years. Although this representation has advanced our understanding of brain function, it represents a simplified model of brain connectivity that has a complex dynamic spatio-temporal nature. Oversimplification of the data may hinder the merits of applying advanced non-linear feature extraction algorithms. To this end, we propose a dynamic adaptive spatio-temporal graph convolution (DAST-GCN) model to overcome the shortcomings of pre-defined static correlation-based graph structures. The proposed approach allows end-to-end inference of dynamic connections between brain regions via layer-wise graph structure learning module while mapping brain connectivity to a phenotype in a supervised learning framework. This leverages the computational power of the model, data and targets to represent brain connectivity, and could enable the identification of potential biomarkers for the supervised target in question. We evaluate our pipeline on the UKBiobank dataset for age and gender classification tasks from resting-state functional scans and show that it outperforms currently adapted linear and non-linear methods in neuroimaging. Further, we assess the generalizability of the inferred graph structure by transferring the pre-trained graph to an independent dataset for the same task. text: Time series forecasting constitutes a critical task across numerous domains, including the prediction of solar plant energy output, electricity consumption, and traffic congestion. This paper proposes to address such forecasting problems utilizing the Transformer architecture [1]. Although its performance in preliminary studies was impressive, two principal weaknesses were identified: (1) locality-agnosticism, whereby the point-wise dot-product self-attention mechanism in the canonical Transformer architecture exhibits insensitivity to local context, potentially rendering the model susceptible to anomalies in time series; and (2) a memory bottleneck, as the space complexity of the canonical Transformer increases quadratically with sequence length L, making the direct modeling of long time series impracticable. To resolve these issues, a convolutional self-attention mechanism is first proposed, wherein queries and keys are produced via causal convolutions, enabling more effective incorporation of local context into the attention mechanism. Subsequently, the LogSparse Transformer is introduced, possessing a memory cost of only O(L(\log L)^), thereby improving forecasting accuracy for time series with fine granularity and strong long-term dependencies under constrained memory budgets. Experimental results on both synthetic data and real-world datasets demonstrate that this approach compares favorably to current state-of-the-art methods.

text: There has been rapidly growing interest in meta-learning as a method for increasing the flexibility and sample efficiency of reinforcement learning. One problem in this area of research, however, has been a scarcity of adequate benchmark tasks. In general, the structure underlying past benchmarks has either been too simple to be inherently interesting, or too ill-defined to support principled analysis. In the present work, we introduce a new benchmark for meta-RL research, which combines structural richness with structural transparency. Alchemy is a 3D video game, implemented in Unity, which involves a latent causal structure that is resampled procedurally from episode to episode, affording structure learning, online inference, hypothesis testing and action sequencing based on abstract domain knowledge. We evaluate a pair of powerful RL agents on Alchemy and present an in-depth analysis of one of these agents. Results clearly indicate a frank and specific failure of meta-learning, providing validation for Alchemy as a challenging benchmark for meta-RL. Concurrent with this report, we are releasing Alchemy as public resource, together with a suite of analysis tools and sample agent trajectories. This finding underscores critical limitations of current meta-learning approaches, suggesting a need for novel algorithmic designs capable of robustly integrating abstract reasoning and causal discovery. Alchemy is thus poised to become a vital platform for the development and assessment of next-generation meta-RL agents that can address these shortcomings and achieve more flexible and generalized intelligence.

text:
Xây dựng công cụ kiểm thử và quản lý lỗi an toàn bảo mật của phần mềm Web là một vấn đề cấp thiết trong lĩnh vực công nghệ thông tin. Với sự phát triển nhanh chóng của công nghệ Web, phần mềm Web ngày càng trở nên phức tạp và dễ bị tấn công bởi các loại malware và exploits khác nhau. Do đó, việc xây dựng một công cụ kiểm thử và quản lý lỗi an toàn bảo mật hiệu quả là cần thiết để đảm bảo an toàn và bảo mật cho phần mềm Web.

Công cụ kiểm thử và quản lý lỗi an toàn bảo mật được thiết kế để tự động hóa quá trình kiểm thử và phân tích lỗi của phần mềm Web. Công cụ này sử dụng các kỹ thuật kiểm thử và phân tích lỗi tiên tiến để phát hiện và phân tích các lỗi an toàn bảo mật trong phần mềm Web. Công cụ này cũng cung cấp các tính năng quản lý lỗi để giúp người dùng theo dõi và quản lý các lỗi an toàn bảo mật đã được phát hiện.

Công cụ kiểm thử và quản lý lỗi an toàn bảo mật được xây dựng dựa trên các nguyên tắc và tiêu chuẩn an toàn bảo mật hiện đại. Công cụ này được thiết kế để dễ dàng sử dụng và tích hợp với các hệ thống quản lý dự án và kiểm thử khác nhau. Công cụ này cũng được thiết kế để cung cấp các báo cáo và phân tích chi tiết về các lỗi an toàn bảo mật đã được phát hiện.

Tổng quan, công cụ kiểm thử và quản lý lỗi an toàn bảo mật của phần mềm Web là một công cụ quan trọng trong việc đảm bảo an toàn và bảo mật cho phần mềm Web. Công cụ này giúp người dùng phát hiện và phân tích các lỗi an toàn bảo mật hiệu quả, đồng thời cung cấp các tính năng quản lý lỗi để giúp người dùng theo dõi và quản lý các lỗi an toàn bảo mật đã được phát hiện.

text: Labeling objects at the subordinate level generally demands expert knowledge, which is often lacking when utilizing random annotators. Consequently, learning directly from web images for fine-grained recognition has garnered significant attention. Nevertheless, label noise and the prevalence of hard examples in web images present substantial challenges to training robust fine-grained recognition models. To address these issues, this paper introduces a novel approach that filters out irrelevant samples from real-world web images during training while selectively leveraging informative hard examples to update the network. In this way, our method mitigates the detrimental impact of irrelevant noisy web images and hard examples, thereby enhancing overall performance. Extensive experiments on three widely used fine-grained datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art web-supervised methods.
