Original Essay: When training a neural network for a desired task, one may prefer to adapt a pre-trained network rather than starting from randomly initialized weights. Adaptation can be useful in cases when training data is scarce, when a single learner needs to perform multiple tasks, or when one wishes to encode priors in the network. The most commonly employed approaches for network adaptation are fine-tuning and using the pre-trained network as a fixed feature extractor, among others. In this paper, we propose a straightforward alternative: side-tuning. Side-tuning adapts a pre-trained network by training a lightweight "side" network that is fused with the (unchanged) pre-trained network via summation. This simple method works as well as or better than existing solutions and it resolves some of the basic issues with fine-tuning, fixed features, and other common approaches. In particular, side-tuning is less prone to overfitting, is asymptotically consistent, and does not suffer from catastrophic forgetting in incremental learning. We demonstrate the performance of side-tuning under a diverse set of scenarios, including incremental learning (iCIFAR, iTaskonomy), reinforcement learning, imitation learning (visual navigation in Habitat), NLP question-answering (SQuAD v2), and single-task transfer learning (Taskonomy), with consistently promising results.

This simple method performs comparably to or better than existing solutions, effectively mitigating overfitting, ensuring asymptotic consistency, and preventing catastrophic forgetting in incremental learning. Activation functions commonly used before ReLU, such as sigmoid and tanh, tend to saturate, which means their outputs approach fixed values (1.0 for large inputs in sigmoid, -1 or 0 for large inputs in tanh). These functions are mainly responsive to input values near their mid-points (0.5 for sigmoid, 0.0 for tanh), leading to a phenomenon known as the vanishing gradient problem. The vanishing gradient problem refers to the issue where gradients become too small for effective learning in deep networks.

Activation functions like sigmoid and tanh, which were widely used before ReLU, often saturate so that their output values become fixed at extremes—1.0 for large inputs in sigmoid and -1 or 0 for tanh. Moreover, these functions are mostly sensitive to variations near their respective mid-points (0.5 for sigmoid and 0.0 for tanh). As a result, they suffer from the vanishing gradient problem, where gradients become too small for the network to learn effectively. The vanishing gradient problem will be briefly discussed next.

text:
This paper addresses the challenge of generating realistic images from scene graphs, focusing on improving the contextualized layout of objects to enhance visual coherence and semantic accuracy. The objective is to bridge the gap between structured scene descriptions and high-quality image synthesis, ensuring that generated images accurately reflect the relationships and attributes defined in the scene graph. To achieve this, we propose a novel approach that integrates a contextualized object layout refinement module into the image generation pipeline. This module leverages graph neural networks (GNNs) to model object relationships and refine their spatial arrangements, ensuring better alignment with the scene graph's semantic structure. Additionally, we employ a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) to synthesize high-resolution images from the refined layouts. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in both visual quality and semantic fidelity compared to existing methods, as validated by quantitative metrics and user studies. The proposed approach not only advances the state-of-the-art in scene graph-to-image generation but also offers practical applications in areas such as virtual reality, content creation, and human-computer interaction. Key contributions include the introduction of a context-aware layout refinement mechanism and a robust framework for generating semantically consistent images from complex scene descriptions.  

**Keywords**: Scene graph, image generation, graph neural networks, generative adversarial networks, object layout refinement, semantic fidelity.
label: deepseek-text

text: In this paper, a new video super-resolution reconstruction (SRR) method with improved robustness to outliers is proposed. Although the R-LMS is one of the SRR algorithms with the best reconstruction quality for its computational cost, and is naturally robust to registration inaccuracies, its performance is known to degrade severely in the presence of innovation outliers. By studying the proximal point cost function representation of the R-LMS iterative equation, a better understanding of its performance under different situations is attained. Using statistical properties of typical innovation outliers, a new cost function is then proposed and two new algorithms are derived, which present improved robustness to outliers while maintaining computational costs comparable to that of R-LMS. Monte Carlo simulation results illustrate that the proposed method outperforms the traditional and regularized versions of LMS, and is competitive with state-of-the-art SRR methods at a much smaller computational cost.

text:
Real image denoising is a critical challenge in computer vision, with significant implications for applications such as medical imaging, surveillance, and photography. This paper addresses the limitations of existing denoising methods, which often struggle with preserving fine details while effectively removing noise. We propose a novel deep learning-based approach that leverages feature attention mechanisms to enhance denoising performance. Our method integrates a multi-scale feature extraction network with an attention module, enabling the model to focus on noise-affected regions while preserving structural details. The proposed architecture is trained on a diverse dataset of real-world noisy and clean image pairs, ensuring robustness across various noise levels and types. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art denoising methods in terms of both quantitative metrics (e.g., PSNR and SSIM) and visual quality. The model achieves superior noise suppression while maintaining high fidelity in texture and edge preservation. This work contributes to advancing real image denoising by introducing a feature-attentive framework that balances noise removal and detail retention, offering practical benefits for real-world applications.  

**Keywords**: Image denoising, feature attention, deep learning, computer vision, noise suppression, real-world images.

text: Phân quyền dựa trên Claims (Claims-based authorization) là một phương pháp quản lý quyền truy cập tài nguyên hệ thống, dựa trên thông tin người dùng được gói gọn trong các Claims. Mỗi Claim là một mẩu thông tin mô tả người dùng, ví dụ như tên, địa chỉ email, quyền hạn cụ thể, hoặc vai trò (role). Khi người dùng xác thực và đăng nhập vào hệ thống, các Claims liên quan đến họ sẽ được nhúng vào một token. Token này sau đó được sử dụng để quyết định quyền truy cập của người dùng đối với các tài nguyên khác nhau. Chẳng hạn, một Claim về quyền truy cập có thể mang giá trị "Admin" hoặc "User", và hệ thống sẽ dựa vào đó để cấp quyền. Tài nguyên hệ thống có thể được bảo vệ bằng cách định nghĩa rằng chúng yêu cầu một hoặc nhiều Claims cụ thể mới cho phép truy cập; ví dụ, một tài nguyên có thể yêu cầu người dùng phải sở hữu Claim "Admin", trong khi tài nguyên khác chỉ cần Claim "User". Tuy nhiên, việc triển khai mô hình phân quyền dựa trên Claims đặt ra những thách thức nhất định, bao gồm sự phức tạp trong quá trình thiết lập ban đầu, yêu cầu đảm bảo an toàn cho các Claims, và sự cần thiết phải duy trì tính nhất quán trong việc sử dụng Claims giữa các tài nguyên. Do hạn chế về tài nguyên và khó khăn trong việc đảm bảo tính chặt chẽ cho một dự án cá nhân, phương án phân quyền dựa trên vai trò (role-based authorization) đã được lựa chọn thay thế.

text: We present a Deep Differentiable Simplex Layer (DDSL) for neural networks for geometric deep learning. The DDSL is a differentiable layer compatible with deep neural networks for bridging simplex mesh-based geometry representations (point clouds, line mesh, triangular mesh, tetrahedral mesh) with raster images (e.g., 2D/3D grids). The DDSL uses Non-Uniform Fourier Transform (NUFT) to perform differentiable, efficient, anti-aliased rasterization of simplex-based signals. We present a complete theoretical framework for the process as well as an efficient backpropagation algorithm. Compared to previous differentiable renderers and rasterizers, the DDSL generalizes to arbitrary simplex degrees and dimensions. In particular, we explore its applications to 2D shapes and illustrate two applications of this method: (1) mesh editing and optimization guided by neural network outputs, and (2) using DDSL for a differentiable rasterization loss to facilitate end-to-end training of polygon generators. We are able to validate the effectiveness of gradient-based shape optimization with the example of airfoil optimization, and using the differentiable rasterization loss to facilitate end-to-end training, we surpass state of the art for polygonal image segmentation given ground-truth bounding boxes.

Mặc dù hệ thống này đã được trang bị module quản lý dự án, nhưng module hiện tại vẫn còn một số tồn tại đáng kể; cụ thể, hệ thống DEClan chưa hỗ trợ các chức năng thiết yếu như quản lý các giai đoạn trong dự án, quản lý các cột mốc quan trọng, và khả năng tìm kiếm dự án hoặc công việc trong dự án dựa trên các thuộc tính đặc thù của chúng. text: Exploration in episodic Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) with complex, high-dimensional observations can be made tractable by leveraging the assumption that these observations are generated from a small set of latent states. By introducing a framework that iteratively estimates a decoding function from observations to latent states through a combination of regression and clustering procedures, it becomes possible to inductively improve the mapping accuracy; previously inferred latent states are used to label subsequent regression tasks, progressively refining the decoding process. This approach facilitates the design of effective exploration policies that are informed by the underlying latent structure of the environment rather than the raw observation space. Theoretical analysis establishes finite-sample guarantees for both the learned state decoding function and the resulting exploration strategies, ensuring robust performance even with limited data. Empirical results on challenging exploration benchmarks demonstrate that this method achieves exponential improvements over standard Q-learning algorithms with naïve exploration strategies, and importantly, outperforms even Q-learning variants that have privileged access to the latent state information, thereby highlighting the practical and theoretical advantages of structured exploration in environments with rich observations.

text: This paper introduces ReMix, a novel approach to addressing class imbalance in deep learning through calibrated resampling. The objective is to develop a method that can effectively handle imbalanced datasets, where one class has a significantly larger number of instances than others, leading to biased models. ReMix achieves this by employing a resampling strategy that adaptively adjusts the sampling rates for each class, ensuring that the model is exposed to a balanced representation of all classes during training. The approach utilizes a calibration mechanism to prevent overfitting to the majority class, while also preserving the underlying data distribution. Experimental results demonstrate that ReMix outperforms state-of-the-art class imbalance techniques, achieving improved accuracy and F1-scores on several benchmark datasets. The key contributions of this work include a calibrated resampling algorithm, an adaptive sampling rate adjustment mechanism, and a comprehensive evaluation framework for class imbalance methods. ReMix has significant implications for real-world applications, such as image classification, natural language processing, and medical diagnosis, where class imbalance is a common challenge. Keywords: class imbalance, deep learning, resampling, calibration, adaptive sampling.

text: Multi-party computation (MPC) -Web3Auth uses MPC to provide a secure and private way for users to share their keys. This allows users to collaborate on dapps without having to reveal their private keys. MPC is a cryptographic protocol that allows multiple parties to jointly compute a function without revealing their individual inputs. This makes it a very secure way for users to share their keys, as only the final result of the computation is revealed. In the context of Web3Auth, MPC ensures that sensitive cryptographic operations can be performed collectively by multiple participants, mitigating the risks associated with single points of failure and enhancing the overall security posture of decentralized applications. By leveraging MPC, Web3Auth enables a robust mechanism for key management that aligns with the decentralized ethos of Web3, where trust is distributed rather than centralized. This approach not only preserves user privacy but also facilitates seamless interaction across various dapps by maintaining the confidentiality of private keys throughout the authentication process. Consequently, the integration of MPC within Web3Auth exemplifies an innovative application of cryptographic techniques to address the challenges of secure identity management in decentralized environments.

text: Task-Agnostic Morphology Evolution (TAME) is a novel approach for designing agent morphologies in reinforcement learning by focusing on inherent capabilities rather than specific task performance. Traditional methods for co-adapting agent morphology and behavior often rely on task-specific reward signals, leading to significant computational overhead from policy optimization and resulting in morphologies that are specialized and lack generalizability. TAME circumvents these challenges by evolving morphologies without predefined tasks or rewards. This is achieved by applying randomly sampled action primitives to a population of agents and employing an information-theoretic objective for evaluation. This objective ranks agents based on their ability to reach diverse environmental states and the causality of their actions. Empirical demonstrations across 2D, 3D, and manipulation environments show that TAME can evolve morphologies matching the multi-task performance of those learned via task-supervised algorithms, highlighting its potential for developing more versatile and adaptable agents.

text: Deep learning, characterized by rapid progress and significant successes across a wide spectrum of applications, is increasingly being deployed in safety-critical environments. However, deep neural networks (DNNs) have recently been shown to be vulnerable to meticulously crafted input samples, termed adversarial examples. These adversarial examples, often imperceptible to humans, can readily deceive DNNs during testing or deployment phases, and this vulnerability constitutes a significant risk to the application of DNNs in safety-critical domains. Consequently, research into attacks leveraging, and defenses against, adversarial examples has garnered considerable attention. This paper reviews recent findings concerning adversarial examples in the context of DNNs, summarizes methods for their generation, and proposes a taxonomy for these methods. Within this taxonomic framework, applications of adversarial examples are investigated. Furthermore, we elaborate on countermeasures against such examples and explore the associated challenges and potential solutions.

text: Active contour models are extensively utilized in image segmentation, with the level set method (LSM) commonly employed to solve these models by implicitly defining the contour through a level set function. Nevertheless, LSM presents challenges such as high computational burden and numerical instability, often necessitating the use of additional regularization terms or re-initialization techniques. This paper introduces a novel representation for geodesic active contours and derives an efficient algorithm, termed the iterative convolution-thresholding method (ICTM), which implicitly represents contours using characteristic functions. Compared to LSM, the ICTM is significantly simpler and more efficient, while also retaining most of the desired features found in level set-based methods. Extensive experiments conducted on diverse image datasets, including 2D synthetic, 2D ultrasound, 3D CT, and 3D MR images for nodule, organ, and lesion segmentation, confirm that the proposed method not only achieves segmentation results comparable to or even better than LSM but also delivers substantial acceleration.

text:
This paper presents a novel approach for 3D parametric wireframe extraction using distance fields, addressing the challenge of accurately reconstructing structured 3D models from complex scenes. The proposed method leverages distance fields to represent geometric relationships between objects, enabling precise identification of edges, junctions, and connectivity in 3D space. A hybrid algorithm combining distance field computation with parametric optimization is introduced to extract wireframe structures efficiently. Experimental results demonstrate the method's robustness in handling noisy and incomplete data, outperforming traditional edge-detection and reconstruction techniques in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The approach achieves significant improvements in preserving topological consistency and geometric fidelity, making it suitable for applications in computer-aided design (CAD), robotics, and augmented reality. This work contributes a scalable and adaptable framework for 3D wireframe extraction, offering potential advancements in automated 3D modeling and scene understanding.  

**Keywords**: 3D reconstruction, wireframe extraction, distance fields, parametric optimization, geometric modeling, CAD.

text:
In the era of data-driven machine learning, fine-tuning pre-trained models has become a standard approach for adapting large-scale models to specific tasks. However, this method often struggles when applied to small datasets, leading to overfitting and suboptimal performance. This paper introduces a novel modular approach to learning on small data, which goes beyond traditional fine-tuning by leveraging task-specific modules that can be dynamically integrated into pre-trained models. The proposed method involves decomposing the learning process into reusable components, enabling efficient adaptation with minimal data while preserving the generalization capabilities of the base model. Experiments across multiple domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, demonstrate that our approach outperforms conventional fine-tuning techniques in terms of accuracy and robustness, particularly in low-data regimes. The modular framework also offers interpretability and flexibility, allowing for seamless integration of domain-specific knowledge. This research contributes a scalable and practical solution for small-data learning, with potential applications in areas such as personalized AI, medical diagnostics, and resource-constrained environments.  

**Keywords**: small-data learning, modular learning, fine-tuning, pre-trained models, machine learning, AI adaptation.

text:
Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have achieved remarkable success across various applications, but their computational and memory demands often hinder real-time execution on resource-constrained mobile devices. Weight pruning, a technique to reduce model size and computational overhead, has emerged as a promising solution. However, existing pruning methods often fail to achieve the desired sparsity patterns that align with hardware acceleration capabilities, limiting their practical deployment. This paper introduces **PCONV**, a novel pruning framework designed to address this gap by identifying and enforcing the "missing but desirable" sparsity in DNN weight pruning. PCONV leverages a structured pruning approach that optimizes for both sparsity and hardware efficiency, ensuring compatibility with mobile device architectures. Through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets and models, we demonstrate that PCONV achieves significant reductions in model size and inference latency while maintaining competitive accuracy. Compared to state-of-the-art pruning methods, PCONV improves real-time execution performance by up to 30% on mobile devices, making it a practical solution for deploying DNNs in resource-constrained environments. This work contributes a scalable and hardware-aware pruning framework, paving the way for efficient DNN deployment in mobile and edge computing scenarios.  

**Keywords**: Deep Neural Networks, Weight Pruning, Sparsity, Mobile Devices, Real-time Execution, Hardware Efficiency, PCONV.

text:
Neural network optimization is a cornerstone of modern machine learning, yet it often encounters challenges related to nondeterminism and instability during training. This paper investigates the root causes of these phenomena and their impact on model performance and reproducibility. We propose a systematic approach to analyze the sources of nondeterminism, including random initialization, stochastic gradient descent (SGD) dynamics, and hardware-level variations. Through extensive experiments, we evaluate the effects of these factors on convergence behavior and model accuracy across diverse architectures and datasets. Our findings reveal that nondeterminism can lead to significant performance variability, even under identical training conditions. To address this, we introduce a novel stabilization technique that mitigates instability while preserving model expressiveness. The proposed method demonstrates improved convergence consistency and robustness across multiple benchmarks, outperforming existing approaches. This research provides valuable insights into the challenges of neural network optimization and offers practical solutions for enhancing training stability, with implications for applications requiring high reliability, such as autonomous systems and healthcare.  

**Keywords**: neural networks, optimization, nondeterminism, instability, stochastic gradient descent, reproducibility, machine learning.

text: Machine learning models are often trained on data from one distribution and deployed on others. So it becomes important to design models that are robust to distribution shifts. Most of the existing work focuses on optimizing for either adversarial shifts or interventional shifts. Adversarial methods lack expressivity in representing plausible shifts as they consider shifts to joint distributions in the data. Interventional methods allow more expressivity but provide robustness to unbounded shifts, resulting in overly conservative models. In this work, we combine the complementary strengths of the two approaches and propose a new formulation, RISe, for designing robust models against a set of distribution shifts that are at the intersection of adversarial and interventional shifts. We employ the distributionally robust optimization framework to optimize the resulting objective in both supervised and reinforcement learning settings. Extensive experimentation with synthetic and real world datasets from healthcare demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach.

text: This paper presents factors influencing the strength of reconstructed embankment materials derived from dredged sludge in Hanoi City (Granular Fill Material: GFM). Based on laboratory experiments, the study examines several factors affecting the strength of the recycled material, including mixing methods, cement and polymer content, and cement type. In the experiments, Tay Ho sludge (B), identified as non-toxic, was dewatered to moisture content within the range [WP; WL], then mixed with cement (X) and polymer (P). The resultant product exhibited a granular form; however, due to the high moisture content, the granules retained plasticity, facilitating sample preparation for testing. To simplify the experiments while adequately assessing factors influencing GFM strength, unconfined triaxial compression tests with free lateral expansion were selected for preliminary strength evaluation. Results indicate that the mixing method significantly affects GFM strength development. For the same mixing ratio, samples mixed as (B+X) first and then P yielded higher strength values than other mixing approaches. Additionally, the strength of GFM samples increased proportionally with cement content; with low cement contents ranging from 5% to 10%, GFM samples attained unconfined compressive strengths from 170.8 kPa to 262.05 kPa, satisfactorily meeting embankment material requirements. Furthermore, the chemical composition of cement, particularly CaO, SO3, and Al2O3 content, notably influenced GFM strength; experimental results demonstrated that soil strength was inversely proportional to CaO content and directly proportional to Al2O3 and SO3 contents.

text: Unsupervised representation learning techniques, such as word embeddings, have significantly impacted natural language processing. Analogous techniques, however, are not yet commonplace in 3D vision, despite physical 3D spaces exhibiting a semantic structure comparable to textual corpora: just as words are surrounded by semantically related words, objects are typically surrounded by other objects similar in concept and usage. This work leverages this inherent structural parallelism to learn semantically meaningful, low-dimensional vector representations of objects by applying an unsupervised algorithm to mine a dataset of scanned 3D spaces. Objects, represented as point clouds—a flexible and general representation for 3D data—are subsequently encoded into these vector representations. We demonstrate that incorporating contextual information through our method enhances a clustering algorithm's ability to distinguish between different semantic classes. Furthermore, interpolation experiments confirm that our algorithm yields continuous and meaningful object embeddings.

text: Image correspondence detection through feature matching is crucial for many computer vision tasks, relying on efficient interest point (keypoint) detection and feature description. This research investigates the performance of eight binary descriptors (AKAZE, BoostDesc, BRIEF, BRISK, FREAK, LATCH, LUCID, ORB) and eight interest point detectors (AGAST, AKAZE, BRISK, FAST, HarrisLaplace, KAZE, ORB, StarDetector). The study decouples the detection and description phases, evaluating pairwise combinations on a standard dataset under various image transformations. Key observations indicate that FAST, AGAST, and ORB detectors were computationally efficient and detected more keypoints. AKAZE and KAZE detectors demonstrated superior performance under photometric variations, whereas the ORB detector exhibited greater robustness to geometric changes. Descriptors generally achieved better results when coupled with KAZE and AKAZE detectors. In terms of speed, BRIEF, LUCID, and ORB descriptors were notable. However, most descriptors performed suboptimally under geometric transformations, with only BRISK, FREAK, and AKAZE showing moderate resilience.

text: This paper introduces an ante-hoc approach to induce semantic grouping of latent concepts for explanations, addressing the need for transparency and interpretability in complex models. Our objective is to develop a methodology that enables the discovery of meaningful, high-level abstractions from latent representations, facilitating a deeper understanding of model decisions. We propose a novel framework that leverages a combination of dimensionality reduction and clustering techniques to identify semantically coherent groups of latent concepts. Our approach is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its ability to uncover insightful explanations and improve model interpretability. The results show that our method outperforms existing post-hoc explanation techniques in terms of accuracy and consistency. This research contributes to the development of more transparent and trustworthy AI systems, with potential applications in areas such as explainable AI, feature attribution, and model debugging. Key keywords: explainable AI, latent concepts, semantic grouping, ante-hoc explanations, model interpretability.

text: When tokens are signed with public/private key pairs, the signature also confirms that only the party with the private key signed it. This cryptographic assurance is fundamental for establishing both data integrity and non-repudiation within a software system. The corresponding public key allows any verifier to computationally confirm that the token's content remains unaltered since its creation and that it authentically originates from the asserted source. In the context of a software system for teaching and learning English, this mechanism is crucial for building a robust trust framework. It directly secures critical operations such as user authentication, protection of sensitive personal data, and verifiable tracking of academic progress. For instance, digitally signed user session tokens prevent unauthorized access, while signed records of completed assignments provide irrefutable proof of their authenticity and integrity, deterring tampering. This robust security paradigm ensures all system interactions, from initial login to assessment result transmission, maintain high trustworthiness and verifiability, essential for a reliable online learning environment.

text: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) often suffers from limited resolution due to physical, technological, and economic constraints. Super-resolution (SR) techniques can enhance MRI image quality, but traditional interpolation-based methods reduce diagnostic accuracy. To address the increasing demand for high-quality brain images, we propose an SR method that leverages overcomplete dictionaries and the inherent self-similarity within images to reconstruct high-resolution (HR) images from single low-resolution (LR) inputs. Our approach exploits nonlocal similarity by searching for similar blocks throughout the image and introduces a joint reconstruction framework based on compressive sensing (CS) with sparsity and similarity constraints. Specifically, we first classify image blocks into smooth, texture, and edge categories using a measurement domain-based dictionary classification method, then train corresponding dictionaries for each category. During reconstruction, we employ the CS algorithm, incorporating both nonlocal similarity and sparsity constraints to recover HR brain MRI images. text: In this research, the architectural design primarily adheres to Domain-Driven Design (DDD) principles, focusing predominantly on the Domain and Application layers, with less emphasis on the Infrastructure and Presentation layers. The project's architecture has been adapted to align with the ABP framework. Within this structure, the Domain layer encompasses several critical components: the `Domain` project, `Domain.Shared`, `DbMigrator`, and the `MongoDB` project. Specifically, the `DbMigrator` layer is responsible for database migrations and initial data seeding. The `MongoDB` project establishes the database context and defines the repository interface. This repository serves as an essential intermediary for retrieving data associated with entities, thereby significantly reducing the business model's dependency on specific storage technologies and enhancing the flexibility for technological upgrades and replacements. The `Domain` project contains the core entities and provides the implementation of the repository interface defined within the `MongoDB` project, while `Domain.Shared` aggregates constants and enumerations accessible across all layers. Subsequently, the Application layer comprises the `Application` and `Application.Contract` components. Finally, the HTTP layer, including `Http.Api`, `Http.Client`, and `Http.Host`, is designed to provide the necessary environment for client applications to invoke remote HTTP services.

text: To improve the performance of deep learning, mixup has been proposed to force the neural networks favoring simple linear behaviors in-between training samples. Performing mixup for transfer learning with pre-trained models however is not that simple, a high capacity pre-trained model with a large fully-connected (FC) layer could easily overfit to the target dataset even with samples-to-labels mixed up. In this work, we propose SMILE - Self-Distilled Mixup for EffIcient Transfer LEarning. With mixed images as inputs, SMILE regularizes the outputs of CNN feature extractors to learn from the mixed feature vectors of inputs (sample-to-feature mixup), in addition to the mixed labels. Specifically, SMILE incorporates a mean teacher, inherited from the pre-trained model, to provide the feature vectors of input samples in a self-distilling fashion, and mixes up the feature vectors accordingly via a novel triplet regularizer. The triple regularizer balances the mixup effects in both feature and label spaces while bounding the linearity in-between samples for pre-training tasks. Extensive experiments have been done to verify the performance improvement made by SMILE, in comparisons with a wide spectrum of transfer learning algorithms, including fine-tuning, L2-SP, DELTA, and RIFLE, even with mixup strategies combined. Ablation studies show that the vanilla sample-to-label mixup strategies could marginally increase the linearity in-between training samples but lack of generalizability, while SMILE significantly improve the mixup effects in both label and feature spaces with both training and testing datasets. The empirical observations backup our design intuition and purposes.

text:
The interpretability of artificial neural networks (ANNs) has emerged as a critical challenge in the field of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly as these models grow in complexity and are increasingly deployed in high-stakes applications. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of existing approaches, techniques, and frameworks aimed at enhancing the interpretability of ANNs. We begin by defining the key challenges associated with understanding and explaining the decision-making processes of neural networks, including issues related to transparency, trust, and accountability. Next, we categorize and analyze a wide range of interpretability methods, such as feature attribution, model simplification, and post-hoc explanation techniques, while highlighting their strengths and limitations. Our findings reveal that while significant progress has been made, there remains a need for more robust and scalable solutions that balance interpretability with model performance. The survey concludes by identifying open research questions and proposing future directions, including the integration of interpretability into the design of neural architectures and the development of standardized evaluation metrics. This work aims to provide researchers and practitioners with a structured overview of the field, fostering advancements in the development of interpretable and trustworthy AI systems.  

**Keywords**: artificial neural networks, interpretability, explainable AI, feature attribution, model transparency, post-hoc explanations.

Evaluation on the KITTI Vision Benchmark Suite demonstrates that our model achieves performance comparable to DeepCLR [1], despite utilizing only about 3.56% of its network parameters. text:
Moving object detection is a critical task in computer vision with applications in surveillance, autonomous driving, and video analysis. This paper addresses the challenge of accurately identifying moving objects in complex scenes, particularly in the presence of dynamic backgrounds and occlusions. We propose a novel approach based on detecting contiguous outliers in the low-rank representation of video frames. By leveraging the inherent low-rank structure of background scenes and the sparse nature of moving objects, our method effectively separates foreground objects from the background. The proposed algorithm employs robust principal component analysis (RPCA) to decompose video frames into low-rank and sparse components, followed by a contiguous outlier detection mechanism to refine the detection of moving objects. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness, particularly in scenarios with illumination changes and camera motion. The proposed method achieves a significant reduction in false positives while maintaining high detection rates. This work contributes to advancing the field of moving object detection by introducing a computationally efficient and highly accurate framework, with potential applications in real-time video processing and intelligent surveillance systems.  

**Keywords**: moving object detection, low-rank representation, contiguous outliers, robust principal component analysis (RPCA), video analysis, computer vision.

text: Reinforcement learning is situated at the crossroads of multiple complex challenges, as many relevant applications involve vast state spaces that necessitate function approximation for feasible computation. Furthermore, since the agent typically has access to only a single sequence of experiences to assess numerous potential strategies, it is essential to utilize algorithms capable of off-policy learning. Yet, combining off-policy learning with function approximation can cause temporal difference methods to diverge. While recent advancements in gradient-based temporal difference approaches offer a route to stability, they often require costly hyperparameter adjustments. Simultaneously, developments in online learning have yielded parameter-free techniques that provide minimax optimal guarantees up to logarithmic terms, but their integration into reinforcement learning remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we bridge these approaches by developing parameter-free, gradient-based temporal difference algorithms. These algorithms operate in linear time and provide high-probability convergence guarantees comparable to those of GTD2, up to logarithmic factors. Our empirical results show that these methods sustain strong prediction performance relative to fully-tuned baselines, all without the need for tuning.

text: Deep generative architectures provide a way to model not only images but also complex, 3-dimensional objects, such as point clouds. In this work, we present a novel method to obtain meaningful representations of 3D shapes that can be used for challenging tasks including 3D points generation, reconstruction, compression, and clustering. Contrary to existing methods for 3D point cloud generation that train separate decoupled models for representation learning and generation, our approach is the first end-to-end solution that allows to simultaneously learn a latent space of representation and generate 3D shape out of it. Moreover, our model is capable of learning meaningful compact binary descriptors with adversarial training conducted on a latent space. To achieve this goal, we extend a deep Adversarial Autoencoder model (AAE) to accept 3D input and create 3D output. Thanks to our end-to-end training regime, the resulting method called 3D Adversarial Autoencoder (3dAAE) obtains either binary or continuous latent space that covers a much wider portion of training data distribution. Finally, our quantitative evaluation shows that 3dAAE provides state-of-the-art results for 3D points clustering and 3D object retrieval.

Để tránh xung đột giữa các AGV, thuật toán này duy trì một danh sách các khu vực với các khoảng thời gian đã được sử dụng bởi các AGV dựa trên các quỹ đạo đã được thiết lập, cùng với một danh sách các khoảng thời gian trống có sẵn để các AGV sử dụng khu vực. Thuật toán định tuyến AGV thông qua một đồ thị, trong đó các đỉnh đại diện cho khu vực cùng với các khoảng thời gian trống của khu vực đó, và các cạnh đại diện cho đường nối giữa các khu vực cùng với khả năng liên kết giữa các khoảng thời gian trống của hai khu vực kề nhau. Điều này có nghĩa là thuật toán sẽ tìm kiếm một con đường đi qua các khoảng thời gian trống của các khu vực để đảm bảo rằng AGV không bị xung đột với các AGV khác. Nói cách khác, thuật toán của Km và Tanchoco giúp định tuyến đường đi cho các AGV một cách an toàn và hiệu quả bằng cách sử dụng thông tin về các khoảng thời gian đã được sử dụng và các khoảng thời gian trống của các khu vực để tránh xung đột giữa các AGV. Độ phức tạp tính toán trong trường hợp xấu nhất của phương pháp này là O(A^4Z^2), trong đó A là số lượng AGV và Z là số khu vực. Do đó, cách tiếp cận này phù hợp hơn cho các hệ thống nhỏ với một số lượng ít AGV. Ter Mors, Zutt và Wtteveen đã trình bày một phiên bản cải tiến của thuật toán này với độ phức tạp thấp hơn là O(AZlog(AZ) + AZ^2).

text: This paper addresses the challenge of out-of-distribution (OOD) detection in deep generative models (DGMs), which paradoxically can assign higher probabilities to OOD images than to those from the training distribution. The authors attribute this counterintuitive behavior to model misestimation rather than a fundamental limitation of likelihood-based detection. They rigorously prove that without explicit assumptions about relevant out-distributions, no OOD detection method can outperform random chance. The work critically examines the typical set hypothesis, which posits that OOD samples may reside in high-likelihood regions and suggests redefining OOD detection around the data distribution's typical set. The study exposes issues arising from assuming support overlap between in- and out-distributions and demonstrates the arbitrariness of the typical set in this context. Key findings indicate that estimation error, even when minimal, can cause OOD detection failures, challenging current assumptions and informing directions for future research in deep generative modeling and OOD detection. text: The core of the database is the `Content` table, which serves as the primary repository for crawled articles from various news websites, storing their essential metadata and raw data necessary for subsequent processing by other modules. Complementing this, the `MainContentEntity` table stores interpretable outputs generated by the Named Entity Recognition module, detailing identified entities from the article text, such as their type (e.g., PERSON, ORGANIZATION, LOCATION) and their precise textual span, enriching the raw content with structured semantic information for deeper analysis. Building upon this, the `EntitySentiment` table stores interpretable outputs from the Sentiment Analysis module, linking sentiment scores and labels (e.g., "Positive", "Negative", "Neutral") directly to specific entities identified in the `MainContentEntity` table or to the article as a whole, providing crucial insights into the emotional tone surrounding particular subjects or events. For user-defined tracking, `KeywordFollowingCluster` and `KeywordFollowingClusterKeyword` work in conjunction to store keyword clusters that users follow, with `KeywordFollowingCluster` defining the overarching user-created topic clusters and `KeywordFollowingClusterKeyword` mapping individual relevant keywords to these clusters, thereby enabling personalized monitoring of specific news narratives or themes across diverse sources. Finally, `DailyTopKeywords` and `DailyOverallSentiment` store aggregated results, such as daily trending keywords based on frequency counts and overall sentiment scores for various topics or entities, respectively, offering concise daily summaries. text:
The rapid advancement of automotive cyber-physical systems (CPS) has heightened the demand for efficient and accurate scene understanding to ensure safety and performance. This paper addresses the challenge of deploying deep neural networks (DNNs) in resource-constrained automotive environments, where computational efficiency is critical. We propose a novel framework that accelerates DNN inference while maintaining high accuracy for tasks such as object detection, semantic segmentation, and trajectory prediction. Our approach integrates model compression techniques, including quantization and pruning, with hardware-aware optimizations tailored for embedded systems. Additionally, we introduce a lightweight attention mechanism to enhance feature extraction without significantly increasing computational overhead. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework achieves a 40% reduction in inference time and a 30% decrease in memory usage compared to state-of-the-art models, while maintaining competitive accuracy on benchmark datasets. The proposed solution is validated in real-world automotive CPS scenarios, showcasing its practicality for deployment in autonomous vehicles and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). This work contributes to the field by bridging the gap between high-performance DNNs and the stringent resource constraints of automotive CPS, paving the way for safer and more efficient intelligent transportation systems.  

**Keywords**: deep neural networks, automotive cyber-physical systems, model compression, scene understanding, embedded systems, autonomous vehicles.

text: While numerous techniques have been recently proposed to generate counterfactual explanations for the predictions of opaque black-box systems, significantly less focus has been dedicated to examining the uncertainty of these explanations. This oversight becomes particularly critical in high-stakes scenarios, where uncertain and misleading explanations could lead to severe consequences, such as in medical diagnosis and treatment planning. Additionally, assessing whether the generated explanations are well-grounded in the training data and sensitive to distributional shifts is often challenging. This paper proposes several practical solutions to address these issues by establishing novel connections with other research areas in explainability, such as trust scores, and uncertainty estimation, such as Monte Carlo Dropout. Two experiments are conducted to demonstrate the utility of our proposed solutions.

text: This paper addresses the challenge of discovering input-output relationships in sequence-to-sequence models, particularly for computer vision tasks like action recognition, where static inputs complicate modeling. We propose the Hierarchical Multi-scale Attention Network (HM-AN), a novel architecture that combines the Hierarchical Multi-scale RNN (HM-RNN) with an attention mechanism. HM-AN employs Gumbel-softmax for stochastic hard attention and temporal boundary detection, enhanced by an adaptive temperature training method to mitigate sensitivity. Experimental results demonstrate HM-AN's improved performance over LSTM with attention on action recognition. Furthermore, visualizations confirm HM-AN's capability to capture both relevant image attention regions and hierarchical temporal structures.

text:
Dung dịch dinh dưỡng đóng vai trò quan trọng trong quá trình sinh trưởng, phát triển và chất lượng của thực vật. Thiết kế và đánh giá ảnh hưởng của dung dịch dinh dưỡng đến sinh trưởng, phát triển và chất lượng của thực vật là một vấn đề được nhiều nhà nghiên cứu quan tâm.

Dung dịch dinh dưỡng cung cấp cho thực vật các chất dinh dưỡng cần thiết như nitơ, phốt pho, kali, canxi, magie, sắt, mangan, bo, đồng, kẽm, molypden, boron, clorua, silicat, và các chất dinh dưỡng khác. Các chất dinh dưỡng này giúp thực vật phát triển khỏe mạnh, tăng trưởng nhanh chóng và tăng sản lượng.

text: Integrating Wikipedia content with mobile and augmented reality in urban settings offers novel interaction paradigms for learning, communication, and knowledge exchange within urban-focused user communities. To achieve this, a mobile application was developed for recognizing notable Wikipedia-featured sites. This application leverages a deep neural network, meticulously trained on extensive crowd-sourced imagery encompassing diverse urban points of interest like architectural landmarks, public sculptures, and cultural institutions. A comprehensive end-to-end pipeline details systematic data collection, robust model training, and thorough evaluation of the application across both online simulations and authentic real-world environments. Challenges inherent in urban site recognition, stemming from visual ambiguities among classified entities and environmental noise, are systematically addressed. The integration of mobile contextual data, such as user geospatial coordinates, device orientation, and attention patterns, significantly mitigates these difficulties. Furthermore, an innovative unsupervised learning technique is presented to de-noise crowd-sourced visual data, demonstrably improving overall classification performance.

text: The deep Q-network (DQN) and return-based reinforcement learning are two promising algorithms introduced in recent years, with DQN advancing complex sequential decision problems and return-based algorithms excelling at utilizing sample trajectories. In this paper, we present a general framework, named R-DQN, that integrates DQN with most return-based reinforcement learning algorithms. We demonstrate that incorporating return-based reinforcement learning significantly enhances the performance of traditional DQN. To further improve R-DQN, we develop a strategy based on two measurements that qualitatively assess policy discrepancy and provide bounds for these measurements within the proposed framework. We show that algorithms employing our strategy can accurately represent the trace coefficient and better approximate returns. Experiments on several representative tasks from the OpenAI Gym library confirm the effectiveness of the proposed measurements, with results indicating that algorithms using our strategy surpass state-of-the-art methods.

text: This research investigates user association, which involves optimally assigning user equipment to base stations to achieve targeted network performance. We specifically address the knowledge transferability of association policies, as traditional non-trivial user association schemes are often scenario- or deployment-specific, necessitating policy re-design or re-learning when user numbers or positions change. In contrast, transferability enables a single user association policy, developed for a particular scenario, to be applied to different user deployments without significant re-learning or re-design, thereby substantially reducing computational and management complexity. To achieve this transferability, we first formulate user association as a multi-agent reinforcement learning problem. Subsequently, we propose a novel distributed policy network architecture, based on a neural attention mechanism specifically designed for this context, which is transferable among users with zero-shot generalization capability, meaning it requires no additional training. Numerical results confirm our solution's effectiveness in terms of overall network communication rate, demonstrating superior performance over centralized benchmarks, even when the user count doubles compared to the initial training point.

text: Unsupervised learning-based depth estimation methods have garnered increasing attention due to their ability to operate without extensive densely labeled training data, which are often difficult to obtain. In this paper, we present a novel unsupervised monocular video depth estimation approach for natural scenes, building upon the state-of-the-art framework of Zhou et al., which jointly estimates depth and camera motion. Our method advances beyond the baseline in three key aspects: (1) we introduce an additional supervisory signal by incorporating left-right binocular image reconstruction loss based on estimated disparities, enabling the reconstruction of the left frame using both temporal and stereo right frames; (2) the network is trained with a combination of two view synthesis losses and left-right disparity consistency regularization to jointly estimate depth and camera pose; and (3) we employ edge-aware smooth L2 regularization to refine the depth map while preserving target contours. Extensive experiments conducted on the KITTI autonomous driving dataset and the Make3D dataset demonstrate the superiority of our algorithm in training efficiency, achieving competitive results with the baseline using only 60% of the training data. Furthermore, our method outperforms classical supervised approaches that rely on ground truth depth or known camera poses for training.

text: Trained machine learning models are increasingly employed in critical sectors such as law enforcement, medicine, education, and employment, necessitating clear documentation of their performance characteristics to ensure appropriate usage. The introduction of model cards provides a structured framework for transparent model reporting, enhancing understanding of model performance across various conditions, including cultural, demographic, and intersectional groups relevant to specific application domains. These concise documents accompany trained models, detailing benchmarked evaluations and specifying the context and intended use cases, along with the procedures employed for performance assessment. Although the focus is primarily on human-centered models within computer vision and natural language processing, the model card framework is applicable to any trained machine learning model. By offering documentation for two supervised models—one for detecting smiling faces in images and another for identifying toxic comments in text—the paper underscores the potential of model cards to foster responsible democratization of AI technology. This approach aims to increase transparency, encouraging developers to release models with comprehensive evaluations and relevant documentation, ultimately enhancing the reliability and accountability of machine learning applications in diverse fields.

text: Machine learning has significantly enhanced clinical analysis, yet the substantial labeled data requirements for supervised learning render model development both time- and resource-intensive. Most dense clinical information exists in narrative reports, which present unique challenges for conventional model development due to their linguistic complexity. In this study, we developed a model pipeline utilizing an unsupervised approach to train an encoder-language model—a recurrent neural network—to generate document encodings. These encodings serve as features for a decoder-classifier model that requires substantially fewer labeled examples to accurately distinguish between fine-grained disease categories. The language model was pretrained on 218,159 unlabeled radiology reports from the Massachusetts General Hospital Radiology Department, achieving a final loss of 1.62. Classification models were subsequently trained on three labeled head CT datasets: large vessel occlusion (n=1,403), acute ischemic stroke (n=331), and intracranial hemorrhage (n=4,350). The models identified diverse findings directly from radiology report text, resulting in AUCs of 0.98, 0.95, and 0.99 for large vessel occlusion, acute ischemic stroke, and intracranial hemorrhage, respectively. The resulting encodings can be integrated with imaging data, enabling the development of models capable of processing multiple modalities. This approach facilitates rapid model development and seamless incorporation of textual data, thereby making clinical reports a more practical and effective input for comprehensive deep learning models in medicine.

text: Specifically, we integrate sparse attention mechanisms and learnable pooling operators that maintain the graph's inherent sparsity throughout the coarsening process, thus significantly reducing both memory consumption and computational overhead. This approach enables end-to-end training of deep hierarchical graph neural networks that dynamically adapt to the underlying graph structure, capturing multi-scale features more effectively than previous global pooling methods. Experimental evaluations on datasets such as PROTEINS, D&D, and IMDB-BINARY illustrate that our model not only matches or exceeds the performance of state-of-the-art methods but also scales efficiently to larger graphs, a critical requirement for real-world applications. Furthermore, ablation studies reveal the importance of preserving sparsity and the benefits of learnable coarsening strategies over fixed heuristics. These findings underscore the potential of sparse, differentiable graph coarsening as a foundational building block in graph representation learning and motivate further exploration into scalable architectures for complex graph-structured data.

text:
Keyword spotting (KWS) is a critical task in speech recognition systems, enabling efficient detection of specific words or phrases within audio streams. This paper introduces a novel approach to enhance KWS performance by incorporating orthogonality constraints into multi-head attention mechanisms. The proposed method, Orthogonality Constrained Multi-Head Attention (OC-MHA), aims to improve the diversity and interpretability of attention heads, addressing the redundancy issue commonly observed in traditional multi-head attention architectures.  

The OC-MHA framework enforces orthogonality among attention heads during training, ensuring that each head captures distinct and complementary features from the input data. This is achieved through a regularization term added to the loss function, which minimizes the correlation between attention head outputs. Experiments were conducted on benchmark KWS datasets, comparing the proposed method against standard multi-head attention and other state-of-the-art approaches. Results demonstrate that OC-MHA achieves superior accuracy and robustness, particularly in noisy environments, while maintaining computational efficiency.  

The findings highlight the importance of attention head diversity in KWS tasks and provide a scalable solution for improving speech recognition systems. The proposed method not only advances the state-of-the-art in KWS but also offers broader implications for other sequence modeling tasks, such as natural language processing and time-series analysis.  

**Keywords**: Keyword Spotting, Multi-Head Attention, Orthogonality Constraints, Speech Recognition, Attention Mechanisms.
label: deepseek-text

text: Building upon this definition, the concept of s-run length limited (RLL) sequences serves as a foundational element in the construction of efficient coding schemes for quantum communication systems. In particular, s-RLL sequences are utilized to mitigate the effects of long runs of identical symbols, which can lead to increased error rates and synchronization challenges in both classical and quantum channels. By constraining the maximum run length of 0’s to s, as stated in Definition 6, the resulting sequences exhibit desirable autocorrelation properties and improved resilience against noise and signal degradation. Furthermore, s-RLL constraints facilitate the design of error-correcting codes that are compatible with the physical limitations of quantum memories and transmission lines, where decoherence and loss are critical issues. In the context of de Bruijn sequences, integrating s-RLL constraints requires careful combinatorial analysis to ensure that every possible substring of a specified length appears exactly once while adhering to the run length limitation. This integration often leads to novel constructions and algorithmic strategies, such as modified greedy algorithms or graph-based approaches, which balance the competing demands of sequence completeness and run length restriction (see Figure A). Consequently, s-RLL de Bruijn sequences have emerged as promising candidates for quantum key distribution protocols and other secure communication applications, where both sequence uniqueness and error robustness are paramount considerations.

The approach is based on a flexible and efficient algorithm that enables the network to selectively focus on relevant features and suppress irrelevant ones. The proposed method achieves significant improvements in terms of accuracy and robustness, making it a promising technique for computer vision applications. Key contributions of this work include the introduction of a large sampling field for dynamic filtering, the development of an efficient and flexible algorithm for feature extraction, and the demonstration of the approach's effectiveness in various vision tasks. text: We advance the task of composed image retrieval, where a query is formed by combining an image with a brief textual instruction describing the desired modification. Prior approaches have been largely restricted to simple images from limited domains, like fashion items, thereby constraining the exploration of advanced visual reasoning in diverse and complex image-language contexts. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the Compose Image Retrieval on Real-life images (CIRR) dataset, comprising more than 36,000 pairs of crowd-sourced, open-domain images alongside human-authored modification descriptions. To adapt existing techniques for broader domains, we present CIRPLANT, a transformer-based model that utilizes extensive pre-trained vision-and-language (V&L) representations to adjust visual features according to natural language cues. Retrieval is accomplished through nearest neighbor search in the modified feature space. Our results show that, despite its straightforward design, CIRPLANT surpasses previous methods on open-domain image retrieval and achieves state-of-the-art performance on established specialized datasets, such as those in the fashion domain. With the introduction of CIRR, we anticipate this work will spark further advancements in composed image retrieval research.

text: Deep generative models, since their inception, have become increasingly more capable of generating novel and perceptually realistic signals (e.g., images and sound waves). With the emergence of deep models for graph structured data, natural interests seek extensions of these generative models for graphs. Successful extensions were seen recently in the case of learning from a collection of graphs (e.g., protein data banks), but the learning from a single graph has been largely under explored. The latter case, however, is important in practice. For example, graphs in financial and healthcare systems contain so much confidential information that their public accessibility is nearly impossible, but open science in these fields can only advance when similar data are available for benchmarking.   In this work, we propose an approach to generating a doppelganger graph that resembles a given one in many graph properties but nonetheless can hardly be used to reverse engineer the original one, in the sense of a near zero edge overlap. The approach is an orchestration of graph representation learning, generative adversarial networks, and graph realization algorithms. Through comparison with several graph generative models (either parameterized by neural networks or not), we demonstrate that our result barely reproduces the given graph but closely matches its properties. We further show that downstream tasks, such as node classification, on the generated graphs reach similar performance to the use of the original ones.

text: Deep neural networks have been shown as a class of useful tools for addressing signal recognition issues in recent years, especially for identifying the nonlinear feature structures of signals. However, this power of most deep learning techniques heavily relies on an abundant amount of training data, so the performance of classic neural nets decreases sharply when the number of training data samples is small or unseen data are presented in the testing phase. This calls for an advanced strategy, i.e., model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML), which is able to capture the invariant representation of the data samples or signals. In this paper, inspired by the special structure of the signal, i.e., real and imaginary parts consisted in practical time-series signals, we propose a Complex-valued Attentional MEta Learner (CAMEL) for the problem of few-shot signal recognition by leveraging attention and meta-learning in the complex domain. To the best of our knowledge, this is also the first complex-valued MAML that can find the first-order stationary points of general nonconvex problems with theoretical convergence guarantees. Extensive experiments results showcase the superiority of the proposed CAMEL compared with the state-of-the-art methods.

text: DarkRift 212 is a fast and highly performant low-level networking solution. Its feature set contains bi-channel TCP and UDP, serialization, and customizable logging. DarkRift requires a dedicated server topology and the entire solution is multithreaded by default. While it does not offer any of the mid- or high-level features, the solution was highly rated for performance. DarkRift targets developers who are in need of full control over networking and are comfortable building additional netcode. Considering the nature of "Funny Zoo - A Casual Game Built With Unity," the selection of DarkRift 212, despite its low-level nature and requirement for extensive custom netcode development, was strategically motivated by the project's emphasis on achieving optimal network performance and scalability. For a casual game that nonetheless anticipates concurrent player activity and potentially complex interactions within a shared virtual environment, the superior performance afforded by DarkRift 212's architecture, including its multithreaded design and direct control over network packets via bi-channel TCP and UDP, presents a significant advantage. While it necessitates a higher initial development overhead to implement features typically abstracted by higher-level networking frameworks, this approach grants the development team granular control over latency optimization, bandwidth usage, and the precise synchronization of game state. This level of control is crucial for ensuring a smooth, responsive user experience in a multiplayer setting, mitigating common issues such as desynchronization or lag, thereby directly contributing to the project's goal of delivering a robust and enjoyable casual game. The choice reflects a deliberate trade-off, prioritizing customizability and raw performance over rapid prototyping convenience, in line with the thesis's objective to explore advanced networking paradigms in Unity.

text:
Cervical spondylosis (CS) is a prevalent condition that significantly impacts quality of life, yet its early identification remains challenging. This paper introduces *EasiCSDeep*, a novel deep learning model designed to accurately identify cervical spondylosis using surface electromyography (sEMG) signals. The proposed approach leverages a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture optimized for feature extraction from sEMG data, combined with a recurrent neural network (RNN) to capture temporal dependencies in the signal. The model is trained and validated on a comprehensive dataset of sEMG recordings collected from patients with and without CS. Experimental results demonstrate that *EasiCSDeep* achieves an accuracy of 94.7%, outperforming traditional machine learning methods and existing deep learning models. The system also exhibits robustness to noise and variability in sEMG signals, making it suitable for real-world clinical applications. This research contributes to the field of medical diagnostics by providing a non-invasive, efficient, and reliable tool for early CS detection, with potential implications for improving patient outcomes and reducing healthcare costs.  

**Keywords**: Cervical spondylosis, surface electromyography (sEMG), deep learning, convolutional neural network (CNN), recurrent neural network (RNN), medical diagnostics.

text:
Ensuring fairness in machine learning models is a critical challenge, particularly when dealing with sensitive attributes such as gender, race, or age. This paper addresses the problem of bias mitigation by proposing a novel approach that leverages orthogonal disentangled representations. The objective is to separate sensitive attributes from task-relevant features in the latent space, thereby reducing unfair correlations while maintaining model performance. Our method employs a deep learning framework that enforces orthogonality constraints between representations of sensitive attributes and other features, ensuring that the learned embeddings are independent. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach effectively reduces bias without compromising accuracy, outperforming existing fairness-aware methods. The results highlight the potential of orthogonal disentangled representations as a robust solution for fairness in machine learning. This work contributes to the growing body of research on ethical AI by providing a scalable and interpretable technique for bias mitigation, with implications for applications in healthcare, finance, and social systems.  

**Keywords**: Fairness, Disentangled Representations, Orthogonality, Bias Mitigation, Machine Learning, Ethical AI.

The approach is demonstrated through a case study in which a robot performs manipulation actions in a kitchen environment, effectively bridging visual and semantic contexts via the generated knowledge graphs. These results highlight the framework's potential to advance semantic understanding in robotic manipulation, suggesting promising directions for future research in enhancing robots' cognitive capabilities through dynamic, knowledge-driven approaches. text: In conducting a comprehensive risk assessment, it is crucial to categorize sensitive information based on both its type and the degree of its visibility, as this can significantly influence the potential impact of a data breach. For instance, exposed API keys are considered high-risk due to their ability to grant unauthorized access to critical systems and data, thereby posing a severe threat to organizational security and operational integrity (Figure A). This risk is further exacerbated if these keys are exposed in public repositories or easily accessible locations, making them prime targets for exploitation (Figure B). On the other hand, email addresses, while still representing a sensitive piece of information, are often deemed medium risk because their exposure generally leads to less severe consequences such as phishing attacks rather than direct system compromise (Figure C). Nonetheless, the visibility of these email addresses can elevate the risk level, particularly when they are aggregated in large volumes or linked to other personal identifiers, which can enhance their utility in social engineering attacks (Smith et al., 2023). Therefore, it is essential to implement robust data protection measures tailored to the specific risk profiles of different types of sensitive information, ensuring that high-risk data is prioritized for immediate and stringent safeguarding actions (Doe, 2023). Such measures may include encryption, access controls, and continuous monitoring to detect and respond to potential threats in real-time, thereby mitigating the likelihood of unauthorized access and data loss (Johnson & Lee, 2023).

text: This paper introduces Pareto GAN, a novel approach to extending the representational power of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to model heavy-tailed distributions. The objective is to address the limitations of traditional GANs in capturing complex, real-world data distributions that exhibit heavy tails. Our method leverages the properties of Pareto distributions to design a new generator architecture and loss function, enabling the effective modeling of such distributions. The Pareto GAN is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its ability to generate high-quality samples that better match the target distributions compared to existing GAN variants. Results show significant improvements in terms of distribution coverage and sample diversity. The proposed approach contributes to the advancement of GAN research, offering a powerful tool for modeling complex data distributions in various applications, including image and data generation, anomaly detection, and uncertainty estimation. Key contributions include the introduction of a novel generator architecture, a tailored loss function, and the demonstration of improved performance on heavy-tailed distributions, highlighting the potential of Pareto GAN in AI, machine learning, and data modeling.

text: The considerable achievements of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in various challenging machine learning areas have underscored the limitations and high costs associated with designing hand-crafted neural networks, leading to a growing emphasis on automated architecture generation. While existing auto-generated network research shows promise, it primarily focuses on the sequential selection of individual layers, such as convolution or pooling. In contrast, meticulously designed hand-crafted networks feature sophisticated block architectures like the Inception-block (GoogLeNet), residual block (residual network), and dense block (dense convolutional network). Drawing on reinforcement learning and the inherent strengths of these specialized blocks, we introduce a novel automated method for designing multi-block neural networks. This approach aims to perform deep neural network structure learning by investigating the feasibility of composing diverse block types into effective architectures. An optimal network is constructed by a Q-learning agent, which is trained to sequentially select various block types. To validate our proposed method, we conducted experiments on the MNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR-10 image classification benchmark datasets using the auto-generated multi-block neural network, under restricted computational resources. The results confirm the high effectiveness of our method, demonstrating comparable or superior performance compared to both hand-crafted and advanced auto-generated neural networks.

text:
Semantic scene understanding is a critical challenge in autonomous driving and robotics, requiring precise interpretation of 3D environments from sensor data. This paper introduces *SemanticKITTI*, a large-scale dataset designed to advance research in semantic segmentation and scene understanding using LiDAR sequences. The dataset extends the popular KITTI Vision Benchmark Suite by providing dense point-wise annotations for 28 semantic classes across 22 sequences, capturing diverse urban driving scenarios. To address the challenges of dynamic environments, *SemanticKITTI* includes temporal information, enabling the development of models that leverage sequential data for improved accuracy. We propose a novel benchmark for semantic segmentation of LiDAR point clouds, evaluating state-of-the-art methods on this dataset. Our experiments demonstrate that incorporating temporal context significantly enhances segmentation performance, particularly for dynamic objects. The results highlight the dataset's potential to drive innovation in 3D perception and autonomous navigation. *SemanticKITTI* is publicly available, providing a valuable resource for the research community to develop and evaluate advanced algorithms for semantic scene understanding in real-world environments.  

**Keywords**: LiDAR, semantic segmentation, 3D perception, autonomous driving, point cloud, temporal modeling.

text: Estimating the 6 Degree of Freedom (6D) pose of objects from a single RGB image is crucial for applications that require physical interaction with the real world, including augmented reality and robotic manipulation. A novel approach is introduced that enables accurate estimation, refinement, and tracking of object poses by leveraging object detection and segmentation techniques. This method operates by matching features from the input image with those from rendered images of target objects, thereby enabling robust pose determination even in complex environments. By integrating segmentation, the system isolates objects of interest, allowing for precise pose estimation despite background clutter or occlusions. The iterative refinement process further enhances accuracy by progressively aligning the input and rendered images. Additionally, the approach supports real-time tracking, maintaining updated pose information as objects move or the viewpoint changes. This pipeline demonstrates strong performance across various scenarios, offering a practical and effective solution for real-world applications where reliable 6D pose estimation from RGB imagery is essential.

The study contributes to the existing body of research by introducing a novel application of CNNs in healthcare cost prediction, highlighting the potential of deep learning techniques in identifying high-risk patients and optimizing resource allocation. The results have significant implications for healthcare providers, policymakers, and insurers, enabling data-driven decision-making and personalized care. Quản lý danh sách người bệnh chờ ghép thận là một vấn đề quan trọng trong lĩnh vực y tế, đặc biệt là trong các trung tâm ghép thận. Có nhiều tiếp cận quản lý danh sách người bệnh chờ ghép thận khác nhau, mỗi tiếp cận có ưu và nhược điểm riêng.

Một trong những tiếp cận phổ biến là hệ thống điểm chờ (Waiting List Point System), nơi mà mỗi người bệnh được phân loại dựa trên mức độ nghiêm trọng của tình trạng bệnh và được xếp hạng theo điểm. Người bệnh có điểm cao sẽ được ưu tiên ghép thận trước.

Một tiếp cận khác là hệ thống phân loại dựa trên mức độ khẩn cấp (Urgency-Based Classification), nơi mà người bệnh được phân loại dựa trên mức độ khẩn cấp của tình trạng bệnh. Người bệnh có tình trạng bệnh khẩn cấp sẽ được ưu tiên ghép thận trước.

Một số trung tâm ghép thận còn áp dụng tiếp cận quản lý danh sách người bệnh chờ ghép thận dựa trên nguyên tắc công bằng và công bằng xã hội. Mục tiêu của tiếp cận này là đảm bảo rằng người bệnh được ghép thận dựa trên nhu cầu và khả năng của họ, chứ không phải dựa trên các yếu tố khác như tuổi tác, giới tính hoặc địa vị xã hội.

Tóm lại, quản lý danh sách người bệnh chờ ghép thận là một vấn đề phức tạp và đòi hỏi sự linh hoạt và sáng tạo trong việc áp dụng các tiếp cận quản lý khác nhau. Mục tiêu cuối cùng là đảm bảo rằng người bệnh được ghép thận một cách công bằng và hiệu quả.
