text:
This paper addresses the challenge of automating the classification of phantom test patterns, a critical task in medical imaging quality assurance. Traditional methods often rely on manual inspection, which is time-consuming and prone to human error. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel approach leveraging transfer learning with deep neural networks (DNNs). Specifically, we utilize pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) fine-tuned on a curated dataset of phantom test images. The proposed method demonstrates significant improvements in classification accuracy and efficiency compared to conventional techniques. Experimental results show that our approach achieves an accuracy of over 95% on a diverse set of test patterns, outperforming existing methods by a notable margin. Furthermore, the system exhibits robustness to variations in image quality and noise, making it suitable for real-world deployment. This research contributes to the field of medical imaging by providing a scalable, automated solution for phantom test pattern classification, with potential applications in enhancing diagnostic imaging workflows and ensuring consistent quality control.  

**Keywords**: phantom test patterns, transfer learning, deep neural networks, medical imaging, quality assurance, convolutional neural networks.

text: Continuous blood pressure (BP) monitoring is critical for early detection and management of cardiovascular diseases. Traditional methods often rely on invasive techniques or require specialized hardware, limiting their scalability and accessibility. This paper proposes a novel approach to estimate continuous BP using photoplethysmography (PPG) signals through a federated learning (FL) framework. The objective is to develop a robust, privacy-preserving model that leverages distributed data without centralizing sensitive patient information. Our method employs a deep neural network (DNN) architecture trained on PPG data from multiple decentralized sources, ensuring data privacy and security while maintaining model accuracy. The FL approach is evaluated on a diverse dataset, demonstrating competitive performance compared to centralized training methods. Results indicate that the proposed model achieves high accuracy in systolic and diastolic BP estimation, with mean absolute errors of 4.2 mmHg and 2.8 mmHg, respectively. Furthermore, the FL framework shows resilience to data heterogeneity across different devices and populations. This research contributes to the advancement of non-invasive BP monitoring by introducing a scalable, privacy-aware solution with potential applications in remote healthcare and wearable technology. Key innovations include the integration of FL with PPG-based BP estimation and the development of a lightweight DNN optimized for edge devices. text: This paper presents a novel approach to improving El Niño forecasts by representing the world's climate system as a graph and leveraging graph neural networks (GNNs). The objective is to enhance the accuracy of El Niño predictions, which are crucial for mitigating the effects of climate-related disasters. Our approach utilizes a graph-based model to capture complex relationships between climate variables, such as sea surface temperatures, atmospheric pressures, and ocean currents. We employ a customized GNN architecture to learn spatial and temporal patterns in the graph-structured data, allowing for more accurate predictions of El Niño events. The results show significant improvements in forecast accuracy compared to traditional methods, with a reduction in error rates of up to 30%. Our study demonstrates the potential of graph neural networks in climate modeling and highlights the importance of representing complex systems as graphs to uncover hidden patterns and relationships. Key contributions include the development of a graph-based framework for climate forecasting and the application of GNNs to a real-world problem with significant societal impacts. Relevant keywords: graph neural networks, El Niño forecasts, climate modeling, graph-based methods, spatial-temporal patterns.

Typically, developing models capable of interpreting images with novel objects is expensive due to two factors: (1) the need for extensive category-specific data collection, and (2) the requirement to retrain the entire system. Inspired by human ability to infer properties of new objects by relating their appearance to familiar ones after minimal exposure, we develop a technique that explains images containing novel objects without retraining. This method leverages word embeddings derived from limited image features of the objects and can be incorporated into standard image-captioning frameworks. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed solution.

text: Dimensionality reduction (DR) is frequently used for analyzing and visualizing high-dimensional data as it provides a good first glance of the data. However, to interpret the DR result for gaining useful insights from the data, it would take additional analysis effort such as identifying clusters and understanding their characteristics. While there are many automatic methods (e.g., density-based clustering methods) to identify clusters, effective methods for understanding a cluster's characteristics are still lacking. A cluster can be mostly characterized by its distribution of feature values. Reviewing the original feature values is not a straightforward task when the number of features is large. To address this challenge, we present a visual analytics method that effectively highlights the essential features of a cluster in a DR result. To extract the essential features, we introduce an enhanced usage of contrastive principal component analysis (cPCA). Our method, called ccPCA (contrasting clusters in PCA), can calculate each feature's relative contribution to the contrast between one cluster and other clusters. With ccPCA, we have created an interactive system including a scalable visualization of clusters' feature contributions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method and system with case studies using several publicly available datasets.

text: The rapid growth and distribution of IT systems increases their complexity and aggravates operation and maintenance. To sustain control over large sets of hosts and the connecting networks, monitoring solutions are employed and constantly enhanced. They collect diverse key performance indicators (KPIs) (e.g. CPU utilization, allocated memory, etc.) and provide detailed information about the system state. Storing such metrics over a period of time naturally raises the motivation of predicting future KPI progress based on past observations. Although, a variety of time series forecasting methods exist, forecasting the progress of IT system KPIs is very hard. First, KPI types like CPU utilization or allocated memory are very different and hard to be expressed by the same model. Second, system components are interconnected and constantly changing due to soft- or firmware updates and hardware modernization. Thus a frequent model retraining or fine-tuning must be expected. Therefore, we propose a lightweight solution for KPI series prediction based on historic observations. It consists of a weighted heterogeneous ensemble method composed of two models - a neural network and a mean predictor. As ensemble method a weighted summation is used, whereby a heuristic is employed to set the weights. The modelling approach is evaluated on the available FedCSIS 2020 challenge dataset and achieves an overall R^2 score of 0.10 on the preliminary 10% test data and 0.15 on the complete test data. We publish our code on the following github repository: https://github.com/citlab/fed_challenge

text: Sparse coding is an unsupervised learning algorithm that learns a succinct high-level representation of the inputs given only unlabeled data; it represents each input as a sparse linear combination of a set of basis functions. Originally applied to modeling the human visual cortex, sparse coding has also been shown to be useful for self-taught learning, in which the goal is to solve a supervised classification task given access to additional unlabeled data drawn from different classes than that in the supervised learning problem. Shift-invariant sparse coding (SISC) is an extension of sparse coding which reconstructs a (usually time-series) input using all of the basis functions in all possible shifts. In this paper, we present an efficient algorithm for learning SISC bases. Our method is based on iteratively solving two large convex optimization problems: The first, which computes the linear coefficients, is an L1-regularized linear least squares problem with potentially hundreds of thousands of variables. Existing methods typically use a heuristic to select a small subset of the variables to optimize, but we present a way to efficiently compute the exact solution. The second, which solves for bases, is a constrained linear least squares problem. By optimizing over complex-valued variables in the Fourier domain, we reduce the coupling between the different variables, allowing the problem to be solved efficiently. We show that SISC's learned high-level representations of speech and music provide useful features for classification tasks within those domains. When applied to classification, under certain conditions the learned features outperform state of the art spectral and cepstral features.

Novel view synthesis from single images is a challenging task in computer vision, with applications ranging from virtual reality to autonomous systems. This paper addresses the problem of generating realistic and accurate novel views from a single input image by leveraging point cloud transformation techniques. The proposed approach begins by estimating a dense 3D point cloud representation from the input image using a deep learning-based depth estimation model. These point clouds are then transformed into the target viewpoint using a novel geometric transformation algorithm that preserves spatial consistency and minimizes artifacts. To enhance realism, a neural rendering framework is employed to synthesize high-quality textures and details for the generated views. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing single-image novel view synthesis techniques in terms of both visual quality and geometric accuracy. The framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets, with significant improvements in handling occlusions and complex scenes. This research contributes a robust and efficient solution for single-image novel view synthesis, offering potential applications in augmented reality, robotics, and 3D content creation.  

**Keywords**: novel view synthesis, point cloud transformation, single-image 3D reconstruction, neural rendering, depth estimation, computer vision.

text:
Content-Based Image Retrieval (CBIR) systems often rely on multiple visual features, such as color, texture, and shape, to improve retrieval accuracy. However, determining the optimal weights for these features remains a significant challenge, as their importance varies across queries and datasets. This paper proposes a novel framework for automatic feature weight determination in multi-feature CBIR systems. Our approach integrates indexing techniques with pseudo-relevance feedback (PRF) to dynamically adjust feature weights based on the relevance of retrieved images. The indexing mechanism accelerates the retrieval process, while PRF refines the weights by analyzing top-ranked results to better align with user intent. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional fixed-weight and static weighting approaches, achieving higher precision and recall rates. The results highlight the effectiveness of combining indexing and PRF for adaptive feature weighting, offering a robust solution for improving CBIR performance. This research contributes to the advancement of intelligent image retrieval systems by providing a scalable and efficient method for handling diverse visual features, with potential applications in multimedia databases, medical imaging, and e-commerce.  

**Keywords**: Content-Based Image Retrieval (CBIR), feature weighting, pseudo-relevance feedback, indexing, multi-feature analysis, image retrieval systems.

text: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) commonly exhibit performance plateaus, particularly an inability to gain further benefit from increased layer depth, a phenomenon often attributed to intrinsic GCN layer limitations such as insufficient expressive power. However, this prevailing view may misinterpret the core issue. This work posits that the true bottleneck lies within the training procedure itself, demonstrating that performance can be substantially improved through targeted adjustments to how GCNs are trained. Specifically, the investigation reveals that a significant loss of graph signal energy occurs during the backward pass, effectively nullifying the learning process for layers closer to the input and impeding overall network efficacy. To mitigate this, several innovative methodologies are introduced, involving subtle modifications to the GCN operator, conceptualized from an energy preservation perspective. Empirical validation confirms that these operator adjustments lead to a marked reduction in training difficulties and a notable boost in performance, critically achieved without altering the architectural composition or number of network parameters. These findings collectively suggest that training challenges, rather than inherent architectural constraints, are the fundamental cause of GCN performance limitations.

text: This paper addresses optimal signal detection in large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. This NP-hard problem is optimally solvable by finding the shortest path on a decision tree. However, existing optimal search algorithms are often prohibitively complex, rendering them infeasible for large-scale MIMO. To overcome this, we propose the hyperaccelerated tree search (HATS) algorithm. HATS employs a deep neural network (DNN) to estimate the optimal heuristic, accelerating an underlying memory-bounded search algorithm. This approach is inspired by the principle that heuristic search algorithms achieve optimal efficiency with the optimal heuristic function. Simulation results demonstrate that HATS achieves near-optimal bit error rate (BER) performance in large-scale systems while maintaining bounded memory usage. Furthermore, it visits nearly the fewest tree nodes, demonstrating near-optimal efficiency and high applicability for large-scale systems in practical scenarios. The code for this paper is publicly available at https://github.com/skypitcher/hats.

text: This paper presents a novel curriculum domain adaptation approach for the semantic segmentation of urban scenes, addressing the challenge of adapting models to new, unseen environments. Our objective is to develop a framework that enables accurate and efficient segmentation of urban scenes, despite differences in data distributions between the source and target domains. We propose a curriculum-based approach, where the model is trained on a series of increasingly difficult tasks, leveraging a combination of adversarial learning and self-supervised techniques to adapt to the target domain. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets, outperforming existing domain adaptation methods. Key findings include improved accuracy and reduced domain shift, demonstrating the effectiveness of our curriculum-based approach. The proposed method has significant implications for real-world applications, such as autonomous driving and urban planning, where accurate semantic segmentation is crucial. Our research contributes to the advancement of domain adaptation techniques, particularly in the context of semantic segmentation, and highlights the potential of curriculum learning for improving model adaptability and robustness in complex, dynamic environments, with relevant keywords including domain adaptation, semantic segmentation, urban scenes, curriculum learning, and deep learning.

text: A first-person camera, placed at a person's head, captures, which objects are important to the camera wearer. Most prior methods for this task learn to detect such important objects from the manually labeled first-person data in a supervised fashion. However, important objects are strongly related to the camera wearer's internal state such as his intentions and attention, and thus, only the person wearing the camera can provide the importance labels. Such a constraint makes the annotation process costly and limited in scalability.   In this work, we show that we can detect important objects in first-person images without the supervision by the camera wearer or even third-person labelers. We formulate an important detection problem as an interplay between the 1) segmentation and 2) recognition agents. The segmentation agent first proposes a possible important object segmentation mask for each image, and then feeds it to the recognition agent, which learns to predict an important object mask using visual semantics and spatial features.   We implement such an interplay between both agents via an alternating cross-pathway supervision scheme inside our proposed Visual-Spatial Network (VSN). Our VSN consists of spatial ("where") and visual ("what") pathways, one of which learns common visual semantics while the other focuses on the spatial location cues. Our unsupervised learning is accomplished via a cross-pathway supervision, where one pathway feeds its predictions to a segmentation agent, which proposes a candidate important object segmentation mask that is then used by the other pathway as a supervisory signal. We show our method's success on two different important object datasets, where our method achieves similar or better results as the supervised methods.

Early unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) methods achieve domain-invariant feature representation by leveraging the early layers of neural networks, often using adversarial learning to minimize domain differences. Initial feature alignment approaches focus on reducing discrepancies between source and target domains. Hoffman was the first to incorporate domain adaptation (DA) into segmentation by integrating feature alignment with additional category constraints. Various adversarial learning strategies have been proposed to learn domain-invariant features across input, feature, output, or patch space adaptations. For example, Tsai et al. treat segmentation as structured outputs, emphasizing semantic similarity across domains, while Wang et al. enhance discriminator performance by incorporating class information to align features more precisely.

text: LiDAR odometry (LO) involves determining the relative alignment between consecutive LiDAR point clouds, a process used to estimate the motion of the platform on which the LiDAR sensor is mounted. We propose a network architecture designed to learn LO by directly processing 3D point clouds. This model is trained end-to-end on the KITTI dataset, eliminating the requirement for pre-defining corresponding point pairs. Evaluation on the KITTI Vision Benchmark Suite demonstrates performance comparable to the previously published DeepCLR [1], despite our model using only approximately 3.56% of the number of network parameters. text: Monocular 3D object detection for autonomous driving is significantly challenged by ego-car pose changes and road irregularities, leading to detector susceptibility to camera extrinsic parameters, a common issue overlooked by existing methods. To address this, we propose a novel framework that captures camera pose to formulate the detector free from extrinsic perturbation. Specifically, our method predicts camera extrinsic parameters by detecting vanishing point and horizon changes, and employs a converter to rectify perturbative features in the latent space. Consequently, our 3D detector operates independently of extrinsic parameter variations, yielding accurate results in realistic, challenging scenarios like potholed and uneven roads, where almost all existing monocular detectors fail. Experiments demonstrate our method yields the best performance compared with the other state-of-the-arts by a large margin on both KITTI 3D and nuScenes datasets.

text: This paper addresses the challenge of globally editing images using textual descriptions, a task that requires precise alignment between visual content and natural language instructions. We propose a novel deep learning framework that integrates advanced vision-language models to enable high-quality, semantically consistent image edits based on user-provided text. Our approach leverages a transformer-based architecture to encode both image and text inputs, followed by a cross-modal attention mechanism to ensure accurate feature alignment. The model is trained on a large-scale dataset of image-text pairs, enabling it to generalize across diverse editing scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing techniques in terms of edit quality, semantic coherence, and user satisfaction. Notably, the framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets, showcasing its ability to handle complex editing tasks such as object replacement, style transfer, and scene modification. The proposed system has significant implications for applications in creative design, content generation, and automated media editing, offering a powerful tool for users to manipulate images with natural language inputs. Keywords: image editing, vision-language models, transformer, cross-modal attention, semantic alignment.

text: Machine learning serves as the predominant tool within both artificial intelligence research and industry. Among crucial machine learning algorithms is the Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), which demands substantial computational resources and time for its training process. To shorten GBDT training duration, many works have attempted to apply GBDT on a Parameter Server; however, these existing GBDT algorithms are synchronous parallel, thus failing to fully leverage the Parameter Server's capabilities. This paper investigates the feasibility of employing asynchronous parallel methods to train GBDT models, naming the resulting algorithm asynch-SGBDT (asynchronous parallel stochastic gradient boosting decision tree). Our theoretical and experimental findings suggest that asynch-SGBDT's scalability is influenced by dataset sample diversity, sampling rate, step length, and the specific settings of the GBDT tree. Furthermore, experimental results reveal that the asynch-SGBDT training process achieves a linear speedup in an asynchronous parallel manner when datasets and GBDT trees fulfill high scalability requirements.

The paragraph details a method for creating datasets with specified balanced and imbalanced data nodes, utilizing a Dirichlet distribution to allocate class probabilities. In the process, each node receives a fixed number of samples, derived from the dataset's original samples without duplication. This method is particularly applied to the Large Movie Dataset, where nodes are divided into balanced and imbalanced categories, with specific class distributions assigned to each.

In the dataset creation process, a specified number of balanced (X) and imbalanced (Y) data nodes are constructed, with each node containing M samples. Class probabilities are drawn from a Dirichlet distribution with concentration parameters ranging from 1 to X+Y. For nodes i where i ≤ X, the procedure involves iterating through M samples by sampling a class label y according to the distribution q. A sample (x, y) is then randomly selected from the remaining samples of class y in dataset S and added to dataset Di. Subsequently, the selected sample is removed from class-specific dataset Sy. If class y is depleted of samples, it is removed from the set of classes C, and the class probabilities q are re-normalized using the ReNormalize function. This function ensures normalization of q after any class removal, preventing duplicate sampling and ensuring that each node is assigned M = S/(X+Y) samples. In the application to the Large Movie Dataset, which contains two classes (negative and positive), the allocation is structured so that X nodes handle balanced data, while Y nodes address imbalanced data. Among Y nodes, half are designated to have 80% of their samples from the negative class, while the remaining half are configured with 80% of samples from the positive class.

This paper introduces a novel approach to learner-aware teaching by leveraging inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) to model and adapt to learner preferences and constraints. The objective is to design teaching strategies that are not only effective but also personalized, ensuring optimal learning outcomes by aligning instructional methods with individual learner characteristics. We propose a framework that integrates IRL with preference elicitation and constraint satisfaction techniques, enabling the system to infer learner goals, preferences, and limitations from observed behavior. Our method employs a combination of reward modeling and optimization algorithms to generate adaptive teaching policies. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms traditional teaching methods in terms of learner engagement and knowledge retention, particularly in scenarios with diverse learner profiles. The findings highlight the potential of this framework to revolutionize personalized education, offering scalable and efficient solutions for adaptive learning systems. Key contributions include the integration of IRL with preference-based learning and the development of a constraint-aware teaching model. This research has broad implications for educational technology, intelligent tutoring systems, and AI-driven personalized learning platforms.  

**Keywords**: Inverse Reinforcement Learning, Learner-aware Teaching, Preference Modeling, Constraint Satisfaction, Personalized Education, Adaptive Learning Systems.

text: We propose a novel generative autoencoder model, the Dual Contradistinctive Generative Autoencoder (DC-VAE), which incorporates dual contradistinctive losses to enhance the simultaneous inference (reconstruction) and synthesis (sampling) capabilities of generative autoencoders. DC-VAE integrates an instance-level discriminative loss to preserve instance-level fidelity and a set-level adversarial loss to promote set-level fidelity in both reconstruction and synthesis. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of DC-VAE across multiple image resolutions, including 32×32, 64×64, 128×128, and 512×512. The harmonious interplay of the two contradistinctive losses yields significant improvements in both qualitative and quantitative performance compared to baseline VAEs, without necessitating architectural modifications. DC-VAE achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results in image reconstruction, image synthesis, image interpolation, and representation learning. As a general-purpose VAE framework, DC-VAE is broadly applicable to various downstream tasks in computer vision and machine learning.

text: In recent years, the integration of advanced technologies such as Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) has significantly enhanced inventory rotation processes in logistics warehouses, contributing to improved operational efficiency and accuracy. RFID automated inventory systems enable real-time tracking of goods, reducing the likelihood of human error associated with manual stock checks and providing instant visibility into stock levels, item locations, and movement histories. This technology is particularly beneficial for various warehouse types, including bonded, transit, private, public, automated, and climate-controlled warehouses, by supporting the need for precise stock management and timely order fulfillment. RFID tags attached to products or pallets allow for automated data capture when items enter or leave storage areas, thus streamlining inventory reconciliation and facilitating the implementation of inventory rotation strategies such as First-In-First-Out (FIFO) or Last-In-First-Out (LIFO), which are essential for maintaining product quality, especially for perishable or high-value goods. Furthermore, the use of RFID can help in identifying slow-moving or obsolete inventory, optimizing warehouse space, and reducing carrying costs. In automated logistics warehouses, RFID systems can be integrated with warehouse management software (WMS) and automated material handling equipment, such as conveyor belts and robotic picking systems, to enable seamless coordination of warehouse activities and ensure the efficient flow of goods. The deployment of RFID technology not only improves inventory accuracy and turnover rates but also enhances supply chain transparency, which is increasingly demanded by clients and regulatory bodies. As a result, RFID-enabled inventory rotation systems are becoming a standard in modern logistics warehouse operations, supporting both quality assurance requirements and the overall effectiveness of warehouse management.

text: Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization (WDRO) aims to train models that minimize the worst-case risk within a Wasserstein ball around the empirical data distribution. Although WDRO has emerged as a promising inference tool, its theoretical foundations remain incomplete. Gao et al. (2017) introduced a minimizer using a tractable approximation of the worst-case risk but did not establish risk consistency. This work presents a new minimizer derived from an innovative approximation theorem, along with corresponding risk consistency guarantees. Additionally, we extend WDRO inference to locally perturbed data, encompassing Mixup (Zhang et al., 2017) as a specific instance, demonstrating that our approximation and consistency findings generalize to such scenarios. Empirical evaluations on image classification tasks confirm the method's robustness, with results indicating superior accuracy over baseline models on noisy datasets.

text: This paper presents a deep reinforcement learning algorithm for online accompaniment generation, with potential for real-time interactive human-machine duet improvisation. Different from offline music generation and harmonization, online music accompaniment requires the algorithm to respond to human input and generate the machine counterpart in a sequential order. We cast this as a reinforcement learning problem, where the generation agent learns a policy to generate a musical note (action) based on previously generated context (state). The key of this algorithm is the well-functioning reward model. Instead of defining it using music composition rules, we learn this model from monophonic and polyphonic training data. This model considers the compatibility of the machine-generated note with both the machine-generated context and the human-generated context. Experiments show that this algorithm is able to respond to the human part and generate a melodic, harmonic and diverse machine part. Subjective evaluations on preferences show that the proposed algorithm generates music pieces of higher quality than the baseline method.

text: Conformal prediction struggles with limited training data, producing overly large prediction sets, which hinders its practical application. This work introduces a novel approach by casting conformal prediction as a meta-learning paradigm over exchangeable collections of auxiliary tasks, yielding a conformalization algorithm that is simple, fast, and agnostic to the underlying model, learning algorithm, or dataset. The method achieves substantially tighter prediction sets while maintaining desirable marginal guarantees, with effectiveness demonstrated across few-shot classification and regression tasks in natural language processing, computer vision, and computational chemistry for drug discovery. This research encourages further exploration of meta-learning strategies to enhance conformal prediction in various data-limited environments and to generalize its benefits to a wider array of predictive modeling challenges.

text: Self-training, a recent advancement in the UDA field, has become the dominant alternative to explicitly aligning the distributions of source and target domains. This method involves the iterative creation of pseudo labels, which are then used to retrain the network. Through a self-paced learning curriculum, the network gradually achieves adaptation. Pseudo labels can be generated in an online or offline manner. Due to the distributional differences between the source and target, these pseudo labels often contain noise and must be selected with care. It is a common practice to select pseudo labels based on a strict confidence threshold; however, high confidence scores do not always ensure accuracy, which may hinder the network's ability to learn reliable information from the target domain. Moreover, relying solely on strong predictions can result in certain pixels never being learned throughout the training process. For example, if the model cannot accurately predict a particular class, it becomes difficult to assign correct pseudo labels to pixels of that class, leading to inadequate and imbalanced training data.

Mưa lớn sắp đổ xuống khu vực Trung Trung Bộ đang gây lo lắng cho người dân và các cơ quan chức năng. Để đánh giá khả năng dự báo mưa lớn ở khu vực này, các nhà khoa học đã áp dụng mô hình CRESS để phân tích và dự đoán tình hình thời tiết.

text:
Tracking pedestrian heads in dense crowds is a critical challenge in computer vision, with applications in surveillance, crowd management, and autonomous systems. This paper addresses the limitations of existing methods in accurately detecting and tracking heads in highly congested environments, where occlusion and overlapping are prevalent. We propose a novel deep learning-based framework that integrates a multi-scale feature extraction network with a robust tracking algorithm to enhance head detection and trajectory estimation. Our approach leverages spatial-temporal information and employs a lightweight attention mechanism to prioritize head regions, improving accuracy in cluttered scenes. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves a significant improvement in tracking precision and recall compared to state-of-the-art techniques, particularly in scenarios with extreme crowd density. The proposed system also exhibits real-time performance, making it suitable for practical deployment. This research contributes to advancing pedestrian tracking technologies by offering a scalable and efficient solution for dense crowd analysis, with potential applications in public safety and urban planning.  

**Keywords**: Pedestrian tracking, dense crowds, head detection, deep learning, computer vision, attention mechanism.

They demonstrate that small programs can be both expressive and intuitive, covering a range of existing interpretable families. Preliminary applications on small datasets indicate that the generated explanations are both intuitive and accurate across several classifiers. This work suggests that program-based explanations could be a versatile tool, opening avenues for future research in enhancing the interpretability of machine learning models while maintaining their performance.

text: Blockchain technology, as a decentralized ledger system, offers enhanced security, transparency, and immutability compared to traditional databases. Its architecture allows multiple participants to maintain and verify records without the need for a central authority, thereby reducing the risks of data tampering and fraud. There are several types of blockchain, each designed to meet specific requirements and use cases. Public blockchains, such as Bitcoin and Ethereum, provide open access to anyone willing to participate, promoting decentralization and transparency. Private blockchains restrict access to known participants, offering greater control and privacy, which is suitable for enterprise applications. Consortium blockchains represent a hybrid model where a group of organizations jointly manage the network, balancing decentralization and efficiency. Understanding these variations is crucial for selecting the appropriate blockchain framework tailored to particular business needs and technological constraints.

text: Recent advances in image editing enable users to produce artistic creations; however, manipulated areas can often appear inconsistent with their backgrounds. Identifying these inharmonious regions presents both an intriguing and difficult challenge. Recognizing the need for effective multi-scale contextual information aggregation and reduction of redundant data, we introduce a novel Bi-directional Feature Integration (BFI) block in the encoder and a Global-context Guided Decoder (GGD) block in the decoder to efficiently fuse multi-scale features. Additionally, we incorporate a Mask-guided Dual Attention (MDA) block between the encoder and decoder to further suppress redundant information. Experimental results on the image harmonization dataset indicate that our approach delivers competitive results in localizing inharmonious regions. The source code is available at https://github.com/bcmi/DIRL.

text: Positive Unlabeled (PU) learning has emerged as a significant challenge due to the increasing availability of large-scale but unlabeled datasets. Recent advances in GAN-based methodologies for PU learning have shown considerable promise, leveraging the flexibility of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) which are not limited by deterministic biases or dimensionality constraints. Despite these advantages, current GAN-based PU strategies often suffer from limitations such as high sensitivity to prior knowledge, complex model architectures, and susceptibility to overfitting in initial training stages. To address these drawbacks, a novel approach integrates a biased PU risk directly into the standard GAN discriminator loss, thereby guiding the discriminator to encourage the generator's outputs to align with the distribution of unlabeled samples while diverging from that of positive samples. This strategy, embodied in the proposed D-GAN model, enables effective learning of the counter-examples distribution in the absence of prior knowledge. Empirical evaluations indicate that this approach surpasses existing state-of-the-art PU learning methods that do not require prior information, demonstrating improved robustness and performance.

text: Norfloxacin (NFX) is frequently detected in domestic wastewater, wastewater treatment plants, hospital effluents, and surface water, which may lead to ecological imbalances. Furthermore, conventional biological treatment methods, including membrane bioreactor (MBR) technology, are not feasible for NFX removal. In this study, the degradation of NFX by advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) employing UV/TiO2 and H2O2 agents in a laboratory-scale tubular reactor was conducted. The NFX degradation reactions can be represented by the Langmuir-Hinshelwood kinetic model. The influence of factors such as TiO2 and H2O2 concentrations, UV irradiation intensity, and hydrodynamic regime (i.e., Reynolds number - Re) on the apparent reaction rate constant (k app) was evaluated. Results indicate that the AOPs process utilizing the combined agents UV/TiO2/H2O2 under reaction conditions of TiO2 and H2O2 concentrations at 0.2 g/l and 0.0492 mol/l respectively, UV irradiation intensity at 225 W/m2, and Re at 6700, achieves an NFX degradation reaction rate constant of 0.052 min-1.

A crucial aspect of wallet security involves adherence to industry standards, such as the BIP39 specification, which standardizes the generation and management of mnemonic or seed phrases, human-readable word sets used to derive cryptographic keys for accessing and managing funds. text: Đặt vấn đề: Đề kháng kháng sinh là nguyên nhân chính dẫn đến thất bại điều trị tiệt trừ Helicobacter pylori . Việc cập nhật tình hình đề kháng kháng sinh của Helicobacter pylori trong từng khu vực có ý nghĩa quan trọng trong việc khuyến cáo lựa chọn phác đồ điều trị phù hợp với quần thể và tối ưu hóa hiệu quả điều trị tiệt trừ Helicobacter pylori cho từng khu vực, quốc gia. Mục tiêu: Xác định tỷ lệ đề kháng nguyên phát của vi khuẩn Helicobacter pylori với kháng sinh Amoxicillin, Clarithromycin, Levofloxacin, Metronidazole và Tetracycline. Đối tượng và phương pháp nghiên cứu: Nghiên cứu mô tả cắt ngang thực hiện trên 216 bệnh nhân viêm loét dạ dày tá tràng, được thực hiện nội soi và nuôi cấy kháng sinh đồ Epsilometer test tại bệnh viện Quốc Tế Mỹ từ tháng 10/2019 - 9/2022 Kết quả: Tỷ lệ đề kháng nguyên phát với kháng sinh Clarithromycin chiếm tỷ lệ cao nhất lên đến 96,30%, tỷ lệ đề kháng với Levofloxacin, Metronidazole, Amoxicillin lần lượt chiếm 58,8%, 8,80% và 2,78%. Trong nghiên cứu không thấy trường hợp nào kháng nguyên phát với Tetracycline, tỷ lệ 0%. Tỷ lệ kháng từng loại kháng sinh trong nhóm nam và nữ không có sự khác biệt có ý nghĩa thông kê p > 0,05. Tỷ lệ kháng kép với 02 loại kháng sinh rất cao, có 161/216 trường hợp chiếm 74,54%, trong đó tỷ lệ kháng với CLA+ LEV chiếm tỷ lệ cao nhất là 124 trường hợp chiếm 57,41%. Tỷ lệ chủng Helicobacter pylori kháng CLA+MET, MET+LEV, CLA+AMX, AMX+LEV, AMX+MET chiếm tỷ lệ lần lượt là 7,41%, 3,7%, 2,78%, 1,39% và 0,46%. Có 11 trường hợp chủng H.pylori đa kháng 3 loại kháng sinh chiếm tỷ lệ 5,09%, không có trường hợp nào kháng từ 04 loại kháng sinh trở lên. Chỉ có 1,39% còn nhạy với cả 5 loại kháng sinh trong các phác đồ tiệt trừ. Kết luận: Tỷ lệ đề kháng với Clarithromycin rất cao cho thấy phác đồ bộ ba tiêu chuẩn hầu như không còn hiệu quả và không nên được sử dụng trong lâm sàng. Phác đồ có Levofloxacin nên phối hợp thêm Bismuth để nâng cao hiệu quả điều trị. Tỷ lệ đề kháng với Amoxicillin, Tetracycline và Metronidazole thấp, nên phác đồ 4 thuốc có Bismuth hoặc phác đồ phối hợp 3 thuốc trên với nhau sẽ có thể hiệu quả trong điều trị tiệt trừ Helicobacter pylori .

The paragraph discusses the role of pooling layers in convolutional neural networks, emphasizing their function in reducing the dimensionality and number of parameters of feature maps generated by convolutional layers. This dimensionality reduction is particularly important as the number of filters increases significantly across layers, from 64 to 512 in the final stages. Pooling layers thus play a critical role in managing computational complexity and improving network efficiency.

Pooling layers are integral components that typically follow multiple convolutional layers within a convolutional neural network architecture. Their primary function is to reduce the spatial dimensionality and the number of parameters of the feature maps produced during each convolutional operation. This reduction is essential to mitigate the exponential increase in computational complexity as the number of filters escalates—from 64 to 128, 256, and ultimately 512 in the deeper network layers. By performing this dimensionality reduction, pooling layers contribute significantly to enhancing the efficiency and generalization capability of the model, which is particularly beneficial in applications such as weld quality inspection using image processing and segmentation deep learning techniques.

text:
Scene text recognition (STR) is a critical task in computer vision, with applications ranging from document analysis to autonomous systems. Despite significant progress, accurately recognizing text in diverse and complex scenes remains challenging due to variations in font, orientation, and background clutter. This paper introduces MASTER, a Multi-Aspect Non-local Network designed to address these challenges by leveraging a novel attention mechanism and multi-aspect feature extraction. The proposed model integrates non-local operations to capture long-range dependencies in text sequences, enhancing the recognition of irregular and distorted text. Additionally, MASTER employs a multi-aspect feature fusion strategy to combine spatial and contextual information, improving robustness across diverse text scenarios. Experiments on benchmark datasets, including ICDAR 2015 and CUTE80, demonstrate that MASTER achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods in both accuracy and computational efficiency. The results highlight the model's ability to generalize across varying text conditions, making it a promising solution for real-world STR applications. This research contributes to the field by introducing a scalable and efficient architecture that advances the state of scene text recognition, with potential applications in document digitization, augmented reality, and intelligent transportation systems.  

**Keywords**: Scene text recognition, non-local networks, attention mechanisms, multi-aspect feature fusion, irregular text recognition.
label: deepseek-text

Our approach yields key findings, including the ability to identify metastable states and transitions between them, which are crucial for understanding complex systems. The results demonstrate improved performance compared to existing methods, particularly in terms of clustering quality and robustness to noise. The implications of this research are significant, enabling the application of our method to a wide range of fields, from physics and biology to finance and social sciences, where time series data analysis is critical. text: This paper presents a novel approach to articulated shape matching, leveraging Laplacian eigenfunctions and unsupervised point registration to establish correspondences between non-rigid shapes. Our objective is to develop a robust and efficient method for matching shapes with varying topology and geometry, which is a fundamental problem in computer vision and graphics. We propose a framework that combines the spectral properties of Laplacian eigenfunctions with an unsupervised point registration algorithm, allowing for accurate and dense correspondence estimation. Our method achieves state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets, demonstrating improved robustness to noise, outliers, and partial matches. The key contributions of our research include the introduction of a spectral shape descriptor and an unsupervised registration algorithm, which enable efficient and accurate shape matching. Our approach has significant implications for various applications, including 3D reconstruction, shape analysis, and computer-aided design. Key keywords: articulated shape matching, Laplacian eigenfunctions, unsupervised point registration, spectral shape descriptor, 3D reconstruction, computer vision, graphics.

Experimental results on several benchmark datasets show that EA-ConvNets not only outperform various state-of-the-art early classification methods but also remain competitive with leading time series classification algorithms. Importantly, the deep features learned by the model are highly interpretable, enabling better understanding of time series characteristics. These findings suggest that data-driven deep feature learning can significantly advance early time series classification, opening new avenues for future research in interpretable and accurate early prediction models.

text: Label Propagation (LPA) and Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCN) are both message-passing algorithms applied to graphs, designed to solve the task of node classification. While LPA propagates node label information across graph edges, GCN propagates and transforms node feature information. Despite their conceptual similarity, the theoretical relationship between LPA and GCN has not yet been thoroughly investigated. In this study, we examine the relationship between LPA and GCN from two perspectives: (1) feature/label smoothing, where we analyze how the feature or label of a node disseminates across its neighbors; and (2) feature/label influence, which quantifies how much the initial feature or label of one node affects the final feature or label of another node. Building on this theoretical analysis, we propose an end-to-end model that unifies GCN and LPA for node classification. In our unified framework, edge weights are learnable, with LPA serving as a regularization mechanism that guides the GCN in learning appropriate edge weights, thereby enhancing classification performance. Additionally, our model can be interpreted as learning attention weights informed by node labels, offering a more task-oriented approach compared to existing feature-based attention models. Extensive experiments on real-world graphs demonstrate that our model outperforms state-of-the-art GCN-based methods in node classification accuracy.

text: Môđun mạng nơron đồ thị: Tiếp theo việc xây dựng đồ thị, mô-đun mạng nơron đồ thị (GNN) đóng vai trò trung tâm trong việc học các biểu diễn ngữ nghĩa và cấu trúc phong phú cho từng hộp văn bản (node) dựa trên các mối quan hệ được định nghĩa. Mỗi hộp văn bản được coi là một nút trong đồ thị, và các đặc trưng ban đầu của nút ($h_v^{(0)}$) được khởi tạo bằng cách sử dụng các mô hình nhúng văn bản tiên tiến (ví dụ: Word2Vec, FastText hoặc các mô hình dựa trên Transformer như BERT) để chuyển đổi nội dung văn bản thành vector mật độ cao, nắm bắt ý nghĩa ngữ nghĩa. Tương tự, các cạnh trong đồ thị, được tạo ra từ thông tin mối quan hệ hoặc sự lân cận không gian, cũng được gán các đặc trưng ($e_{uv}$) để mã hóa loại mối quan hệ hoặc vị trí tương đối giữa hai nút, thường là dưới dạng vector nhúng hoặc mã hóa one-hot. Mô-đun GNN hoạt động dựa trên nguyên lý truyền tin (message passing) lặp đi lặp lại qua nhiều lớp. Ở mỗi lớp GNN thứ $k$, thông tin từ các nút lân cận ($N(v)$) được tổng hợp và truyền đến nút đang xét $v$. Quá trình này bao gồm ba bước chính: (1) Tạo thông điệp: Một hàm thông điệp ($M_k$) tính toán thông điệp ($m_{uv}^{(k)}$) mà nút $u$ gửi đến nút $v$, dựa trên đặc trưng hiện tại của $u$, $v$ và đặc trưng cạnh $e_{uv}$. (2) Tổng hợp: Một hàm tổng hợp ($A_k$) kết hợp tất cả các thông điệp đến từ các nút lân cận của $v$ để tạo ra một biểu diễn tổng hợp ($m_v^{(k)}$) cho nút $v$. Các hàm tổng hợp phổ biến bao gồm tổng, trung bình, hoặc các cơ chế chú ý tự động (self-attention) như được sử dụng trong Graph Attention Networks (GAT). (3) Cập nhật: Cuối cùng, một hàm cập nhật ($U_k$) tích hợp biểu diễn tổng hợp mới ($m_v^{(k)}$) với đặc trưng hiện tại của nút ($h_v^{(k)}$) để tạo ra đặc trưng cập nhật cho lớp tiếp theo ($h_v^{(k+1)}$). Công thức tổng quát cho quá trình cập nhật đặc trưng của nút $v$ ở lớp $k+1$ có thể được biểu diễn như $h_v^{(k+1)} = U_k(h_v^{(k)}, A_k(\{M_k(h_v^{(k)}, h_u^{(k)}, e_{uv}) | u \in N(v)\}))$. Sự lặp lại của quá trình truyền tin qua nhiều lớp cho phép mỗi nút tích lũy thông tin từ các láng giềng xa hơn, từ đó thu thập được một cái nhìn tổng thể hơn về cấu trúc đồ thị và ngữ cảnh của nó. Các kiến trúc GNN cụ thể có thể được áp dụng bao gồm Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN), Graph Attention Networks (GAT) và GraphSAGE, mỗi kiến trúc mang lại các ưu điểm riêng về cách tổng hợp thông tin và xử lý mối quan hệ giữa các nút. Sau khi đi qua một số lớp GNN, mỗi hộp văn bản sẽ có được một biểu diễn vector (node embedding) cuối cùng ($h_v^{(L)}$) có khả năng mã hóa toàn diện cả nội dung ngữ nghĩa của văn bản và vị trí cấu trúc của nó trong tài liệu. Những biểu diễn này là nền tảng cho các tác vụ hạ nguồn như phân loại hộp văn bản (ví dụ: xác định tiêu đề, đoạn văn, chú thích hình ảnh), trích xuất thông tin cụ thể (ví dụ: ngày tháng, số tiền), hoặc phân tích bố cục tài liệu tổng thể, bằng cách đưa các node embedding này vào một lớp phân loại hoặc hồi quy. text: Object detection is crucial in numerous visual applications, yet there is often a trade-off between the precision and speed of detectors. One key issue affecting the precision of fast detectors is the challenge in detecting small objects. To address this issue, we introduce a multiple receptive field and small-object-focusing weakly-supervised segmentation network (MRFSWSnet) aimed at achieving rapid object detection. In MRFSWSnet, a multiple receptive fields block (MRF) is employed to assign varying weights to different spatial locations of the object and its surrounding background, thereby enhancing the discriminative capacity of the features. Furthermore, to improve accuracy in detecting small objects, a small-object-focusing weakly-supervised segmentation module, which specifically targets small objects instead of all objects, is incorporated into the detection network for auxiliary training to enhance precision. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the efficacy of our method on both PASCAL VOC and MS COCO detection datasets. Notably, MRFSWSnet achieves 80.9% mAP on the VOC2007 test with a lower resolution of 300x300 and an inference speed of 15 milliseconds per frame, marking it as the state-of-the-art detector among real-time detectors.

We selected intents and utterance templates to allow realistic variation while controlling overall task complexity and limiting vocabulary size to about 700 unique words. We provide audio data along with transcripts and annotations for speaker identity, caller intent, dialog actions, and emotional valence. The data size and domain specificity makes for quick transcription experiments with modern end-to-end neural approaches. Further, we provide baselines for representation learning, adapting recent work to embed waveforms for downstream prediction tasks. Our experiments show that tasks using our annotations are sensitive to both the model choice and corpus size.

text: The rapid development of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) requires industrial production towards digitalization to improve network efficiency. Digital Twin is a promising technology to empower the digital transformation of IIoT by creating virtual models of physical objects. However, the provision of network efficiency in IIoT is very challenging due to resource-constrained devices, stochastic tasks, and resources heterogeneity. Distributed resources in IIoT networks can be efficiently exploited through computation offloading to reduce energy consumption while enhancing data processing efficiency. In this paper, we first propose a new paradigm Digital Twin Networks (DTN) to build network topology and the stochastic task arrival model in IIoT systems. Then, we formulate the stochastic computation offloading and resource allocation problem to minimize the long-term energy efficiency. As the formulated problem is a stochastic programming problem, we leverage Lyapunov optimization technique to transform the original problem into a deterministic per-time slot problem. Finally, we present Asynchronous Actor-Critic (AAC) algorithm to find the optimal stochastic computation offloading policy. Illustrative results demonstrate that our proposed scheme is able to significantly outperforms the benchmarks.

Các nghiệp vụ cơ bản được triển khai trên hệ thống bao gồm: **(1) Quản lý tài khoản người dùng**: Cung cấp khả năng đăng ký, đăng nhập, cập nhật thông tin cá nhân, xem lịch sử mua hàng và quản lý địa chỉ giao hàng. That is why I always begin the target sequence by the token < BOS > , and the decoder starts predicting from the second token on. Besides, the decoder needs a signal to stop its generative prediction. I always end a prediction by ”end-of-sentence” token or < EOS > . Therefore, instead of predicting [a, b, c, d, e ], the decoder predicts [a, b, c, d, e, < EOS > ]. text:
Neural sequence models have become a cornerstone of modern natural language processing, yet their computational demands often limit their practical deployment. This paper investigates the trade-off between computational efficiency and output quality in neural sequence models, aiming to provide a framework for balancing these critical factors. We propose a novel adaptive computation mechanism that dynamically adjusts the computational resources allocated to different parts of the input sequence based on their complexity. Our approach leverages lightweight heuristics and reinforcement learning to optimize resource allocation without compromising model performance. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method reduces computational overhead by up to 40% while maintaining competitive accuracy compared to state-of-the-art baselines. The results highlight the potential of adaptive computation as a scalable solution for deploying neural sequence models in resource-constrained environments. This work contributes to the growing body of research on efficient AI systems and offers practical insights for real-world applications in machine translation, text generation, and beyond.  

**Keywords**: neural sequence models, computational efficiency, adaptive computation, reinforcement learning, natural language processing.

Tỷ lệ trầm cảm ở phụ nữ điều trị thụ tinh trong ống nghiệm (IVF) dao động từ 10,9% đến 44,3%. Mục tiêu của nghiên cứu này là xác định tỷ lệ trầm cảm cũng như các yếu tố tác động đến trầm cảm ở bệnh nhân chuyển phôi thất bại. Mục tiêu: Xác định tỷ lệ và các yếu tố liên quan đến biểu hiện trầm cảm ở bệnh nhân chuyển phôi thất bại. Phương pháp nghiên cứu: Nghiên cứu cắt ngang. Dữ liệu được thu thập bằng cách phỏng vấn trực tiếp 278 bệnh nhân chuyển phôi thất bại tại khoa Hiếm muộn Bệnh viện Hùng Vương TPHCM từ tháng 12/2022 đến tháng 9/2023. Thang đánh giá trầm cảm được sử dụng là PHQ-9 với điểm cắt là 10. Kết quả: Tỷ lệ bệnh nhân có biểu hiện trầm cảm là 9,71%. Kết luận: Biểu hiện trầm cảm ở bệnh nhân chuyển phôi thất bại là vấn đề thường gặp, cần được quan tâm, chẩn đoán và điều trị sớm để nâng cao chất lượng cuộc sống người bệnh. text: Convex duality, particularly Fenchel-Rockafellar duality, presents a versatile framework that can be effectively applied to various reinforcement learning (RL) scenarios. This duality is instrumental in addressing problems such as policy evaluation and optimization, whether in online or offline settings and with either discounted or undiscounted rewards. By leveraging this framework, researchers can derive insightful results, such as conducting policy evaluation and on-policy policy gradient using behavior-agnostic offline data. Additionally, it facilitates learning a policy through maximum likelihood optimization. While these findings have been explored in disparate studies, a comprehensive synthesis offers a cohesive perspective, enabling a broader understanding and application of convex duality in RL. This unified approach aims to empower researchers to exploit these sophisticated mathematical tools more effectively, potentially driving significant advancements in the field of reinforcement learning. The insights gained from this synthesis underscore the profound impact of convex duality in enhancing the theoretical and practical aspects of RL, promoting innovative solutions and deeper exploration of complex RL challenges.

text: We tackle the blackbox issue of deep neural networks in the settings of reinforcement learning (RL) where neural agents learn towards maximizing reward gains in an uncontrollable way. Such learning approach is risky when the interacting environment includes an expanse of state space because it is then almost impossible to foresee all unwanted outcomes and penalize them with negative rewards beforehand. Unlike reverse analysis of learned neural features from previous works, our proposed method \nj an RL policy network to learn interpretable latent features through an implementation of a disentangled representation learning method. Toward this end, our method allows an RL agent to understand self-efficacy by distinguishing its influences from uncontrollable environmental factors, which closely resembles the way humans understand their scenes. Our experimental results show that the learned latent factors not only are interpretable, but also enable modeling the distribution of entire visited state space with a specific action condition. We have experimented that this characteristic of the proposed structure can lead to ex post facto governance for desired behaviors of RL agents.

text: This paper aims to establish a framework for extreme learning machines (ELMs) on general hypercomplex algebras. Hypercomplex neural networks are machine learning models that feature higher-dimension numbers as parameters, inputs, and outputs. Firstly, we review broad hypercomplex algebras and show a framework to operate in these algebras through real-valued linear algebra operations in a robust manner. We proceed to explore a handful of well-known four-dimensional examples. Then, we propose the hypercomplex-valued ELMs and derive their learning using a hypercomplex-valued least-squares problem. Finally, we compare real and hypercomplex-valued ELM models' performance in an experiment on time-series prediction and another on color image auto-encoding. The computational experiments highlight the excellent performance of hypercomplex-valued ELMs to treat high-dimensional data, including models based on unusual hypercomplex algebras.

text:
Camouflaged object detection (COD) is a challenging task in computer vision, where objects blend seamlessly into their surroundings, making them difficult to distinguish. This paper introduces a novel deep learning framework that leverages texture-aware features to improve the accuracy of camouflaged object detection. The proposed approach integrates a multi-scale texture analysis module within a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, enabling the model to capture fine-grained texture patterns that are critical for identifying camouflaged objects. By combining texture information with spatial and semantic features, the framework achieves superior performance in detecting objects that are intentionally concealed in complex backgrounds. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in terms of detection accuracy and robustness. The findings highlight the importance of texture-aware features in addressing the challenges of COD and provide a foundation for future research in object detection and scene understanding. This work has potential applications in fields such as surveillance, wildlife monitoring, and medical imaging, where detecting hidden objects is crucial.  

**Keywords**: Camouflaged object detection, texture-aware features, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, multi-scale analysis, computer vision.

text:
Sequence prediction is a fundamental challenge in various domains, including natural language processing, time-series analysis, and bioinformatics. Traditional recurrent neural networks (RNNs) often struggle with capturing long-term dependencies and suffer from vanishing gradient problems. This paper introduces Spectral RNNs, a novel approach leveraging spectral transformations to enhance sequence modeling capabilities. The proposed method integrates Fourier-based spectral analysis into the RNN architecture, enabling efficient learning of both short-term and long-term patterns in sequential data. We evaluate Spectral RNNs on benchmark datasets for time-series forecasting and language modeling tasks, comparing their performance against state-of-the-art models such as LSTMs and GRUs. Experimental results demonstrate that Spectral RNNs achieve superior accuracy and faster convergence, particularly in scenarios requiring the modeling of complex temporal dependencies. The findings highlight the potential of spectral methods to address key limitations in traditional RNNs, offering a promising direction for future research in sequence prediction. This work contributes to the advancement of deep learning architectures by introducing a computationally efficient and scalable solution for sequential data analysis.  

**Keywords**: Sequence prediction, Spectral RNNs, Fourier transform, recurrent neural networks, time-series analysis, language modeling.

text: Hợp chất chống cháy cơ phốt pho (OPFRs) bị phân hủy bởi tổ hợp 10 chủng vi khuẩn được phân lập từ sông Tô Lịch, Hà Nội bị ô nhiễm các OPFRs. Tổ hợp vi khuẩn được nuôi cấy trên môi trường A-Cl có bổ sung riêng lẻ các hợp chất thuộc OPFRs (nồng độ 10 mg/l) cho kết quả mật độ quang ở bước sóng 600 nm nằm trong khoảng 1-1,5. Tổ hợp 10 chủng vi khuẩn này có khả năng phân hủy tris(2-ethylhexyl) phosphate (TEHP) đạt hiệu suất 98,5 và 100% sau 2 và 3 ngày nuôi. Triethyl phosphate (TEP) cũng bị phân hủy 76,1 và 100% sau 2 và 5 ngày nuôi cấy. Hiệu suất phân hủy trimethyl phosphate (TMP), tris(2-chloroethyl) phosphate (TCEP), tris(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TCDPP) và tributoxy ethyl phosphate (TBEP) đạt 97-100% sau 4 ngày nuôi. Trong thí nghiệm bổ sung hỗn hợp 7 chất thuộc OPFRs có nồng độ 10 mg/l mỗi hợp chất, chỉ có TEHP bị phân hủy hoàn toàn sau 6 ngày nuôi. Hiệu suất phân hủy của các OPFRs khác tăng lên từ 93,2 đến 100% sau 6 ngày nuôi. So sánh tốc độ phân hủy các hợp chất thuộc OPFRs ở cả 2 thí nghiệm, kết quả thể hiện mẫu nuôi cấy có bổ sung từng hợp chất riêng lẻ cho tốc độ phân hủy xảy ra nhanh hơn so với khi bổ sung hỗn hợp các OPFRs.

text: Various methods for multi-domain machine translation are explored, with a primary focus on data-centric and a mention of model-centric approaches. Data-centric adaptation involves selecting or generating appropriate in-domain data, which can include choosing natural data from larger generic corpora based on domain-specific criteria, or filtering existing in-domain corpora. Additionally, source or target sentences can be generated by neural models when only monolingual natural data is accessible. Semi-synthetic bilingual data can be created through forward or back translation, and in-domain bilingual data can be partially synthesized from small natural datasets using noising or simplification. Finally, purely synthetic data can also be utilized for adaptation. A framework is proposed for training a single, multi-domain neural machine translation (NMT) model capable of translating across multiple domains without increasing inference time or memory usage. This model has demonstrated improved translation performance on both high and low-resource domains compared to strong multi-domain bases.

text:
This paper presents a full probabilistic model designed to address the challenges of yes-no type crowdsourcing in multi-class classification tasks. The objective is to improve the accuracy and reliability of crowdsourced labels, which are often noisy and inconsistent due to the varying expertise of annotators. The proposed model leverages a probabilistic framework to estimate the true class labels by integrating the responses of multiple annotators, each providing binary (yes-no) answers to specific questions about the data. The approach incorporates latent variables to model annotator reliability and class priors, enabling robust inference even in the presence of ambiguous or conflicting annotations. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the model outperforms existing methods in terms of classification accuracy and label consistency. The findings highlight the model's ability to effectively aggregate noisy crowdsourced data, making it a valuable tool for applications requiring scalable and cost-effective labeling solutions. This research contributes to the field of crowdsourcing by providing a novel, probabilistic approach that enhances the quality of multi-class classification tasks, with potential applications in areas such as image annotation, sentiment analysis, and data labeling for machine learning.  

**Keywords**: crowdsourcing, probabilistic model, multi-class classification, yes-no labeling, annotator reliability, label aggregation.

text: Benefiting from the spatial cues embedded in depth images, recent progress on RGB-D saliency detection shows impressive ability on some challenge scenarios. However, there are still two limitations. One hand is that the pooling and upsampling operations in FCNs might cause blur object boundaries. On the other hand, using an additional depth-network to extract depth features might lead to high computation and storage cost. The reliance on depth inputs during testing also limits the practical applications of current RGB-D models. In this paper, we propose a novel collaborative learning framework where edge, depth and saliency are leveraged in a more efficient way, which solves those problems tactfully. The explicitly extracted edge information goes together with saliency to give more emphasis to the salient regions and object boundaries. Depth and saliency learning is innovatively integrated into the high-level feature learning process in a mutual-benefit manner. This strategy enables the network to be free of using extra depth networks and depth inputs to make inference. To this end, it makes our model more lightweight, faster and more versatile. Experiment results on seven benchmark datasets show its superior performance.

Here is a 130-word abstract for the paper titled "Improved Consistency Regularization for GANs":

Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) benefit from discriminator consistency costs, yet this regularization can introduce sample artifacts. We address this by first elucidating the artifact source and proposing a mitigation strategy. Further, we introduce several novel modifications to consistency regularization designed to enhance GAN performance. Through extensive experimentation, we demonstrate significant improvements across various architectures and datasets. For unconditional image synthesis on CIFAR-10 and CelebA, our approach yields new state-of-the-art FID scores. On conditional CIFAR-10, we improve the FID from 11.48 to 9.21. Applying our technique to BigGAN on ImageNet-2012, we achieve a superior FID of 5.38 from 6.66, marking the best score for that model size. Our contributions include identifying and resolving regularization-induced artifacts and achieving leading performance in GAN training.

text:
Visual odometry and depth estimation are critical tasks in computer vision, enabling applications such as autonomous navigation and 3D scene reconstruction. This paper presents a novel approach leveraging Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) for both supervised and unsupervised learning of monocular video-based visual odometry and depth estimation. The proposed method addresses the challenges of scale ambiguity and temporal consistency in monocular sequences by integrating temporal dependencies through RNN architectures. Our approach employs a unified framework that jointly optimizes pose estimation and depth prediction, enabling end-to-end training with minimal supervision. For unsupervised learning, we introduce a self-supervised loss function that leverages photometric consistency and geometric constraints across consecutive frames. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance in both odometry and depth estimation tasks, outperforming existing unsupervised methods and closely matching supervised baselines. The key contributions of this work include a scalable RNN-based architecture, a robust self-supervised training strategy, and a comprehensive evaluation of its applicability in real-world scenarios. This research advances the state-of-the-art in monocular visual odometry and depth estimation, offering a promising direction for applications in robotics, augmented reality, and autonomous systems.  

**Keywords**: Recurrent Neural Networks, Visual Odometry, Depth Estimation, Monocular Video, Unsupervised Learning, Self-Supervised Learning.

text:
**Tóm tắt ý chính:**
Giả mạo định danh người dùng (user identity spoofing) trên website là một kỹ thuật tấn công phổ biến. Kẻ tấn công sử dụng kỹ thuật này để lừa người dùng tiết lộ thông tin cá nhân hoặc truy cập tài khoản của họ. Nhiều nghiên cứu trước (ví dụ: Chen & Park, 2019; Kumar & Sharma, 2022; Nguyen et al., 2020; Lee, 2021) đã ghi nhận mức độ phổ biến và tác động tiêu cực của hình thức tấn công này. Nghiên cứu hiện tại đề xuất một phương pháp phát hiện và ngăn chặn tấn công giả mạo định danh dựa trên phân tích hành vi người dùng theo thời gian thực, nhằm nâng cao an toàn cho người dùng.

**Đoạn văn viết lại:**
Giả mạo định danh người dùng trên các nền tảng website, thường được biết đến với thuật ngữ tiếng Anh là "user identity spoofing", là một hình thức tấn công mạng tinh vi và ngày càng phổ biến. Kỹ thuật này được các tác nhân độc hại khai thác nhằm mục đích lừa dối người dùng, dẫn đến việc họ vô tình tiết lộ thông tin cá nhân nhạy cảm hoặc cấp quyền truy cập trái phép vào tài khoản của mình (Nguyen et al., 2020; Lee, 2021). Mức độ phổ biến và tác động tiêu cực của các cuộc tấn công giả mạo định danh đã được ghi nhận rộng rãi trong nhiều công trình nghiên cứu trước đây (Chen & Park, 2019; Kumar & Sharma, 2022), nhấn mạnh sự cần thiết của các giải pháp phòng chống hiệu quả. Trong bối cảnh đó, nghiên cứu này đề xuất một phương pháp phát hiện và ngăn chặn tấn công giả mạo định danh dựa trên phân tích hành vi người dùng theo thời gian thực, hứa hẹn góp phần nâng cao tính an toàn và bảo mật cho người dùng cuối khi tương tác trong môi trường trực tuyến.
label: gemini-text

text:
Đoạn văn này giải thích rằng học có nguyên tắc (policy learning) đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc giúp chatbot mang lại trải nghiệm hài lòng cho người dùng cuối bằng cách tạo ra các chuỗi hành động hợp lý để điều hướng cuộc trò chuyện một cách mạch lạc. Quá trình này bao gồm việc chatbot học hỏi từ tương tác trước đây của người dùng và theo dõi luồng trò chuyện với những người dùng tương tự, từ đó lưu trữ thông tin và hiểu rõ hành vi cùng phương thức giao tiếp của người dùng nhằm hoạt động hiệu quả.

Học có nguyên tắc (policy learning) đóng vai trò then chốt trong việc kiến tạo trải nghiệm tổng thể thỏa mãn cho người dùng cuối trong các hệ thống chatbot. Điều này được thực hiện thông qua việc thiết lập các chuỗi hành động logic, đảm bảo luồng hội thoại được điều hướng một cách mạch lạc và phù hợp với kỳ vọng của người dùng. Cụ thể, chatbot thực hiện quá trình học hỏi liên tục từ các tương tác lịch sử của người dùng, đồng thời phân tích luồng trò chuyện đã diễn ra với những người dùng có đặc điểm tương đồng trong quá khứ. Qua đó, hệ thống tích lũy dữ liệu, phát triển sự thấu hiểu sâu sắc về hành vi và phương thức giao tiếp của người dùng, từ đó tối ưu hóa khả năng vận hành và mang lại hiệu quả cao.

text: cụ thể các nhiệm vụ đó là: công tác quản lý đảng viên, công tác tuyên giáo, lãnh đạo phát triển kinh tế - xã hội địa phương, xây dựng hệ thống chính trị cơ sở, và công tác báo cáo, thống kê. Mỗi nhiệm vụ này đòi hỏi sự chính xác, kịp thời và khối lượng công việc lớn, đặt ra thách thức đáng kể cho các phương pháp quản lý truyền thống hiện hành. Cụ thể, công tác quản lý đảng viên bao gồm việc duy trì toàn diện hồ sơ cá nhân, quá trình sinh hoạt, đóng đảng phí, khen thưởng, kỷ luật, và đánh giá đảng viên. Với số lượng đảng viên tại một chi bộ cấp xã thường xuyên biến động và nhu cầu cập nhật thông tin liên tục, việc quản lý bằng giấy tờ dễ dẫn đến tình trạng hồ sơ cồng kềnh, khó tra cứu, dễ hư hỏng hoặc thất lạc, đồng thời gây khó khăn trong việc tổng hợp, đối chiếu dữ liệu. Mặc dù ứng dụng Excel đã cải thiện phần nào khả năng lưu trữ và tổ chức dữ liệu so với giấy tờ, nhưng bản chất của nó là các tệp độc lập, thiếu tính năng cơ sở dữ liệu tập trung, dẫn đến tình trạng dữ liệu phân tán, trùng lặp và thiếu đồng bộ. Việc thiếu cơ chế kiểm soát truy cập và bảo mật mạnh mẽ trên Excel cũng là một hạn chế lớn đối với thông tin nhạy cảm của đảng viên. Khi số lượng đảng viên tăng lên hoặc các nghiệp vụ quản lý trở nên phức tạp hơn, Excel bộc lộ rõ những giới hạn về khả năng mở rộng và hiệu suất, khiến việc tổng hợp báo cáo trở nên thủ công, mất thời gian và dễ phát sinh sai sót. Tương tự, trong công tác tuyên giáo, chi bộ có trách nhiệm phổ biến các nghị quyết, chỉ thị của Đảng, chính sách pháp luật của Nhà nước đến đảng viên và quần chúng nhân dân; đồng thời nắm bắt dư luận xã hội. Việc theo dõi và đánh giá hiệu quả triển khai các nội dung này gặp rào cản khi dữ liệu không được số hóa và hệ thống hóa một cách bài bản. Các phương pháp thủ công không thể cung cấp cái nhìn tổng thể, đa chiều về tình hình thực hiện nhiệm vụ, gây khó khăn cho Chi bộ trong việc đưa ra các điều chỉnh hoặc quyết sách kịp thời. Trong vai trò lãnh đạo phát triển kinh tế - xã hội địa phương và xây dựng hệ thống chính trị cơ sở, Chi bộ cần thường xuyên theo dõi, đôn đốc việc thực hiện các chủ trương, dự án tại địa bàn. Sự thiếu hụt một hệ thống quản lý thông tin tập trung khiến việc giám sát trở nên kém hiệu quả, dữ liệu về tiến độ và kết quả thường bị phân mảnh, cản trở khả năng đánh giá tổng thể và kịp thời của lãnh đạo. Công tác báo cáo, thống kê cho cấp trên – một nhiệm vụ thường xuyên và quan trọng – trở nên nặng nề hơn rất nhiều khi phải tổng hợp dữ liệu từ nhiều nguồn giấy tờ và các tệp Excel riêng lẻ, đòi hỏi nhiều nhân lực và thời gian, đồng thời tăng rủi ro về sai sót dữ liệu. Điều này ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến tính kịp thời và độ chính xác của thông tin phục vụ công tác lãnh đạo, chỉ đạo của Chi bộ cũng như của cấp ủy cấp trên. Tổng thể, việc duy trì các phương pháp quản lý truyền thống và ứng dụng Excel đơn thuần đã tạo ra nhiều thách thức lớn cho Chi bộ xã Ngọc Lũ. Đầu tiên là hiệu quả hoạt động: Tốn kém thời gian và nguồn lực đáng kể vào các tác vụ hành chính lặp lại, thay vì tập trung vào công tác chuyên môn và phát triển. Thứ hai là độ chính xác của dữ liệu: Việc nhập liệu thủ công và sao chép giữa các hệ thống rời rạc làm tăng nguy cơ sai sót, dẫn đến thông tin không đáng tin cậy. Thứ ba là khả năng tra cứu và tổng hợp: Việc truy xuất thông tin cụ thể hoặc tổng hợp báo cáo đa chiều trở nên vô cùng khó khăn, đặc biệt khi cần phản ứng nhanh với các yêu cầu đột xuất. Thứ tư là tính bảo mật: Thông tin nhạy cảm của đảng viên và các tài liệu quan trọng dễ bị lộ hoặc thất lạc khi chỉ dựa vào lưu trữ vật lý hoặc các tệp không được bảo vệ chặt chẽ. Cuối cùng, và quan trọng nhất, là khả năng hỗ trợ ra quyết định: Với dữ liệu phân tán và thiếu công cụ phân tích, lãnh đạo Chi bộ khó có thể đưa ra các quyết sách chiến lược dựa trên cơ sở dữ liệu toàn diện và kịp thời. Những hạn chế này không chỉ làm giảm năng lực quản lý nội bộ của Chi bộ mà còn ảnh hưởng đến khả năng hoàn thành xuất sắc các nhiệm vụ chính trị, góp phần xây dựng tổ chức Đảng vững mạnh, đáp ứng yêu cầu của tình hình mới và chủ trương chuyển đổi số của Đảng và Nhà nước.
